News.title: Twisted undertaker & wife ripped gold teeth from bodies ‘using brute force’ & looted jewellery from 250 coffins
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

COFFIN RAID Twisted undertaker & wife ripped gold teeth from bodies ‘using brute force’ & looted jewellery from 250 coffins







Next

A TWISTED undertaker who ripped gold teeth from corpses with pliers and plundered hundreds of coffins has been jailed over a grave-robbing racket.

Karl-Heinz K., 63, secretly stripped dead bodies of jewellery, watches and precious metals while working at a cemetery in Germany.

The depraved funeral worker used “brute force” to wrench gold teeth from the dead before smashing them with a hammer to extract the valuable metal.

His horrifying operation saw at least 250 bodies desecrated between 2013 and 2024, with eight kilograms of precious metal stolen.





The haul was valued at a staggering €250,000 (£217,000), with his wife Simone, 41, helping to flog the stolen treasure.

Their grisly racket funded an increasingly lavish lifestyle, with bigger homes, flashier cars and season tickets to a popular theme park.

But the couple’s crimes eventually caught up with them when they appeared before Freiburg District Court in Baden-Württemberg.

Karl-Heinz admitted the offences, while his estranged wife confessed to helping sell the gold despite suspecting its gruesome origins.

She told the court: “Our cars and apartments kept getting bigger. And we had season tickets for Europa-Park.”

On Wednesday, the disgraced undertaker was sentenced to two years and six months behind bars for theft and disturbing the peace of the dead.

Simone, who has since separated from her husband, escaped jail with an 18-month suspended sentence.

But Karl-Heinz’s vile conduct extended beyond his lucrative corpse-looting operation.



He was also convicted of photographing murdered woman Dana Walleser, 46, and sharing the disturbing images on WhatsApp.

In a sickening message accompanying the pictures, he wrote: “She slashed her whole throat. Holes in her throat from the knife. Brutal. Disgusting.”

Dana’s devastated sister, Corina Apachite, 48, condemned the horrifying violation of her sibling’s dignity.

She told BILD: “Even in death, Dana wasn’t safe from a man’s violence.”

Karl-Heinz was ordered to pay the family €2,000 (£1,740) in damages, but Corina questioned whether the payout reflected the suffering inflicted.



She said: “Whether this sum does justice to the injustice is something I’m raising for public debate.

“This verdict only provides a limited conclusion. It shows how necessary further public and legal engagement with such acts and their consequences is.”

News.title: Girl, 3, killed after FORKLIFT driven by uncle smashes into her at biscuit factory in horror accident
News.content:
FAMILY HEARTBREAK Girl, 3, killed after FORKLIFT driven by uncle smashes into her at biscuit factory in horror accident







Next

A THREE-YEAR-OLD girl has been killed after her uncle allegedly struck and killed her with a forklift.

Police said Elliza Ramos Salvador’s uncle smashed into her with the heavy machinery at a biscuit factory.



The uncle, a co-owner of the factory in Andradas, southern Brazil, had allegedly been manoeuvring the forklift at the end of the working day when little Elliza suddenly stepped into its path.

He told police he had not seen his niece running through the building.



Elliza’s dad desperately shouted to the forklift driver after the horror accident, telling him he had hit the little girl.

Her uncle stopped the vehicle and rushed to help his niece.



The tragic accident took place around 6.30pm on Tuesday.

Elliza was rushed to hospital but arrived in cardiac arrest.

Despite medics’ best efforts, she could not be saved.

The little girl had reportedly been in the factory yard, appearing suddenly from behind a storage rack.



That rack is thought to have stopped Elliza’s uncle spotting her sooner in the moments before the accident.

Police launched an investigation into the tragic death.

Cops carried out a forensic examination.

Officers tried to interview Elliza’s parents, Eduardo and Ana Heloísa, but they were too distraught to give statements.

It comes after a forklift operator fell to his death whilst working on a hanging platform outside a building project in Vietnam last year.



Horrified colleagues could do nothing to save the crushed construction worker.

And in December, a man who was cut in half in a horror forklift accident in Montana told of a bitter family feud and how he became a “spectacle” after surviving against all odds.

Loren Schauers was just 18 when a catastrophic workplace accident in September 2019 left him severed from the waist down.

The teenage construction worker was driving a forklift across a bridge in Great Falls when he was forced to veer off the road.

The vehicle plunged 50ft, pinning him beneath it. He remained conscious throughout and later recalled seeing his right arm destroyed and his lower body crushed.



He told the Daily Mail: “It seemed like as soon as my family knew I wasn’t going to just up and die, they all quit showing up and providing any support.

“Once I got home my friends and family came around but quickly I noticed it was to more see what’s up than caring about me.

“They just wanted to see the spectacle.”

News.title: Inside scandal-hit Abu Dhabi royal family… from ‘slave’ servants to ‘torture tape’ with ‘victim’ beaten & set on fire
News.content:
Next

WHEN passers by went over to check on the woman they found slumped on a busy London street, barefoot, while a three-year-old played next to dangerous traffic, few would have guessed she was part of a family with more than a quarter of a trillion pounds in wealth.

But Mahrah Al Nahyan, who had passed out as a result of a cocaine binge, was in fact a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family – one of the richest and most powerful royal families in the world, rulers of the oil-rich Emirate.



This week Al Nahyan, 32, a member of the family by marriage, pleaded guilty to one charge of child neglect following the incident in June.

Video released by the CPS showed Al Nahyan sitting on the pavement without any shoes on, her back against black railings.



Around her lay children’s toys, including a scooter and a plane.

Rio Pahlavanpour, prosecuting, said at around 1.50pm a passerby “noticed the child was unattended, without shoes on the street with a scooter and seemed to be in close proximity to moving traffic”.



The court was also told that Al Nahyan had been undergoing treatment for drug addiction at The Priory, the private rehab centre that has counted Kate Moss and Johnny Depp among clients.

The royal, who receives an £8,000 monthly allowance, was slapped with a two-year community order and fined £5,000 plus £1,000 prosecution costs.

But this is just the latest crisis to hit a royal family whose recent history includes serious human rights abuses and a controversial court case over torture allegations.

In 2009 a tape was leaked that showed Sheikh Issa bin Zayed al-Nahyan, a senior member of the ruling family, brutally beating and torturing an Afghan man he accused of cheating him in a business deal.



Issa, the half-brother of Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour, is seen in the 45-minute video filmed in the desert relentlessly brutalising the grain merchant, Mohammed Shah Poor, who miraculously survived.

He fires an automatic weapon into the ground around him, forces a cattle prod into his anus and switches it on, and beats him with a wooden plank with nails.

Later on in the video, Issa urges the cameraman to move closer to “let his suffering show”, while a man in police uniform can also be seen helping to tie the victim up.

He had also been run over with a Mercedes SUV, and had lighter fluid poured onto his testicals and set alight. Salt was also poured onto his wounds.



The tape was smuggled out of the country to ABC news, who then posted an abridged version of it.

In response, Abu Dhabi’s Ministry of the Interior said the torture depicted was not part of a “pattern of behaviour” and added that a review found “all rules, policies and procedures were followed correctly by the police department”.

They added that the matter had been settled privately between the two men.

The Minister of the Interior was one of Issa’s brothers.



Following international outcry, the authorities finally acted and put Issa on trial.

But Issa was declared innocent – and that he was actually the victim..

Instead, the court convicted the man who had smuggled the tape out of the country, an American businessman named Bassam Nabulsi, who was put on trial in absentia.

Despite never being told he was being charged with anything, the court declared that Nabulsi and his brother had secretly injected Issa with drugs, making him incapable of having any responsibility over his actions.

They ended up being sentenced for “drugging, recording and publishing a video and blackmail”.



As they were in Texas, they avoided actually going to jail.

Nabulsi said the result had left him feeling “nauseous”.

In the years since Issa has largely stayed out of the spotlight.

However in 2025 made a rare public appearance along with other senior members of the family at a show to mark the UAE’s national day, Eid Al Etihad.



But this wasn’t to be the last time one of the Al Nahyan’s would be caught committing abuse.

In 2017, eight of the royal princesses were convicted on human trafficking and abuse charges that happened while they were renting out a whole floor at a luxury hotel in Belgium.

Sheikha Hamda Al Nahyan and seven of her daughters had rented out part of the Conrad Hotel in Brussels for eight months in 2008, bringing with them more than 20 servants.

But they were accused of holding the workers in conditions close to slavery, prevented from ever leaving the hotel by private guards and being forced to eat the princesses’ leftovers.

The case only came to light when one of the servants escaped the hotel.



Victims also revealed that they had to take orders 24 hours a day, were forced to sleep on the floor, and one even said they had been deprived of food and water for three days.

Many of the 23 women had originally been citizens of African countries and were smuggled into the country without proper documentation or visas.

The eight princesses were found guilty and each handed a 15-month suspended sentence and fined £139,600, though they did not attend the trial.

In 2020, the family hit the headlines again after Sheikh Nahyan Al-Nahyan was accused of sexually assaulting a British woman in Abu Dhabi.

Caitlin McNamara, then 32, was curating the Hay literary festival which was being staged in the UAE, when she alleges she was attacked by the then 69-year-old, who was Minister of Tolerance, at a secluded palace.



She told the Sunday Times she had reported the incident to the Metropolitan Police on her return to the UK but the CPS declined to bring charges, as the alleged assault took place abroad and did not meet the strict criteria to go ahead.

The sheikh denied any wrong- doing and said he was “surprised and saddened” by the claims.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Even today, the Abu Dhabi government and the wider United Arab Emirates are accused by groups like Amnesty of serious failings around human rights.



This includes the handing life sentences to human rights defenders, the exploitation of migrant workers, and for providing support to Rapid Support Forces in Sudan, a paramilitary organisation responsible for war crimes who are fighting the Sudanese Armed Forces.

News.title: Schoolgirl held captive for a month by twisted teen who raped her multiple times and also sexually abused two others
News.content:
SICK FIEND Schoolgirl held captive for a month by twisted teen who raped her multiple times and also sexually abused two others







Next

A SCHOOLGIRL was held captive for almost a month by a teenage boy after he had raped another girl and a woman.

Lucan Wright, now 20, raped a woman and a teenage girl multiple times when he was 17-years-old.

He also subjected them to threats of violence, and controlling and coercive behaviour.

Between last December and January of this year, Wright imprisoned his third victim, another teenage girl, for nearly a month.





While she was held captive at a property in Worksop, Nottinghamshire, Wright strangled the girl, physically assaulted her multiple times and threatened her.

His horrific crimes were only revealed when the three victims bravely reported him to the police.

He was charged with multiple counts of rape, engaging in controlling and coercive behaviour, strangulation, false imprisonment and making threats to kill.

He was later charged with multiple counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and assault by beating.

Wright, from Worksop, admitted to the latter charges but denied the rest. He was found guilty after a trial at Nottingham Crown Court in July this year.

He was given an extended 15-year custodial sentence on Tuesday after appearing at the court via video-link.

Judge Michael Auty declared Wright a dangerous offender and jailed him for 12 years – of which he must serve a minimum of half before being eligible for release – with a further three years on licence.

Wright will have to sign the sex offenders’ register for the rest of his life and was handed a restraining order against his three victims.



Detective Constable Chloe Buckley, of Nottinghamshire Police, said: “As the judge rightly summarised, Lucan Wright is a dangerous individual who poses a real threat to women and teenage girls.

“It is hard to comprehend the harrowing experience each of these three victims were put through at the hands of Wright.

“He was responsible for raping two of them on more than one occasion and for subjecting the other to a horrible ordeal of prolonged violence.

“These are horrendous crimes that can devastate people’s lives, so it is to their absolute credit that they found the strength to come forward.

“The bravery they showed played a critical role in ensuring the truth about Wright was revealed and he received this deserved custodial sentence.



“Putting a stop to all incidents of violence against women and girls remains a key priority for this police force.

“We hope this sentence encourages more victims to have the confidence to report offenders, so we can put them before the courts.”

News.title: Murdered BBL doc ‘made Brit woman sign NDA’ after botched op left her with ‘bum sewn together’ as cops probe new theory
News.content:
Next

A CELEBRITY BBL doctor allegedly made a British woman sign an NDA after a botched operation before he was shot dead in his Marbella clinic.

Dr Alexander Aslani, 57, was assassinated in front of horrified customers by a masked gunman last week.



The world renowned surgeon’s client list included reality stars like Towie’s Chloe Sims and Love Island’s Hannah Elizabeth.

But one former client has now revealed Aslani refused a refund after fitting a silicon implant in the “wrong place”.



The British woman, who has not been named, visited Aslani’s Costa del Sol clinic, Circumed, for a but lift in 2021.

But soon after the operation she began to feel unwell and was unable to eat.



She told the Olive Press: “With Aslani, he always minimised everything, like it wasn’t an issue.

“So I felt reassured, but I also felt like death. And that’s when my partner looked over and he told me that they had sewn my bum together.

“He said he could see little blood clots coming out of the stitches.”

The woman said she was convinced she was going to die on her flight back to the UK.



Within an hour of returning home, the mum-of-one was hospitalised in London with early stages of sepsis.

In a letter the slain surgeon admitted to feeling “incredibly frustrated and sad” about the operation and offered a refund.

But he denied that he had botched the procedure and demanded she sign a “disclaimer” before the reimbursement was paid.



A document attached to the letter even barred the client from posting “any type of criticism or negative comment” about Aslani online.

If she did, she would have to return the full €9,600 reimbursement plus costs and interest.

An 18-year-old Swede arrested less than 24 hours after the surgeons shooting admitted to gunning down the surgeon, according to Spanish sources.

The alleged killer – who has since been remanded in custody without bail – is reportedly refusing to answer questions.

Detectives believe a furious patient may have hired a hitman after a row over cosmetic surgery.



The latest lines of inquiry being probed by cops is Aslani’s refusal to return a £17,000 advance payment for an op.

Aslani reportedly vetoed requests by a patient for a refund because he considered the sum a standard charge for preliminary examinations.

Detectives are said to be focusing on the financial dispute as a possible new motive as they continue to trawl through patient case files.



It emerged over the weekend that a different woman allegedly threatened Aslani after he refused to refund her for butt lift.

Reports claimed Aslani received angry messages and threats over mobile hours before he was killed.

A major hunt has been launched for the client who reportedly fled Spain to her home country in the Persian Gulf, according to local outlet Okdiario.

On Friday local outlet Sur reported Aslani had gone to cops in April to complain he had been receiving “work-related” threats.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It was not clear whether he had pointed the finger at named individuals in his police statement or not.



Cops have ruled out an earlier theory that Aslani was killed in revenge for a patient dying during surgery, after finding no evidence of any such death.

News.title: ‘Sad day’ as huge UK Bonfire Night is axed after more than 30 years
News.content:
Next

A MAJOR UK Bonfire Night event has been cancelled after more than 30 years in a “sad day” for locals.

The news was confirmed on social media this week after organisers announced their departure from involvement in the event.

A community bonfire hosted in Wirrall has been cancelled just weeks ahead of Bonfire Night this year.



It is regarded as one of the largest bonfire spectacles to take place in Merseyside.



Woodchurch Connect, a community support charity involved in the organisation of the event, confirmed the news via its Facebook page.

In a post to Facebook, Woodchurch Connect said: “Unfortunately Woodchurch Connect is now not involved with the community bonfire this year.

“The lads who normally organise this have faced numerous challenges for the last couple of years which were unachievable for them and disappointing for them as they’ve done such a great job in the past and should be appreciated for their efforts in trying to create a community event.

“It was not for want of trying, everyone tried their best to make this event happen.

“Thank you to everyone who supported and helped raise funding.”

“Sad day for the community.”

Woodchurch Connect became involved with running the event last year when they were asked by the community to participate in the organisation of the bonfire.



The Sun has contacted Wirral Council for comment.

Another Bonfire Night in Truro, Cornwall has been axed for the second year in a row to the disappointment of locals.

The event was scrapped after the council announced that it “can only stage events where it is satisfied that it can do so safely and within available budgets”.

Another bonfire firework display in Shaldon, Devon has also been cancelled owing to a road closure that is still in place.

News.title: Shocking moment Ryanair cabin crew scream ‘sit down’ after tourist ‘ignored seatbelt sign & attacked passengers’
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a Ryanair cabin crew member yells at a passenger to sit down after he allegedly attacked other passengers and ignored the seatbelt sign.

Dramatic footage from inside the cabin of the Ibiza-bound flight shows a brawl breaking out mid air.



An air hostess can be seen trying to break up the commotion.

She yells at a passenger to “sit down” as other travellers watch the chaos unfold.



The flight from London Stansted was preparing to land on the Spanish party island on October 5 when all hell broke loose.

According to holidaymaker Harry Watson, 28, the man at the centre of the fight had stood up to go to the toilet despite the seatbelt sign being on.



Harry witnessed the brawl and said as the man stood up to use the bathroom, other passengers began to shout at him.

He said one person was being “very verbal” as the man went back to his seat.

Harry added: “The lad didn’t like it, so he got angry and violent towards the guy, which caused a fight to break out.

“This happened multiple times.”



The passenger then allegedly started a scrap, lashing out at other travellers.

Harry said: “The lad started attacking the other passengers and had to be restrained a lot.

“There was then another guy that got up and hit the lad.”

As the chaos continued, pilots could not prepare to land, causing the flight to be delayed.

Passengers were not happy about the delay.



Harry added: “Everyone got very annoyed after a while, especially because the plane couldn’t land and had to go back in the air again.”

Spanish cops arrested and cuffed the man when the plane was finally able to land at Ibiza Airport.

A spokesperson for Ryanair said: “Crew on this flight from London Stansted to Ibiza (5 Oct) called ahead for police assistance after a passenger became disruptive onboard.

News.title: When is the first day of winter 2026? The official dates of the UK seasons and this year’s winter solstice
News.content:
Next

WINTER is only a few turns of the calendar away as we barrel toward the final days of 2026 – but when does the cold season technically begin?

Depending on who you ask, there are two completely different answers to this question.



Weather experts might tell you one thing, while those more concerned with the position of the stars may have a different answer.

This leaves us with two different dates to mark the start of the chilliest time of the year.



What is meteorological winter?

If you follow the meteorological calendar, the answer is straightforward: winter always starts and finishes on the same dates each year.

This system splits the year into four neat, three-month blocks based on the Gregorian calendar we all use every day.

This makes it easier for weather and climate experts to compare seasonal statistics, like average rainfall and temperature, year over year.

Meteorological winter always covers the three coldest calendar months of December, January and February.

This year, it begins on Tuesday, December 1 and ends on Sunday, February 28, 2027.

This means autumn officially ends on Monday, November 30.



What is astronomical winter?

The much older, astronomical calendar is based on the Earth‘s position relative to the sun.

According to this system, the first day of winter coincides with the winter solstice.

The Earth is tilted at an angle of 23.4 degrees, meaning different parts of the planet receive varying amounts of sunlight throughout the year.

In the UK, the winter solstice occurs when the Earth’s Northern Hemisphere is tilted at its furthest possible point away from the sun.

Because of this, the winter solstice marks the year’s “shortest day” – London will get just seven hours and 49 minutes of sunlight.



In 2026, this will fall on Monday, December 21, with the precise moment of solstice occurring at exactly 8.50pm.

Because the Earth technically takes 365.24 days to orbit the sun, the exact dates and times of the astronomical seasons shift slightly each year.

What are the ‘official’ dates of the other seasons in 2027?

According to meteorological definitions, the other seasons in 2027 are:

Spring: March 1 to May 31

March 1 to May 31 Summer: June 1 to August 31

June 1 to August 31 Autumn: September 1 to November 30

September 1 to November 30 Winter: December 1 to February 28 (or February 29 in a leap year)

Note that these dates remain the same every single year.

News.title: Tiger attack – latest: Yorkshire Wildlife Park to reopen as tiger 'safe and well'
News.content:
Yorkshire Wildlife Park will reopen on Friday after former child actor William Chapman, 24, was killed when he jumped into the tiger enclosure last weekend

Yorkshire Wildlife Park has confirmed it is set to reopen following the deadly tiger attack last weekend.

William Chapman, 24, was mauled to death by a tiger called Altai after climbing into its enclosure. An inquest opening today heard Mr Chapman died from "multiple traumatic injuries", and his family had "expressed a number of concerns in relation to his contact with mental health services leading up to his death". Mr Chapman had been diagnosed with schizophrenia and suffered previous bouts of psychosis, but was living independently.

In an update this afternoon, Yorkshire Wildlife Park said it would reopen on Friday. It also confirmed again that Altai was "safe and well" and will not be euthanised.

"Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies remain with the family, friends and loved ones of William Chapman," the park added.

Mr Chapman filmed his last moments as he approached Altai, and posted it online. The inquest opening heard how he had scaled two fences to enter the pen.

Mr Chapman's devastated family, who were not at the inquest opening, have said he was "bright, warm, and engaging".

News.title: Andy Burnham hits out at 'poison' and challenges Nigel Farage over Reform racism sting
News.content:
Andy Burnham hits out at 'poison' and challenges Nigel Farage over Reform racism sting

WARNING: DISTRESSING CONTENT Andy Burnham said a 'poison' has been allowed into British politics as he called on Nigel Farage to take 'immediate and firm' action following an ITV undercover sting

ITV Exposure documentary goes undercover inside Reform UK

Andy Burnham has demanded Nigel Farage takes "immediate and firm" action against Reform councillors caught using racist and sexist language in an undercover TV sting.

‌



‌



Reform UK is in crisis after footage broadcast by ITV showed one councillor describing Asian homeowners as "parasites" and another suggesting the King should be beheaded for secretly being Muslim.

‌



Mr Burnham said it was time to draw a line under the "poison" in British politics. Reform says it is investigating a number of cases and has suspended some members after the videos came to light.

‌



The Prime Minister said: "We've allowed a poison into our politics in recent years, and it's time to draw a line under it. In fact, I praised the Leader of the Opposition (Kemi Badenoch) in the House of Commons yesterday afternoon, who herself drew a line at her party conference between her party and that type of politics, and we all need to call it out more.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood threatens to ban all visas from African nation over migrant row READ MORE :

View 4 Images Former Reform councillor Alan Feeney was filmed making racist comments in an undercover sting (Image: ITV)

"I'm pleased ITV has done this. There is no place for any form of racism, antisemitism, discrimination in British politics, and we all should be relentless in repeating that and taking the firmest possible action.

‌



"And I hope the Reform Party will take immediate and firm action against those who've been revealed to be making these abhorrent comments."

On Wednesday footage showed Reform councillor Alan Feeney, deputy mayor of Solihull, claim that his area was "infested" with Asian homeowners. He was seen suggesting the government should "drag them out of their homes".

Another clip showed a South London councillor, Dean Miller, saying the King should be beheaded after claiming the monarch is secretly a Muslim. He also described Black children as "f***** animals".

‌



And Raymond Dunning, who claimed to have been asked by Reform to run as an MP, said on camera: "I'm so far-right it's unbelievable." Further clips, recorded during a year-long investigation, showed councillor Chris Whelen making vile sexual remarks about a female Reform colleague.

View 4 Images Andy Burnham called on Nigel Farage to act (Image: STEVE FINN PHOTOGRAPHY)

The footage - set to feature in a 90-minute documentary to be screened on Sunday - raises questions about vetting by Reform UK.

‌



Secretly-recorded video shows Mr Feeney looking at cars on a driveway in an area he claims has too many Asian homeowners. In it he said claimed it was "infested" - and added: "They're parasites, absolute parasites”.

And unaware he was being filmed, he told an undercover reporter: "When a house comes up for sale, white people need to be in there. You almost need to f***ing out-Muslim the Muslims.”

Mr Feeney also said: "I’d be saying no more than 1% of [the] British population can be non-white… you'd need a proper nuclear option, like literally drag them out of their homes..."

‌



And he also said the UK was getting to a point where Muslims could be banned from public office.

View 4 Images Former Reform councillor distanced himself from remarks caught on camera (Image: ITV)

Mr Feeney announced he had left Reform for personal reasons this week. Another undercover clip shows Dean Miller, a Reform councillor in Bromley, South London, claiming King Charles was Muslim, because "someone from the inside" had seen a prayer mat.

‌



He branded the monarch "traitorous" and in an expletive-filled diatribe said his head should be cut off.

In a statement sent to The Mirror, Mr Miller said he had resigned the party whip, adding: "This decision was taken due to a catastrophic, multi-layered failure of the duty of care and safeguarding by party leadership at both local and national levels."

He continued: "Any footage obtained by undercover operatives occurred when I was suffering from acute physical and neurological distress, sleep deprivation, and heavily under the influence of strong, legally prescribed neurological pain medications. Any remarks captured during this period of severe cognitive impairment does not reflect my character, my beliefs, or my years of dedicated humanitarian and public health service."

‌



Another Solihull Reform councilor, Chris Whelan, is accused of making misogynistic comments about a female Reform candidate. He announced on Monday that he had resigned from Reform.

The Mirror has contacted Mr Feeney, Mr Dunning and Mr Whelan for comment. A statement from Reform UK said: "Where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced. In some cases, there have been suspensions and due process must be followed.

View 4 Images Chris Whelan was recorded making mysoginistic comments about a Reform colleague (Image: ITV)

‌



"Reform UK has improved and prioritised its vetting procedures, but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting. This is the same for all organisations. However good the vetting, one cannot vet a future comment especially in circumstances where an individual is entrapped in a discussion with an undercover reporter. There is no room for racism in Reform UK."

Labour chair Bridget Phillipson said: "The extreme racism and appalling behaviour exposed by this investigation is truly sickening. Nigel Farage can't shrug these latest revelations off as being a few bad apples.

"Every Reform councillor, council candidate or party member found to have made such despicable comments must be thrown out of Reform UK immediately.

Article continues below

"Nigel Farage needs to explain why this keeps happening in his party and why he is failing to deal with blatant racism among those who stand for public office with his backing. It's clear that Farage and his party are determined to poison our politics and threaten the shared British values Labour will always proudly defend."

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey described ITV's report as "chilling", and said: "I feel for anyone watching this tonight who is frightened to see such racism and hatred festering in their community. It's the very worst of what we're seeing in Trump's America. We can't let it become Farage's Britain."

The accusations are among those set to feature in 90-minute film Undercover: A Year In Reform, Sunday 18th October at 10.20pm on ITV1, ITVX, STV & STV Player

News.title: Should Harry and Meghan be allowed to undertake faux royal engagements? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should Harry and Meghan be allowed to undertake faux royal engagements? Take our poll and have your say

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have completed their first joint engagement back in the UK, six years on from quitting their royal roles

Harry and Meghan in Nottingham on first joint engagement since UK return

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have completed their first joint engagement since moving back to the UK, after spending Thursday attending back-to-back engagements in Nottingham. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex spent their away day with three charities close to their hearts, just seven weeks on from relocating back to Britain.

‌



‌



The couple started their day at the Community Recording Studio (CRS), a youth and community charity based in St Ann’s. Originally established to give young people access to music and recording facilities, it now offers a broader range of creative activities, sport, mentoring and youth development.

‌



Before heading inside, Harry and Meghan spent 25 minutes meeting excited fans who were waiting to catch a glimpse of the couple, as they took selfies with fans and Meghan accepted numerous bouquets of flowers. While they were outside, Meghan declared: “Oh it’s great to be back."

‌



Prince William makes rare radio appearance hours before Harry and Meghan 'royal-style' engagement READ MORE :

View 3 Images Harry and Meghan spent a day completing back-to-back engagements in Nottingham on Thursday (Image: Getty Images)

At the recording studio, Harry and Meghan were treated to theatrical and musical performances, while the Duchess also joined a jewellery making class with a group of young girls to talk about self confidence.

Then, Harry and Meghan made their way to Himmah Hub, a food poverty community action group. Himmah is a Nottingham charity tackling poverty, food insecurity, racism and social exclusion through community meals, food parcels and wider practical support.

‌



Meghan reconnected with the women of the Hubb Community Kitchen, with whom she collaborated with for the 2018 project Together: Our Community Cookbook , before Harry and Meghan helped prepare food packages. The Duchess embraced each of the women in the kitchen before enveloping them in a group hug as she said: "It's been too long!"

The couple finished their day with Epic Partners, a charity which supports children, young people and families in St Ann’s and Sneinton, Nottingham, through youth work, sport, mentoring and education.

‌



The visit highlighted a relationship between the organisation and the Duke spanning more than a decade, built around a shared commitment to early intervention, community-led support and creating lasting opportunities for young people.

While their trip is not an official royal visit, given that the Sussexes took a step back from their royal duties in 2020 and moved to America, they spent their day engaging with various charities and people in the community.

Since moving back to Britain in late August, Harry has attended numerous engagements in the UK for various causes, namely the inaugural Invictus Spirit Awards and the United for Freedom gala to raise money for organisations supporting Ukraine.

‌



View 3 Images Prince Harry at the Invictus Spirit Awards (Image: David Levene/Invictus Games Foundation/PA Wire)

For Meghan however, the trip to Nottingham marked the first time in four years that the Duchess has appeared publicly at events in the UK – the last time being the late Queen’s funeral in 2022.

Earlier this year, before they moved back to Britain, the Duke and Duchess undertook two international trips: one to Jordan in February, and another to Australia in April. In Jordan, Harry and Meghan spent two days visiting several charities and mingled with locals, and even joined a roundtable discussion hosted by the WHO with individuals from major leading bodies like the United Nations.

‌



The couple were invited to the region by the World Health Organization’s (WHO) director-general Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesu to learn more over a two-day trip about the tireless humanitarian effort to support the health and wellbeing of displaced Syrians and Palestinians who have sought sanctuary in Jordan over many decades.

View 3 Images Harry and Meghan spent two days in Jordan earlier this year (Image: PA)

In Australia, the couple undertook events both together and separately, visiting a children’s hospital in Melbourne and meeting with locals in Sydney in the wake of the deadly attack at Bondi Beach together. Individually, Harry travelled to the War Memorial in Canberra, while Meghan spoke at a wellness retreat and appeared as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia.

Article continues below

Following their quasi-royal tour of Jordan, body language expert Judi James explains how the Duke and Duchess of Sussex seem more at ease with a non-official tour as opposed to the work of a senior royal.

Judi told the Mirror at the time: "So far this looks like an important expression of pared-back-to-basics 'royalty' from the couple in the face of the stubborn storm clouds hovering in the UK. It seems to suggest a disconnect from a couple happier to be seen playing kick-about in crumpled casuals right now than anything more formal or high-status."

News.title: Prince Harry's 'habit' reveals his true feelings at event with Meghan Markle, expert claims
News.content:
Prince Harry's 'habit' reveals his true feelings at event with Meghan Markle, expert claims

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle were greeted by fans as they stepped out together for their first joint engagement since returning to the UK in August

View 3 Images The Duke And Duchess Of Sussex visit Nottingham (Image: Getty)

A body language expert has claimed Prince Harry made a telltale gesture during his latest public appearance with Meghan Markle. The pair's outing in Nottingham on Thursday (October 15) marked the couple's first joint public engagement since returning to the UK in August.

‌



‌



Ahead of taking part in a series of events linked to their charitable work in the city, the pair stopped to chat with well-wishers and also collected gifts.

‌



Observing the pair, body language specialist Beth Dawson noticed the return of a habit from Harry.

‌



While some might expect Meghan to be the more anxious of the two, Beth believes the Duke of Sussex showed clearer signs of nervousness throughout the engagement.

She shared: "What is interesting is Harry’s behaviour. We see him going from side to side and moving quite quickly.

"He does not use slow relaxed movements and he is repeatedly wiping his palms against his trousers," she added, reports The Express.

‌



View 3 Images The couple were greeted by a cheerful crowd (Image: Getty)

"This tells me he might be nervous as either he has sweaty palms, which can occur during stress, or it could be a self-soothing gesture," she added.

"I have seen him do this before and it seems to be one of his habits and go-to gestures when he's in public.

‌



"Although we can't know whether he is actually sweating. What interests me is the possibility that we're seeing a small self-soothing and nervous habit during a very public encounter," she continued.

Meanwhile, Beth also believes Meghan may find it easier to conceal any nerves thanks to her background in acting.

"Meghan's background as a trained actress is relevant here, particularly when considering her familiarity with cameras, audiences and public-facing events," she added.

‌



"Meghan understands the importance of making individual members of a crowd feel acknowledged and she does this well with smiles, handshakes and closeness."

The expert also believes a gesture Harry made towards Meghan during the engagement could reveal something significant about their marriage.

View 3 Images The event marks their first joint engagement together since returning to the UK (Image: Getty)

‌



The couple were last seen in Nottingham in December 2017, just four days after announcing their engagement. They married the following year and have since welcomed two children, Archie and Lilibet.

Harry and Meghan stepped back from their senior royal duties in 2020 before relocating to California.

They returned to the UK in August, although they remain non-working members of the Royal Family.

‌



The couple are believed to be living in the Cotswolds, an area popular with numerous celebrities, including the Beckhams, Ellen DeGeneres and Princess Anne.

Earlier this month, they were spotted walking into a local pub where they are believed to have enjoyed lunch.

A friend of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex told The Sun: "They are enjoying exploring the area including local watering holes.

Article continues below

"Meghan has been spending a lot of time since their move to the UK making sure the children are settled and working on her As Ever brand. When they aren’t working, like most couples they like to spend time together.”

News.title: 'Mum was passed out at the wheel. I was screaming. It was up to me to save us'
News.content:
'Mum was passed out at the wheel. I was screaming. It was up to me to save us'

When his mum fell unconscious while driving at 60mph, 12-year-old Zac Howells sprang into action and saved their lives. On Monday he will receive the Pride of Britain Child of Courage award for his bravery

View 4 Images Zac's quick thinking saved the lives of him, his mum Nicola, and countless others (Image: WalesOnline/Rob Browne)

Seeing his mum collapse while driving at 60mph quick-thinking Zac Howells reached over and grabbed the wheel to steer their car to safety. The 12-year-old’s calmness prevented a potentially devastating crash and saved lives, including his and mum Nicola Crump.

‌



‌



For his heroic actions Zac, now 13, will receive his Child of Courage Award on stage at the Daily Mirror’s Pride of Britain Awards in partnership with P&O Cruises on Monday.

‌



Nicola, 38, who worked in a children’s home at the time, was driving him to a Christmas market in Warwickshire from their home in Ebbw Vale last December.

‌



Peter Crouch hails 'amazing' family duo who save men from suicide READ MORE :

They were travelling at 60mph on the A40 in Herefordshire when Nicola began feeling unwell. She managed to slow the car and steer it half off the road on to a narrow verge before she passed out.

View 4 Images Proud mum Nicola with her hero son Zac (Image: WalesOnline/Rob Browne)

She says: “I was going up to a market just past Birmingham. I still had shopping to do, so I asked Zac to come with me. Things changed within minutes. I said, ‘Zac, I feel hot’. I said, ‘Zac, I don’t feel well, I need to pull over’. I was panicking. Is anyone going to see me in time? That’s all I remember.”

‌



Zac says: “It was like any other drive, listening to music, it was just like normal. But all of a sudden she just looked really flustered.”

Nicola passed out. And, with the automatic gearbox still in drive, her foot jammed on the accelerator and the car veered back out on to the dual carriageway.

Zac recalls: “All of a sudden, the car started to speed up really fast. I was like, ‘That’s not like her at all’. I started screaming, and I looked over and she was just passed out. It was terrifying. There was confusion.

‌



“It was all up to me. Either I stop the car or we’ll be going into a tree or fly over the banking. I just knew I had to bring us to safety somehow.”

View 4 Images Zac Howells was given a tour at West Mercia Police and awarded a Chief Constable’s Commendation for his bravery (Image: West Mercia Police / SWNS)

He bravely leaned across and grabbed the steering wheel, crashing the car into the central reservation to bring it to a stop, before turning off the engine and calling 999. Zac says: “I was just keeping the car straight, then I just started drifting towards the central reservation. And that’s where I started bumping it off and scraping it to a stop.”

‌



Remaining calm, he used the car’s satnav to pinpoint their location for the emergency handler, allowing police and paramedics to arrive quickly.

Chief Insp Julian Smith said: “The thing about Zac’s action that immediately stood out to me was just how calm he was. It could have led to a multi-car pileup. That moment of terror must have been incredibly scary.

“Then what Zach did was to phone 999, realising he was still in danger. Having taken that lifesaving action, he wasn’t thinking about himself. You can hear him reassuring his mum, it was just incredible. That combination of courage, clear thinking, and compassion is beyond exceptional.”

‌



View 4 Images Zac will be presented with his award on Monday at the Mirror’s annual ceremony at Grosvenor House in London (Image: WalesOnline/Rob Browne)

On Zac’s 999 call he can be heard saying: “I’m driving on a motorway, and my mum’s fainted, so I had to crash the car to stop. I’m really scared.”

Nicola, who was unconscious for around seven minutes, was found to be suffering from extremely low blood pressure and is awaiting further cardiology tests before she gets back behind the wheel. She says: “It must have been really frightening for him. He just knew he had to do something.

‌



“When I woke up I could see the blue lights coming towards us and I was really confused. Zac was physically trembling but he kept saying, ‘I’m fine’. He was just worried about me. I just feel so lucky to know that he was there to look after me that day.”

Proud Nicola will be cheering Zac on when he is presented with his award on Monday at the Mirror’s annual ceremony at Grosvenor House in London.

She says: “He literally saved our lives and who knows who else’s lives. He must have felt so scared but he’s so humble. He thinks it was a normal thing to do. He is a remarkable son. He is definitely a hero.”

Article continues below

*The Pride of Britain Awards will take place on 19th October, before airing on ITV and ITVX from 22nd October. Find out more about the Pride of Britain Awards 2026 at prideofbritain.com

News.title: Waterford 'arson attack': Two arrests after couple and 2 children killed in fire
News.content:
Waterford 'arson attack': Two arrests after couple and 2 children killed in fire

A man and a woman have been arrested as part of the investigation into a suspected arson attack on a home in Waterford County, Ireland, which killed four people

View 3 Images Philip and Kim English died alongside their boys Callum (left) and Jayden

Two people have been arrested as part of a murder investigation into a suspected arson attack on a home in Ireland.

Philip and Kim English and two of their children, 12-year-old Callum and nine-year-old Jayden, died in a fire at their home on Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford, in the early hours of Tuesday.

Two other children, a 14-year-old girl and a six-year-old boy, remain in hospital in a critical condition, according to Gardaí.

A man in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were arrested on Thursday afternoon in connection with the incident, Gardaí said.

Both suspects are being held at a Garda station in the Garda Eastern Region.

View 3 Images Gardaí at the scene of an arson attack on a home in County Waterford (Image: Danny De Vaal)

The house remains sealed off as a crime scene and is undergoing a technical examination by the Garda Technical Bureau, CorkBeo reports.

Post-mortem examinations on the four victims have been completed. The results are not being released for operational reasons.

Gardaí continue to appeal to anyone with information about the incident to come forward.

Family Liaison Officers remain in contact with the bereaved family, who have been kept updated on the investigation.

A online fundraiser on GoFundMe, which was set up to help pay for the family's funerals and support the surviving children, has raised more than €50,000 at the time of writing.

Today's arrests come after what Gardaí described as an "intense" and "very active" investigation into the attack this week.

On Wednesday, officers confirmed they had searched multiple premises in Waterford city and seized vehicles and electronic devices.

View 3 Images Brothers Callum and Jayden

A Garda spokesperson said on Thursday afternoon: "Investigating Gardaí have arrested a male (aged 20s) and a female (aged 30s) for alleged offences contrary to section 72 Criminal Justice Act 2006 in connection with the arson attack and murder of 4 persons at 7 Birch avenue, Birchwood, Waterford.

Article continues below

"Both individuals are currently detained under section 50 Criminal Justice Act 2007 in a Garda Station in the Garda Eastern region. The two children admitted to Children’s Health Ireland (CHI) Crumlin continue to receive treatment for their injuries. Their condition remains critical."

The spokesperson added: "An Garda Síochána continue to appeal to any person if you have any information on the murderous arson attack please speak to the Garda investigation team at Waterford Garda station or contact the Garda Confidential Line 1800 666 111 or speak with any member of An Garda Síochána that you know."

News.title: Nursery 'health and safety' lunch box policy slammed with white bread ban and odd raisin demand
News.content:
Nursery 'health and safety' lunch box policy slammed with white bread ban and odd raisin demand

A pre-school in Devon has provoked anger after banning certain foods and wrongly-cut fruit and veg in a bid to ensure children only bring in 'safe and healthy packed lunches'

View 3 Images Busy Otters sent parents slips will details of the foods not allowed - and how fruit and veg must be prepared (Image: William Dax / SWNS)

A nursery has been hit with backlash for slapping parents with a 'health and safety' lunch box policy - with white bread forbidden, and fruit and vegetables only allowed if cut a certain way.

‌



‌



Busy Otters pre-school in Ottery St Mary, Devon, has left mums and dads confused and annoyed after being told only "safe, healthy" meals can be brought in, with bosses issuing a set of strict guidelines called a 'safer eating policy'.

‌



All treats are banned, with crisps, chocolate, brioche buns, biscuits, cake bars, sausages and cheese strings all off-limits, with raisins also now allowed- unless they are cut in half. The rules state white bread must not be on the menu unless it is toasted because it is a choking hazard.

‌



In a message to parents, the nursery wrote: "Please remember larger and harder fruits: Apples, pears and melons should be cut into thin slices. Small fruits: Grapes, cherries, berries, strawberries and cherry tomatoes should be cut lengthways into quarters.

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

View 3 Images School bosses are demand parents cut raisins in half (Image: William Dax / SWNS)

‌



Mum says she was sacked by NHS after taking too much time off fighting cancer READ MORE :

"Oranges: Must be peeled, segmented and checked for pips. Vegetables: Carrots, cucumber, peppers and celery should be cut into narrow batons or sticks.

"Cheese: Should be cut into thin strips or grated. Please avoid cheese strings. Bread: White bread should not be included in lunch boxes, as it can form a dough-like ball in the throat and pose a choking risk if not chewed properly.

"Brown bread or toasted white bread are alternatives. Bread, chapatis, naan and other breads should be cut into narrow strips."

‌



It adds: "It is equally important that food is prepared appropriately before being placed in your child's lunch box, helping to reduce the risk of choking."The school says the rules are in line with the government's healthy eating guidance, Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) requirements and a recent Ofsted.

Busy Otters Pre-school said in its post: "Over the coming days, you may notice slips coming home in your child's lunch box. These slips will inform you if any items have been included that are not permitted under our Safer Eating Policy, or if food has not been prepared safely.

"They help us promote healthy eating, support children's wellbeing and reduce the risk of choking. We understand that these reminders may require a little extra preparation, and we genuinely appreciate your understanding and cooperation.

‌



View 3 Images Oranges must be peeled, segmented and checked for pips (Image: William Dax / SWNS)

But parents were far from impressed by the policy, with one venting: "Unless a place is providing food for your child, this includes schools. I don't feel they have a right to tell you what your child is allowed to eat.

"I'm paying for the stuff in my kids lunch so Il send what they are going to eat not what is begin dictated.

‌



Chair of the Busy Otters Preschool committee, Thomas Prideaux, said: "Busy Otters Pre-School is a charity-run setting, and our decisions regarding lunchbox guidance are based on our responsibility to follow the Early Years Foundation Stage framework, relevant safer eating guidance and advice from our local authority.

"These decisions have not been made to inconvenience families, but to help ensure the safety and wellbeing of the children in our care.

"We want to reassure parents that no child will be left hungry. We recognise that every child is different, with individual needs, preferences and circumstances.

‌



"Children who may struggle with the guidance, including those with specific dietary needs or who are particularly selective eaters, will be supported on a case-by-case basis, working in partnership with their families to find appropriate solutions.

"We understand that parents may have concerns, and we remain committed to working constructively with our families and community.

"However, we also ask people to remember that there are real people behind Busy Otters. Our dedicated staff and voluntary committee work incredibly hard to support local children and families, alongside full-time jobs and family commitments.

Article continues below

"The backlash surrounding this issue has had a genuine impact on our team's wellbeing, and nobody should have to face hostility or threatening messages for carrying out their responsibilities and following the guidance expected of early years settings."

News.title: Former DUP leader Donaldson sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sex abuse
News.content:
Jeffrey Donaldson has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for a series of child sex offences, including one count of rape.

The former DUP leader stood with his hands clasped in front of him in the dock of Newry Crown Court as his sentence was handed down.

Judge Paul Ramsey said Donaldson's crimes had led to a "catastrophic descent into disgrace".

He was sentenced to 11 years for his crimes against Victim B and four years for offences against Victim A. Both the sentences will run consecutively.

The 63-year-old is seeking to appeal his convictions.

Donaldson will also be required to sign the Sex Offenders Register for life.

He was convicted in June of 18 counts of sex abuse, which he committed against two women when they were children.

The former Lagan Valley MP has been in Maghaberry Prison since then and returned to it on Thursday afternoon after being sentenced.

Judge Ramsey said aggravating features include the length and protracted nature of the offending spanning many years.

He also took into account the youth of the victims and the age difference between them and Donaldson, adding that he could not accept Donaldson's lack of other convictions as a mitigating factor.

The judge said by contesting a case, a defendant avoids the reduction in sentence they would have got if they had pleaded guilty.

"It is highly significant that the defendant denied the offences to the police, he denied them in evidence and to the probation officer he continues to maintain his denials," the judge said.

"He has doubled-down in his denials.

"There has not been, and doubtless will not be, one word of regret, apology or shame from this man to at least provide his victims with some crumb of comfort."

News.title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says
News.content:
Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.

It says when this is not "clinically appropriate" then alternative arrangements should be made.

But the guidance also says decisions may have to be made on a case-by-case basis and must ensure clinical needs are met, and that the dignity and safety of the trans patient and of other patients are maintained.

Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.

That meant that a trans woman â a biological male who identifies as a woman â could have chosen to be on a women's ward, or a trans man â a biological female who identifies as a man â could have opted for a men's ward.

That guidance was withdrawn following the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 that under equality law the term "sex" means biological sex and "woman" refers to a biological woman.

The judgment said for a space or service to be single sex it should only allow those of the same biological sex to use it.

Also under the new guidance issued on Thursday, NHSE emphasised that in order to avoid discriminating against trans people they should be offered gender neutral spaces.

It also makes clear that there are circumstances where clinical need is the overriding priority, including on emergency units and urgent care settings.

In addition to the patient document of the guidance, NHSE has published advice for trusts on how to organise changing rooms, toilets and other single-sex facilities for staff.

Again, it says they should be used by people based on their biological sex, not their gender identity.

The document encourages NHS trusts in England to carry out an audit to ensure they are offering enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, for instance, gender neutral or single occupancy toilets.

Pressures on hospitals mean many have already struggled to keep wards single sex.

NHSE data shows that the number of breaches of the previous mixed-sex accommodation guidance has been growing every year since 2021- where members of the opposite sex were placed on a single-sex ward.

The most recent figure for August 2026 shows there were 5,520 breaches, compared to 3,853 in June 2025.

Sex-based rights charity Sex Matters has welcomed the guidance as a "momentus shift back to reality", but is concerned about how it will be applied.

"NHS patient data is a mess, with potentially thousands of trans-identifying people recorded as the opposite sex," CEO Maya Forstater said.

Trans rights organisations TransActual and Trans+ Solidarity Alliance have said they are concerned NHS staff will be unclear on how to safely look after trans patients.

"This guidance will not survive contact with reality in resource-strapped hospitals and will create unworkable operational challenges," they said.

The NHS has been at the centre of a number of high-profile arguments over the interpretation of equality law and workplace regulations.

In January 2026, Darlington Memorial Hospital was found to have violated the dignity of a group of nurses who complained about a transgender colleague - a biological male who identified as a woman - being allowed to use the female changing rooms. The nurses were told they should change somewhere else if they objected.

The tribunal concluded that the trust had indirectly discriminated against them.

The nurses are currently seeking Â£400,000 from the NHS to cover their legal costs.

One of the nurses who brought the action, Bethany Hutchison, who is now president of the Darlington Nurses Union, says they welcome the "clear and necessary guidance" from NHSE, but the test will be whether trusts follow it.

"The Darlington nurses should never have had to take their own employer to court to secure privacy, dignity and lawful single-sex facilities," she said.

"Enforcement cannot continue to depend on the courage and personal sacrifice of individual nurses."

In Scotland, another employment tribunal found, in December 2025, that a nurse, Sandie Peggie, had been harassed by NHS Fife over its interpretation of rules on single sex spaces.

Peggie had complained about a doctor, who was a trans woman, using the female changing rooms.

She was suspended after raising concerns. The tribunal dismissed her other claims of discrimination and victimisation.

An appeal is under way and expected to reach the courts next year.

News.title: Russell Brand accuser says alleged rape left her afraid she may be pregnant
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

A woman who alleges Russell Brand raped her in a hotel has said she was left feeling "dirty" and afraid she may be pregnant in the aftermath of the alleged attack.

The 51-year-old actor and comedian faces seven charges - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.

Video evidence played to the jury at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday showed one of his complainants tell the police: "He raped me basically and I know that happened."

The jury heard one of Brand's accusers say she had met him in 1999, before he was famous.

The woman was heard speaking in a police interview recorded in 2023, when reporting the alleged crime.

She said she had attended the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth and went to a fringe event where she said she spoke to Brand. She alleges he later raped her.

The complainant said they had both gone back to a hotel room. She told the officer she thought Brand "was gay" when they met earlier and she didn't feel like he was "trying it on with her".
