News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has made her first official public appearance since moving back to the UK, telling well-wishers "it's great to be back".

Meghan arrived at a youth charity in Nottingham alongside her husband, the Duke of Sussex, on Thursday morning. The pair, who are also expected to visit a food bank later, hugged and posed for selfies with the public.

The duchess spoke to a number of people in the crowd, telling one "we got lucky" as they chatted about the weather.

She has shared glimpses of her life back in the UK on social media, but this is the first time she has attended any public events since the family returned from California.

News.title: Watch: Swimmer's emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM
News.content:
Swimmer Archie Goodburn has been successful in his efforts to improve brain cancer care for patients as the UK government announce new measures.

The Scottish athlete, who was diagnosed with three inoperable brain tumours two years ago, met Prime Minister Andy Burnham after making an emotional plea on BBC Breakfast for more investment to be put into brain cancer research.

After the meeting, Burnham announced a new national brain cancer clinical lead and promised a review of brain cancer progress and action to get patients treatment sooner.

Goodburn, 25, thanked the prime minister and said all three of his requests have been "promised to some extent" but "fleshing out" needs to be done on the details.

The prime minister described the swimmer an "inspiration to us all" and said he was "delighted" to welcome him to Downing Street.

News.title: Man killed by tiger climbed two fences before suffering multiple injuries, inquest hears
News.content:
Brookes told the hearing: "He was approached by the tiger and the ensuing physical contact between the tiger and Mr Chapman led to him sustaining multiple traumatic injuries which rapidly led to his death."

Park staff secured the tiger and paramedics attended but confirmed his death at the scene.

The senior coroner said her office was awaiting a more substantial report as to the extent of his injuries.

South Yorkshire Police provided a number of witness statements from the public and staff who were at the wildlife park at the time, the hearing was told.

Mundy instructed staff to contact Yorkshire Wildlife Park to ask them to keep any relevant CCTV and inform the coroner of any previous visits by Chapman to the park.

After opening the inquest, which Chapman's family chose not to attend, on Thursday morning, Mundy adjourned proceedings until 18 March 2027.

Speaking after the hearing, a neighbour of Chapman told the BBC he was "very polite and well-spoken" and a "lovely man".

Josh, 24, who lived in the same building as Chapman, said: "He'd always have a laugh and a joke. He was quite well kept, he'd look after himself physically. He loved his F1, he'd talk for hours about his F1 if he could."

Discussing the online comments and speculation in the aftermath of the incident, he said: "People didn't know him. If you don't know him, don't make a comment."

News.title: Infantino apologises to Fifa Council - but told he is still not fit to lead
News.content:
President Gianni Infantino has apologised to the Fifa Council for his World Cup sell-off plan - but has been told he is not fit to lead unless he releases all of the documents and answers key questions.

The Fifa Council met in Zurich on Thursday for the first time since Infantino's secret Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal emerged.

Under FFE, which Infantino scrapped within days, a portion of the commercial rights of football's world governing body would have been given to a private investment firm.

In a three-and-a-half-hour meeting, Infantino also faced questions about US striker Folarin Balogun's suspended red-card ban, the Fifa Peace Prize and funding for national associations.

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt - a Fifa vice-president - said afterwards that many questions remained unanswered despite the "most robust, most frank, most open Council meeting" she had experienced.

"One of the disappointing things is that we didn't get answers to anything that we had specifically requested - for example getting the papers from FFE," Hewitt said.

"I asked the question 'why not?' - and we were asked to submit those questions in writing.

"I think the man has to answer those questions and if he doesn't answer those questions now, he's not fit to be Fifa president - and that was what was shared in the meeting."

Hewitt added: "I've repeatedly asked for the papers to be shared. I haven't received them and still in spite of the request today, I haven't received them.

"It is the rationale for why FFE happened in the way that it did, the Balogun case, the Peace Prize.

"The responses to those questions, which I still don't have answers to, will determine from my personal point of view whether or not Gianni is the right candidate.

"That will be the point at which or not we can say that any individual that was involved in FFE can or cannot be trusted because until we see what actually happened it's very difficult to say behaviour needs or not to change."

Hewitt acknowledged there had been "some contrition" in Infantino's apology.

"Then there were no holds barred in terms of what we felt about what had happened," she added.

"What he really apologised for was not bringing it to the Council. If you regret it that deeply, share it with us."

Uefa - European football's governing body - has been one of Infantino's fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down.

It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts for all documents related to FFE to be released.

Hewitt hopes Infantino now freely releases the documents so the Council can understand what happened.

"Those papers coming to Council are a crucial next part of us feeling comfortable as to what, if any, criminal proceedings need to take place," Hewitt said.

Asked if there was any change in stance from Uefa about Infantino, she added: "From my position, nothing has shifted. I've no new information that makes me feel any differently, other than we do have a president who is apologetic."

News.title: Another man admits raping woman drugged by husband over 20 years
News.content:
Another man has pleaded guilty to raping a woman who was drugged and abused by her husband without her knowledge for over 20 years.

Graham Brougham, 74, is the oldest of 13 men who were charged with sexual offences against the victim after being allegedly invited into her home, in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, to abuse her by her husband.

The husband, in his sixties, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife - including rape - and has given a witness statement detailing "what he says happened".

Brougham, from Northwich, was told by a judge at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court that he "should be under no illusion his sentence will be custody and a long time in custody."

The victim, who held hands with a family member, watched on from the public gallery as Brougham answered "guilty" in the dock to a charge of raping her in September 2024.

News.title: Crew in Lewis fishing boat tragedy named by police
News.content:
Three fishermen who were on boat that went missing off the Western Isles on Tuesday have been named.

The body of Douglas Craigie, 49, was found on Wednesday morning, while his crew-mates, Norman Murray, who is 40 and known as Tam, and 23-year-old Murdo Morrison are still missing.

Their fishing boat, called Kilda, disappeared during stormy weather off Port of Ness in north Lewis.

Isles MP Torcuil Crichton said the islands had been "struck by a maritime tragedy", and First Minister John Swinney said his heart went out to the men's families.

The search for the missing crew and boat has resumed after being suspended overnight.

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) said aircraft and coastguard teams were involved.

Police Scotland said it was believed the fishermen had sailed from Brevaig in Lewis at about 07:30 on Tuesday before travelling to the Port of Ness area to fish.

The Kilda was reported overdue at about 21:20 on Tuesday.

Extensive searches were conducted on Wednesday despite bad weather, with gale-force winds.

News.title: UK threatens to ban Eritreans over migrant return policy
News.content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has threatened to ban all Eritreans from entering the UK if the east African country's government does not accept more returns of small boat migrants and foreign national offenders.

From Thursday, Eritrean diplomats will face restrictions on their movement outside London. Fast-track visas will also be stopped for VIPs.

Ministers have previously pressured other countries into accepting returns by threatening visa bans.

Eritreans were the most common nationality among small boats migrants in the 12 months to June - accounting for 18% of arrivals, external, according to figures from the House of Commons Library.

The Eritrean embassy in London has been contacted for comment.

"Eritrea has had every chance to accept the return of criminals and those with no right to be in the UK. Unlike other countries, it has refused," said Mahmood.

She said she would not hesitate "to impose further measures on other countries refusing to co-operate".

The UK government accused the Eritrean authorities of "abruptly" withdrawing co-operation earlier this year.

The restrictions mean diplomats are banned from travelling 60km outside London without permission.

The Home Office said this mirrored restrictions on British officials in Eritrea's capital Asmara.

In the 12 months to June only seven people from Eritrea were returned there from the UK, according to Home Office figures. A further 244 Eritreans were returned to other countries.

Over the same period, more than 5,800 Eritreans arrived in the UK via small boats. A further 1,300 were given visas, mostly to join people already settled in the UK.

Dr Madeleine Sumption, director of the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford, said targeting Eritrea would have little impact.

"Eritrea is one of the major countries of origin for asylum seekers coming to the UK - we had roughly 7,000 asylum applications in the last year of data, roughly 8% of the total," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

"Most Eritreans who come and claim asylum are not removable at all - the government would never be in negotiations to remove them because 84% are successful at initial decision; more will be successful on appeal."

She added that about 1,400 people were initially refused asylum, but that this number would reduce after appeals.

Many young Eritreans try to leave the country - which is a one-party state - to avoid military conscription, which can last for decades.

News.title: Nandy 'minded to intervene' in Sky's £1.6bn takeover of ITV entertainment arm
News.content:
But Nandy has told Sky and ITV that she is considering issuing a public interest intervention notice (PIIN) to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) and regulator Ofcom, forcing an investigation into the tie-up.

In a letter to both companies, she said she was minded to order the probe to address public interest considerations including:

The need for free expression of opinion in news media

The need for a range of views in news media across the UK

The need for a range of people controlling the media across the UK

The need for a wide range of programmes to be offered across the UK

The letter said Nandy recognised Sky News and ITV News were two of the most prominent sources of television news in the UK, with a joint 26% share of those viewing news on linear TV.

Consumers would still have access to other sources of news such as the BBC and Channel 4, it added.

But Nandy believes that, over time, the tie-up could undermine the range of views available to viewers, with 86% of the linear TV news market controlled by the BBC and Sky/ITV.

The North of England could be particularly hard hit as well as nations of the UK other than England and those from lower socio-economic backgrounds, the letter argued.

This is because their main source of news is broadcast news, it added.

Sky and ITV have been given until 20 October to respond to the culture secretary's concerns.

A Sky spokesperson said: "We have already made clear commitments to protect ITV's identity, its free-to-air services and public service broadcasting obligations, and to ensure ITV News and Sky News remain distinct editorial voices."

An ITV spokesperson said: "We welcome the publication of the secretary of state's 'minded to' issue a public interest intervention notice letter as was expected and look forward to fully co-operating in the process.

"This is another important milestone in the regulatory review process towards creating a UK player with the scale and resources to better compete with global streaming platforms, benefiting viewers, advertisers and the UK creative industries."

Nandy's intervention would be made under a new public interest consideration.

This would need legislation to be brought forward, given that current laws do not cover the effect of a merger on streaming or on-demand programmes.

She said: "If I decide to intervene on the basis of this new public interest consideration, I will bring forward legislation... to extend the application of the public interest consideration relating to the availability of a wide range of broadcasting to on-demand programmes."

News.title: Farage defends Reform's vetting after councillors filmed making racist comments
News.content:
On a different day in the ITV broadcast, Feeney is joined by two other Reform candidates, Jamie Campbell and Chris Whelan, who discuss speculation of a mosque being built in the local area.

"There's got to be a way of stopping them - like, go and buy some pork chops; we'll bury it in the ground," Campbell is heard saying in the film.

Whelan says "we'll take pictures of it", prompting Feeney to add: "I was gonna say, 'Unfortunately, this is a pig cemetery, mate'."

Discussing a female Reform candidate from Birmingham, Feeney is heard saying, "I didn't know where to look", before Whelan adds: "I'd have been sniffing that seat as soon as she got up."

The BBC has tried to contact Feeney for a response. ITV has reported that on Monday evening he had "mutually agreed" to resign from Reform UK, citing "personal reasons" and would be continuing as an independent councillor.

The BBC has contacted Campbell and Whelan, who has resigned as a councillor, for a response.

A Reform UK Solihull spokesman condemned Feeney and Whelan's "misogynistic and offensive comments" and confirmed they were no longer Reform councillors.

The spokesman said Campbell's comment "was a joke in poor taste but with no malicious intent", adding: "It's something that he deeply regrets, and the party will not be taking any further action."

Elsewhere in the film, Dean Miller, a councillor in the south London borough of Bromley, is shown campaigning for Reform in the Makerfield by-election.

"We've been ethnically cleansed out of London because you never used to get any blacks over in Bromley," he tells an ITV undercover reporter. "And now, you know, Bromley's like massive Nigerian communities there."

Miller says he is "not racist", before later adding: "The Muslim thing, that is going to be that thing that takes over everything and then everyone just has one religion. Because, apparently, King Charles is a [expletive] Muslim... I think that's [expletive] traitorous."

ITV reported that Miller would now sit as an independent councillor having resigned from Reform and had told them in a statement that he was heavily medicated due to a chronic pain condition when he made the comments.

The BBC has contacted him for comment.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Reform should take "immediate and firm action against those who've been revealed to be making these abhorrent comments".

He added: "There is no place for any form of racism, antisemitism, discrimination in British politics, and we all should be relentless in repeating that and taking the firmest possible action."

The Conservatives said: "Nigel Farage promised to make Reform ready for government. These sorry individuals are proof he has failed."

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said: "This is chilling. I feel for anyone watching this tonight who is frightened to see such racism and hatred festering in their community."

A Green Party spokesman said: "Vilifying migrants and Muslims is Reform's main focus, and these racist comments reflect party policy."

News.title: UK temperatures to rise to 23C before autumn chill sets in
News.content:
Thursday will bring unusually high temperatures as warm air wafts across the south of the UK, while colder conditions dig into northern areas.

Afternoon highs in parts of eastern England are likely to be about 5-8C (9-14F) above typical mid-October values, probably peaking at 23C (73F).

It will be a different story further north and west with temperatures in much of Scotland and Northern Ireland sitting around the seasonal norm.

The two air masses are divided by a weather front which will bring outbreaks of rain. As that sinks southwards, chillier air will spread to all parts of the country bringing a colder feel to the weekend, though there will still be plenty of sunshine.

Frost and patchy fog are likely to develop in some locations.

News.title: Charlotte Church to 'pause' wellness retreat and consider its future
News.content:
Charlotte Church will "pause" her wellness retreat from December to "germinate new dreams for the future", the star has shared.

The Dreaming, based in Rhydoldog House near Rhayader, Powys, offered retreats aimed at helping people reconnect with nature and spirituality.

The singer-songwriter bought the former home of fashion designer Laura Ashley in 2021, with its renovation later featuring in a Discovery Channel documentary series.

In a statement on social media, the team said the retreat had hosted more than 3,000 guests over the last five years, and wanted to "reassess" what it should offer in a changing world.

They said: "Through the harvest season, it is important to discern what requires attention from that which is falling away, what needs to be put to compost.

"We need the chance to compost, mulch, go fallow, listen deeply to the earth, so that we can germinate new dreams for the future."

The statement said the world was "different" today from when the project began and that The Dreaming needed to consider what services it should offer.

"As we stare clear-eyed at the exponentially complexifying crises that have been spreading out ahead of us all like cracking ice, we at The Dreaming need to reassess, with candour and courage, what it is we should be offering to be in service," it said.

The team said it could not give a date for when the retreat might return, but added: "We cannot say when exactly we will be returning from the dream realm, but return we shall."

News.title: Cult Leicester Square cinema saved from potential closure
News.content:
The Prince Charles cinema in Leicester Square has been saved from potential closure after signing a 25-year lease.

It has faced a lengthy period of uncertainty following difficulties with its landlord, Zedwell LSQ Ltd, whose parent company is Criterion Capital.

Now the Leicester Square cult cinema has secured the new lease with no break clause, offering it security so the "projectors will keep rolling for years to come".

Vaq Farooq, CEO of Criterion Capital, said he was pleased to reach an equitable solution for all, and said: "A 25-year commitment provides real security for the cinema and its fans, and we are delighted to be continuing our partnership for many years to come."

The venue faced closure at the start of 2025 due to the potential addition of a six-month break clause in its contract. Prince Charles launched a petition to withdraw the break clause from its contract.

In May 2025, the cinema was declared an Asset of Community Value by Westminster City Council, which grants it additional protections from redevelopment.

Despite this, the cinema's boss, Ben Freedman, told the media in August that a resolution had still not been found.

However it seems that both parties have now reached an agreement, with the Prince Charles announcing the signing of the new lease on its Instagram earlier.

A spokesperson for the cinema thanked the 168,645 people who had signed the petition to save it and said: "The Prince Charles Cinema is thrilled to announce that we have signed a new 25-year lease with no break clause, ensuring our projectors will keep rolling for years to come.

"After 21 months of uncertainty, we're delighted to have secured the future of the cinema, and we couldn't have done it without the support, commitment and belief of many, many people.

"We are so incredibly thankful to each and every one of you. You have all placed your trust in us, and as we continue on for at least another 25 years, we promise to never forget that. We'll be right hereâ¦"

News.title: At least 6 explosions heard near Yemen government-used palace in Aden, witnesses say
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

At least six explosions struck Thursday near the palace used by Yemen's internationally recognized government in the port city of Aden, witnesses said. Iran-backed Houthi rebels based in northern Yemen quickly claimed responsibility.

The explosions caused panic among residents who fled the area. A security official said at least two of the explosions were on top of the hill near the Maashiq palace, and two others were heard near the security gate.

It was a rare attack on the palace area, as fighting has escalated between the rebels and a Saudi-led coalition in the latest front in the Iran war.

Many of the government leadership are living in exile and those in Aden were safe, a government official said. Both officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.

The Houthis said they attacked a military operations headquarters with the “Saudi enemy," part of their strategy of attacking Saudi targets that has included a series of attacks on airports and oil infrastructure inside the kingdom.

Earlier Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted a cruise missile over the province of Medina. Flightradar 24, a tracking platform, said dozens of flights were cancelled or delayed at Jeddah airport.

The coalition statement did not assign blame for the attack. The Houthis’ military spokesperson, Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, denied the rebels carried it out. The group previously pledged not to attack airports in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia also said it destroyed a drone over the country's Eastern province, a major oil-producing region.

News.title: FBI investigating after letters with 'suspicious substances' are sent to congressional and election offices
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The FBI and Postal Service are investigating letters containing “suspicious substances” that were sent to congressional and election offices across the United States.

Authorities are urging recipients to treat the letters as “potentially hazardous” as they investigate an unknown substance found inside some of the pieces of mail.

“The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating a series of suspicious mailings sent to various addresses nationwide, including Secretary of State offices and their related election offices,” an FBI spokesperson said in a statement.

“Some of the letters contained an unknown substance and we are working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident. We are also working with our partners to identify the individual or individuals responsible for the letters. This FBI will continue to safeguard the public and secure elections for American citizens.”

open image in gallery Federal authorities are investigating letters with ‘suspicious substances’ that have been mailed to congressional and election offices nationwide ( Getty Images )

In Congress, the situation appeared isolated to the Senate, but the House was monitoring, a person familiar with the matter told The Associated Press.

Meanwhile, packages containing a powdery substance triggered the evacuation of election offices in at least two states, Louisiana and Oklahoma. The Postal Service intercepted a package containing a white powder intended for the Ohio secretary of state, who said similar mailings had been sent to election officials in multiple states.

The warning over the suspicious letters comes three weeks before Election Day. A similar threat caused alarm in 2023, when several election offices were sent envelopes containing the powerful opioid fentanyl.

The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors issued a statement condemning the letters sent this week, which they said were threats against election staff.

“Those who administer our elections should never fear for their safety while carrying out their essential duties,” they wrote.

More to follow...

News.title: BBC to force more to pay licence fee with ‘YouTube tax’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The government is set to unveil plans to extend the BBC licence fee to online streaming services in what is unofficially being dubbed a “YouTube tax”.

A white paper on the BBC charter renewal will be published before Christmas and will include proposals on how to overhaul the current funding model to increase revenue and reflect how audiences consume content.

A senior Whitehall source told The Independent the plan is to expand the licence fee to streaming platforms to prevent people dodging it by logging on to the internet via their phones, tablets or computers.

open image in gallery The BBC is currently negotiating its charter renewal ( Reuters )

Currently, anyone who uses a television to watch content must pay the licence fee even if they do not watch the BBC. Under the proposed changes it would be expanded to cover all other online providers, such as Netflix, Amazon, Disney Plus, YouTube, which are currently exempt.

It is understood any new cash raised under the plan will need to be spent on reviving local journalism and tackling misinformation, which has fuelled the rise of parties such as Reform UK.

The Whitehall source explained that the move was “because people are able to use them to avoid paying currently”. They added: “It’s not fair that people are essentially able to watch television content but avoid the licence fee.”

The source said there had been a “hold up” with the charter renewal talks under the previous administration. “But now we have had a change of prime minister we are able to press ahead with the plan to expand it to streaming platforms”, they added.

The new arrangements have been dubbed the YouTube tax because the site is by far the biggest online video platform in the UK with around 55 million users.

The proposal would be a means of helping tackle the crisis facing the BBC amid fears millions of people will stop paying the licence fee, which is currently £180 a year but free for people aged 75 and older, and 50 per cent discounted for the visually impaired.

open image in gallery Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy’s department is leading the talks with the BBC ( PA )

It comes as the BBC has announced that it will launch the news channel on Youtube.

It also follows the BBC director-general Matt Brittin saying he wants BBC News to be on streaming sites such as Netflix in a bid to reform how the broadcaster’s content is consumed and paid for.

Mr Brittin previously said the corporation was being “held back” by its TV licence fee, which is “no longer fit for purpose”, and suggested it be replaced by a household levy instead.

Speaking on the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg programme, he emphasised the need to modernise the current funding model to ensure it is fair and reflects how audiences consume content.

He said: “What we need to look at is the current model. You pay the licence fee if you watch live TV or you’re on iPlayer.

“I’d like to see reform that allows us to be where audiences are. I think BBC content should be on Netflix, on YouTube, on TikTok, on Spotify, and Instagram, and everywhere where audiences are.

“Particularly news, actually, which I think is part of disinfecting misinformation. It’s our job to be everywhere.”

The most recent figures revealed that around 539,000 fewer TV licences were in force in the year to 31 March 2026. There has been a drop of around 2 million in the past five years.

The BBC has been facing spending cuts with question marks over flagship programmes such as Newsnight, and recently cut 10 per cent of its staff. Despite collecting around £3.8bn to £3.9bn from the licence fee, the BBC recorded an operating deficit of £121m for 2025/26.

However, the Whitehall source warned the income from the levy would not be able to use the increased revenue from the extended licence fee to fill gaps in its spending.

“The money needs to be used to help support local journalism and counter a lot of the conspiracy theories and fake news which we have seen help parties like Reform getting elected in different parts of the country,” they said.

A BBC spokesperson said: “We have consistently argued that the current funding model is outdated and needs reform. We will continue to engage with government to secure a new charter that provides sustainable, sufficient and universal funding so the BBC can deliver for audiences for generations to come.”

The royal charter is being renegotiated by culture secretary Lisa Nandy’s Department of Culture, Media and Sport and sets out the arrangements for the governance of the BBC, including how it is funded.

It currently has to be renewed every 10 years and is set to end in December 2027.

News.title: Hurricane Trudy looms over Mexico’s Pacific coast as it strengthens into huge storm
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Hurricane Trudy has strengthened into a Category 1 storm as it edges toward Mexico’s Pacific coastline, officials reported on Thursday.

Data from the U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami placed the storm roughly 300 miles (480 kilometers) southwest of Acapulco, Mexico, recording maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (120 kph).

Traveling northwest at 9 mph (15 kph), the storm is projected to draw near the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend, according to forecasters.

Forecasters added that Trudy is anticipated to intensify into a major hurricane on Friday, bringing 4 to 8 inches (101 to 203 millimeters) of rainfall across Colima and Jalisco states through the weekend.

Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4-8 inches of rainfall, with isolated totals around 12 inches across the southwestern Mexican states of Colima and Jalisco.

Forecasters warned residents to be prepared for the rain to produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting portions of the coast of southwestern Mexican over the next day or so, with the swells likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.

Earlier this month, Hurricane Rachel has intensified into a Category 3 system off Mexico's Pacific coast, hitting the region just as parts of the US Southwest and northern Mexico recover from widespread damage and severe flooding triggered by the remnants of Hurricane Polo the week before.

Parts of northern Mexico were still reeling from floods and wider destruction left by Polo when Rachel hit. Hundreds of people remained displaced or had their homes destroyed, and at least 13 municipalities remained flooded for days, according to local authorities.

News.title: Danny Trejo’s son says legendary father ‘cant say how he feels’ about starring in new ICE movie
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Danny Trejo’s son is pushing back against the narrative that his father knew what he was getting into by signing onto the controversial Daily Wire film Pawn Shop.

The 82-year-old Mexican actor came under fire after he was cast in the pro-Immigrations and Customs Enforcement movie, which is being produced by conservative commentator Ben Shapiro’s company. The film is set in Minneapolis in the aftermath of the fatal ICE shooting of Renee Good.

Danny denied being “pro-ICE” and said he was “pro immigrant” in a short statement shared last week.

But now his son, Gilbert Trejo, is claiming that the Spy Kids actor is being forced to keep quiet due to his contract for the film — and that he was tricked into joining the movie in the first place.

“My dad can’t really come out and say how he feels about any of this in any real way,” Gilbert, a 38-year-old director based in Los Angeles, told The Independent in a conversation Wednesday.

open image in gallery Danny Trejo has more than 450 credits to his name, per IMDB ( Getty )

open image in gallery Gilbert Trejo (left) spoke to 'The Independent' about his father Danny's involvement with Ben Shapiro's pro-ICE film ( Gilbert Trejo/Instagram )

As his father’s speech is limited due to promotional clauses in his film contract, Gilbert posted an Instagram Story speaking out on his behalf, saying: “My 82-year-old dad has never heard of Ben Shapiro, I had to explain to him who that is, and what kind of guy he is. My dad contractually can’t bad mouth him, the film, or walk away without being sued for breach of contract. He couldn’t even release the statement he wanted to.”

He continued, “He’s handcuffed to this stupid project, and swaths of people have instantly turned their backs on him without knowing any of the facts.”

Gilbert shared with The Independent that when his father took the acting job, the Heat actor was told that it was an action movie being filmed in Montana. Then, two weeks into filming, Shapiro’s company joined the production team.

“He had already been on camera for a substantial amount of time,” Trejo’s son explained. “You can’t, as an actor, walk away from that without everyone working on that losing their job and the entire production getting shut down.”

The younger Trejo went on to claim that a “substantial” amount of the cast and crew did not know that the original script would be adjusted to fit the Daily Wire’s political message — and that several people walked off set when the changes were made.

He said: “I was sitting next to him when he got the phone call from his agent saying, you’re the good guy in this movie. There are protesters, they’re clashing with these guys and you’re just trying to protect your store and bring peace to everyone.”

open image in gallery Danny Trejo is set to star in ‘Pawn Shop’, a controversial film being produced by Ben Shapiro’s Daily Wire ( AFP/Getty )

In reality, the film follows an ICE officer, played by Jesse Ray Gentry, who is barricaded inside Trejo’s character’s pawn shop during an altercation with protesters after Good’s shooting. The movie, which is slated for a 2027 release, is directed by Michael Polish and also stars Harvey Keitel and Henry Thomas.

The film has already been met with protests. Locals complained that they were not warned about the use of blank gunshots and other disturbances, and production was temporarily suspended until a new permit was issued.

The Independent has contacted Danny, Shapiro, Daily Wire, and the film’s production company for comment.

Danny addressed his involvement in the film in an Instagram post earlier this month, stating: “Hey everyone. I want to address some social media comments about me. Make no mistake. I am a proud Mexican who has always been and will always be a supporter of my community. I am also obviously pro-immigrant. I am not pro ICE. I know where I come from and I know our struggles. I am an actor. My job is to tell a story. God bless you, Danny.”

Further, Gilbert says the movie’s messaging could not be further from the truth about his father’s political views.

Danny, known for his machismo, previously hit the campaign trail for Democratic politicians like Karen Bass and Gavin Newsom. He told IndieWire in 2020: “Like I said, I stay out of politics. I’ve got fans on both sides of the ticket. But I still speak my mind. I tell my Republican friends, ‘Hey, we don’t discuss politics or I’ll beat you.’”

Gilbert continued to The Independent: “I have conversations with friends all the time where they’re like, I don’t know how to talk to my Trumper parents. And I’m like, I cannot relate to that. I can’t relate to that because my dad is actively campaigning for Democratic candidates every election cycle.”

He described his father as often being “the only Mexican guy in the room,” Gilbert said, “which is one of the reasons why he’s sort of heartbroken to be framed as representing something he doesn’t. The idea that he doesn’t stand with or stand for his community is heartbreaking and depressing.”

To critics who have questioned why Danny did not pull out of the film and face the financial repercussions, Gilbert said: “People don’t know what goes into these contracts.”

open image in gallery ‘People don’t know what goes into these contracts,’ Danny Trejo’s son told ‘The Independent’ ( Getty )

“He’s very much a working actor,” he said, referencing Danny’s more than 450 acting credits on IMDb. “He works for a living. He has well-documented financial hardships and troubles. He’s not, as some people are saying on social media, a multimillionaire.”

Gilbert also addressed Danny’s previous work with The Daily Wire on an adult animated comedy series called Mr. Birchum. Danny lent his voice to one episode in 2024.

The younger Trejo said his father had known the show’s creator Adam Carolla for decades and agreed to the day gig without much conversation, unaware that Carolla “had made this giant right hand turn” and started speaking out in support of border enforcement.

“He’s not online,” Gilbert said of Danny. “My dad had a flip phone until about a year ago when they just stopped sending a signal to it and he had to get an iPhone.”

Thankfully, his dad has been largely spared from seeing the backlash and anger toward him on social media after being cast in Pawn Shop. But Gilbert says the anger is just an outpouring of the hatred brought on by Donald Trump’s anti-immigration policies.

“People need a place to put their outrage because what’s going on is outrageous,” he said. “My entire family is upset about what is happening in our country right now with ICE. But getting mad at an 82 year old Mexican man is not the solution.”

News.title: Celebrity Traitors 2026: Speculation builds on Traitors’ next move as fan-favourites are up for ‘murder’
News.content:
From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.

At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.

The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. News.title: Gianni Infantino apologises for World Cup sell-off plan, but told he’s ‘not fit to be Fifa president’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Gianni Infantino has apologised to the Fifa Council for his World Cup sell-off plan but has been told he’s still “not fit to be Fifa president” after failing to answer questions from his critics.

The FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who sits on the Fifa Council, told reporters in Zurich that Uefa’s position in opposing Infantino has not changed after he attempted to sell stakes in the World Cup and Fifa tournaments to private investors this summer.

Hewitt also said that Infantino did not answer the Council’s questions relating to other recent controversies, including his involvement in overturning Folarin Balogun’s suspension at the World Cup after a call from Donald Trump and the Fifa Peace Prize.

Hewitt said Infantino has requested members to submit their questions in writing, despite a three-and-a-half hour meeting of the Fifa Council in what was their first official gathering since details of the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan emerged in July.

“The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions, no, he’s not fit to be Fifa president, and that was what was shared in the meeting,” Hewitt told reporters in Zurich.

“He’s told us to submit those questions. There were so many of them, and now it’s up to him to do that, and do that in the open way. The minimum is having the papers from FFE [the Fifa Forward Enterprise plan], because if there’s nothing to hide, then share them with us.”

Infantino outlined his plans for form within Fifa last month and is planning to stand for re-election in March after coming under pressure to resign following the collapse of his World Cup sell-off plan.

Uefa led calls for Infantino to step down with further opposition coming from the Asian confederation and Concacaf, which represents countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

Gianni Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council in Zurich on Thursday ( PA )

FA chair Hewitt also wrote to Infantino last month calling for an independent review into the World Cup private investor plan and the handling of the Balogun case.

The decision to pause Balogun’s suspension came before US president Donald Trump admitted he personally contacted Infantino to request that the red card given to the forward against Bosnia and Herzegovina be re-examined.

Hewitt said Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for not sharing the FFE plan with them before details of it were reported by The Times in the week following the World Cup final and that she believed he “regrets that deeply”.

But she added that she received “no new information” to change her position after the FA withdrew their support for Infantino following the loss of confidence in his leadership.

“We spoke a lot about the issues and it’s fair to say Gianni apologised for what happened,” Hewitt said. “He said that with some contrition and there were no-holds barred on what we felt about what happened.

“We were asked to submit our questions and one of the disappointing things is we did not get the answers to those questions. We didn’t get answers to anything we had specifically requested, for example getting the papers from FFE.

“I asked the question ‘why and why not?’ and we were asked to submit those questions and then we will get answers. To be fair, there were so many questions. Certainly I’ve left the room feeling there’s nothing I wished I had said and didn’t say.

“I have no new information that makes me feel any differently about how I felt when I went in, other than we do have a president of Fifa who is apologetic about what has happened, and secondly, a promise again that we will get the information that we’ve requested.”

A police sergeant who appeared on Police Interceptors will face a misconduct hearing after he was accused of having sex with another officer while on duty and in public places.

Cleveland Police’s website lists a disciplinary hearing for former temporary police sergeant Ben Sutcliffe, who featured on the Channel 5 show Police Interceptors.

On the show’s website, he was listed as having 11 years service with the force and was an advanced driver trained in tactical pursuit, an armed response officer, a medic, a public order instructor and a family liaison officer.

It is alleged that he engaged in a personal relationship with a female colleague but denied it when challenged a number of times.

The ex-officer is accused of sending and receiving a large number of sexually explicit texts and images to the officer while on duty.

open image in gallery Cleveland Police’s website lists a disciplinary hearing for former temporary police sergeant Ben Sutcliffe, who featured on the Channel 5 show Police Interceptors ( Channel 5 )

The website entry alleges: “The exchanges were to such an extent that they interfered with the proper performance of his duties.”

It also claimed that he “engaged in sexual activity with the officer in public places, knowing and intending that there be a risk of being caught”.

Mr Sutcliffe is also alleged to have shared restricted information with the female officer without operational policing purpose.

He is also accused of failing to challenge improper conduct on behalf of the woman when she told him she would lie to the Professional Standards Department and deny the relationship.

Cleveland Police said the alleged breaches of Standards of Professional Behaviour related to discreditable conduct; authority, respect and courtesy; honesty and integrity; orders and instructions; confidentiality; and challenging improper conduct.

If proven, the allegations would constitute gross misconduct, the force said.

His misconduct hearing will take place on Wednesday next week in Stockton, Teesside.

News.title: Economy slows before Healey’s maiden Budget
News.content:
The Chancellor said banks are too often seen as “distant financial institutions”, in a sign he will not raise taxes on the industry in the Budget.

John Healey has faced pressure to impose a windfall tax on bank profits to help rebuild an expected decline in his wiggle room in the public finances.

John Healey said: “My observations on the banks are just that people too often see them as a big distant financial institutions when they are hardwired into the economic fabric of this country and our future prospects.

“That said, you know I’ve got decisions to take in the Budget, and I will. I’ll set those out in two weeks’ time.

“And my special responsibility as Chancellor is to protect the resilience of the British economy for the future. That the resilience that the IMF has reported on this week by upgrading our growth figures in the UK this week, that the welcome monthly growth figures published this morning reinforce, and importantly, alongside that, the IMF reports said that Britain stands out for our deficit reduction plans, and will have his forecast actually a reflection not just on forecast plans but performance over the last couple of years. You know, a consolidation plan in place and underway.

“I’ve said from day one and week one, and I’ve had Andy Burnham in lockstep alongside me, I will meet those fiscal rules in full.

“That will be part of the Budget that I set out in two weeks’ time, and I think the IMF report reinforces that that is not just a not just a reinforcing the strength of Britain’s position, but something that they say they want to see other countries doing as well.”

News.title: Ukrainian Vampire drones drop food on town besieged by Russian army
News.content:
On Ukraine’s front lines, drones are the deadliest weapons in Kyiv’s arsenal, hunting Russian soldiers one by one with chilling precision.

But across the Dnipro River, the same machines have been given a very different mission: keeping trapped civilians from dying of starvation.

Since March, Ukrainian drones have been flying food and medicine into occupied Oleshky, on the river’s left bank, where residents are surviving on grass and weeds.

The town is less than three miles from Kherson, a city battered by Russian drones and shelling.

Since December, Oleshky has been under an effective blockade. Its roads are mined and shops have closed, with no food arriving by road since late May. Humanitarian agencies are blocked from entering, and the health system has all but collapsed.

Only around 2,000 of its 24,000 pre-war residents remain. For them, the drones are now their only lifeline.

“With the onset of winter, the situation is only getting worse,” said Elvina Osmanova of the Kherson regional military administration. “Food supplies are running out. People are facing a life-threatening choice: risk their lives trying to find food outside the city or remain without food.”

News.title: Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle
News.content:
When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

News.title: Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six
News.content:
Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Second Ebola case confirmed in Kenya
News.content:
Kenya has recorded its second-ever case of Ebola after a relative of a patient who died last week tested positive for the virus, officials have said.

A 39-year-old man fell ill on Tuesday and has since been confirmed to be infected with Ebola, according to Kenyan health authorities.

The patient, who is now isolated, is a family member of Kenya’s first-ever Ebola case, who died in a hospital in Nairobi last Monday.

The index case, a 40-year old businessman, had travelled to Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the deadly outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has so far killed more than 4,300 people.

Kenyan authorities have identified 128 of his contacts and have successfully tracked down 113 of them, who are having their temperatures checked daily for a period of three weeks, the country’s Director-General for Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said in a statement.

“There is no evidence of spread in the wider community,” the statement, issued on Wednesday, added.

However, questions remain over whether more cases will crop up in the coming weeks.

News.title: I tried Apple’s new smart home hub – the brand faithful will love it
News.content:
HomeView can control smart lights, heating, security cameras and video doorbells via touch or voice, but devices must support Matter – the cross-brand smart home standard. That means you aren’t confined to Apple-approved gadgets, but you are still limited – Ring video doorbells, for example, aren’t Matter-compatible, so they won’t work with HomeView, which could be a deal-breaker for even the biggest Apple fan.

But for anyone put off by the complexity of setting up a smart home, Apple is trying to simplify things. It has partnered with LG on Home Collection – a range of devices, including security cameras and a video doorbell – that connect with a single tap, just as AirPods do with an iPhone. They won’t be available until later in the year, but they could mark a major step towards making smart home set-up less complicated.

My early verdict

HomeView is built for the Apple faithful: set-up requires an iPhone or iPad, personalised AI features need a recent Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, and some apps work only when your phone is nearby. In a household split between iPhone and Android, Android users will get a much thinner experience, and Apple’s own services come first at every turn.

Still, HomeView is the most polished smart display I have seen. Face recognition makes it both a great shared and personalised device; the sound quality is excellent; and Siri AI is finally worth talking to, especially when it can draw on your personal context. I’ll need to live with it for a few weeks before giving a final verdict, but so far it’s a beautifully designed device I’d be happy to invite into my home.

News.title: Ed Miliband calls for ‘new deal on debt’ as developing countries face spiralling borrowing costs
News.content:
Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has called for a “new deal on debt” as spiralling borrowing costs force developing countries to spend more on interest payments than on education or health.

In a speech in Bangkok on Wednesday, Mr Miliband warned that the global financial system is failing emerging markets, and promised to use the UK’s diplomatic heft to push for urgent reform.

He said: “The short-term repayments are crippling, and while many are not defaulting on their payments they are being forced, if you like, to default on the lives and prospects of future generations.

“So we need a new deal on debt, a deal that supports countries to repay over longer time horizons and, crucially, refinancing with better rates to give developing countries precious fiscal space.”

Although public debt is not inherently problematic, servicing costs are at a 25-year-high – squeezing government coffers just as conflict, climate change and a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño push food and fuel prices ever higher.

Emerging economies in particular have little headroom: according to the Rockefeller Foundation, average interest payments now exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing nations, while UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) analysis found 3.7 billion people live in countries where debt servicing costs exceed spending on health or education.

At the same time, overseas development aid (ODA) spending from wealthy countries has plummeted – hitting social, infrastructure and humanitarian projects, and disaster response.

The mounting global debt pile has dominated discussions in Bangkok this week, where some 15,000 people have descended for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings.

This included the first meeting of the newly formed Borrowers’ Platform on Monday. A group of finance ministers and central bank governors from some 30 countries, it was formed to exchange ideas about how to deal with debt burdens – and how to avoid pitfalls.

News.title: Trump backs down in Zambia mineral and data-sharing row
News.content:
Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US government after the US dropped demands for access to sensitive health data and separated the deal from negotiations over the country’s mineral resources.

The agreement follows months of negotiations over a $2.49 billion health aid package, with Zambia pushing back against US demands to share medical data and give preferential access to the country’s rich mineral reserves in exchange for money to provide lifesaving healthcare.

Under the final agreement, Zambia will not be required to hand over individual patient records or biological specimens, which the US had previously argued was important for global disease surveillance.

Data sharing will be restricted to monitoring and evaluating US-funded health programmes.

A separate agreement covering US access to Zambia’s critical minerals has also been decoupled from the health financing deal, it was confirmed last week.

“The government will not be sharing any specimens with the United States because we removed all those aspects that raised concern,” Zambian Health Minister Roma Chilengi said last week as the agreement was signed.

Zambia’s Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe also confirmed that the health and mineral agreements had been separated.

“There was this [memorandum of understanding] on health and another on critical minerals, and we were saying that these need to be decoupled, and this has been done,” he said.

ROY KEANE has once again branded Manchester United a “circus” following a shock outburst from Lisandro Martinez this week.

Martinez took aim at the United board on Tuesday following a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.



He said: “Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it is a reflection of the mirror of how our club is at the moment.

“We had a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well.



“Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today. I expect more. One hundred per cent. I expect more from our technical director.”

His criticism was not well received by several club legends, with record goalscorer Wayne Rooney claiming it could “rip the dressing room apart” and Ashley Young suggesting it might cause “fractions” within the squad.

Sports.title: Arsenal job cuts ‘will fund one player’s salary for three days a week’ as brutal cost of redundancies revealed
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL have scored a “big own goal” with their decision to axe 60 members of staff.

The club informed employees on Wednesday that cuts would be coming and the brutal cost of the redundancies have been revealed.



Analysis from football finance expert Kieran Maguire estimates that the Gunners will save around £3million a year with the cuts.

And, going off the latest accounts for the 24-25 season, that equates to around just one player’s salary for three days a week.



Maguire believes this underlines how Arsenal’s owners have scored a “big own goal”, especially off the back of winning the Premier League title in May.

Boss Mikel Arteta last week also penned a huge new contract, at around £20million-a-year.

Maguire wrote on social media: “Arsenal winning the Premier League resulted in a lot of praise for the club from neutrals in the title race last season.

“This was partially due to the way the club is so embedded into the community. The announcement of 60 job cuts yesterday has shown that relationship to be hollow.

“If assume a (generous) £50k a year salary to those who have lost their jobs then Arsenal will save £3m.

“The average first team player earned £7.7m in 24-25, and likely to be much higher last season when bonuses for winning the title kick in. So the redundancies will fund one player’s salary for 3 days a week.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“The club will have earned about £198m in money from Premier League in 25/26 and £125m from Uefa for making the Champions League. Sponsors will have paid bonuses too for the Premier League title.

“Overall revenue has increased by £319m between 2022 to 2025, and likely to go up by a further £50m or more in 25-26.

“It’s unknown how much the report from the consultants will have cost, but they tend to do these things for money, not love.

“Not sure how much owner ‘silent’ Stan Kronke, the biggest private landowner in the US, knows or cares about those who have been made redundant, or whether he’s aware of what happens at Arsenal.

“I’m not questioning his Gooner credentials but suspect he doesn’t have a Steve Bould tattoo on his arm though.



“Big own goal from the owners.”

US firm Boston Consulting Group are conducting the review, which will not affect the men’s or women’s coaching and performance set-up.

FORMER Chelsea youth star Ato Ampah is set for a lengthy period on the sidelines after undergoing surgery on a serious knee injury.

The Stoke City winger, 20, only joined the Potters in February after ten years with his boyhood Blues.



Ampah has never featured for Stoke after recovering from a toe injury last season before suffering a setback in pre-season.

But he picked up a severe knee issue while stepping up his comeback bid for the Under-21 side.



Ampah has been forced to go under the knife to fix the problem and manager Mark Robins expects him to be out for “a fair amount of time”.

Robins told the Stoke Sentinel: “It’s really disappointing. It was an impact injury during the break and he was looking like he was ready to go in terms of his fitness and his availability and all of those things.



“But he had an impact injury that meant he’s had to have surgery and it was quite serious surgery.

“He’s going to be out for a fair amount of time and everybody is really disappointed for him.”

Robins said the surgery was a success but doctors had to ensure his joints were not “compromised for the rest of his life”.

He added: “Surgery has gone well, so I’m told, but it will take a long time for that to heal to ensure that the surfaces of his joints are not compromised for the rest of his life.

Oslo abode

Three years ago, Haaland was listed as the owner of an apartment in the Sommerro project in Oslo.



Real estate agent Hans Houeland said that the apartment has a view of the city but is in a top-secret location that can barely be seen.

Fans will have to imagine it to be a James Bond-esque property, or maybe even a real-life Batcave.

The £2.8m price tag brought two garages and a wealth of upgrades from the floors to the kitchen.

Bed of roses

Next up is a posh £950,000 apartment with a small balcony, two bedrooms and two bathrooms.

In the Frogner neighbourhood, it’s found in the upscale borough in the inner city of Oslo.



The capital city’s largest park is nearby and has Norway’s biggest collection of roses, with 14,000 spread across 150 different species.

The property’s listing details, from 2024, included high ceilings, decorative plasterwork and ceiling roses – perhaps inspired by the famous park.

Dad’s old pad

Haaland’s property empire is so crazy that he has even bought a £872,000 house from dad, Alfie, according to VG.



After the deal went through at midday on October 5, 2022, he went on to score twice against FC Copenhagen in the Champions League.

Alfie bought the apartment back in 2000 for less than £140,000, then he sold it to his mum in 2011 for around £222,000.

But it was not all bad from Erling’s granny after Alfie bought it back for about £464,000 a decade later.

The apartment is not far from Bryne Stadium where Haaland laid the foundation for his blockbuster career.

One floor down

In the same building as his 2022 Bryne purchase, the superstar striker splashed out £436,000 on another unit in 2025.



But this one is on the floor below, according to land registry records.

Desert oasis

In October, Ohana Residences launched the second phase of their Yas Residences project in collaboration with Man City.



The major development is set to decorate Yas Island in Abu Dhabi and Haaland revealed he and dad Alfie had secured villas along the gorgeous canal.

Appearing on a giant screen at the Etihad Centre, Haaland said: “We will be neighbours in Abu Dhabi… I just got a house and so did my father.”

It is set to be the perfect sports-focused community, with facilities including a City Training Academy and oxygen therapy, cryotherapy and hydrotherapy spaces.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The average five-bedroom villa pad looks to set residents back about £2.2m.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte ‘open to joining Man Utd’ as pressure builds on Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Next

ANTONIO CONTE is open to joining Manchester United if they sack Michael Carrick, according to reports.

Man Utd’s latest defeat to Atletico Madrid saw the club drop to a winless streak of five games, piling the pressure onto Carrick.



Lisandro Martinez’s explosive interview targeting the club higher ups, including specifically Jason Wilcox, added fuel to the fire raging around the Red Devils at the moment.

SunSport understands club chiefs aren’t looking to replace the manager at this stage.



However, talkSPORT claim ex-Chelsea and Napoli boss Conte would be willing to take on the responsibility if the chance arose.

The Italian won the league title with the Blues in 2017 before adding the FA Cup in 2018.

He also won the Serie A with Napoli in 2025 before leaving by mutual consent, adding to the three back-to-back titles he won with Juventus between 2012 and 2014 as well as the 2021 title with Inter Milan.

Conte appeared to hint at wanting the Man Utd hotseat earlier this month.

The 57-year-old said in an interview with The Athletic he would love the chance to bring back a fallen giant.

He said: “If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself — a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories — you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back — if it isn’t there today — to fight for those goals…



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history. I’d like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more.

“Clubs where there’s pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you’re not going there just to take part, but to compete.”

United, who – assuming they do not win the league this season – will be 14 years without a league title, certainly fit that billing of a club who has lost its way.

They have not properly competed for league titles since then, with their two runner-up finishes in the league since then putting them way off the pace of the Manchester City team’s which did win the league in those years.

Sports.title: Former Premier League star now working as an UBER DRIVER in shock career change after retirement
Sports.content:
Next

EX-PREMIER LEAGUE star Hugo Porfirio has swapped points for pick-ups … by becoming an Uber driver.

The Portugal winger spent the 1996-97 season on loan with West Ham and made 23 top-flight appearances for the Hammers.



Porfirio scored four goals in all competitions during his time in east London before returning to his hometown club, Sporting Lisbon.

A loan spell with Nottingham Forest would materialise in early 1999, in which he scored one goal in nine appearances while on loan from Benfica.



Porfirio would win three caps for his country, for whom he played at Euro ’96, before ending his playing days in 2008 in Saudi Arabia with Al Nassr.

He disappeared from view after leaving his scouting role with Sporting 13 years ago.

But the 53-year-old has now been spotted driving an Uber in Portugal‘s capital city.

Influencer Andre Ramalho unmasked the ex-pro on social media earlier this month after Porfirio took him and a pal on a journey.

He said: “We had a ten-minute walk to make, but we were late and tired, so decided to call an Uber.

“We were amazed by the guy driving the car. How could he be doing something so ordinary?



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“This is the fella who played at Euro 96, and played alongside Rui Costa, Luis Figo and Vitor Baia.

“He is the coolest guy of all time, and a great bloke as well.

“He also drove very well. Footballers aren’t usually known as good drivers!”

Ramalho’s post received thousands of likes on Instagram.



And Porfirio’s daughter Madalena paid tribute to him, writing: “My father is a machine.”

Porfirio found the back of the net in the Premier League for West Ham with goals against Chelsea and Blackburn.

And he also netted in cup ties against Forest and Wrexham.

He also found the back of the net against Sheffield Wednesday during his spell at the City Ground.

Sports.title: McIlroy four off lead on delayed first day in India
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy shot a two-under par opening round to finish four shots behind the clubhouse lead on a part-suspended first day of play at the DP World India Championship in New Delhi.

McIlroy was midway through the back nine when play was stopped for thunder and lightning in the area, with players then off the course for over four hours.

When play did resume at 4pm local time, McIlroy completed a round of 70 to sit tied 13th.

The world No 2 started from the par-four 10th, which he bogeyed, and went out in 34 after birdies at the 13th, 15th and 18th.

He found another birdie at the second hole but followed that with a second bogey of the round at the third, before finishing with six successive pars.

Image: Tommy Fleetwood and Rory McIlroy in discussion during round one at Delhi Golf Club, where both finished at two-under

Denmark's Niklas Norgaard holds the clubhouse lead on six-under thanks to a 66, with McIlroy's fellow Northern Irishman Tom McKibbin one of three players at five-under with Eugenio Chacarra, who is second in the Race to Dubai standings.

"Yeah, it was okay," McIlroy, who sits third in the Race to Dubai rankings, said of his first round.

"I felt like I hit the ball pretty well for the most part. Missed a few putts early on, got it going a little bit around the middle and then maybe missed a couple opportunities when we came back out after the delay.

Sports.title: 'Not helping me or my future' - Colapinto asks fans to stop online abuse
Sports.content:
Alpine driver Franco Colapinto has asked his fanbase to stop directing online abuse at other Formula 1 drivers and figures within the sport because it is "not helping" his career.

After becoming the first Argentine driver to compete in F1 for more than 20 years when he was drafted in by Williams midway through the 2024 season, Colapinto has received huge support from his home nation.

However, since Colapinto joined Alpine in 2025, the team have had to issue several statements condemning online hate and abuse following incidents involving the 23-year-old driver.

Colapinto had previously spoken out against online abuse but suggested on several occasions that it was a societal issue rather than a specific problem with his fanbase. His position now appears to have changed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lionel Messi meets Franco Colapinto in the paddock at the Miami Grand Prix.

In a video posted on social media, Colapinto said: "Hello everyone. There's something very important that I've needed to talk to you about for some time.

"I probably should have spoken to all of you sooner, but this is something that needs to be addressed, something we need to change and improve.

"I will always be grateful, and I genuinely feel incredibly fortunate to have had you all supporting me from the very beginning.

"I'm grateful for all the support you give me, for how you help me achieve results, and for how you constantly push me to aim higher.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ted Kravitz visits Buenos Aires to catch up with Argentina's local hero Franco Colapinto to discuss how Formula 1 has become so popular in his home country.

"You help me and the team achieve our results, race after race, day after day, as we train and try to improve. And I'm genuinely grateful for all of that.

"I know it makes you incredibly proud when things go well for me, when I score points for myself and the team. And I have always been very grateful for that support.

"But sometimes, we go too far.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"Instead of supporting me, we end up criticising people and attacking other drivers, other colleagues, my team-mates, my mechanics, my engineers - people I work with every single day.

"I know you think you're defending me, but you're actually doing the opposite. You're not helping me or my future."

There have been several notable incidents of drivers facing online abuse in situations that appeared to be related to Colapinto's fanbase.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Franco Colapinto shares the response of Pierre Gasly and Flavio Briatore to his Azerbaijan GP crash.

There was major hostility towards Jack Doohan at the start of the 2025 season before Alpine replaced the Australian driver with Colapinto after just six rounds.

Then, during the 2026 season, FIA race stewards were abused after Colapinto received a penalty at the Dutch Grand Prix, before his team-mate Pierre Gasly hit out at "disturbing" threats he received following the Spanish Grand Prix in September.

Reigning world champion Lando Norris then received abuse after making heavily critical comments about Colapinto after the Argentine caused a crash that took him out of the race during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris reflects on his critical comments about Franco Colapinto.

Norris later apologised for his comments about Colapinto, but Alpine once more issued a statement condemning social media abuse.

In August, Alpine confirmed a one-year contract extension for Colapinto to remain with the team for the 2027 season.

He responded well to that news with points-scoring results in Italy and Spain at the start of September, but has failed to score at the three races since.

Sports.title: 'Unsatisfactory' Lord's pitch dug up by MCC after first demerit point
Sports.content:
The Lord's pitch that was used for England's Test against New Zealand in June has been re-laid by the Marylebone Cricket Club and will be out of action for two or three years.

Pitch 9, one of five central strips at Lord's, was handed its first demerit point and deemed "unsatisfactory" by the ICC after match referee Andy Pycroft found excessive seam movement and inconsistent bounce during this summer's Test against the Kiwis.

All 40 wickets fell in just 166 overs during the match.

In response, the MCC has recently re-laid the pitch following a review of the Lord's square.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player All 17 wickets from day two at Lord's during the Test match between England and New Zealand.

Work to reconstruct the pitch began earlier this month.

The MCC told members this week that the decision to dig up the pitch was taken after the most comprehensive review of Lord's pitch conditions.

The MCC also plans to use hybrid pitches, which the data has found to be more durable than traditional pitches. Hybrid pitches are not permitted to be used in Tests.

The club is also producing the first of three drop-in trays, which will be moved to the main square in 2028.

The 'permanent drop-ins' will be installed on a long-term basis, rather than being removed and replaced seasonally like those found at multi-use venues in Australia.

Lord's is currently scheduled to stage two Tests next year - against Bangladesh in May and Australia at the end of June in the Ashes.

The Kia Oval has been chosen as the host venue for the World Test Championship final.
