Sports.title: Bournemouth will consider Scott sale in January for over £80m
Sports.content:
Bournemouth's stance on selling Alex Scott is softening, with the England midfielder continuing to refuse offers to sign a new contract at the south coast club, Sky Sports News has been told.

If a big offer came in for him in January, it is something the club would have to consider. While Scott will not agitate for a move, he is ambitious and keen on exploring his options with bigger clubs.

Chelsea and Liverpool retain a serious interest in the 23-year-old, as did Manchester City, Arsenal, Manchester United and Tottenham before they strengthened their midfield with other options in the summer, after being told by Bournemouth Scott was not for sale.

Scott's existing contract expires in just over 18 months, and Bournemouth are aware that his value will only shrink further as time passes.

While they do not want to sell him, we have been told they may be open to offers for him in January if the club is practically safe from relegation. Bournemouth have yet to win a Premier League game so far this season, and lost 5-1 at Chelsea last weekend.

Sources have suggested to Sky Sports News an offer in excess of £80m with add-ons would have to be taken seriously by Bournemouth in January.

Scott faces many more weeks on the treatment table after exacerbating a thigh tendon injury whilst away with England, when he made his full senior debut.

Rose: Scott still committed to Bournemouth

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Peter Smith explains why so many clubs are after Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose has insisted Scott is committed to the club despite talk growing about a January exit.

Asked about Scott's future on Wednesday ahead of Bournemouth's Europa League game with Sturm Graz, Rose said: "We just closed the other transfer window and we're now talking about the next one.

"We are just focused on the game [against Sturm Graz] and the upcoming game in the Premier League - and not commentating on rumours that show up right after the last transfer window closes.

"It's not frustrating anyway for us. I told you that Alex Scott was going to stay in the summer. We got questions after questions in press conferences for I don't know how many weeks.

"He's a player of our club and now he's injured, we are looking forward to having him back in a couple of days and weeks and we'll continue with Alex Scott.

"And he's quite committed, everyone can see it from the first games [of the season]."

Sports.title: Alex Scott quits Disney+ role as Women’s Champions League presenter
Sports.content:
Alex Scott has left her role as a presenter of the Women’s Champions League coverage on Disney+. It is understood it was Scott’s decision to walk away and focus on other projects, including her new show, One More Word WSL, which she works on with her fellow former England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams.

Scott had fronted the streaming platform’s coverage of the leading women’s European club competition since it obtained the rights in 2025. Disney’s production levels were criticised after the opening round of fixtures this season after a series of technical problems, including an unscheduled advert break that interrupted the second half of Arsenal’s 1-0 win over HB Køge for more than three minutes.

A spokesperson for Disney+ told the Guardian: “We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the Uefa Women’s Champions League on Disney+. Her passion for the women’s game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success.”

Scott, a former England and Arsenal defender and former contestant on the BBC’s Strictly Come Dancing and ITV’s I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!, has also presented major sports shows for the BBC, including coverage of the 2020 Olympics. Scott’s representatives said: “Alex is grateful for the opportunities she has had to work with the team at Disney+ and hopes that they continue to work together in the future.”

Scott also presented the BBC’s Football Focus show for five seasons before its closure this year. At the start of this season’s Women’s Super League campaign she launched One More Word through her own production company, First Cap Productions Limited, and she has previously explained that show was created in response to the BBC cancelling it’s weekly, televised WSL highlights show.

Scott, who turned 42 on Wednesday, told the Observer, this month: “I feel like there’s always an excuse about women’s football shows not working because of the viewership or needing to save money. Whereas I think if they are done right, they can work, if things are given a fresh idea or a fresh format, they can work.”

In the same interview, discussing some of the criticism aimed at Disney’s Women’s Champions League coverage this term, Scott said: “Ultimately, do I agree with all the decisions that were made? Absolutely not. Did I try and advise? Yes, but I can only do so much.

“But nobody sees the conversations, the fights I have behind the scenes. But I can hold my head up and know that I’ve always tried my best for the greater good of women’s sport.”

Sources have told the Guardian the presenter’s relationship with Disney remains positive. Disney, whose coverage is produced by ESPN, secured an exclusive five-year deal to broadcast the Women’s Champions League across European broadcast territories in 2025. It is understood its presenting team will continue to include Shebahn Aherne, Nedum Onuoha and Lianne Sanderson. Their lineup also includes commentators such as Vicki Sparks and Jacqui Oatley. The competition resumes on 28 October.

Sports.title: Apologetic Infantino ‘not fit’ to lead Fifa, claim European FA heads after meeting
Sports.content:
European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, with the heads of the English and German Football Associations questioning his fitness to govern after a three-and-a-half-hour council meeting.

Infantino began the long-awaited gathering of Fifa’s 37-strong executive board by apologising for failing to consult them over his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan but failed to provide answers to dozens of questions posed by the European FAs on a range of subjects including the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, Donald Trump’s Fifa peace prize and the Folarin Balogun affair, when the USA striker’s World Cup suspension was overturned after lobbying from the US president.

Infantino’s apology was followed by a 30-minute presentation on FFE from an American law firm, which described the $20bn (£15.1bn) valuation and proposed sale of a 20% stake to Thrive Capital as a good deal for Fifa. The lawyers left the meeting without answering any questions, however, to the annoyance of many present.

Quick Guide How do I 

“The main objective for Gianni was to survive this meeting and nothing more,” one council member told the Guardian.

Council members succeeded in deferring, until they receive more information on Balogun, a Fifa proposal to amend its disciplinary regulations by removing the scope for players shown a straight red card to have it rescinded. Infantino pledged to provide that information by their next meeting in Doha on 16 December, after nominations close on 18 November for March’s presidential election.

The issue of whether the Fifa peace prize will be revived this year or Trump left as a standalone winner has been contracted out to Fifa’s social responsibility committee, and the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, has been appointed to chair a new committee examining governance reform, but otherwise the meeting broke up without tangible answers, to the frustration of the English FA’s chair, Debbie Hewitt.

“We didn’t get answers to anything that we had specifically requested,” Hewitt said. “I think the man [Infantino] has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions, he’s not fit to be Fifa president. That was what was shared in the meeting.”

The German FA’s president, Bernd Neuendorf, went further by calling for wholesale reforms of Fifa’s administration, which he hopes will fall within the purview of Sheikh Salman’s governance committee.

“The whole administration has to be reformed and the whole governance has to be reformed,” Neuendorf said. “But I’m pretty clear here that this is not possible with Gianni as the responsible person at Fifa. So we need a complete restart, I think, a political restart of persons who represent Fifa.

“Yes he apologised, but I didn’t have the feeling that this apology was because of the FFE project in total. My impression was it was just because it wasn’t brought forward to the council and no one was involved.”

Neuendorf also said he was “very confident” that an alternative candidate would be found to stand against Infantino, a view shared by senior figures at Uefa, who expect a late declaration to limit the amount of time for Fifa to scupper the nomination.

The respective presidents of the three continental confederations who have called for Infantino to go, Aleksander Ceferin of Uefa, Victor Montagliani of Concacaf and Sheikh Salman, have ruled themselves out and suggestions that high-profile figures such as Arsène Wenger or Michele Kang could put themselves forward have been dismissed.

A proposal to distribute $3.5bn (£2.6bn) from Fifa’s financial reserves, which would involve each national association receiving £25m over the next four-year cycle, was approved by council.

Montagliani is also understood to have been critical of Infantino, but Fifa’s president received strong support from council members from Asia and Africa.

“I am certain that Gianni Infantino is the right president,” Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritania Football Federation said. “‘The majority want Gianni Infantino to stay. After finally withdrawing this proposal, president Gianni Infantino apologised to the members of the executive committee. This was followed by a responsible debate, during which this issue was more or less shelved.

“In the interests of football, the executive committee is looking ahead and seeking solutions, by focusing on the good aspects that football has to offer and trying to move forward.”

Sports.title: FA spending on Wembley hospitality and free tickets for FA Council rises by 25%
Sports.content:
The Football Association spent 25% more on Wembley hospitality and freebies for FA Council members last season, the Guardian can reveal. Latest accounts show expenditure on tickets and hospitality rose from £452,300 in the 2024-25 season to £564,400 in 2025-26.

While fans across the country have staged protests and walkouts in recent years over ticket price rises, and the cost-of-living crisis has made football increasingly unaffordable, the FA has upgraded the hospitality it offers to VIPs. Liverpool scrapped plans to increase ticket prices over three successive seasons following widespread unrest from supporters at the end of last season.

There are more than 120 FA Council members, including some of the most influential figures in the game, such as the English Football League chairman Rick Parry, Professional Footballers’ Association chief executive Maheta Molango and senior Premier League executives.

Quick Guide How do I 

FA Council members can attend England and FA matches – including the FA Cup semi-finals and final – held at Wembley and bring one guest free of charge. They receive complimentary meals and drinks, and sit in premium seats.

“FA Council members are invited as our guests to the England matches and FA competitions that we host,” an FA spokesperson said. “They are just one of the groups invited to these fixtures, alongside others such as the competing clubs and any visiting national associations. The hospitality offering at these matches was updated over the past year to better reflect the hospitality offered by clubs and other football stakeholders, which has resulted in an increase in expenditure in this area.”

The accounts indicate ticket and hospitality costs are likely to increase further due to the Fellowship of Council, an honorary membership scheme introduced in 2017. It allows members who have served on the FA Council for at least nine years to continue receiving free tickets, food and drinks even after stepping down.

“As the number of members of the Fellowship increases annually, the costs associated with match tickets and hospitality are likely to increase,” the FA company secretary, Richard McDermott, writes in the accounts. “We propose to introduce changes to the benefits that go with membership of the Fellowship so that from 2027 these costs will start to reduce.”

The cost of hosting FA Council meetings also almost doubled, rising from £18,600 to £33,200, with much of the increase attributed to higher hospitality expenditure.

Sports.title: Southgate ‘hardly watches’ football and does not envisage Premier League return
Sports.content:
Gareth Southgate has all but ruled out a return to Premier League management and revealed he “didn’t even enjoy the wins” for more than a couple of minutes towards the end of his time in charge of England.

Southgate, who has moved away from football since stepping down as the manager of the England men’s team after defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final, said he had not attended a game since watching his boyhood club Crystal Palace beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final last year.

The 56-year-old’s only taste of club management came when he spent almost three-and-a-half years at Middlesbrough after replacing Steve McClaren in 2006. Southgate was unable to keep Middlesbrough in the Premier League in 2009 and he indicated during an appearance on the Amol Rajan Connection podcast that he had no interest in seeking a return to top-flight management.

Quick Guide How do I 

“I don’t see a scenario where I do that,” he said. “Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying … at the very least for a period, the wins keep you going. By the end, I didn’t even enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes. So, I’ve hardly watched football.

“I went to the FA Cup final to see my team, Crystal Palace, win their first trophy. I’ve not been to a football ground since. So my sort of desire to be involved in football has changed.”

Southgate managed England for almost eight years and came close to ending their hunt for a first men’s trophy since the 1966 World Cup. But he has sought different opportunities since leaving the role. He has launched a podcast and fronted a BBC documentary this year in which he travelled across the UK to understand the challenges facing young men and boys.

“I’ve loved the last 18 months of my life,” Southgate said. “I’ve had 37 years where my sense of self depended on did I win or lose on Saturday. And actually I’ve loved having different experiences.

“I’ve met politicians, I’ve met people in the media industry, I have learned about leadership in all sorts of areas, I’ve travelled around the world learning things. I’ve just enjoyed playing a different film in my life.”

Sports.title: Vinícius claims he is targeted by referees and says flair players need protection
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior is not happy with how he is being treated by referees and wants more protection for talented players such as himself, Lamine Yamal and Julián Álvarez.

Vinícius spoke out after Real Madrid’s 4-3 come-from-behind win at Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday. The Brazil forward also acknowledged he was going through a slump, but said he had “no doubt” he would regain his best form soon.

The match against Roma came hours after he was handed a four-game suspension in the Spanish league after being sent off for pulling the hair of an opponent and for protesting against the referee. “I don’t recall any other player receiving a four-match suspension,” he said. “I tried to move the player in front of me out of the way, and I ended up getting caught in his hair.

“That was it – a red card – which is why I was so surprised. I didn’t say a single offensive word to the referee that would warrant a four-match ban. But when it comes to Vini, it’s all too easy. The opposing team will always say it’s justified, and the press will say the same. I understand that. I’m here to keep evolving and improving, because I know where I’ve come from and what I’m capable of achieving.

View image in fullscreen Vinícius Júnior leaves the pitch after his red card against Villarreal. Photograph: Alejandro Martinez Velez/Reuters

“It’s understandable for the opposing fans to jeer me, because my job is to score goals against their team, but I don’t get the referees. I’ve seen the stats: I’ve been on the receiving end of 500 fouls, yet that has only resulted in five red cards. In the end, the yellow cards always seem to go to Vini, to the attacking players. We need to protect the players who bring something different to the game, like Lamine at Barcelona or Julián at Atleti. Defenders are allowed to foul me the entire match but in the end it’s me who gets the card.”

José Mourinho complained about the timing of the announcement of the suspension. “Do you think it’s normal for a player from a Spanish team, preparing for an important match that’s also crucial for Spanish football, to find out about his four-match suspension just two hours before kickoff?” Madrid’s manager said. “We were on the bus about to arrive at the stadium when we found out … they’ve started doing things without any shame.”

Vinícius, who hasn’t scored for Madrid since August, was replaced in the 59th minute of Madrid’s victory before the team rallied from 3-1 down. “I’m working to get back to my best as soon as possible,” Vinícius said. “I know I’m not at my peak right now, but I’ve been through worse, and even when people have doubted me, I’ve always stood up for this club. That’s why I signed a six-year contract extension. The good run of form will return, and the goals will come back, too. I’m certain of that. I have no doubt. I’m here to help the team.”

The 26-year-old downplayed his frustration after Mourinho substituted him. “It’s natural for me to get upset when I’m substituted because I always want to play every single match,” he said. “I’m well aware of my current form and how I’m playing. I’m here to help the team, and sometimes you have to come off so that other players can get on and change the dynamic.

“Mourinho and I have a great relationship. He’s always straight with me. Of course I got a little annoyed when I came off today, but that’s normal. In the end he was right, the team improved, and that’s what matters most.” Vinícius was replaced by Endrick, who scored an 85th-minute equaliser before Antonio Rüdiger gave Madrid the win in the 90th.

Among the games Vinícius will miss because of his suspension is the clásico at Barcelona on 25 October.

Sports.title: Champions League review: PSG’s benchmark, Viking uprising and an Italian-German dilemma
Sports.content:
A big week for

Famous faces in the crowd for English teams’ home matches on Wednesday. While Prince William delighted in his beloved Aston Villa’s 6-0 romp over Fenerbahce, Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City homecoming was spoiled by Paris Saint-Germain showing they still represent the benchmark in European club football this season.

The center-circle inquest led by Erling Haaland after Vitinha put PSG 3-0 up was a jarring contrast to the triumphalism shown when City were winning at Liverpool last weekend. The Parisians put on a devastating display in the first half and, although the defiance City exhibited at Anfield on Sunday was on display again in the second half, PSG held on for a 4-2 win. “We could’ve lost this match if they scored the chances they created,” said a magnanimous Luis Enrique.

City may soon be absent from the competition, after they were found guilty of more than 100 charges of breaking the Premier League’s financial regulations. If City wish to sign off with a valedictory trophy lift they now know the standard they must meet – and beat. PSG have had their own issues with financial regulations in the era of petrodollar state ownership but, with the club president Nasser Al-Khelaifi a major powerbroker in European football, they have become an establishment club. While City are now pariahs, PSG have become near untouchables, not least on the field of play.

“He who brings glory to Rome, Rome honors for ever,” read a banner in the Stadio Olimpico. “Your hands are blessed and the people will give you eternal glory!” José Mourinho won hearts during his time in charge of Roma. But his popularity ratings are nowhere near as high in Madrid, though the manner of Real Madrid’s 4-3 comeback win over Roma will calm the gathering storm he has faced since returning to work for Florentino Pérez. The comeback came via Madrid’s next generation: Carlos Espí, 21, pulled the scoreline back to 3-2; the unlikely aerial threat of the 5ft 8in Endrick, 20, made it 3-3; and Antonio Rüdiger scored the winner, via a second assist for Arda Güler, 21. Mourinho embracing youth is a fresh development. This week saw Mourinho block a loan move to Milan for Endrick, and he admitted in Rome: “The first half was the coach’s fault; the second half was the players’ fault.”

A record 78 goals flew in this game week; the previous record was 71. On the wrong end were the Serie A clubs. In addition to Roma’s defeat, Como lost 3-2 at Feyenoord, the decisive moment coming via an own-goal for Robert Sánchez, the keeper loaned from Chelsea. Inter also lost, 4-3 to Club Brugge, whose performances in the competition in recent years meant the result was not much of a surprise. Napoli lost 3-1 to Villarreal, the Yellow Submarines’ first Champions League win in eight matches. Neapolitan focus was on a running battle between Massimiliano Allegri, the Napoli coach, and Kevin De Bruyne. Scott McTominay’s return to the team has pushed De Bruyne deeper. The Belgian made clear his feelings on playing there with some highly demonstrative body language.

Player of the week

There were two hat-tricks this week. Bradley Barcola ignited his Liverpool career with a treble at Lask, whose defending during their 6-3 defeat was suboptimal to say the least. That 4-3 Brugge win was mostly thanks to Nicolò Tresoldi. The striker was born in Italy, but moved to Hanover when he was 13, and he plays for Germany’s under-21s. Italian soul-searching after missing out on the last three World Cups has cast Tresoldi as a new savior. “I always speak Italian at home; I was born in Italy too,” he said post-match. “We’ll see.”

Paolo Di Canio, on Sky Italia, was pessimistic: “He has already chosen.”

View image in fullscreen It was a memorable night for Viking. Photograph: Lise Åserud/NTB/AP

Club in focus: Viking Stavanger

After Bodø/Glimt’s exploits over the last couple of seasons and the national team’s admirable World Cup showing, the true football hipsters have a new destination in Norway. Viking play a thousand miles south-west of Bodø, in Norway’s oil capital, Stavanger. The club has co-managers in Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim and Morten Jensen: the pair were interviewed for the top job before deciding it was best they share duties. Viking are in the Champions League for the first time since the 1992-93 season, and at one point on Tuesday the Eliteserien champions led Bayern Munich 2-0. But a seismic shock was averted via two Harry Kane goals and another from Luis Díaz that put Bayern 3-2 up. Once Herman Haugen headed home at the back post, Viking had rescued a point with a 3-3 draw. “I could have played another 90 minutes,” said the captain, Zlatko Tripić, “I’m so incredibly proud.”

They said it

“I expect more. I’m not going to close my mouth; we need more ambition, we need to talk more about winning Champions Leagues and Premier Leagues in terms of other things.” Lisandro Martínez was undeterred by Peter Schmeichel’s soft-shoe questioning on Tuesday’s CBS broadcast after Manchester United’s defeat to Atlético Madrid.

“If we don’t say the truth, nothing will change,” added Martínez, whose Manchester United contract expires in June. Martínez’s interventions exposed the cracks at United – and highlighted the dubious merits of having a football celebrity do a journalist’s job.

Looking ahead

A quick turnaround sees the third round staged next week, with Manchester United heading to Como for another examination of Michael Carrick’s regime. That follows a difficult Sunday trip to Leeds for United.

A couple of heavyweight ties catch the eye. Barcelona’s 4-1 win at Galatasaray continued their perfect start to the season, and Tuesday sees them visit PSG, a meeting of the two favorites to claim the title. On Wednesday, Arsenal v Bayern may trigger unhappy memories among Gunners fans. Arsenal lost 5-1 to Bayern three times in succession over the 2015-16 and 2016-17 seasons, and lost in the 2023-24 quarter-finals to the Germans too. Arsenal did, though, beat Bayern in last season’s Champions League.

Sports.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
Sports.content:
Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season, given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence.

For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast.

But traducing the messenger will always be easier than hearing the message, even if Martínez’s views are widely shared within the United dressing room. If the fallout from the Manchester City legal case has demonstrated anything, it is English football’s ingrained reluctance to scrutinise the owners and executives who hold more influence over the sport than anybody else. Men in boots, not men in suits. Hey, watch the ball. It’s going to move!

All the same, it’s worth parsing exactly what Martínez was complaining about, because it’s a good deal more complex than it may appear on first viewing. Player calls out board – and specifically “technical director” Jason Wilcox – for failing to invest sufficiently in the squad over the summer. This was a summer in which United brought in three midfielders (Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba), a reserve goalkeeper (Karl Darlow), nobody up front and nobody in defence. So far, so simple.

But let’s begin to unpick the threads. Why did United not buy a defender in the summer, despite pursuing deals for Lewis Hall and Myles Lewis-Skelly? Because they were unable to sell a defender. There was no interest in Diogo Dalot or Noussair Mazraoui, nor in Harry Maguire, nor in Luke Shaw or Martínez, whose contracts are up next summer in any case. This is the product of recruitment decisions made and deals signed years ago. But why do United, one of the world’s most lucrative clubs, need to sell to buy in the first place?

Perhaps for the same reason they baulked at the asking price for Elliot Anderson and decided to sign the inconsistent Santos and the adequate but overpromoted Tielemans instead: this is a club in austerity measures, whose part-owner Jim Ratcliffe has been furiously cutting costs and raising ticket prices, determined to curb the years of excess that preceded him, where mediocre players were signed on ridiculous money, where failing coaches were paid to leave. But why would United, one of the most commercially successful clubs in footballing history, ever need to cut costs?

Perhaps as a result of the more than £1bn drained out of the club by the Glazers in their 21 years of ownership, not just in dividends but share sales and interest payments on the debt they undertook to buy the club, while neglecting the maintenance of Old Trafford and the training ground at Carrington. Whether he knows it or not, when Martínez is criticising the lack of investment he is in effect holding the Glazers accountable for more than two decades of avarice and mismanagement.

All of which lends a certain significance to Martínez’s intervention that goes beyond the churn of the weekly news cycle. Has any serving United player spoken out so frankly about the ruins of the Glazer ownership? Ole Gunnar Solskjær made a minor stand in early 2005, before they had arrived at the club. Cristiano Ronaldo threw some hand grenades over his shoulder a few days before he left for the second time in 2022. Countless others waited for the safety of retirement, when their disgruntlement could be monetised for personal gain, rather than used to stigmatise them, as Martínez will doubtless be stigmatised in the coming days.

View image in fullscreen A Manchester United supporter shows off a jumper protesting against the club’s owners and executives. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

Does any of this help United to win games in the short term? Almost certainly not. Martínez attempted to clarify his comments in a social media post on Wednesday night. He may still be dispatched to the bomb squad anyway, for the crime of pointing out that the emperor secured his throne almost entirely through the use of payment-in-kind loans.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Inevitably Michael Carrick too will be gone before long, away to the great Overlap podcast in the sky. A few months ago I wrote hopefully that Carrick might be the ideal man to cut through the noise and nonsense. I was wrong. The noise has beaten him; the nonsense always wins; any accumulated credit from last season has long since evaporated.

Of course it’s not Carrick’s fault that United haven’t signed a new defender in almost two years, that Bruno Fernandes is so clearly playing through discomfort, that Joshua Zirkzee is still somehow hanging around the place, that the ownership decided to embark on a purge of season-ticket holders in the summer, generating a huge wave of ill-feeling and apathy that can be felt at Old Trafford on matchdays: an entire fanbase trying to work out whether they actually still care about this.

But accountability is for the little people, and far easier to replace a coach on a modest 20-month contract than to oust Ineos or the Glazers, to replace Wilcox or Omar Berrada, even if we now know they partly built their reputations on the success of a club that has been found to have serially cheated. Bumper returns for the owners, price hikes for the fans, corners cut on the pitch; this is the story of the modern Manchester United, which by no coincidence is also the story of modern football.

Sports.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
Sports.content:
On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch.

The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there.

“The plan was always to get here as soon as possible,” Pinnock says, “with a bit of breathing space in case that didn’t happen … Now we have to figure out how to establish ourselves. I think the massive opportunity here is to join something so new but under the umbrella of a very established strong brand and club. It feels as if it’s startup-like but there’s a nice safety net.”

Having the infrastructure of the wider club behind them is a positive. They have drawn on their marketing and commercial expertise to build a distinct identity for their women’s team, giving them a different kit, bringing in their own sponsors and establishing a unique matchday experience. Their most recent derby against Brøndby drew 8,047 to Parken, an A-liga record.

Secure foundations, however, take time to build. Operating in a semi-professional environment, their first season at the top has come with teething pains. They parted ways with their head coach Kasper Klarskov Nielsen after three matches and sit second from bottom after 10 fixtures. Many players continue to juggle football with work or study while trying to adapt to the physical demands of the top flight.

“It’s been tough so far,” the forward Maria Hovmark says. “It’s our first year in the league and we have to get used to that. Around 80-90% of the girls have never played in the top league so it’s a challenge … It’s also a huge challenge for the club because they’ve never been through this as well. It’s a chance for all of us and we’re slowly getting there.”

FCK’s rise is being played out in the context of a league working to establish itself. The country has produced highly technical players such as Pernille Harder, and the Danish Football Association (DBU) is trying to develop a stronger domestic game through greater investment, increased exposure and the establishment of minimum standards while also featuring in European competition. The champions, HB Køge, have returned to the main Champions League for the first time since 2022 and Brøndby will be involved in the Europa Cup last 16.

View image in fullscreen ‘It’s been tough so far. It’s our first year in the league and we have to get used to that.’ Maria Hovmark of FC Copenhagen takes on Brøndby. Photograph: Freja Borne

“I expected more of an egalitarian setup because of the politics of Denmark and what I’ve found is actually women’s football is still at the early stages of a journey,” says Pinnock, who is South African and was previously head of women’s football at Bristol City. “There are a few clubs who are really pushing the envelope but the majority need to lift their game. That is also an opportunity. It’s exciting to see how we can look to our neighbours and say: ‘How are they doing it?’”

FCK are operating on a different model to Køge, who have been able to invest immediately on the pitch. FCK’s longer-term ambition is to challenge for trophies, compete in Europe and become players in the global transfer market. They also want to develop homegrown players who regard staying in Denmark as an attractive option, while bringing experienced talent, such as Hovmark, back home.

“The league is going more professional in terms of some teams being more full-time now,” Hovmark says. “It is getting more serious and I think that attracts people. That also brings the level higher.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The wider societal impact the club can have is key for FCK. Their “Hall of Femmes” campaign with their main partner, Andel, gives young female footballers the opportunity to be featured on banners at Parken and offers two annual scholarships for players aged 14-19. FCK are also testing an academy model in which girls and boys train together according to their age, ability and development needs rather than by gender.

For now, the priority is to ensure they remain an A-Liga side. The club, however, have an eye on on-field success and patience will not last for ever. “We’re going to get a grace period of two or three seasons,” Pinnock says. “Then we’ve really got to embrace the FCK model, which is that we’ve got to be winners and we’ve got to head for the top.”

Sports.title: Graeme Souness: Goal machine Harry Kane is a worthy Ballon d’Or winner but there is one catch
Sports.content:
Graeme Souness: Goal machine Harry Kane is a worthy Ballon d’Or winner but there is one catch

Harry Kane is deserving of winning the Ballon d'Or because he can do the 'hardest thing in football'.

That is according to Graeme Souness, who has hailed the England captain's ability to score goals.



3 Kane has been warned one factor could stop him winning the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

However, he has questioned whether playing in the Bundesliga for Bayern Munich could impact Kane's hopes of glory.

The 33-year-old is amongst the favourites to win the prestigious award later this month.

A ceremony at the London Palladium on Monday, October 2026 will see the latest recipient announced.



Kane is fresh from scoring 61 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions for Bayern last season.

His strikes helped Vincent Kompany's side win a domestic double as Kane clinched the Bundesliga golden boot and the European Golden Shoe.



He then went on to score six goals in seven matches for England at the World Cup as they finished third in North America.

Can Kane win the Ballon d'Or?

Those numbers can be the difference when it comes to securing the Ballon d'Or, says Souness.



Speaking to Alan Brazil and Tony Cascarino on Thursday's Breakfast show, he was asked if Kane would be his choice to win this year's award.

The three-time European Cup winner replied: "The hardest thing to do in football is score goals. He scores goals for fun.

"I’d have to factor in this, the Bundesliga is not the greatest league. It’s not got the intensity that the Premier League has.

3 Kane's goal-scoring ability is enough to win him the Ballon d'Or, says Souness Credit: Getty



"I’d have to say that, but he’s a goal machine and the single biggest reason he’s a goal machine is (because) he’s a lovely, lovely striker of the ball.

"He gets his shots off accurately from anywhere within 25 yards. He’s a proper player and he’s got a football brain. He can see a picture and deliver on it as well.

"I think that would be a good shot because generally it is strikers that win it.

"I know Rodri won it recently, (Luka) Modric a couple of years ago, but it’s generally the guys that put the ball in the back of the net.



"I suppose that's very deservedly so because that is the hardest thing to do in the game of football."

Bundesliga Ballon d'Or winners

Kane is amongst the 30 nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or alongside fellow internationals Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice.

Last 10 Ballon d'Or winners 2025: Ousmane Dembele - PSG and France 2024: Rodri - Manchester City and Spain 2023: Lionel Messi - Inter Miami/PSG and Argentina 2022: Karim Benzema - Real Madrid and France 2021: Lionel Messi - PSG/Barcelona and Argentina 2019: Lionel Messi - Barcelona and Argentina 2018: Luka Modric - Real Madrid and Croatia 2017: Cristiano Ronaldo - Real Madrid and Portugal 2016: Cristiano Ronaldo - Real Madrid and Portugal 2015: Lionel Messi - Barcelona and Argentina

Meanwhile, three of his Bayern team-mates have also been nominated in Luis Diaz, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano.

They are the only current Bundesliga players in the running for the award.



If Kane is victorious, he would become the first German-based player to win the Ballon d'Or since Matthias Sammer in 1996.

The former Borussia Dortmund captain is one of six players to do so whilst plying their trade in the Bundesliga.

Others include Hamburg legend Kevin Keegan in 1978 and 1979 as well as Borussia Monchengladbach's Allan Simonsen in 1977.

As for Bayern, they have had three separate winners, with the most recent coming 45 years ago.



3 Sammer is the last Bundesliga-based player to win the Ballon d'Or Credit: Alamy

Karl-Heinz Rummenigge won the Ballon d'Or two years in a row in 1980 and 1981.

The only other Bayern players to receive the award were Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer.

Sports.title: The eight players who have run the furthest in the Premier League this season
Sports.content:
The eight players who have run the furthest in the Premier League this season

Every Premier League team needs a workhorse - someone to do all the dirty work for their side and give their all for the cause.

Certain teams have more of those stars than others, but there are some standouts so far this season for total distance covered.



5 Gross has covered the most distance in the Premier League so far this season amid his incredible start with Brighton Credit: Getty

Here are the top flight players who have run the most...

1. Pascal Gross - 72.5km

Brighton's star of the campaign so far is surely Pascal Gross.

And at 35 years old, Gross has covered the most distance of all players in the Premier League, running 72.5km in six games.

That's an average of 12.1km per 90 minutes for the veteran, who has four assists and three goals to his name already.

2. Anton Stach - 70.9km

Anton Stach comes next, with the Leeds midfielder clocking just under 71km covered across six outings.



The German has averaged 11.9km per 90 minutes.

He has played all but two minutes of Daniel Farke's side's impressive start to the Premier League season.

3. Vitaly Janelt - 70.8km

Another midfielder. Another German.

Brentford's Vitaly Janelt is also one of the leading runners in the league, totting up 70.8km in total distance covered.



Janelt is currently averaging 11.8km per 90 minutes.

5 Leeds' Stach is a workhorse in the Leeds midfield and the numbers back his efforts up Credit: Getty

5 Armstrong has secured a starting spot for Everton and is making sure that he keeps it Credit: Getty



4. Harrison Armstrong - 70.3km

Also above the 70km mark is Everton's Harrison Armstrong.

19-year-old Armstrong, who has started every game for the Toffees so far this season, has covered 70.3km altogether.

The ex-Preston and Derby loanee averages 12.1km per 90.

5. Ethan Ampadu - 69km

Ethan Ampadu rounds out the top five, as the Leeds captain leads by example when it comes to effort on the pitch.

The Wales international has covered 69km so far this season, averaging 11.5km per game.

Ampadu has played every minute for the Whites, with their midfield full of workhorses, as he joins Stach in the list.



5 Sunderland skipper Xhaka is also one of the leading runners, with the 34-year-old leading by example Credit: Getty

6. Granit Xhaka - 68km

Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka is also one of the furthest runners in the Premier League this season.

He has covered 68km altogether, averaging 11.3km per 90.

At 34 years old, Xhaka, who has recently been punished for obtaining a fake COVID certificate, has played every minute this term.

7. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall - 67.5km

Averaging 11.3km per 90 minutes, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is another of the leading runners in the Premier League.



The ex-Chelsea midfielder has run a total of 67.5km so far.

And as a reward for his effort on the pitch, Dewsbury-Hall has also scored two goals and provided one assist.

5 Dewsbury-Hall is the second Everton midfielder sitting among the Premier League's running leaders Credit: Getty

8. James Justin - 67.1km

Farke clearly has Leeds working hard for their results.

James Justin is the third Leeds player in the top eight players who have covered the most distance so far this season.

Justin has run 67.1km in six Premier League games.

Sports.title: UEFA continue plot to oppose Gianni Infantino as FIFA president after $15million move
Sports.content:
Senior figures within UEFA continue to work on a candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in March's FIFA presidential election, talkSPORT understands.

Infantino is currently face-to-face with several of his critics at the FIFA Council meeting in Zurich and has promised to address his failed and controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise plans, which intended to part-privatise FIFA.



2 Infantino is struggling to drum up support ahead of his re-election vote next year Credit: Getty

Ahead of the FIFA Congress on Thursday, Infantino pledged $15million in additional funding to each of FIFA's 2011 members, taking their total for the 2027-2031 cycle to $25million.

The move comes off the back of calls from UEFA and CONCACAF to use more of FIFA's reserves to fund members.

Infantino has also put forward an amendment stopping automatic one-match bans being suspended at FIFA tournaments. This follows US striker Folarin Balogun being allowed to play against Belgium in the last sixteen of the World Cup despite being sent off in the round before against Bosnia.



Infantino has insisted he played no role in making the call, yet he was asked to review the incident by US President Donald Trump, as talkSPORT revealed.

Several key members within UEFA are not satisfied with extra funding or even reforms.



UEFA's comments

"There has to be a challenger to Infantino because he will certainly, as he already said, be a candidate in the election unless something dramatic happens in the coming weeks," UEFA VP Laura McAllister told talkSPORT. "Of course, it could do, but legal processes [including UEFA putting together a criminal case against Infantino and FIFA] take a long time, so let's not hold our breath over that.

"There has to be a candidate who, first of all, can command the support of all modernisers beyond just Europe. Football doesn't belong to Europe. Yes, we [UEFA] are a very powerful confederation and, yes, we generate a lot of funds, but football belongs to every single federation and club across the world. On this, I agree with Infantino that football doesn't belong to anyone in any geographical location.



"We have to unite people around a candidate, or maybe more than one candidate, and that candidate, whoever he or she is, has to stand on a manifesto of agreed reform: of greater transparency or greater accountability, of less political interference and must recognise the role of the FIFA President should be to run football, and not [like Infantino] to involve himself in other ventures, whether that's via the private or political sectors.

2 Infantino's decisions throughout the summer have put him under serious pressure to keep his job Credit: Getty

"I hope very much there will be a candidate [to rival Infantino] and I think that's where we are at the moment. Lots of work is happening behind the scenes. But we need a candidate with an ethos of credibility and modernisation showing why they should win the election next March."

Who could challenge Infantino?

UEFA, with strong support from CONCACAF, are still determining who to put forward on the ballot. So far, former Spurs defender Ramon Vega is the only name to come forward. He does not yet have the five federations required to officially stand, and it is uncertain if he even meets the eligibility criteria of working for two-years in football within the last five years.



talkSPORT understands there is firm support for Arsene Wenger, the former Arsenal boss who is now FIFA's head of football development. It is unclear whether Wenger has an appetite to stand, but his name has been brought up at multiple UEFA meetings, including last week in Berlin.

Luis Figo is another name who would draw considerable support. The ex-Barcelona and Real Madrid footballer has been a vocal critic of Infantino. He has also been earmarked as a potential replacement for Aleksander Ceferin, but the UEFA President is seeking another term next year.

Victor Montagliani was viewed as a leading contender but has decided to seek a new term with CONCACAF.

Nasser Al-Khelaifi would be well capable of challenging Infantino, and winning support in key battleground Asia, but the PSG President insists he doesn't want to stand.



"I have zero ambition," Al-Khelaifi told talkSPORT at the EFC General Assembly in Copenhagen earlier this month. "I don't think I am the right guy. I don't want to go [to FIFA]. I am enjoying what I am doing. I am having fun."

EFC vice-chair Dariusz Mioduski is another name who has been discussed and is highly-regarded within the game.

The head of the Norwegian FA, Lise Klaveness, AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, former FIFA presidential candidate Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein and London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang are other contenders that executives within UEFA or CONCACAF have suggested.

Senior UEFA sources say they want only one name so as not to fragment the vote.



The expectation, should a candidate emerge, is their unveiling could run close to the November 18 deadline so as to give Infantino the least possible time to prepare for a challenge.

Even if someone can't be found to beat Infantino, several sources within football, spoken to by talkSPORT, feel it's important not to let him get re-elected unopposed, and to use the four-month campaign period as means to fuel genuine debate.

Sports.title: Manchester United told exactly what to do if they appoint Antonio Conte
Sports.content:
Manchester United told exactly what to do if they appoint Antonio Conte

Simon Jordan believes Antonio Conte will succeed at Manchester United if the club 'give him what he wants'.

talkSPORT understands Conte would be open to the United job should they axe current boss Michael Carrick.



3 Conte would be open to succeeding Michael Carrick in charge of Manchester United Credit: Getty

And speaking on White & Jordan on Thursday morning, Simon has told the club's decision makers what to do in order for the Italian to restore the Manchester giants to their former glory.

What did Jordan say?

"I think if you give Conte what he wants and deliver that on a regular basis, then he will deliver regular success for you," Jordan said.

Conversely, Conte is the sort of manager that if you give an inch, he'll take a mile, as Jordan alluded to.



"The consequence of that is, you have to give him precisely what he wants, endlessly, and probably have to deal with some other nonsense you probably won't appreciate," he continued.

"It depends how much you want a winning football club."

3 'Give Conte what he wants' is Jordan's advice to United Credit: talkSPORT



Conte has been out of work since leaving his role as Napoli head coach earlier this year.

The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss had guided the Partenopei to the Scudetto in the 2024/25 season before finishing second to Inter Milan last term.



Carrick under the cosh

Carrick is under increasing pressure to turn United's fortunes around following a poor start to the season.

United sit 13th in the Premier League table having collected six points from the opening six games of the season.

They failed to maximise their numerical advantage in the recent 1-1 home draw with winless Tottenham Hotspur after Dominic Solanke cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's second-half strike.

3 United are now winless in five under Carrick Credit: Getty



And talkSPORT's Jason Cundy was left fearing for Carrick's Old Trafford future following the home stalemate.

"Carrick is on the rack. I'm telling you now, he is in trouble," he said on GameDay Phone-In.

"That is terrible. The last three games, they lost to 10-man Man City, could've got beaten by Fulham and they draw at home, 1-0 up, to 10-man Spurs.

"They have been absolutely terrible. The heat on Carrick now is going to be unbelievable."



United followed up Saturday's stalemate with a 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid.

The post-match chat, however, centred around Lisandro Martinez's comments after the Argentine spoke out against the United board.

They return to domestic duties with a trip to rivals Leeds United on Sunday afternoon.

Ruben Amorim's final game as United boss was a 1-1 draw with Leeds at Elland Road back in January.

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea starlet suffers devastating injury setback at new club
Sports.content:
Stoke City winger Ato Ampah has suffered a second serious injury setback just eight months after joining the club.

The England Under-20 international has yet to make his debut for the Potters since signing from Chelsea in February.

3 Ampah joined Stoke from Chelsea on a three-year deal in February Credit: Getty

Following a decade with the Blues, Ampah penned a three-year deal with Stoke earlier this year.

However, a toe injury disrupted his first few months at the club as his recovery stretched into the new season.

Despite an impressive return to action with the Under-21s last month, Ampah is now set for another lengthy spell on the sidelines.

The 20-year-old suffered a knee injury as he stepped up his recovery which has required surgery, manager Mark Robins has confirmed.

It comes after the forward scored twice in four matches for the Under-21s after goals against Wolves and Bournemouth.

As well as those Premier League 2 appearances, Ampah recently featured in a Premier League International Cup defeat to Borussia Monchengladbach.

Robins confirms Ampah surgery

Robins provided an injury update during his pre-match press conference on Thursday.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's trip to Derby County, he explained: "It’s really disappointing.

"It was an impact injury during the break and he was looking like he was ready to go in terms of his fitness and his availability and all of those things but he had an impact injury that meant he’s had to have surgery and it was quite serious surgery.

"He’s going to be out for a fair amount of time and everybody is really disappointed for him.

3 Injuries have prevented Ampah from making his first-team debut for Stoke Credit: Getty

"Surgery has gone well, so I’m told, but it will take a long time for that to heal to ensure that the surfaces of his joints are not compromised for the rest of his life.

"You don’t know what he could have been and what he could have given us and we’re just going to have to wait.

"For him it’s really, really difficult. He’s not been able to get going at all but this one was a challenge under a challenge that has really affected his knee.

"He’s had that surgery done, he’s had some corrective stuff done and that’s the bit that will take time because you’ve got to give it a chance to heal properly."

Who is Ato Ampah?

Born in Ghana, Ampah joined Chelsea's academy at Under-11 level before progressing through the club's famed youth system.

He made one senior appearance during his time with the Blues in December 2024.

3 Ampah made one Conference League appearance during his time at Chelsea Credit: Getty

Ampah featured off the bench in a Conference League victory over Astana, earning himself a winner's medal at the end of the campaign.

His first-team debut came aged 18 after producing impressive numbers for Chelsea's Under-18 side.

Across 31 appearances for the team, Ampah scored 10 goals and added nine assists.

He was also part of the side which lost the 2024 Under-18 Premier League national final to Manchester United two years ago.

Ampah made a further 40 appearances after being promoted to Chelsea's Under-21s, scoring seven goals and providing four assists.

At international level, he has also turned out for the Young Lions in both the Under-18 and Under-20 age groups.

Sports.title: The six fastest players in the Premier League this season
Sports.content:
The six fastest players in the Premier League this season

By having some of the world's best players featuring in the Premier League, it means we also have some of the fastest.

And so far in the top flight this season, some stars have ran so quick that they'd get a speeding fine in the City of London.



4 Liverpool's Barcola is the current fastest player in the Premier League after reaching his highest speed on his debut for the Reds Credit: Getty

Here are the current fastest players in the Premier League...

1. Bradley Barcola - 22.3mph

Topping the list of fastest players in the Premier League is Liverpool's big-money summer signing Bradley Barcola.

The £123million French winger has reached a high of 22.3mph.

He reached that rapid top speed on his top flight debut for the Reds against Ipswich Town after coming off the bench.

2. Antoine Semenyo - 22.1mph

Antoine Semenyo is up next, having reached a high speed of 22.1mph playing for Manchester City this season.



Semenyo moved up to second in this list with a rapid sprint against Liverpool in Man City's 3-0 victory at Anfield.

He may have been revved up by the hostile atmosphere as City played their first game since being found guilty of 114 charges for breaching the Premier League's financial rules.



3= Oscar Bobb - 22mph

Fulham have struggled under Alvaro Arbeloa, who is under intense pressure to keep his job, but they've been quick.

Ex-Man City winger Oscar Bobb reached a speed of 22mph during the Cottagers' late 2-1 loss to Ipswich.



His teammate Gonzalo Garcia is also one of the fastest in the league, but he just misses out on a spot in the top six so far.

4 Semenyo's top speed came during Man City's first game since being found guilty of 114 charges at Anfield against Liverpool Credit: Getty

4 Everton's Barry is also one of the quickest players in the Premier League, posting an impressive speed against Hull City Credit: Getty

3= Thierno Barry - 22mph

Also clocking in at 22mph is Everton striker Thierno Barry.

Barry reached his top speed in a 2-2 draw with Hull City.

On top of his speed, the 23-year-old has also upped his scoring, netting three goals in the Premier League so far this season.



5= Bryan Mbuemo - 21.9mph

It have been a campaign of misery so far for Manchester United, but at least they're high up on the speed list...

Their quickest player so far this season has been Bryan Mbuemo.

Mbuemo reached 21.9mph during a 2-2 draw against Everton.

4 Man United may be having a miserable year, but Mbeumo is giving his all, reaching one of the top speeds of all players in the league Credit: Getty

5= Matias Fernandez-Pardo - 21.9mph

Newcastle's £55m summer arrival, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, rounds out the top six, posting the same speed as Mbeumo.

Fernandez-Pardo's sprint high of 21.9mph came on a disappointing night, as the Magpies were thrashed 4-1 by Coventry.



The Belgian may be quick, but he's yet to provide a goal or an assist in the Premier League so far this season.

Sports.title: Why Barcelona have change kit for upcoming El Clasico
Sports.content:
Why Barcelona have change kit for upcoming El Clasico

Barcelona will be changing their kit once again for their upcoming clash with rivals Real Madrid.

It has become a Barca tradition ahead of El Clasico in recent years to feature artists on their kits.

3 Barcelona will have a new kit for the upcoming El Classico Credit: Instagram @fcbarcelona

Due to their massive sponsorship deal with Spotify, Barca have featured the biggest sporting acts logos when they face their biggest rivals in La Liga.

It's a trend they have started since 2022, with the first 2026 edition being revealed to feature rapper Tyler, The Creator.

The multi-Grammy-winning star becomes the ninth musical act to have their logo worn by Barca during El Clasico in the space of the last five years.

The special shirt will have his streetwear label 'GOLF WANG' when they welcome Real Madrid on Sunday, October 25.

Additionally, it will also be worn during Barcelona Women's Liga F match the day before against Granada at the Estadi Johan Cruyff.

Barca will also be organising an event on the evening prior to the game to celebrate the collaboration.

GOLF WANG released a statement, that read: "There are few stages in the world bigger than El Clásico. To see GOLF WANG alongside iconic global brands.

"FC Barcelona and Spotify sets a new benchmark for collaboration across sports, music and fashion, bringing the worlds of football and fashion together in a way that feels truly unique to GOLF WANG."

Which other artists have featured?

Drake became the first musician to have his logo placed on their red-and-blue striped jersey in October 2022, with the 'OVO' owl label on display at the Bernabeu - they went on to lose 3-1 to Los Blancos.

Rosalia was proved to bring better fortune for the Catalan side as they wore her logo for the Motomami album in the reverse fixture - it was a 2-1 victory for the home side at the Camp Nou.

3 Alongside the home kit, GOLF WANG are also making turquoise-coloured kit and a whole apparel collection Credit: Getty

The following season, the Rolling Stones released their first album in 18 years and celebrated by putting their iconic lips and tongue logo on the Barcelona shirt - it was Lamine Yamal's debut appearance in El Clasico.

The second meeting that year meant Barca narrowly lost by a late Jude Bellingham strike as they wore the barbed-wire heart logo of Colombian singer and songwriter Karol G on the front.

In the 2024/25 campaign, Coldplay had a lunar-themed logo for their Moon Music album - it brought a lot of luck for Hansi Flick in his first El Clasico event as his side secured a convincing 4-0 victory.

3 Barcelona lifted the league trophy after beating Real Madrid last season Credit: Getty

Then Travis Scott's Cactus Jack logo featured as the Catalan-outfit completed the league double over Los Blancos despite Kylian Mbappe weighing in with a hat trick.

Last season, they sported Ed Sheeran's eighth album called 'Play' in the fixture but lost on that occasion.

However, Olivia Rodrigo's OR butterfly logo saw Flick's side clinch the La Liga title at the Camp Nou in May 2026.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr's nightmare 24 hours: Real Madrid star fumes at being subbed early by Jose Mourinho against Roma - after four-game ban for hair-pull rules him out of El Clasico
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr's nightmare 24 hours: Real Madrid star fumes at being subbed early by Jose Mourinho against Roma - after four-game ban for hair-pull rules him out of El Clasico

Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior has endured a nightmare 24 hours after being hooked early against Roma - and being slapped with a four-match ban for a wild hair pull.

The winger was subbed by Jose Mourinho before the hour mark with Madrid 3-1 down at Roma in the Champions League - only to see his team-mates go on to thrive and win 4-3.

His frustrations were evident and he said: 'It’s only natural for me to be angry when I’m substituted, because I always want to play every minute, to be at my best and help the team, and today that wasn’t possible.'

He did acknowledge the positive impact of his replacement, 20-year-old Endrick, who scored his first goal of the season as Madrid completed a monumental comeback in the dying minutes.

The Brazilian will not have much of a chance to blow off steam, though, after he was hit with a ban for violent conduct after his outrageous hair pull during a recent 1-0 win over Villarreal.

And the Brazilian will miss the El Clasico against Barcelona next week as a result, with Real Madrid already playing catch-up in La Liga.

Vinicius Jr has been slapped with a four-match ban for this hair pull during Real Madrid's 1-0 win over Villarreal

He was also fuming after he was hooked early in Real Madrid's 4-3 comeback win over Roma

He was astonished when he heard the news on Wednesday night before Madrid's incredible 4-3 comeback win against Roma, saying afterwards: 'We've never had this [hair pulling] explained to us.

'Someone from La Liga and the referees' association always comes to explain the rules, but never this specific point. It was a red card for me, simple as that... I've never been violent towards another player. I get hit quite a lot, yet the cards end up going to me.'

Vini Jr was sent off with a direct red card after tugging the long locks of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba on Saturday.

And he was fuming at his dismissal, with referee Isidro Díaz de Mera noting: 'after being sent off and still on the field, he continued to protest my decision loudly, heading towards the area where I was with an aggressive attitude.'

The referee also noted that Vinicius 'had to be restrained by team-mates' before eventually leaving the field of play.

He even appeared to shove a La Liga official as he stormed off. Authorities condemned his 'aggressive attitude'.

Vinicius Jr later posted a brief apology on Instagram, writing: 'Sorry to my team and my fans'.

But he also posted a series of clips of flashpoints from other matches where he believes players should have been sent off, but were not.

That post came with the caption: 'And the one who always sees yellow and red is Vinicius. A disgrace.'

Mourinho was highly irritated at the fact that they found out of his ban a couple of hours before the Roma game.

He told AS: 'Is it normal for a player to find out two hours before a match that he is going to be suspended for four games? There is no need to answer me. Is that normal? Could they not have announced the decision now or tomorrow morning? Did they have to do it while we were on our way to the stadium?

He protested against his dismissal and was condemned for his 'aggressive attitude'

'"In Portuguese we say: the cat is hiding but its tail is showing. It seems to me that the cat is no longer hiding now. The cat is acting freely, and there are things happening without shame. It is acting freely.

'Two hours before a match, a player at a Spanish club who contributed three points towards strengthening the standing of Spanish football, I do not see that as normal. But I am starting to consider it normal, because the cat is no longer hiding. What is the question?

'At the very least, it shows a lack of respect. Playing in Athens on Wednesday evening, arriving in Madrid at five in the morning, then playing on Saturday in Valencia, during a week before the international break, does not seem to me to be innocent.

'I do not believe the usual excuses, such as that the reason is television (broadcasting rights). I do not believe that. I have grown too old for that. As for the Vinicius story, and him finding out two hours before the match that he had been given a four-match suspension, Real Madrid fans are not stupid.'

The ban will only apply to domestic competitions, so he will miss fixtures against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. The next La Liga match he will be available for is against Celta Vigo on November 22.

Madrid, being a rather argumentative club in these circumstances, may still appeal the suspension according to the Spanish press.

Manager Jose Mourinho held his tongue in his post-match press conference, saying: 'I’m not going to speak because I want to be on the bench against Sevilla and Barcelona.'

In any case, he will be allowed to play against RB Leipzig and AEK Athens in the Champions League during the period of the ban.

His domestic absence is a blow but the No7 has not been at his prolific best this term, only scoring once and creating three assists in eight games.

'He is going to emerge,' Mourinho told TNT Sports in a display of confidence. 'It is just a question of when.'

Oddly enough, Vinicius thought he had scored his second goal of the season against Villarreal, but after the referee was called over to the monitor, he was sent off for the hair pull during the build-up and his effort was chalked off.

Madrid sit fourth in La Liga, six points behind Barcelona, who have made a perfect start.

They found their mojo at Roma in the Champions League, coming from 3-1 behind to win 4-3 late on as the Italian hosts paid tribute to their former manager Mourinho with a tifo, making him visibly emotional.

Sports.title: Matthijs de Ligt's ex-wife speaks out on divorce 'hell': Model AnneKee Molenaar bares all on split after Man United star 'couldn't handle' her 'spiritual' lifestyle
Sports.content:
Matthijs de Ligt's ex-wife speaks out on divorce 'hell': Model AnneKee Molenaar bares all on split after Man United star 'couldn't handle' her 'spiritual' lifestyle

Matthijs de Ligt's model ex-wife says facing up to their divorce was 'hell' – and says the break-up brought 'physical pain'.

AnneKee Molenaar, 26, split from the 27-year-old Manchester United star last year, only 12 months after they got married, but insists they still 'love' each other platonically.

Daily Mail Sport previously reported how Molenaar's 'spiritual' lifestyle and social media output – centred around crystals, tarot cards, flower remedies, and alchemy – had seemingly come between them.

De Ligt could apparently 'no longer handle AnneKee's exaggerated "spiriwiri-content"', according to Realityfbi. He and Molenaar got married in June 2024 after years of dating, right from when he was a teenager at Ajax, but the spiritual content had been a theme for years even before he popped the big question in 2023.

The Dutch defender is now dating a model called Amber Yuusef, while Molenaar is single and open to finding love again.

She told RTL Boulevard that facing her feelings was 'hell': 'It has been a tough year. A year with a lot of change, but also a year I am very grateful for.

Matthijs de Ligt's model ex-wife AnneKee Molenaar says divorcing has been 'hell' (Instagram: annekeemolenaar)

Molenaar says their break-up has caused 'physical pain' and that they still 'love' each other platonically (Instagram: annekeemolenaar)

'It was like I was having open-heart surgery,' she said of their divorce just a year after their wedding (Instagram: annekeemolenaar)

'It is an abrupt change and you miss something and you are sad about that. You are in pain. I really experienced it as something physical. Just physical pain... that is really just a process of grieving.'

'It was like I was having open-heart surgery and someone was blowing on my heart. That is how fragile and vulnerable I felt. Bruised.

'I understand that people think: something must have happened there. I hate to say it, but that is really just not the case.

'We had a wonderful time all those years, and yet last year we came to the conclusion that it is no longer there in a romantic way.

'There is a lot of love between Matthijs and me. There really is a lot of love. I think the most loving thing we did was saying: you go this way and I go that way.'

Molenaar is currently writing a book about alchemy, one of her passions which she has an Instagram page about.

Alchemy is a broad category but is partly known as a Middle Ages science in which individuals tried to transform regular metals into gold.

In March last year she passed a course dealing with flower remedies at the Bach Centre, a foundation devoted to following the practices of Dr Edward Bach, a British physician who believed that illnesses developed from a negative state of mind. She has continued following his teaching as recently as this month.

Her increasingly 'spiritual' lifestyle - centred around crystals, tarot cards, flower remedies, and alchemy - reportedly got on De Ligt's nerves (Instagram: annekeemolenaar)

She regularly posts about what she has been studying and is bringing out a book (Instagram: annekeemolenaar)

In June, De Ligt confirmed that he was dating Amber Yuusef after the duo were spotted kissing and cuddling in Ibiza.

He was confronted by the photos and addressed it on Realityfbi's Instagram account, after some screenshot allegations that Yuusef was only attracted to his fame and money.

'Normally I never feel the need to respond, but I do this time,' he said.

'In this day and age, we know that anything can be faked, and that is the case with this screenshot as well.

'Amber and I are getting to know each other better, and we would like to do that in privacy.'

De Ligt isn't the first footballer that Yuusef has been romantically linked with. As reported by Sportnieuws, she was spotted cuddling Jobe Bellingham, the brother of Real Madrid and England star Jude Bellingham, last year.

As for his on-field excursions, De Ligt underwent surgery in May and is yet to feature for United this season. He made the bench against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick issued a positive update recently, saying: 'I'm definitely comfortable with him playing.

De Ligt has been recovering from a long-term injury and surgery and was on the bench against Atletico Madrid

'Of course, there is the element of when that time is and how much it is. He played a little bit of the Lausanne [friendly] game and he's done a fair bit of training but, of course, we're working our way through it.

'So it's not too much, too soon. I've definitely got the confidence in him, no doubt about that.'

The injury meant he was ruled out of the Netherlands World Cup squad but ended uncertainty about the issue.

Speaking in May, he said: 'Since November I have done everything, pushing myself in every session and exploring every option, to get back to doing what I love, playing football.

'I am grateful to everyone who has supported me throughout a difficult period in my career. I remain as determined as ever to represent Manchester United and play in front of our incredible supporters as soon as possible.'

Sports.title: Liverpool fans hit the jackpot with Austrian football team's eco scheme that pays supporters to recycle their plastic cups
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans are celebrating a windfall by covering their Champions League trip fares by collecting beer cups in the stands at Austrian side LASK.

Supporters were given £2.50 for each cup they returned – leading some to gather dozens and pose triumphantly with their gigantic 'beer snakes'.

One Liverpool fan told Daily Mail Sport that they had made as much as £250, roughly enough to cover the cost of the excursion. Others danced in the concourse of the Raiffeisen Arena, with the tower of cups, numbering in the dozens, almost tipping over.

LASK are big pushers of eco-friendly schemes and boast of being the first club in Austria to create a stadium free of plastic bottles. Their stadium was built with 'sustainable and environmentally friendly construction and materials'.

'I think I saw one of the nine goals scored,' said one supporter who had been enjoying the revelry.

One father posted a proud picture of his son's 'first day earning money', claiming he had made almost £170 from his good deed.

Liverpool fans made a quick buck collecting beer cups at their away clash at LASK in Austria (X: @greggmunikwa)

Some collected so many that they claimed they were able to cover the cost of their trip (X: @EPLBible)

Supporters were given around £2.50 for each cup they returned, a policy not so common in English football (X: @LFCmagnus)

It is not the first time Liverpool fans have made a quick buck in this way on their travels.

Sparta Prague also gave fans the opportunity to do the same for their Europa League clash in March 2024.

It was the same policy in Leipzig in October that year when Liverpool visited in the Champions League.

The policy is not widespread within English football but Lewes, who play in the seventh tier, did introduce the scheme in September last year.

On the pitch there was plenty for Liverpool to celebrate as they thrashed the Austrian champions 6-3, with Bradley Barcola scoring a hat-trick.

While frail at the back, the Reds looked electric going forward, with Florian Wirtz in exquisite form and registering an assist.

Young striker Lewis Koumas bagged his first goal of the season – after having two disallowed for offside – as he continued to fill in for the injured Alexander Isak.

Defenders Ronald Araujo and Jeremie Frimpong also got on the scoresheet on a night Andoni Iraola hailed as 'very good'.

He said of Barcola: 'I think he played so well today and not just the goals. He had more chances to score, he was always a threat attacking the spaces in behind.

'In training sometimes you feel when a player is in the zone, and fortunately tonight for us he has shown the level that he has.'

Iraola added on Wirtz: 'I think he was amazing in possession. I think he had lively passes, good assists, he helped us to control the game, especially in the first half where he was roaming around and finding good spots. It was a good game from Florian.'

Sports.title: 'The first time I saw him play, I thought: "God exists"': Inside Estevao Willian's journey from Brazil to Stamford Bridge - KIERAN GILL is given exclusive access to intimate documentary which offers hint on teenager's future
Sports.content:
Ivo Goncalves turns to Estevao Willian and gently rests his hand on the arm of his son. ‘A movie plays in our heads, everything we’ve been through to get here, and you get to a moment like this, and I want to have other moments just like it,’ he says.

It is a loving exchange, of a father telling his lad how proud he is of him, with his mother, Etienne Almeida, sitting and smiling on his other side on the sofa in their living room.

It follows a little reminiscing about the time Estevao scored in Chelsea’s 3-0 Champions League win over Barcelona; the night a star was born as the boy from Brazil upstaged Lamine Yamal at Stamford Bridge.

For Estevao, that game was the culmination of a long journey from Franca to Cruzeiro to Palmeiras to Chelsea, where he arrived aged 18. But there were a few who saw this coming.

Such as Gustavo Ferreira, the now-director of Santos FC who took him to Cruzeiro: ‘The first time I saw Estevao play, I thought, “God exists”. Our Under 20s coach, having watched Estevao train when he was still 13 or 14 years old, came into my office and said that if there was no physical component, Estevao at 13 would already be playing for Cruzeiro’s Under 20s.’

Such as Serginho Carioca, his youth coach: ‘Estevao, when he was six, used to play against kids who were eight or nine. He would always finish off the game, always stand out, and I had this problem – the parents asked me to take Estevao out because he always unbalanced the games.’

Chelsea wonderkid Estevao Willian offers a glimpse into his family life in a new as-yet-unreleased film called I Am Estevao

In the documentary, Estevao reminisces about his goal in a 3-0 win over Barcelona (pictured)

He also recalls meeting Cole Palmer for the first time when Palmeiras played Chelsea at the Club World Cup. 'I didn’t understand him much,' admits Estevao

Such as Joao Paulo, his academy director at Palmeiras: ‘The first time I saw him play, I said, “This is a great gem to be the best in the world... wow". I saw (Joaquin) Piquerez, who’s one of our captains and an experienced left back of ours. On the second or third day (of Estevao joining first-team training), he asked me, “Who’s this annoying, talented kid?”’

Such as Nike, who made him the youngest Brazilian to sign a sponsorship deal at the age of 10, with Francisco Godoy, Estevao's representative, explaining: ‘A huge global brand identifying his talent, for us, really confirmed that we were on the right path.’
