Sports.title: Colapinto tells his supporters to stop abusing rival drivers: “They don’t help me” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto has urged his supporters to stop abusing his rivals and others involved in the series online.

“They are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite,” Colapinto told his followers in a video posted on social media.

The FIA and Alpine issued statements in the last two months condemning the abuse which occured following the Dutch, Spanish and Azerbaijan grands prix. Neither specifically mentioned Colapinto’s supporters but both identified the victims of the abuse, including his team mate Pierre Gasly and FIA officials. “It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned,” said Alpine in a statement last month.

Colapinto told his supporters the online abuse must stop.

“I know it makes you feel very proud when I do well, when I get points, me and the whole team, and I will always be very grateful for that,” he said. “But there are times when we end up attacking other pilots, other colleagues, my team mates, my mechanics, my engineers, people I work with day by day.

“I know they are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite. They don’t help me. And I really want you to understand that this is what we have to change, all together.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have to try to improve as a society, and to help me have a better performance, to help get my dream and my results, that is, to score points, I need you to help stop this, all of us together.”

Colapinto made his F1 debut with Williams in the second half of 2024, but the team had no space for him in their line-up for the following season. He joined Alpine, who promoted him to a race seat in place of Jack Doohan early in the season. Doohan later revealed he received death threats from those who wanted him out of the car.

Alpine issued the first in a series of reactions to abuse from Colapinto’s supporters this year following the Chinese Grand Prix, when Esteban Ocon collided with him. Some Colapinto supporters also accused Alpine of sabotaging Colapinto and failing to provide him with the same equipment as Gasly.

Recent flashpoints included the penalties Colapinto received for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags at Zandvoort, Colapinto’s brief delay behind Gasly at the Madring and the collision between the Alpine drivers and Lando Norris in Baku.

Mekies took over from Christian Horner in charge of the team last year. Horner had run Red Bull since it entered F1 in 2005.

Under Mekies, Red Bull rebounded from a poor start to last season. From over 100 points behind, Max Verstappen came within two points of retaining his drivers’ championship title in one of the closest ever finishes to a world championship.

Sports.title: Verstappen says Red Bull’s car was “scary” to drive early in 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull has made huge progress with a car which felt “scary” to drive early in the season, says Max Verstappen.

The four-times world champion has won the last two grands prix in a row and also took victory in the sprint race in Singapore last week. The team’s form has improved significantly since the beginning of the season, when Verstappen only reached the podium once in the first seven rounds.

Verstappen spun out of the British Grand Prix suffered costly spins in qualifying at the Red Bull Ring and Hungaroring as the team struggled to get on top of its car. However their most recent upgrades have transformed its performance.

“The car definitely felt a lot nicer from Baku onwards,” said Verstappen. “It’s just been a lot more balanced. Then naturally, of course, when you can compete a bit further up front without having too many issues with the car compared to the beginning of the year, where it was actually sometimes a bit scary to drive, that makes it a lot nicer.”

Verstappen finished a close second behind George Russell in Baku. He qualified only eighth but was in contention for pole position until his final lap was compromised by a yellow flag.

He has been undefeated since then and expects to remain competitive over the final rounds. “We’re not in a championship fight, and that’s why I think ’til the end we’ll just try to have a good time and try to add more podiums and hopefully a few wins.”

It is the second time in as many years that Red Bull has made a breakthrough with a troublesome car in the second half of a season. “Two completely different cars as well, with the regulations,” Verstappen noted. “Also two completely different problems.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We had to find lap time. Plus, of course, also this year with the engine side of things, I think for everyone it’s been sometimes a bit complicated to get the most out of it.”

Red Bull needs to ensure they begin next year in better shape, said Verstappen.

“From race one to now, I think we’ve gained a lot of experience. Of course, we’re still not where we want to be, but I guess everyone will say the same thing.

“But we have learned so much and definitely also on the car side have fixed a lot of our weaknesses. We just need to keep improving, keep learning this year that so we can apply that also into next year.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 teams need decision ‘by mid-October’ on whether final races will go ahead | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses say they need to know by the middle of this month whether the series’ final two races will go ahead as planned.

Qatar and Abu Dhabi are due to hold the final two races of the season in November and December. However the war in Iran, which forced the cancellation of races in nearby Bahrain and Saudi Arabia six months ago, put those plans in jeopardy.

F1 has a back-up plan to hold an alternative event at Imola. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali previously said a decision would be made by mid-September. Teams say they need to know one way or the other soon.

“I believe Stefano was targeting to tell us in mid-October,” said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu in Azerbaijan. “So, we all know what the situation is.

“I believe that Imola is getting ready in case we have to do it. I think the challenges are, for instance, things like European motorhome structure, etcetera. All those people who look after them, they have a winter job, so we need to find alternative people to do that.

“But I’m sure we all, as a family, community, will make sure if we have to do that, that will happen. But hopefully, as a baseline, we can go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. That would be really good.”

Drivers have pointed out the conditions could be very cold if the series races in Imola in December. However Audi team principal Mattia Binotto believes it would be no cooler than some other venues the series visits.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The main challenges are more organisation and logistics,” he said. “I would think, from a technical point, often we may say wintertime and snow tyres, but at the end, as a matter of fact, the average temperature in Imola in that time of the year is hotter than Las Vegas.

“So I don’t think that’s a true concern. It’s more from the organisation and the logistics, really. And again, mid-October, hopefully we may do the right decision.”

Domenicali told the Financial Times the “decision is done” but also admitted “Imola is the place that eventually, in case of a force majeure before a certain date, would be ready to host it.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 announces it will race in Rwanda from “early 2030s” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has announced it will return to race in Africa for the first time since 1993.

The series has agreed a 10-year deal to race in Rwanda, which has never previously held a round of the world championship. Unusually, no year for the inaugural race has been confirmed, with F1 saying only that it will “join the calendar in the early 2030s”.

A new circuit will be constructed in Bugesera, in the Eastern province of Rwanda. The track will be located 40 kilometres south of Rwanda’s capital Kigali, which hosted the FIA’s General Assembly and award ceremony in 2024.

F1 published an image of the planned RISE Motordrome circuit, which was created by Tilke Gmbh and Wurz Design, but gave no details of its specifications.

“Further details regarding the inaugural race date, circuit development milestones and race weekend plans will be announced in due course,” said F1.

According to Rwanda’s president Paul Kagame the race will be called the “Formula 1 African Grand Prix”.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali called the announcement “a landmark moment for Formula 1.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the world championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.”

F1 first raced in Africa in 1958, when Morocco’s Aib-Diab circuit held the final round of the season. However the series never returned to the northern African state.

The series found a longer-term home in South Africa, first at a track in East London, then at the popular Kyalami circuit near Johannesburg. South Africa held 23 grands prix, though the series faced growing criticism for holding events under the country’s racist apartheid regime, which led some teams to boycott the 1985 race.

Following a seven-year absence, F1 returned to a heavily revised Kyalami circuit for two races in the nineties.

By the time Rwanda hosts its first grand prix, up to 40 years may have passed since F1’s last race in Africa.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia–Teofimo Lopez Talks Advance For Early 2027
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are moving closer to a welterweight title fight in the first quarter of 2027, according to Mike Coppinger.

The January-through-March target gives Ryan a major payday to pursue without squeezing in another appearance in December. No firm date or venue was included in the update, and the fight has yet to be announced.

Teofimo’s WBA mandatory obligation to Jack Catterall remains unresolved, but that doesn’t have to stop the Ryan fight. The WBA belt isn’t needed to sell this matchup. Ryan’s WBC championship would still be available, and the appeal comes largely from putting these two recognizable names together.

The belt’s greater value to Teofimo could be at the negotiating table. Arriving as a fellow champion gives him another argument when discussing his share of the money. Relinquishing it would remove that bargaining point.

However, if Ryan, his promoters, and the financial backers are willing to offer Teofimo comparable money without the WBA title, keeping it becomes harder to justify. He could surrender the belt, remove the mandatory obligation, and proceed directly toward the bigger payday.

Facing Catterall first would introduce a risk that negotiations alone cannot remove. Teofimo could lose, suffer an injury, or come through a difficult fight needing more recovery time. Any of those outcomes could affect the timing or financial terms of a Ryan matchup.

Catterall has publicly opposed stepping aside. The WBA ordered the fight and gave the camps until October 22 to reach an agreement, leaving Teofimo with a decision if the organization insists on enforcing its mandatory.

That makes the financial terms of the Ryan negotiations especially interesting. If the offer depends heavily on Teofimo bringing his championship, he has a reason to seek permission to bypass Catterall. If the money is essentially the same either way, relinquishing offers a straightforward route.

The WBA can determine what Teofimo must do to retain its belt. Whether that belt is worth keeping could ultimately come down to how much Ryan’s side is willing to pay him without it.

Sports.title: Agility Drills Cannot Mask Canelo Alvarez’s Fading Gas Tank
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is putting his feet through plenty of work ahead of Christian Mbilli, but a movement-heavy approach could leave him short of energy before their October 31 fight reaches its toughest rounds.

Alvarez trying to reinvent himself as a nimble mover at age 36 looks like a recipe for disaster. The math simply does not add up when looking at his gas tank and output history.

Against Terence Crawford, Canelo was barely working, averaging just 28 punches a round while trying to plant his feet, load up on single power shots, and conserve energy. Even with that rock-bottom volume and virtually zero ring traversal, he was visibly gassing by round six. His body has shown clear signs of mileage for several fights now, and stamina has always been his primary limitation whenever opponents force him to work at a sustained clip.

Now his camp is circulating clips of him running agility ladders, doing cone drills, and practicing lateral movement to stay off the ropes against Christian Mbilli. While it makes for good social media optics, applying that in a real fight is completely detached from reality. Moving your feet constantly under pressure takes far more conditioning than standing your ground and picking spots.

The work doesn’t stop for Canelo! 💯 🎥: @Canelo 🎟️ Buy #CaneloMbilli NOW at https://t.co/yxybEeoyF5 | Oct 31 | Mexico vs The World | Live on DAZN | @RingMagazine https://t.co/zDOn7OR9xH — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 15, 2026

Mbilli is a pure volume puncher who thrives on throwing 70 to 80 punches a round, pressing forward with reckless abandon. If Canelo’s tactical adjustment is to skip around the ring, make short escapes, and play keep-away, he is volunteering to burn the exact energy reserve he does not have. Avoiding shots on the move still costs cardio, and Mbilli will not politely hit pause between drills to let him recover.

Canelo has never been an elusive ring mechanic. He built his career on upper-body slips, tight high-guard defense, and brutal counter-punching off a solid base. The only way he beats a swarmer like Mbilli is by doing what he has always done best: planting both feet and landing shots hard enough to break Mbilli’s spirit and stop the forward march. If he spends the first four rounds burning his legs on lateral movement, Mbilli is going to drown him in volume before the second half of the fight even gets started.

That script is practically already written. If Canelo gasses out trying to play Willie Pep at 36 and drops the belt to Mbilli, the post-fight press conference will be a masterclass in deflection.

Fighters with that level of clout rarely say, “I cooked up a terrible game plan in camp, convinced myself I could turn the clock back eight years, and completely misjudged my own gas tank.” Instead, the narrative instantly shifts into passive corporate speak. It becomes “we made tactical adjustments that didn’t materialize on the night,” or Eddy Reynoso will quietly take the heat to protect the brand, talking about camp fatigue or lingering elbow issues that allegedly flared up in the dressing room.

The irony is that Canelo’s entire late career identity has been built on stubborn pride. He genuinely believes his ring IQ can outsmart the physiological clock. Attempting to dance and pivot away from an engine like Mbilli is purely an ego-driven attempt to prove he still possesses the agility of his prime 154- and 160-pound runs.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Puts Rematch Pressure on Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley believes Daniel Dubois faces the greater pressure in their rematch, with the champion needing to repeat his victory against a challenger who believes he has corrected the mistakes that cost him their first fight.

Dubois recovered from two early knockdowns to win. Wardley admits he became overconfident after that success, giving the champion an opportunity to recover. If Wardley avoids those mistakes, Dubois could face a different task this time.

“I think that for me, like again, it’s something Daniel’s gone through, but now he’s got three losses on his record,” Wardley told Fight Wire. “Two of those to Oleksandr Usyk, so you chalk them up a bit differently.”

Wardley argues that another defeat would put Dubois in a difficult position, while he views his own first loss as something he can repair.

“It just frees me up. It’s okay, we had a loss. Things didn’t go too great. Not the end of the world,” he said.

The pressure on Dubois goes beyond the number of defeats. He needs to demonstrate that his previous victory was repeatable, rather than a result that depended on Wardley getting careless after putting him down twice.

Wardley believes he has identified how he let that opportunity slip. Better decisions could leave Dubois with fewer chances to recover, although maintaining pressure without wasting energy or walking into punches will require more than determination.

“There’s a few adjustments to be made, a few things we need to capitalize on better, and then the fight’s ours,” Wardley said.

Dubois proved he could beat Wardley that night. Whether he can handle a more disciplined version remains unanswered. Wardley still has to deliver those improvements under fire, but the champion cannot assume the same openings will appear again.

Wardley also questioned Dubois’s conflicting comments about his punching power, suggesting some of his opponent’s remarks sound rehearsed.

“Especially when the camera comes out, some of the lines you can very much tell are forced, or they’ve at least been told to him to put in there,” he said.

The verbal sparring adds to Wardley’s portrayal of himself as the more relaxed fighter. Dubois’s harder task is showing that he has answers for the changes Wardley brings into the ring.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Calls Sebastian Fundora A Cheat Code
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga can’t understand how Sebastian Fundora fits into the 154-pound division. Looking at a workout photo of the WBC champion, he compared Fundora to a video game character and suggested he should be making his money in the NBA.

Fundora’s long legs and arms dominate the picture. Berlanga fights two divisions above him at super middleweight, yet even he sounds taken aback by the sight of someone that tall competing at light middleweight.

How do they allow him to box at 154lb he’s a cheat code character from GTA WTF 🤣🤣🤣 listen he would have been a 200 million dollar NBA player. This is unacceptable he looks like a building https://t.co/AYW3y9aSuM — Edgar Berlanga Jr (@EdgarBerlangaJr) October 15, 2026

Berlanga isn’t the first fighter to reach for a video game comparison. After Fundora stopped Erickson Lubin in April 2022, Terence Crawford called him “a cheat code,” comparing him to a created Fight Night boxer with the height turned up in a smaller weight class.

It’s an understandable reaction. Finding sparring partners who can prepare an opponent for Fundora is difficult enough. Then comes the task of getting past those long arms and landing on a head that sits well above the usual target.

The odd thing is that Fundora often gives opponents a chance by coming to them. He likes fighting up close, throwing short punches rather than spending every round keeping shorter men at the end of his jab. They don’t always have to chase him to get their shots off.

That makes him entertaining, even if Berlanga thinks his dimensions look unfair. Fundora can make 154. The men across from him have to figure out the rest.

His WBC title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj this Saturday is a harder sell. Hadribeaj is the mandatory challenger, but most fans know little about him. They’re waiting to see Fundora against the bigger names in a division with plenty to offer.

Hadribeaj gets his chance to make himself known once the fight starts. Until then, Fundora’s unusual frame is likely to draw more conversation than the matchup itself.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Faces Long Wait For Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Liam Paro booking another defense puts more distance between him and Ryan Garcia, though Garcia’s alternative choices present a far bigger hurdle. Matchups with Teofimo Lopez or Devin Haney carry massive commercial appeal, which could strand Paro well past his ideal timeline.

“We’re not going to sit on the sideline,” Paro told Fox Sports Australia.

Staying active is the smartest move Paro can make. Continuing to take bouts keeps him sharp instead of burning months chasing an opponent who sees little urgency to fight him.

Teofimo gives Garcia an established American audience. A return bout with Haney carries built-in personal drama. Paro holds a world championship belt, yet hardware alone might not outweigh the bigger paydays Garcia could chase instead.

The calendar for Ryan creates another headache. If Garcia sits out until May, that single appearance eats up the first half of 2027. Another high-profile date could easily swallow the remaining months, leaving Paro on the outside looking in despite handling his business in the ring.

Teofimo’s mandatory duty against Jack Catterall adds some problems, but it will not kill a potential Garcia meeting. The WBA might grant Teofimo an exception so he can keep the strap. Teofimo could also surrender the belt outright to lock down the more lucrative bout.

That situation does not assure Teofimo gets the nod. Still, Paro cannot count on sanctioning body politics to eliminate a popular name from contention.

Title dynamics bring further chaos. If Garcia meets Teofimo first, Paro must hope Garcia wins so the WBC unification prize remains intact. A Garcia loss instantly ruins that scenario before Paro ever secures a signed contract.

Paro holds the power to defend his title and keep his phone line open. He cannot dictate Garcia’s opponent, dictate fight results, or force Garcia to pursue undisputed status.

Taking another bout makes complete sense. Chasing Garcia is worth the ambition, but Paro must build an active calendar that keeps rolling even if Garcia never calls. Paro landing that fight in 2027 makes zero sense from Ryan’s financial perspective.

Ryan operates purely on box office scale. A return match with Devin Haney already has massive public heat, personal grudge, and built-in history that sells pay-per-view buys effortlessly. A fight with Teofimo Lopez brings two huge American fanbases together for an absolute blockbuster. Those two events generate monster gates. Paro simply cannot generate that kind of revenue in the United States.

On top of the financial gap, Paro presents a terrible risk profile for Ryan. Paro is a tough southpaw with an awkward style who makes life miserable inside the ring. Taking on that kind of stylistic headache for a fraction of the money Ryan can make elsewhere is bad business. Fighters in Ryan’s tax bracket do not volunteer for difficult nights unless huge checks back it up.

Then you have the calendar reality. Ryan is not fighting four times a year. If he takes a marquee date in the spring, that eats up the first half of 2027. A massive fall date takes care of the rest. Between Teofimo, Haney, or other lucrative names floating around, 2027 fills up instantly.

Paro holding a title belt does not move the needle for Ryan either. Ryan transcended the need for sanctioning body belts long ago because his name alone drives the promotion.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Approval Leaves Meiirim Nursultanov Waiting
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames got the green light to take an interim bout before dealing with mandatory challenger Meiirim Nursultanov. The WBC approved a November 17 date above 160 pounds, but it includes a massive catch. If Adames loses, he loses his middleweight world title on the spot, even with the belt not officially on the line.

The WBC confirmed the ruling in an October 14 update. They left out the opponent, the venue, plus the exact weight limit. Because of that, nobody knows how tough this assignment will actually be.

Meiirim Nursultanov gets stuck waiting again. Holding the mandatory slot didn’t lock down his crack at the belt. Now he has to sit back, hoping Adames survives this detour so their scheduled clash can take place.

It puts Nursultanov in a weird spot. If Adames wins, Nursultanov still gets his shot at the active champion. If Adames stumbles, the title gets stripped, which leaves the top contender waiting on fresh orders for a vacant belt.

The WBC laid out clear terms. An Adames win routes him directly into the Nursultanov defense. Whoever walks away with the victory there has to face interim titlist Jesús Ramos Jr next.

There is a road map to clean up the division, but getting there takes three separate bouts. Every detour before the mandatory introduces the threat of an injury or an upset that blows up the entire schedule.

NEWS: Per sources, Carlos Adames’ @Zuffa_Boxing debut in a nontitle bout OK’d by the WBC is planned for November in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where Zuffa is planning a show in November & one in December (obviously depends on status of the war & unrest in the region). #boxing — Dan Rafael (@DanRafael1) October 15, 2026

That vacant title rule also creates a bizarre setup for whoever steps into the ring on November 17. If the opponent beats the middleweight champ, Adames loses the belt, yet the winner walks away empty-handed without claiming it. Anyone signing that contract needs to realize what a victory actually delivers.

Adames lands the flexibility he wanted, while Nursultanov collects yet another promise about future dates. Until the promotion names a foe, nobody can tell if Adames is taking a dangerous test or just booking a tune-up above middleweight. Either way, Nursultanov stays on the sidelines waiting for his turn.

It sends a terrible message when a sanctioning body lets a champion put their mandatory obligations on ice just to chase an untitle bout above the weight class.

The whole point of a mandatory challenger is that you earn the number one spot through actual ring results, not politics. Nursultanov did the work, secured the position, and now he is forced to sit on the shelf watching the champion go hunt for bigger money elsewhere.

Nursultanov is not getting compensated while Adames takes this detour. Time away from the ring burns prime years, brings zero purse money, and creates ring rust. If Adames gets hurt on November 17, the layoff stretches out even longer. If Adames loses, Nursultanov does not even get the satisfaction or the profile boost of taking down the sitting champion. He gets stuck in a vacant title match that generates far less fanfare and a smaller check.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Rules Out Saudi Arabia For Boots Fight
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the winner of Jaron Ennis against Josh Kelly next, but the WBC junior middleweight champion insists Saudi Arabia will not host it. Fundora aims for spring 2027 to stage a unification bout, making it clear that facing Boots will not convince him to travel abroad to Riyadh.

That stance sets a firm condition on his future plans before his title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj on Saturday. Fundora expects Ennis to defeat Kelly, calling Boots the premier matchup at 154 pounds.

“I think the winner of Boots and Kelly should be the opponent for our next fight,” Fundora said to Ariel Helwani. “I think that’s early, early maybe springtime of next year, 2027.” Asked whether that reflected discussions or simply his preference, Fundora clarified: “That’s what I want. I think that’s what I’ll get as well.”

His preferred schedule remains a target rather than a signed contract, yet his refusal regarding Saudi Arabia sounded absolute.

“There’s a reason why I haven’t fought in Saudi Arabia,” Fundora said. “I wouldn’t feel comfortable, me being an American and everything like that.”

Asked directly if he would turn down an Ennis bout in the Gulf nation, Fundora confirmed he would walk away because that option feels unrealistic to him.

Securing an Ennis encounter would require common ground on location alongside purses. If promoters propose Saudi Arabia, Fundora makes it obvious that organizers must secure an alternate venue to get his signature.

He has not turned down an active offer to box Ennis. The scenario remains hypothetical right now, even while his desire to face the Ennis vs. Kelly victor is genuine.

Fundora must handle business against Hadribeaj first. Once Saturday concludes, his focus centers on collecting the remaining belts at 154 pounds in an arena he can accept. His stance puts him in a tricky spot financially. Crossing Riyadh off the list immediately shrinks the money pool, because nobody in the United States or the UK is writing those blank checks right now.

“My mother being a veteran and all the politics and that. It’s bigger than boxing. It’s way bigger than boxing,” said Fundora.

If PBC or another promoter has to finance an Ennis against Fundora unification on regular domestic pay-per-view, the numbers have to make sense organically, and that means significantly smaller paydays for both men.

Boots wants the belts, but he also wants to get paid like an elite fighter. If Fundora demands the bout take place in Vegas or Los Angeles, Ennis might look at the revenue split and decide the headache is not worth the discount, especially when other opportunities exist.

None of it matters if he looks past Saturday, either. Hadribeaj is not flying in just to collect a check and hand over the belt. If Fundora gets sloppy or gets caught while daydreaming about spring 2027, the whole discussion vanishes overnight. He will have priced himself out of an imaginary payday while holding empty hands.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois’ Odd Preparations For His World Title Fight On Saturday
Sports.content:
As the WBO world title fight between Champion Daniel Dubois and Challenger and former WBO Champion Fabio Wardley in The O2 Arena in London, England approaches, it is interesting to observe how both fighters are preparing during fight week.

Both Dubois and Wardley are taking part in the usual media engagements this week to promote their fight. Other than that, Wardley is more low-key in his preparations. However, Dubois is attracting much more attention in the pre-fight buildup not just because he is the reigning WBO Champion, but also due to his rather strange pre-fight preparations.

In this regard, he went on a walkabout in Brixton, London, England, at the beginning of this week with his WBO belt. While it is admirable that Dubois is seen with people, and welcoming photos to be taken with him and well-wishers, he gives the impression that he is an all-conquering hero rather than a fighter preparing to defend his world title against a dangerous opponent. It would surely have been better for Dubois to delay his meet and greet until after he had actually beaten Wardley in Saturday’s fight.

Yet, this is not the first time that Daniel Dubois has done something peculiar in the week leading up to a world title fight. Who can forget his baffling presence at a party in the afternoon of his heavyweight world title clash against Oleksandr Usyk on 19 July last year at Wembley Stadium, London, England? On that occasion, some argued that Dubois allowed his focus to wander by attending this party, when it should have been squarely on making last-minute preparations for his fight against Usyk. They had a valid point, as Dubois ended up losing this fight by knockout in the 5th Round, and his IBF title in the process.

This opens up the debate about whether Dubois is taking Wardley’s challenge too lightly. In the buildup to Dubois v Wardley II, the WBO Champion has gone on record saying that beating Fabio Wardley on Saturday night will be easy. However, Wardley is right to say that if this is the case, Dubois would not have been knocked down twice in the early Rounds in their world title fight on 09 May.

Confidence is one thing. But complacency is a different thing altogether, and Dubois should be wary that he does not fall into this trap. To his credit, Wardley says that he has learned from the mistakes he made in his first fight with Dubois, and will correct them on Saturday. The Ipswich fighter is even honest enough to admit the punches, which earned him his two knockdowns of Dubois in the pair’s first fight, did not land completely accurately. Wardley argues that if they had done so, they would have caused more damage. Further, the video footage from this fight seems to bear this out.

We shall see on Saturday night whether Dubois has prepared correctly for the challenges Fabio Wardley brings. Will it be Repeat or Revenge? One thing for sure is that Daniel Dubois would be foolish to underestimate Wardley, who, like Dubois, has beaten convincingly a former World Champion. Wardley did so when he beat former WBO Champion Joseph Parker by TKO in the 11th Round on 25 October 2025 for the WBO interim heavyweight title.

Time will tell who will be the victor on Saturday night. It should be one helluva fight.

Romer Cherubim

Freelance journalist

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: Eduwatch calls for sex offenders’ register and mandatory background checks for teachers
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch (Eduwatch), Kofi Asare, has called on the Ghana Education Service (GES) to introduce standardised safeguarding procedures, a sex offenders’ register and mandatory criminal background checks for teachers to address what he describes as systemic gaps in handling misconduct allegations in schools.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Thursday, October 15, Mr Asare said the absence of consistent standard operating procedures (SOPs) had contributed to uneven responses to safeguarding concerns within the education system.

His comments come after the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, directed the Ghana Education Service to suspend the headmaster of the Obuasi Senior High Technical School over allegations of sexual misconduct.

The directive from the minister follows a media report suggesting the headmaster misconducted himself sexually against a female student of Obuasi SHTS in the Ashanti Region.

He cited the case of the former headmaster of Benkum Senior High School, who he said was interdicted following an unverified allegation by a student of inappropriate advances.

According to Mr Asare, the headmaster was not found guilty but was asked to step aside and transferred to ease tensions within the school after some teachers were perceived to have supported the complainant.

He argued that clearly defined procedures were necessary to ensure allegations were handled fairly, protecting students while safeguarding the rights of accused staff.

Mr Asare also questioned the handling of concerns surrounding the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School following violence at the institution about two months earlier.

He maintained that consistent procedures would have provided a clear framework for determining the appropriate administrative response, rather than leaving matters to emerge through investigative journalism.

Describing the situation as a systemic challenge, he said the GES needed to prioritise safeguarding and establish consistent processes for addressing allegations of misconduct.

READ ALSO: GES recommends reposting of Obuasi SHTS headmaster after August 2026 campus riot

The Eduwatch director further advocated a sex offenders’ register, arguing that such a system could help education authorities identify individuals with relevant histories.

He suggested that, had such a register existed, the Obuasi SHTS headmaster would have been recorded following an earlier case in Toase.

He also called for mandatory criminal background checks for prospective teachers, noting that several jurisdictions had adopted the practice and that Nigeria had begun introducing similar measures.

Mr Asare said Eduwatch had been calling for these reforms for years, stressing that stronger institutional safeguards were necessary to prevent misconduct and improve accountability in schools.

Ghana News.title: GloMeF CEO urges intensified public education on new road traffic regulations
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Global Media Foundation (GloMeF), Raphael Godlove, has called for intensified public education on the new Road Traffic Regulations 2026 (L.I. 2519).

The enforcement of L.I. 2519 introduced updated safety rules, automated enforcement, and stricter penalties for drivers, passengers, and pedestrians.

In an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA), Mr Ahenu noted that although laudable, a lack of public understanding of the new road traffic regulations would undermine its full implementation.

He said relying heavily on digital platforms for mass education would not be beneficial to many drivers, motorists and other road users, particularly those in rural communities.

Mr Ahenu called on the government, law enforcement agencies and relevant institutions to adopt a more inclusive and community-based approach in educating the public on the regulation to enhance compliance.

“We need face-to-face education, and the relevant authorities must go beyond social media and organise community engagements, public fora and directly sensitise the masses”, he suggested and called for collaboration among key stakeholders towards enforcing the Regulations.

He said strengthened collaboration between the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), transport unions, driver associations and road agencies and traditional authorities was required for an effective public education campaign on the regulations.

“Road traffic laws must not be understood only by people who have smartphones, internet access or the ability to follow discussions on social media”.

“In fact, a farmer at Yawsae and a commercial driver at a lorry station and a pedestrian in a rural settlement all deserve to understand the law”, he added.

The nation’s new road traffic framework comprises the Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1153), and the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519).

President John Dramani Mahama assented to the amendment on December 24, 2025, with Parliament approving the Regulations on May 28, 2026.

The framework introduces several changes to improve road safety, strengthen traffic enforcement, and promote discipline among road users.

Among the major reforms are automated traffic enforcement systems, including speed and red-light cameras, and a demerit point system linked to drivers' licenses.

It also pushes stricter penalties for serious traffic offences and a reduction in the permissible blood alcohol concentration for drivers from 0.08 to 0.05.

The regulations introduced new requirements for commercial transport operations, vehicle inspections, speed control, and the commercial use of motorcycles, tricycles, and quadricycles for passenger services.

Ghana News.title: ‘Any tax on ChatGPT is an attack on education and innovation’- Akim Swedru, MP
Ghana News.content:
Member of Parliament for Akim Swedru, Kennedy Osei Nyarko

The Member of Parliament for Akim Swedru, Kennedy Osei Nyarko, has opposed calls to introduce a tax on ChatGPT, arguing that such a move could undermine education and innovation.

In a post on Facebook, the legislator questioned the rationale behind abolishing the betting tax while considering a tax on ChatGPT, a widely used artificial intelligence tool for learning, research, and other productive activities.

“We cannot abolish the betting tax; rather, we should introduce a tax on ChatGPT, which is for education and innovation. Any tax on ChatGPT is an attack on education and innovation,” he wrote.

The MP's comments come amid public debate over the Ghana Revenue Authority's new digital VAT collection system, which takes effect on October 15, 2026.

The GRA has clarified that the new system does not introduce a new tax or increase the existing VAT rate. Rather, it is intended to improve the collection and accounting of taxes already applicable to digital services supplied by non-resident companies to consumers in Ghana.

The applicable effective tax rate remains 20%, comprising 15% VAT, a 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy (NHIL) and a 2.5% Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) Levy.

According to the GRA, approximately 92 non-resident digital service providers are currently registered and remitting VAT. Where the applicable taxes are already included in subscription prices, the introduction of the new collection system will not result in an additional charge on the same transaction.

However, the Authority has identified approximately 100 additional non-resident digital service providers that are not currently charging and remitting the applicable taxes. These providers will be progressively brought into the tax net.

However, the scope of the original digital tax measures should be distinguished from any specific proposal to impose a separate tax on ChatGPT. The applicable rules and rates may also have changed since 2022.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse scandal exposes systemic failure in child protection – Moving Masculinity
Ghana News.content:
Creator of Moving Masculinity, Esther Amarh, has described the alleged sexual abuse of female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School as evidence of a systemic failure in Ghana’s child protection system.

She says the failure of authorities to act on complaints against the suspended headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, until a media report by JoyNews raises serious questions about the effectiveness of systems meant to protect students from sexual harassment and abuse in schools.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Middaynews on Thursday, October 15, Ms Amarh called for collective outrage over what she described as a persistent failure to protect children, insisting that accountability must extend beyond the alleged perpetrator to officials who failed to respond to complaints.

“As a nation, we should be collectively outraged by this ongoing systemic failure to protect girls, children, and boys. This sexual abuse often happens to boys as well,” she said.

Her comments follow a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, which found that municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures had received reports about alleged sexual abuse involving female students months before Mr Abdulai’s suspension.

Ms Amarh said the fact that action appeared to follow public exposure rather than the initial complaints was particularly troubling.

“The only tool that these authorities paid attention to was national shame and exposure, not conscience, not morality, not the right of those girls to have an education, and not their own structures and systems,” she said.

She questioned the effectiveness of existing procedures for handling allegations of sexual harassment, assault, defilement and rape involving students, arguing that institutions must be held accountable when they fail to respond appropriately.

“There must be consequences, not just for what the teacher or the individual did. There must be consequences for inaction. There must be an audit done of exactly who did not do what,” she added.

She also proposed sanctions that could affect the salaries and promotion prospects of officials found to have neglected their duties, arguing that disciplinary measures must be strong enough to deter similar failures.

“I have worked on these issues for over seven, eight, nine years, and it is exactly the same scenario: a girl reports, inaction, silence, no action. It escalates, more girls, more lives ruined, more education interrupted,” she said.

Ms Amarh further urged Ghana to treat sexual abuse in schools as a national public health crisis rather than isolated incidents affecting individual students.

Ghana News.title: Hubtel CEO calls for national data-sharing framework to boost AI development
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of Hubtel, Alex Bram, has called for a national data-sharing framework that encourages companies to preserve and make data available under appropriate arrangements to support the development of artificial intelligence (AI) in Ghana.

He believes the absence of an effective system for sharing data between institutions remains a major obstacle to developing AI technologies locally, warning that investment in computing infrastructure alone will not be sufficient to drive Ghana's AI ambitions.

Mr. Bram wants the government to introduce incentives that encourage businesses to retain useful data rather than discard it, while establishing clear arrangements for how institutions can share information.

“At the least, we should have a data framework that will sort of call on companies to actually not delete data, but store them, and have a framework for incentivising companies to store data,” he said.

He explained that Ghana's planned national AI compute centre would require substantial amounts of data to support the development and training of AI systems.

“Because at some point when we finish the AI data centres, we will need a lot of data. But it's a step in the right direction,” he added.

Speaking in an interview ahead of the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum, Mr. Bram drew on Hubtel's experience developing its own artificial intelligence systems to explain why the country must prioritise data availability alongside investment in computing infrastructure.

The opportunities and challenges associated with AI adoption will form part of discussions at the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum, under the theme “AI and the Ghana Economy: Opportunity or Disruption?”

The forum, held in partnership with Hubtel, will feature the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George; Economist and Technical Advisor at the Finance Ministry, Dr Theo Acheampong; Founder of AI for Ghana, Adam Watkins; Head of Engineering at Hubtel, Augustine Adjei; and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons.

It will air live on JoyNews and Joy 99.7 FM on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 8 p.m.

Hubtel's struggle to access data

Mr. Bram revealed that Hubtel established an AI laboratory in 2023 after beginning experiments with the technology in 2022.

The company initially sought to develop its own AI models using machine learning and neural network technologies, working with other businesses to test some of the systems it had developed.

However, the company encountered difficulties obtaining sufficient data to improve the performance of its models.

According to Mr. Bram, Hubtel approached several large companies to explore opportunities for sharing data but discovered that there were no clear arrangements governing how such exchanges should take place.

“At a point, we tried to connect with other large companies to see if they can give us, they can share data with us, we can share some of our data with them,” he explained.

“We realised there's still no framework in Ghana for sharing data. And so some of them were like, do we sign NDAs? Do we copy our data in Excel and give it to you? Do we have an agreement to share the data, and how do we even share it? There's just no framework.”

He said the uncertainty made companies reluctant to share information, limiting Hubtel's ability to obtain the data required to improve its AI models.

https://youtu.be/bfzoN-r37CE?t=3

“We just found that in Ghana it wasn't. So there weren't that many companies willing to share data with us to improve. So it became another obstacle that didn't really help our success,” he said.

Mr. Bram contrasted Ghana's situation with developments in the United States, China and parts of Europe, where he believes established data-sharing arrangements have contributed to the advancement of artificial intelligence.

He argued that Ghana must learn from these experiences by creating conditions that allow local technology companies to access useful data through structured arrangements.

Data critical to Ghana's AI compute centre

The Hubtel CEO welcomed the government's plans to establish a national AI compute centre, but maintained that the investment would achieve limited results without sufficient data to support the development of AI applications.

He described the proposed facility as an important step towards positioning Ghana in the global AI economy, while urging policymakers to accelerate the development of the supporting systems.

“So that data framework is important. If that AI compute centre is to succeed, because when a computer centre is there, without the data, it's nothing,” he stressed.

Asked whether the data-sharing framework should be established even before the physical computing infrastructure is completed, Mr. Bram agreed.

“Yes, yes. I think we need that. I think at the least, if not maybe enforcing it on private companies, I think at least we can enforce it with the government institution. Because AI is just data,” he explained.

His position suggests that government institutions could take an early lead in establishing clearer arrangements for retaining and sharing data, while incentives encourage private companies to participate.

Mr. Bram believes such a framework could have significantly improved Hubtel's own AI development efforts.

“We will need that. If we had that, I'm sure our AI lab would have been a success. But we didn't have that,” he said.

Protecting personal and commercially sensitive data

While expanding data availability could accelerate AI development, it also raises questions about how personal information and commercially sensitive records would be protected.

A national data-sharing framework would need to establish clear rules governing which information can be shared, who can access it, how it can be used and what safeguards are required to prevent misuse.

Such arrangements would be particularly important where information contains customers' personal details, financial transactions, confidential business records or other sensitive material.

The retention of data would also need to be distinguished from permission to share or use it for AI training. Preserving information does not automatically authorise its disclosure to third parties.

Ghana News.title: Twelve Golden Rules of real estate development in Ghana, Africa
Ghana News.content:
By Dr Prince-Joseph M. K. Ayiku

Real estate development is one of Africa's greatest opportunities for economic growth and wealth creation. With a young population, rapidly expanding cities, and rising demand for quality housing, commercial, industrial and mixed-use properties, the potential is enormous.

However, success requires far more than buying land and constructing buildings. Many projects fail because developers start building before resolving fundamental issues.

True success demands the right location, quality materials, careful research, secure title, sound financing, and disciplined execution. These twelve golden rules provide a practical blueprint from land acquisition to construction, sales and long-term estate management.

Rule 1: Choose the Right Location

The value of a property begins with where it stands. A beautiful building in the wrong location will struggle, while a well-planned property in the right location will enjoy strong demand and lasting value.

Location determines accessibility, rental income, security, resale value and future growth. Developers must assess access to roads and transport, proximity to schools, hospitals and markets, availability of water, power and internet, security, environmental risks like flooding, population growth, and planning restrictions.

A location must not be judged only by its present state, but by how it will develop in the next 10 to 20 years with new roads, hospitals and commercial centres.

Rule 2: Build With Quality Materials and Workmanship

Quality may cost more today, but poor construction will cost much more tomorrow. Quality is the foundation of a developer's reputation.

Developers must use durable, standards-approved materials and engage skilled, qualified professionals to supervise every stage. Cheap materials cause cracks, leakages, electrical faults and structural failure.

Quality control must cover soil testing and foundations, concrete and steel, roofing and waterproofing, plumbing, electricals, doors and windows, finishes, roads and gutters and fire safety. Every stage should be inspected before the next begins.

Never secretly reduce specifications to increase profit. Every completed property is a public .

Rule 3: Conduct Proper Market Research

Do not build what you want to sell. Build what the market wants to buy. Every project must satisfy a real, measurable need. Developers must not rely on personal excitement.

Research must answer: Who is the buyer? What property type do they need? What price can they afford? What features and payment terms do they want? How fast are competing properties selling? Is demand from residents, investors, or diaspora? An excellent property that does not match the market will not sell. Research must guide location, design, size, price and payment terms before major funds are committed.

Rule 4: Secure the Land Before Investing

A building is only as secure as the title beneath it. Land is the foundation of every project, and land administration remains a major challenge in Africa, with multiple sales, unclear boundaries, family disputes and forged documents.

Developers must conduct full legal and technical investigations before purchase, verifying the seller's identity and authority, ownership history, boundaries, existing mortgages or court disputes, approved land use, rights of way, and family or traditional interests.

Qualified lawyers and licensed surveyors must be involved from the start, with searches at the lands commission and traditional authorities. No large payments should be made before ownership is confirmed, and every agreement must be documented.

Rule 5: Respect Planning Laws and the Environment

Responsible development works with the environment, not against it. Developers must obtain all necessary approvals - planning permission, building permits, environmental and fire clearances - before construction. Wetlands, waterways, flood plains and protected areas must be respected. Building in unsuitable locations causes flooding, damage, and loss of life. Responsible development must preserve natural drainage, provide proper stormwater systems, and consider waste management, sanitation, landscaping and energy use. Compliance protects the investment, the environment and the occupants.

Rule 6: Prepare a Complete Feasibility Study

Before breaking ground, make certain that the figures can carry the project. Every proposal must be tested financially. A professional feasibility study must estimate land and legal costs, design fees, construction and infrastructure costs, financing and interest, taxes and permits, marketing and administrative costs, contingencies, expected sales income, completion period, and profit margin.

Developers must test what happens if material costs rise, sales slow down, or interest rates increase. Expected sales are not guaranteed cash. Profitability and cash flow must be examined separately, as a profitable project can still collapse from cash shortages.

Rule 7: Protect Cash Flow and Control Costs

Profit is important, but cash keeps the project moving. Cash flow is the lifeblood of development. Developers must prepare detailed budgets and monthly cash flow forecasts, matching customer deposits, loans and sales proceeds against expenses.

Project funds must be separated from personal spending. Customer deposits must be used responsibly for their intended projects. Strong controls must cover procurement, materials inventory, contractor payments, payroll, variations, receipts, loans and taxes. Management must compare actual spending against budget monthly and identify overruns early.

Rule 8: Deliver Infrastructure, Not Only Buildings

A house becomes a home when the surrounding community works. Successful communities need more than buildings. Buyers expect roads, drainage, water, electricity, security, waste services, street lighting and internet, plus schools, shops and recreation.

Infrastructure costs must be included in the budget from the beginning, not as an afterthought. Where public infrastructure is limited, developers need partnerships with utility providers and local authorities. A developer who builds buildings completes a project; a developer who provides infrastructure creates a functioning community.

Rule 9: Put the Customer at the Centre

A property sale may happen once, but a customer's experience lasts for years. The customer is the reason the project exists. Marketing must be truthful, with clear prices, specifications, payment terms and completion dates.

Developers must avoid unfulfillable promises and communicate early and honestly when delays occur. A clear customer service process should cover enquiries, reservations, payments, progress reports, inspections, handover, defect reporting and after-sales support. Satisfied customers become ambassadors.

Rule 10: Build a Competent and Accountable Team

Strong buildings come from skilled hands, clear leadership and honest supervision. No developer can succeed alone. The team may include architects, engineers, surveyors, lawyers, accountants, marketers and contractors. Every person must have a clear role and measurable responsibility.

Contractors should be selected not just on price, but on experience, financial strength, safety and reliability. Every appointment must have a written contract defining work, price, timeline and quality. Leaders must promote honesty and eliminate bribery, inflated invoices and material theft.

Rule 11: Manage Risks and Prepare for Change

The best developer does not ignore risk; the best developer prepares for it. Every project faces risks including land disputes, construction delays, rising material prices, currency and interest rate movements, weak demand, contractor failure, flooding, policy changes and safety incidents. Each project should have a risk register identifying each risk, its impact, responsible person and response plan. Suitable insurance must protect workers, buildings and third parties. Risk management does not remove all problems, but helps respond quickly and reduce losses.

Rule 12: Develop for Profit, People, and Posterity

The greatest developments do not only occupy land; they improve lives and create legacies. Profit is necessary for survival, but development carries wider responsibility. Every project affects traffic, drainage, employment, services and community life.

Developers should create safe, attractive, inclusive places that consider children, older people and persons with disabilities, offer fair opportunities to local workers, engage communities respectfully, and plan for long-term maintenance of roads, drains, parks and common areas.

The most respected developers are remembered not just for buildings completed, but for communities created.

In conclusion, Africa does not simply need more buildings. It needs quality developments in the right locations that endure, create value and support human progress.

Dr. Prince-Joseph M. K. Ayiku, the writer

Ghana News.title: Five new telephony cell sites in Ashanti Region to be activated in October 2026 – Sam George
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, Samuel Nartey George, has announced that five new telecommunications sites in the Ashanti Region are expected to be activated by the end of October 2026.

He also disclosed plans to extend telecommunications services to three additional communities in the Sekyere Afram Plains District, directing the Ghana Investment Fund for Electronic Communications (GIFEC) and its contractors to accelerate work to improve connectivity in the area.

Mr George announced this during an inspection of four Rural Telephony Project sites at Nyameama No. 1, Nyameama No. 2, Dawia and Abenua in the Sekyere Afram Plains District.

The tour was intended to assess construction progress, identify implementation challenges and ensure the timely completion of outstanding works.

The Minister said the Rural Telephony Project was designed to bridge the digital divide by extending network coverage to communities that mainstream telecommunications operators might consider commercially unviable.

He noted that communities in the Sekyere Afram Plains District were among those prioritised for improved network coverage.

He commended the area’s Member of Parliament for advocating better telecommunications services and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to addressing connectivity gaps across the country.

Mr George also disclosed that the government was collaborating with MTN Ghana to deploy 800 additional telecommunications sites nationwide.

He stressed the need to upgrade existing rural networks from 3G to 4G, warning that expanding digital services in urban centres without corresponding improvements in rural communities could widen the digital divide as Ghana moved towards broader 5G deployment.

The Minister further announced plans to conduct a comprehensive audit of all Rural Telephony Project sites inherited by the current administration.

The exercise will establish the actual completion status of the sites and verify whether facilities reported as operational are actively providing network services.

He urged traditional authorities and residents to protect the installed equipment against vandalism to prevent service disruptions.

The District Chief Executive for Sekyere Afram Plains, Abubakar Issaka, commended the Minister for prioritising the district’s connectivity needs and pledged the Assembly’s support in protecting and maintaining the facilities.

The inspection formed part of the Minister’s ongoing efforts to monitor rural telecommunications projects, address implementation challenges and extend reliable digital connectivity to underserved communities.

Mr George was accompanied by Mr Issaka, GIFEC Administrator Rashid Tanko and officials from the Ministry and GIFEC.

Ghana News.title: Mahama cuts sod for Afienya Industrial Park, targets 120 enterprises
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has cut the sod for the construction of the Afienya Industrial Park, a major industrial development expected to accommodate more than 120 enterprises and create jobs as part of the government’s efforts to position Ghana as a manufacturing and logistics hub for West Africa.

The 1,238-acre industrial park is expected to provide businesses with serviced plots, ready-to-use factory shells and essential infrastructure, including electricity, water, roads, drainage, waste treatment facilities and security.

Speaking at the sod-cutting ceremony, President Mahama said the project responds to growing investor interest in Ghana and the need to provide space and infrastructure for businesses to establish factories and expand production.

“When the Ghana Free Zones Authority informed me that the Tema Export Processing Zone had no space left to allocate to interested industries, it was an encouraging sign of investor interest in Ghana's economic progress,” he said.

He added that the government has a responsibility to ensure that the growing interest translates into factories, jobs and increased exports.

“Today, we take an important step towards fulfilling our commitment to make Ghana a manufacturing and logistics hub for the West African sub-region,” President Mahama stated.

The President said the Afienya Industrial Park will address some of the challenges investors face in acquiring land and setting up businesses, particularly disputes over land ownership and the cost of providing essential services.

He assured investors that the new industrial enclave would offer litigation-free land and the necessary infrastructure to facilitate the establishment of factories.

“You come, the land is litigation-free, the services will be available, and we will bring the power, the water, the waste treatment plants, security, roads, everything here,” he said.

“All you need is to come, build your factory, bring your machines, and start to produce.”

President Mahama said the project would receive infrastructure financing support under the government’s proposed $10 billion New Economy Programme, which is expected to invest $2 billion annually over four years in productive sectors of the economy.

He said half of the planned investment would go into agriculture and agro-processing, with the remainder supporting industry and infrastructure linking producers to markets.

“The New Economy Programme will assist the Free Zones Authority to provide these facilities for the Afienya enclave,” he said, adding that the full framework would be presented to Parliament in the 2027 Budget.

The President said the industrial park’s location along the Eastern Corridor Road, its proximity to the Port of Tema and the Tema-Mpakadan standard-gauge railway line would give businesses a strategic advantage in transporting raw materials and finished products to domestic, regional and international markets.

Priority investment areas include cocoa, cashew and oil palm processing, textiles and garments, pharmaceuticals, medical consumables, automotive components and assembly, and light engineering. The park is also expected to create opportunities in logistics, data services, business process outsourcing, renewable energy and green manufacturing.

President Mahama stressed that the benefits of the project must extend beyond businesses operating within the industrial park to surrounding communities, including Afienya.

He called for local farmers, transport operators, suppliers and small businesses to be integrated into the supply chains of companies that establish operations there.

“I believe that if enterprises are located here, there should be a programme that trains the local people so that they can get some of the jobs created in this industrial park,” he said.

President Mahama said the Afienya Industrial Park should build on the experience of the Tema Export Processing Zone by strengthening local industrial production, creating sustainable employment and expanding Ghana’s export capacity.

“Establish your businesses here, develop your products here, and use Ghana as the launching pad to reach customers across Africa and beyond,” he urged investors.

He expressed confidence that the private sector would respond to the opportunities created by the project, adding that the ultimate measure of success would be operational businesses, employment for Ghanaians and products reaching wider African markets.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
