World.title: Police arrest four over missing human heads, suspected ritual hands in Kwara
World.content:
The police in Kwara State have arrested four men in connection with two separate incidents involving the alleged removal of human heads from graves and possession of suspected human hands for alleged money-making rituals.

The Commissioner of Police in the state, Adekimi Ojo, disclosed this while briefing journalists at the command headquarters in Ilorin.

In the first incident, two suspects, Abu Jimoh and Ayo Jimoh, were arrested over the alleged exhumation of graves and removal of heads from buried bodies at a cemetery in Omupo, Kwara State.

Mr Ojo said the investigation began in May 2026 after residents visiting the cemetery to bury a deceased person discovered that some graves had been disturbed and the heads of the bodies buried there were missing.

He said police operatives arrested the two suspects at about 5 a.m. on 8 October while they were allegedly digging graves at the cemetery.

According to the commissioner, the suspects reportedly confessed to the crime during interrogation and identified a herbalist, Mukaila Bello, as the alleged buyer of the missing human heads.

Police said investigations were ongoing and that they would arraign the suspects after the investigation concluded. The information provided did not establish whether police had arrested Mr Bello.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a separate incident, police arrested two other men, Kamalden Lukmon and AbdulGaniyu Ibrahim, after recovering two suspected human hands during an operation along Bakase Road in Alapa, Kwara State.

The arrests were made around 4 p.m. on 8 October.

Mr Ojo said preliminary interrogation indicated that the suspects intended to use the body parts for money-making rituals.

“During preliminary interrogation, the suspects stated that they intended to use the body parts for money-making rituals,” he said.

The suspects reportedly told investigators that a vigilante member, identified as Abdulrauf Apata, had handed the suspected human hands to them.

The commissioner said the allegation against Mr Apata was being investigated to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine whether other people were involved.

Mr Lukmon and Mr Ibrahim were being held at the command’s Violent Crimes Response Unit as investigators worked to establish the origin of the body parts and identify any possible victim.

The police urged residents to provide credible information to security agencies to support investigations and help prevent crime.

World.title: Reps advance bill to establish renewable energy authority
World.content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has passed the Electricity Act (Amendment) Bill, 2025, for second reading, setting the stage for further legislative consideration of a proposed National Authority for Renewable Energy (NARE).

The bill, sponsored by Afam Victor Ogene, member representing Ogbaru Federal Constituency, Anambra State, and Chairman of the House Committee on Renewable Energy, seeks to consolidate renewable energy regulatory functions currently spread across different government agencies under a dedicated authority.

Leading the debate, Ogene said the proposed legislation would address structural gaps in the power sector by transferring relevant renewable energy functions from the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), the Rural Electrification Agency (REA) and the Rural Electrification Fund (REF) to the proposed authority.

“This specialisation will improve coordination, reduce institutional overlaps and provide focused direction for the effective development of the renewable energy sector,” he said.

The lawmaker argued that Nigeria needed to look beyond expanding the national electricity grid to tackle persistent electricity access challenges, particularly in rural and underserved communities.

“We must embrace innovative, decentralised and renewable energy solutions that can reach communities and businesses more efficiently,” Ogene said.

Under the proposed legislation, NARE would regulate and supervise renewable energy development, promote mini-grid and off-grid electricity systems, and expand access to electricity in rural, unserved and underserved communities, including island communities.

The bill also seeks to encourage investment in the renewable energy sector through financial, fiscal and regulatory incentives designed to promote local manufacturing, research, innovation and capacity building.

It provides for the development of renewable energy sources, including solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass and hydrogen, as part of efforts to diversify Nigeria’s energy mix.

Other proposed responsibilities of the authority include issuing licences, establishing standards, ensuring fair tariffs and resolving disputes in the renewable energy market to strengthen consumer protection and transparency.

The proposed authority would also collaborate with NERC and the Federal Ministry of Finance to facilitate effective grid integration and harmonise renewable energy policies.

A key provision proposes allocating 40 per cent of the annual funds of the Rural Electrification Fund to NARE to finance renewable energy development.

The proposed funding arrangement is intended to support the authority’s operations and expand the deployment of renewable energy solutions across the country.

Following deliberations, the House unanimously adopted the bill for second reading and referred it to the relevant committee for further legislative scrutiny.

The committee is expected to examine the bill’s provisions, including the proposed transfer of personnel, assets and ongoing projects from existing agencies to the new authority.

World.title: Martinez’s comments reflect ‘circus’ at Man Utd — Roy Keane
World.content:
Keane

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane says Lisandro Martinez’s public criticism of the club’s hierarchy reflects the “chaos” surrounding the Premier League side.

According to the BBC, Keane described United as being “like a bit of a circus” following Martinez’s comments about the club’s failure to strengthen its squad during the summer transfer window.

Martinez spoke out after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday, criticising the club’s recruitment and demanding more from its leadership.

The Argentine defender said he expected more from director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy following United’s qualification for the Champions League.

Speaking on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast, Keane questioned the timing of Martinez’s remarks, particularly given the defender’s own performances and United’s difficult run.

“There will be some fans saying it’s great and some saying you’re letting the team down, especially from a player who hasn’t been at his best, when the team is struggling,” Keane said.

He added that the club appeared divided and criticised the atmosphere surrounding United.

“They’re obviously not together. It is chaotic there from the top to the bottom. We go there on match days and I don’t like the feeling around the club,” Keane said.

He continued: “I think as a reflection of the club, it’s obviously chaos there, like a bit of a circus.”

Keane also questioned players who publicly criticise their clubs during difficult periods, arguing that they should first examine their own performances.

“When you’re going through a difficult spell like United are, the issue I have with certain players saying things is you always have to start with the man in the mirror before you start coming out with all these comments,” he said.

Martinez later said on social media on Wednesday that he had spoken out of “anger and frustration”.

The 28-year-old’s contract expires at the end of the season, although United have the option to extend it by another year.

Keane also cast doubt on Martinez’s standing within the squad, saying he did not regard the defender as a senior figure at Manchester United.

“I don’t think it will be a big falling-out – because I think we have question marks over this dressing room anyway,” he said.

“I don’t think there’s enough characters – enough men in there – but I don’t see him as a senior player at Manchester United. I see him as a centre-half who’s making lots of mistakes.”

Former United defender Gary Neville also criticised Martinez’s remarks, arguing that they could be interpreted as an attack on his teammates.

Neville said senior players, including Harry Maguire and Bruno Fernandes, would have reason to be angry because Martinez’s comments suggested the squad needed more players.

United will travel to Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday.

World.title: Four feared dead, many injured as fuel tanker explodes in Edo
World.content:
FILE IMAGE to illustrate incident

By Ozioruva Aliu, Beni City

Tragedy struck in Oluku, Ovia Noth East local government area around the Benin-Lagos Highway on Thursday as a tanker laden with petrol exploded in the afternoon, consuming four people, including military personnel, while several persons suffered various degrees of injuries and burns.

Several vehicles were burnt in the fire incident, while a market in the area belonging to a popular businessman, Chief Osamede Adun, popularly called Bob Izua, also got burnt.

The tanker was said to have fallen on the road, and people were scooping fuel.

Witnesses said the tanker fell at about 7:30am, and residents rushed to scoop fuel into their houses.

The witness, who owns a shop opposite the scene of the incident, said efforts by security agencies to stop residents from scooping fuel failed.

“It was as they were scooping fuel that the fire started. It spread to the Bob Izua market along the road.

“Many cars were affected in the incident because the fire spread quickly. We have counted four persons that died. One soldier is among the dead.”

Ten burnt persons were reportedly rushed to the University of Benin Teaching Hospital after suffering severe burns.

A victim who did not want his name mentioned said, “I was also among those who were scooping the fuel. I escaped with whiskers. It was a soldier who called me and drew my attention to the fact that it was sunny and way the people rushed to scoop the fuel might ignite fire.

“As I looked back after he spoke to me, the tanker busted into flames as people around the area ran for dear lives. I thank the soldier; if not, I would have been burnt by now.

“Two men from the northern part who were directly under the tanker were burnt, while stores that were built on the drainage were burnt. The store was also burnt down, as we are yet to know the number of people that died. However, 10 people were rushed to the emergency unit of the UBTH.

The UBTH, the management swiftly mobilised emergency services, treating those that were brought to the hospital.

The Chief Medical Director of UBTH, Prof. Idia Ize-Iyamu, took charge of the emergency effort, leading the response team across the accident, emergency, and burns units to stabilise severe casualties and minimise fatalities.

World.title: Intersociety claims 7,500 Christians killed in Africa
World.content:
Alleges Nigeria accounts for 4,300 deaths in nine months

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety) has claimed that about 7,500 Christians were killed in attacks across several African countries between January and October 10, 2026, alleging that Nigeria accounted for approximately 4,300 of the deaths.

The group also claimed that thousands of Christians were abducted and more than 1,000 churches were destroyed or burnt across the affected countries during the period.

In a statement, Intersociety Chairman, Emeka Umeagbalasi, said the figures were based on the organisation’s findings on attacks against Christian communities in Nigeria and other African countries.

The figures and allegations could not be independently verified.

Umeagbalasi claimed that the Democratic Republic of Congo recorded about 2,000 deaths, while Nigeria accounted for between 3,426 and 4,300 Christian deaths in the period under review. He attributed a further 1,100 deaths to Mozambique, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Burkina Faso and other countries.

He also alleged that 3,395 Christians were abducted in Nigeria during the period covered by the group’s report.

According to him, 343 Christian deaths were recorded between September 1 and October 10, 2026, including 130 in Plateau State and 64 in Adamawa State.

He further claimed that 202 people were abducted, 10 churches destroyed, eight pastors abducted and two pastors killed during the period.

The group also raised concerns about the reported captivity of 150 Christian schoolchildren, whom it said had been held by Boko Haram since May 2026, and alleged that Christian communities in Kebbi State had faced threats to convert to Islam or risk being killed.

Nigeria, DRC figures

Umeagbalasi claimed that Nigeria had recorded an estimated 19,810 churches attacked or destroyed since the Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009.

He also put the cumulative number of Christian deaths at about 130,893 and the number of abducted Christians at 82,805.

The figures were presented as Intersociety’s estimates and were not independently verified.

The group alleged that attacks against Christians, their homes, farmlands, places of worship and livelihoods were being sustained by both state and non-state actors. It also accused successive Nigerian governments since 2015 of complicity in the attacks, an allegation that was not substantiated with independently verified evidence in the statement.

On the Democratic Republic of Congo, Umeagbalasi said the country had recorded an estimated 2,000 Christian deaths between January 1 and October 10, 2026.

He attributed several attacks to the Islamic State-affiliated Allied Democratic Forces and the Islamic State Central Africa Province.

Among the incidents cited were an attack on a gold mine on March 11, which he said killed 17 Christians; a raid in Beni in June, in which he claimed more than 20 Christians were killed; and a reported fire outbreak on September 10 that allegedly killed 27 children associated with Our Lady of Mercy Catholic Parish in the Bukavu region.

These accounts and casualty figures were not independently verified.

Other African countries

The group also alleged that Islamic State-linked militants carried out attacks against Christian communities in Mozambique, particularly in Cabo Delgado Province, forcing residents to flee their homes.

It cited a reported attack on September 6, 2026, in which Christians were allegedly killed or abducted in Cabo Delgado, followed by an attack in neighbouring Niassa Province in which a Catholic church was reportedly burnt.

In discussing Sudan and South Sudan, Umeagbalasi alleged that Christian communities had faced attacks, abductions and restrictions on religious activities. He also cited alleged attacks in Kenya, Ethiopia, Burkina Faso and Uganda, which he attributed to groups including Al-Shabaab, Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Islamic State-linked factions.

The group estimated that attacks in countries other than Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of Congo accounted for at least 1,100 Christian deaths during the period.

Allegations in Abia

In Nigeria, Intersociety raised concerns about alleged criminal activity in parts of Umunneochi Local Government Area of Abia State.

Umeagbalasi claimed that 28 human skulls and bones were discovered in the area on September 26, 2026, suggesting they could belong to travellers, farmers and other road users. The identities of the remains and the circumstances surrounding their discovery were not established in the statement.

He also referred to alleged abduction camps and previous security operations in the area, including the reported abduction of Methodist Church Prelate Samuel Kanu-Uche and two other clerics in May 2022.

The group called for further action by relevant authorities to address insecurity and investigate reported attacks and disappearances.

The allegations contained in the report, including claims of official complicity and the attribution of specific attacks to particular groups, were not independently established in the statement. Intersociety’s casualty estimates and other claims require independent verification.

World.title: Super Falcons captain Rasheedat Ajibade suffers ankle fracture
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Super Falcons captain Rasheedat Ajibade is facing at least three months on the sidelines after suffering a fracture to her right ankle during Nigeria’s 5-0 victory over Comoros in the 2028 Olympic Games qualifiers on Tuesday, according to ESPN.

The Paris Saint-Germain forward sustained the injury in the first half of Tuesday’s second-leg encounter at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, Ogun State, after a collision with Comoros defender Diore Miriame Kaina Said.

Ajibade landed heavily on her right foot and was unable to continue, leaving the pitch on a stretcher before being replaced by Folashade Ijamilusi.

According to ESPN, an MRI scan at the hospital confirmed the fracture, with the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) saying the captain would undergo surgery in Paris on Friday.

“The MRI showed that she suffered a fracture on her ankle and she saw a surgeon here immediately after,” NFF head of communications Ademola Olajire told ESPN.

“But because of her flight back to Paris, she couldn’t wait and I spoke to our team doctor and we understand she’ll be having surgery on Friday in Paris.”

Olajire said further updates on the extent of the injury and Ajibade’s recovery would follow after surgery and an assessment by PSG’s medical team.

The injury is a major setback for both Nigeria and PSG, with the forward potentially missing several UEFA Women’s Champions League matches and Nigeria’s November international fixtures.

Her availability for the Super Falcons’ third-round Olympic qualifier against Morocco in March 2027 could depend on her recovery.

Despite the setback, Ajibade reassured supporters that she remained positive about her recovery.

“I’m fine and doing well. I’ll be back stronger, for good and for God’s greater glory,” she wrote in a message on her WhatsApp status.

“Thank you so much for all your calls and messages. I’m sorry I can’t reply to everyone right now, but once I settle in, I’ll get back to each of you.

“I see all your messages, your love and your kind wishes. Thank you, thank you, thank you! God bless you all.”

Ajibade’s injury overshadowed Nigeria’s emphatic victory over Comoros, which secured a 7-0 aggregate win and passage into the third round of the 2028 Olympic qualifiers. Toni Payne and Uchenna Kanu each scored twice, while Christy Ucheibe converted a penalty as the Super Falcons produced a four-goal second-half surge to complete the victory.

Nigeria had taken a 2-0 advantage from the first leg and will now face Morocco in a two-legged encounter scheduled for March 2027.

The Super Falcons are seeking to qualify for a second consecutive Olympic Games appearance after ending a 16-year absence by reaching the Paris 2024 tournament.

Ajibade captained Nigeria to a record-extending 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in 2025 and remains one of the team’s most experienced players.

The 26-year-old joined PSG from Atletico Madrid in 2025 on a contract running until June 2027, making the injury a significant disruption to her first full season with the French club.

World.title: NCC phone approval USSD code: How to check if your phone is approved in Nigeria
World.content:
The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) phone approval USSD code is *315#, which Nigerians can dial to check whether their mobile phones and other eligible devices are approved and verified for use on local telecommunications networks.

The service, known as the NCC Device Checker, allows consumers to verify a device’s status before purchasing it, particularly when buying a second-hand phone or a smartphone imported from abroad.

Users can also check their devices through the Commission’s official website at www.ncc.gov.ng/devicechecker.

The initiative forms part of the NCC’s strengthened Type Approval Compliance framework, which took effect on October 7, 2026, to improve device compliance, protect consumers and safeguard Nigeria’s telecommunications networks.

How to Check Your Phone’s NCC Approval Status

Nigerians can follow these steps to check whether their phones are approved for use on local mobile networks:

Open the phone’s dialler. Dial *315# using the device you want to check. Follow the prompts displayed by the NCC Device Checker. Review the result to confirm whether the device is type-approved and verified for use on Nigerian mobile networks.

If you want to check a different device, the system may request its 15-digit International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number. To find the IMEI of most mobile phones, dial *#06#. You can also find it in the phone’s settings or on its original packaging.

Consumers can alternatively visit the NCC’s official Device Checker portal to verify their devices online.

What Is the NCC Phone Approval Code Used For?

The *315# USSD code helps consumers determine whether a SIM-enabled device has received the required NCC type approval and whether the particular device is verified for use on Nigerian mobile networks.

Type approval is a regulatory requirement designed to ensure that communications equipment meets applicable technical standards before it is sold or used in Nigeria.

The Device Checker covers eligible devices that connect to mobile networks, including smartphones, feature phones, cellular tablets, modems, SIM-enabled laptops and Point of Sale (POS) terminals.

The service is also intended to help consumers avoid counterfeit, cloned or non-compliant devices that could pose quality, security or network-integrity concerns.

Will the NCC Disconnect Phones That Are Not Approved?

The NCC’s strengthened compliance framework requires applicable devices to meet its type-approval and verification requirements. Devices confirmed to be non-compliant, including counterfeit devices, may be denied access to Nigerian mobile networks.

However, a failed or incomplete verification does not automatically establish that a phone is counterfeit. Users who receive an unsuccessful result should follow the official instructions and contact their seller, mobile network operator or the NCC for clarification.

According to the Commission, phones already connected to Nigerian mobile networks before the framework took effect on October 7, 2026, were automatically verified, meaning their owners do not need to take additional action under the initial process.

Consumers who already own a phone and receive a compliance warning should therefore verify the device’s status and seek assistance before making decisions about replacing it.

Do You Need to Check a Phone Bought in Nigeria?

The NCC advises consumers to check a device before paying for it, including when purchasing a brand-new or second-hand phone.

Although businesses responsible for manufacturing, importing and supplying devices must meet the applicable approval requirements, buyers can use the Device Checker to confirm a phone’s status before completing a transaction.

People purchasing phones from local retailers are not generally expected to obtain type approval themselves. However, they should ask sellers to confirm compliance and verify the device where necessary.

For phones personally imported from abroad, additional verification procedures may apply. The NCC advises affected users to contact the Commission for guidance on the applicable process.

What Should You Do if Your Phone Is Not Verified?

If the NCC Device Checker does not confirm your phone’s approval and verification status, do not immediately assume that the device is fake.

Instead, follow the instructions displayed by the service and contact your phone seller or mobile network provider for assistance. You can also call the NCC’s toll-free Device Checker support number, 315, or contact the Commission through its official support channels.

The NCC also cautions consumers against verification scams. Use only the official USSD code or Device Checker website, and never disclose a one-time verification code to a caller, seller or other third party.

In summary, Nigerians can dial *315# to check their phone’s NCC approval status, use the online Device Checker at ncc.gov.ng/devicechecker, or call 315 for assistance.

Vanguard News

World.title: Imo APC primaries: Group urges aspirants to resolve dispute
World.content:
By Dennis Agbo

A political group, Democracy Alliance (DA), has urged aspirants seeking the All Progressives Congress (APC) tickets for Imo West and Imo North senatorial districts to resolve their differences through the party’s established channels ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The group also called on political actors involved in the dispute to avoid actions or statements that could heighten tensions and distract the party from preparations for the elections.

DA made its position known in a statement jointly signed by its Chairman, Dr Ejiro Ernest, and Secretary, Dare Adu, in reaction to the controversy surrounding the APC senatorial primaries in the two districts.

According to the statement made available to journalists on Wednesday, the group urged the aspirants to work towards resolving their differences and strengthening the party’s electoral preparations.

It also appealed to those involved in the dispute to avoid making unsubstantiated claims about the APC Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Ben Nwoye.

The group said Nwoye was focused on his party responsibilities and efforts to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and other APC candidates.

“Whatever is happening in Imo State is an internal party matter, and the name of the Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Nwoye, should not be drawn into the dispute without a clear basis. The parties involved should seek ways to manage their differences,” the statement said.

Democracy Alliance urged aspirants in Imo West and Imo North to concentrate on party unity and mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections.

“We are using this medium to call on the key actors in Imo West and North to resolve their differences and plan on how to deliver votes for the APC,” the statement added.

The group’s reaction followed a petition by the Justice and Democracy Network to the APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, alleging irregularities involving party and Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) documents relating to the senatorial primaries in Imo State.

The allegations have not been established as proven wrongdoing. The dispute has raised questions about the documents in question and the circumstances surrounding the primaries.

DA urged all parties to allow the relevant authorities to examine the issues and address them through appropriate procedures.

It said resolving the disagreement through established channels would help prevent the controversy from distracting the APC from its preparations for the 2027 general elections.

World.title: APC ruined Nigerians’ lives — Abdullahi; We’re solving problems Atiku created, Morka replies
World.content:
By Bayo Wahab

The spokesperson of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Bolaji Abdullahi, has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of ruining Nigerians’ lives through its policies, while the APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, blamed former Vice President Atiku Abubakar for contributing to the country’s economic problems.

The two party spokespersons exchanged views on the APC’s performance ahead of the 2027 general election during an appearance on News Central’s Breakfast Central on Thursday.

Abdullahi argued that the Tinubu administration’s policies had worsened the economic and social conditions of Nigerians, insisting that the government should admit its shortcomings and change direction.

He likened the administration’s efforts to fixing a pothole but ending up damaging the entire road.

“What they tried to do in the last three is like trying to fill a pothole, and in the process they end up leaving the economy in a ditch,” Abdullahi said.

The ADC spokesperson argued that government policies should be assessed by their impact on citizens’ lives and livelihoods, rather than by official claims about their success.

“There is nothing wrong in admitting that your prescription or your solution has not worked,” he said, adding that the consequences of the APC’s policies could be seen across the economy, society and security.

According to Abdullahi, life had become increasingly difficult for ordinary Nigerians, adding that the ruling party had failed to provide a clear explanation of its Renewed Hope agenda.

“Nigeria is the capital to the largest number of poor people, and all you hear them is talking about this Renewed Hope agenda and you ask them, what is this Renewed Hope? They cannot come up with any articulated explanation,” he said.

Morka, however, rejected Abdullahi’s criticism, arguing that the ADC’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, contributed to the economic challenges facing Nigeria.

He accused Atiku of failing in leadership and alleged that his tenure contributed to the country’s economic decline.

“Let me make clear that my good friend speaks for a candidate who is easily the most critical actor in the economic sabotage of this country,” Morka said.

He also accused the former vice president of leaving behind a poor record in office and alleged that the administration in which Atiku served squandered $16bn earmarked for electricity projects.

Morka said the APC government was now attempting to address problems created by previous administrations, including the one in which Atiku served.

According to him, Atiku “left a sordid record of performance; destroyed Nigeria’s national assets; created the economic void that governments since then have been trying to fill; squandered 16 billion US dollars meant to provide electricity.”

“When a man like that comes along to mount this sort of very cosmetic, emotional critique of a government that is trying to solve problems that he principally created, please, my dear brother, don’t pontificate,” he said.

The APC spokesman maintained that Atiku’s record in government should be considered when assessing his criticism of the current administration.

World.title: World Bank, FG Mobilise $1.2bn for Catchment Management, Climate Resilience Programme
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The World Bank and the Federal Government have advanced plans to implement 20 Strategic Catchment Management Plans (SCMPs) across 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) as part of efforts to combat environmental degradation, strengthen climate resilience and secure Nigeria’s water resources for future generations.

Speaking at the Stakeholders’ Engagement for the Implementation of Strategic Catchment Management Plans, World Bank Task Team Leader and Senior Environmental Specialist, Dr. Joy Iganya Agene, described ACReSAL as fundamentally a catchment management project designed to promote integrated landscape management beyond state and political boundaries.

Agene said the plans represent the first government-led watershed management initiative undertaken at such scale in Nigeria and would provide a blueprint for sustainable management of land, water and environmental resources.

According to her, environmental and hydrological systems are interconnected, making collaboration among states and communities essential for long-term sustainability.

“What you do upstream affects what happens downstream. There are no state limits when it comes to water resources and environmental management,” she said, urging stakeholders to embrace a shared vision for protecting the environment.

She also announced that the World Bank had approved an additional $500 million financing package for ACReSAL over the next four years, bringing total funding for the programme to about $1.2 billion, to ensure sustainability of ongoing investments and interventions.

Presenting the implementation overview of the Aloma-Konshisha Strategic Catchment Management Plan, Managing Director of MECON Geology and Engineering Services Ltd, Chuka Offodile, said the catchment spans Benue, Kogi, Cross River, Ebonyi and Enugu States and faces increasing threats from flooding, deforestation, erosion, land degradation and water pollution.

He disclosed that forest cover in the catchment declined significantly between 2017 and 2024, while agricultural expansion and settlement growth continued to place pressure on ecosystems and water resources.

Offodile said the plan seeks to restore degraded landscapes, strengthen water resources management, promote climate-smart agriculture, improve livelihoods and enhance disaster preparedness through coordinated interventions involving governments, development partners and communities.

He noted that successful implementation would improve water security, boost agricultural productivity, reduce flood and drought risks, restore biodiversity and strengthen climate resilience across the catchment.

As the session drew to a close, stakeholders agreed that the challenge before Nigeria is no longer planning but implementation.

With 20 strategic catchment plans validated, an additional $500 million in financing secured, and unprecedented collaboration among federal and state institutions, the focus now shifts to translating the blueprints into measurable outcomes.

For the World Bank, ACReSAL and participating states, the ultimate goal remains clear: restoring degraded landscapes, securing water resources, strengthening climate resilience and creating a healthier environment for millions of Nigerians today and generations yet unborn.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu Charges Betta Edu, APC Women to Secure Women’s Votes
World.content:
Jonathan Eze

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has charged Dr Betta Edu, Director of Women Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, members of the Women’s Directorate, all APC Women and other campaign leaders to intensify grassroots engagement and mobilise women across the country to secure victory for the party in the 2027 general election.

The President gave the charge on Wednesday afternoon at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa, Abuja, where he acknowledged the invaluable contributions of Nigerian women to the nation’s political development and expressed confidence in their capacity to play a decisive role in determining the outcome of the forthcoming election.

Tinubu commended women for their longstanding commitment to the APC and their contributions to the party’s electoral successes, noting that their organisational abilities, numerical strength and influence within families and communities make them indispensable to the party’s re-election project. “ Women are the greatest mobilizers”

He urged members of the campaign council, particularly the Women Mobilisation Directorate under Dr Edu, to translate the enthusiasm and support of women into a well-coordinated nationwide campaign capable of delivering electoral victory for the APC.

The President’s charge places the women’s mobilisation structure at the centre of the party’s strategy for securing a renewed mandate for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, with particular emphasis on reaching voters at the grassroots, strengthening existing political networks and sustaining direct engagement with communities across the federation.

For Dr Edu and her team, the task is to consolidate the support of women in markets, rural communities, professional associations, cooperatives, faith-based organisations and other social networks, while ensuring that the administration’s policies and programmes are communicated effectively to prospective voters.

The Women Mobilisation Directorate has already established an ambitious target of securing 40 million women’s votes for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket through an expansive mobilisation framework covering 176,846 communities, as well as structures across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The strategy is designed to take the campaign beyond major rallies and political gatherings by strengthening ward-level organisation, household engagement, community outreach, and polling-unit mobilisation.

Tinubu’s recognition of women’s contributions also reinforces the importance of their participation beyond election periods. Women remain central to household economic management, community development, small businesses, agriculture, education, and social welfare, giving them considerable influence in shaping public opinion and political choices.

The President’s charge is therefore expected to galvanise APC women leaders and grassroots organisers into a more coordinated effort to present the administration’s record, explain its policies and engage citizens on the issues that matter to their daily lives.

The mobilisation drive is also expected to build on the activities of First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, whose engagement with women and support for empowerment initiatives have featured prominently in the campaign’s preparations.

At the October 5 pre-inaugural Women’s Summit and Empowerment Programme in Abuja, the First Lady brought together women stakeholders from across the country, while the programme featured the distribution of livelihood-support items, including motorbikes and farm trucks, to beneficiaries.

The gathering also underscored the campaign’s determination to connect political mobilisation with women’s economic participation.

Dr Edu has consistently expressed confidence in the ability of APC women to secure victory for the President in 2027. She has called for unity, discipline, and sustained grassroots engagement, arguing that the party’s women must work as a coordinated network rather than rely solely on high-profile campaign events.

The inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council formally advances the APC’s preparations for the next general election, bringing the party’s political structures and mobilisation machinery into sharper focus.

With the President’s marching orders now placing renewed emphasis on women’s electoral contribution, the responsibility before Edu and other campaign officials is to turn political enthusiasm into measurable grassroots participation and votes.

For the APC, the 2027 contest will require more than endorsements and public declarations. It will demand sustained contact with voters, credible communication of government policies, and an organisational structure capable of reaching communities across the country.

Tinubu’s message to the women’s mobilisation team is clear in its political implication: women must not merely participate in the campaign; they must be organised, empowered and strategically positioned to help deliver the party’s electoral objective.

World.title: Implementing the Four-Point Proposition on Mining Cooperation to Write a New Chapter in China-Africa Common Devt
World.content:
By Yu Dunhai

On October 13, 2026, Chinese President Xi Jinping put forth a four-point proposition on advancing China-Africa mining cooperation during his meeting with President Duma Gideon Boko of Botswana, who was on a state visit to China. Grounded in the profound transformation of the global critical minerals landscape and Africa’s urgent need for independent development, and anchored in the broader context of traditional China-Africa friendship, the proposition charts the course for China-Africa mining cooperation in the new era.

As the Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, I am keenly aware of the strategic vision, forward-looking perspective, and practical relevance of these four points. They present a concrete embodiment of the concept of a China-Africa community with a shared future, and provide strong support for Nigeria and other African countries in transforming their resource endowment into development dividends. Drawing on the realities of China-Nigeria mining cooperation, I would like to share with Nigerian friends a deeper understanding of the rich substance of this four-point proposition.

First, we must adhere to the principle that African resources belong to Africa. This is the fundamental premise of mining cooperation with African nations. Africa has long been locked at the lower end of global industrial and value chains by an inequitable international division of labour–a historical injustice that must be corrected. Resource sovereignty is an integral component of national sovereignty, and the ability to control one’s own resource destiny is the cornerstone of sustainable development for African countries. China fully understands and respects Africa’s legitimate aspirations. We have always respected the development paths independently chosen by African countries and stand ready to share our experience to help them formulate mining development plans suited to their national conditions. China supports Nigeria and other African countries in independently charting their mining development paths, ensuring that decision-making power and the benefits of resource development remain firmly in their own hands.

Second, we must uphold the principle of pursuing the greater good and shared interests, and seeking mutual benefit and win-win results. This is the core philosophy of China-Africa mining cooperation. In conducting mining cooperation, China and Africa must uphold a correct view of righteousness and benefit. China never pursues unilateral maximization of benefits in its cooperation with Africa, and always adheres to win-win cooperation and common development. In Nigeria, Chinese enterprises involved in energy and mining sector not only bring capital and technology, but also adhere to localized operations, and attach importance to skills training and community contributions. The Chinese Embassy will continue to guide Chinese enterprises in Nigeria to enhance their operational capabilities, transfer green technologies, strengthen public welfare assistance, drive local employment and talent training, and promote South-South cooperation in the mining sector.

Third, we must pursue high-quality development. This is the direction of progress for China-Africa mining cooperation. Promoting local processing, extending industrial chains and increasing value addition are the key pathways for Africa to convert resource advantages into development strength. China has always been a doer in supporting Africa’s development and will continue to drive the transformation of China-Africa mining cooperation towards higher industrial value addition. We will deepen the alignment between China’s 15th Five-Year Plan and Nigeria’s “Renewed Hope” Agenda, push projects further into deep processing and high-value-added segments, and help Nigeria build a more complete industrial system. In this way, resources can truly become a driver of modernisation rather than a source of so-called “resource curse.”

Fourth, we must maintain a fair and open cooperation environment. This is an important safeguard for mining cooperation with Africa. Africa’s resources should never be turned into tools of geopolitical rivalry. Any attempt to politicize or instrumentalize African resource issues as well as to create confrontation and division will seriously damage the fundamental interests of the African people. China consistently advocates open cooperation and fair competition. We welcome all parties that genuinely wish to support Africa’s development and stand ready to work with African partners to maintain a stable and predictable market environment for mining cooperation, thereby creating more favourable conditions for enterprise investment and operations. China is ready to join hands with Nigeria in rejecting any attempt to treat mineral resources as bargaining chip in geopolitical games, ensuring that resource development always serves development and benefits the people.

I would like to emphasise in particular that the Chinese government requires all Chinese enterprises and citizens in Nigeria to strictly abide by Nigerian laws and regulations and to operate in a lawful and compliant manner. We maintain a zero-tolerance policy toward illegal mining and other criminal activities. China supports Nigeria in taking strong measures to strengthen mining governance. The facts show that the overwhelming majority of Chinese mining enterprises in Nigeria operate in accordance with the law, actively fulfil their social responsibilities and protect the environment. Isolated and inaccurate allegations that exaggerate individual cases or distort the facts are neither fair nor conducive to the overall China-Nigeria friendship and cooperation. We stand ready to work with the Nigerian side to further regulate market order, jointly combat illegal mining, and foster a healthy and transparent business environment.

China and Africa share a common future and a bright outlook. Mechanism platforms such as the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation continue to provide solid support, while the dividends of China’s zero-tariff policy for all diplomatic partners in Africa continue to unfold, creating favourable conditions for deeper China-Africa cooperation. I am convinced that as long as both sides uphold mutual respect and mutual benefit, we can turn Africa’s resource endowment into tangible development outcomes, deliver greater benefits to the Chinese and African peoples, and make greater contributions to building a China-Africa community with a shared future.

China stands ready to work hand in hand with Nigeria and other African countries to fully implement President Xi Jinping’s four-point proposal on China-Africa mining cooperation, write a new chapter of high-quality development in China-Africa mining cooperation, ensure that Africa’s resources truly serve the development of the African people, and make China-Africa mining cooperation a model of South-South cooperation and an important force in advancing Africa’s modernisation.

*H.E. Yu Dunhai is Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria

World.title: 32nd CJN Sports Competition Begins Friday in Kaduna
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

The 32nd edition of the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) Sports Competition to be hosted by Kaduna State will begin from October 16, the National Sports Association for Judiciary (NASAJ) has announced.

NASAJ, in a statement, noted that the competition which will run through October 29, will be officially opened on Saturday, October 17, 2026.

The association observed that the Chief Justice of Nigeria Sports Competition has evolved into one of the most anticipated annual events within the Nigerian Judiciary.

“Beyond its role as a sporting festival, it serves as a unique platform for fostering unity, friendship, physical fitness, mental well-being, and professional camaraderie among judicial officers and judiciary staff across the federation. The competition also provides participants with an opportunity to showcase their sporting talents and creativity while strengthening the bonds that unite the judicial family,” the statement read in part.

NASAJ disclosed that each year, the tournament brings together participants from courts and judicial institutions nationwide in an atmosphere of healthy competition, teamwork, mutual respect and fellowship, adding that through sport, the competition continues to reinforce the enduring values of discipline, integrity, fairness, excellence and professionalism that are the hallmarks of the judiciary.

The association, which described the successful hosting of the 31st edition in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, as a significant milestone in the history of the games, expressed gratitude to the Almighty God for the success recorded and expresses its profound appreciation to the Government and people of Akwa Ibom State, the Akwa Ibom State Judiciary, and all stakeholders whose hospitality, support and contributions made the event a resounding success.

“This year’s edition promises to be one of the most exciting and memorable in the history of the competition. Participants will compete in a wide range of sporting events, including football, volleyball, handball, lawn tennis, table tennis, badminton, swimming, athletics, scrabble, chess, ayo and other recreational activities. These events are designed to encourage broad participation, strengthen institutional relationships, and promote a healthy work-life balance among members of the judiciary,” the statement added.

Meanwhile, NASAJ expressed profound gratitude to the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, for her unwavering support and commitment to the advancement of sports within the judiciary, stating that her visionary leadership and steadfast encouragement continue to inspire initiatives that enhance the welfare, unity, productivity and overall well-being of judicial officers and staff through sporting activities.

The association also commended the Governor of Kaduna State, Senator Uba Sani, the Government and people of Kaduna State, the Kaduna State Judiciary, the Local Organising Committee, and all stakeholders involved in the preparations for their dedication and commitment towards delivering a successful and memorable tournament.

“As preparations enter their final stages, NASAJ warmly invites members of the media, corporate organisations, development partners, stakeholders, and the general public to support and participate in this unique gathering of the Nigerian Judiciary. Beyond celebrating sporting excellence, the competition will further strengthen the bonds of unity, friendship, cooperation, and understanding that are essential to the effective administration of justice in Nigeria.

“NASAJ looks forward to welcoming participants and guests from across the country to Kaduna State for what promises to be an outstanding celebration of sportsmanship, fellowship, wellness, and judicial excellence,” the statement read.

World.title: APEN Plans Homegrown AI Model for Nigerian Classrooms
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The Association of Private Educators in Nigeria (APEN) has unveiled plans to develop a contextualised Artificial Intelligence (AI) model tailored to Nigeria’s socio-cultural realities and educational needs, as more than 300 delegates have registered for its forthcoming 16th annual conference.

The association said the initiative was aimed at ensuring that AI adoption in Nigerian classrooms preserved local values, cultural identity and ethical standards while equipping learners with the skills required to compete globally.

The conference, themed: ‘Human First: Leading with Purpose in the Age of AI’, is scheduled to hold in November 2 and 3,

at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Briefing journalists on Wednesday, the Chairperson of the Planning Committee, Mrs. Bolanle Adewole, said excessive reliance on foreign AI models could produce educational content that failed to reflect Nigeria’s realities.

She said APEN was exploring the development of its own AI engine that would enable schools to access tools and resources relevant to the country’s educational environment.

“AI has not come to kill education; on the contrary, it has come to enhance and support it by promoting innovation, sustainability, and efficiency,” Adewole stated.

She, however, cautioned against unrestricted adoption of the technology, stressing the need for locally developed models that reflected Nigerian experiences rather than generating outputs primarily suited for Europe and other parts of the world.

The conference, according to Adewole, is expected to attract school proprietors, administrators, teachers, parents and international education partners from 14 states in Nigeria and parts of East Africa.

“Although the event was initially projected to attract 350 participants, more than 300 delegates had confirmed their attendance weeks before the conference,” she said, expressing optimism that participation would exceed the target and approach the venue’s capacity of 600.

The conference, she noted, has also secured the support of more than eight corporate sponsors, including several returning partners.

A member of APEN’s Board of Trustees, Mrs. Olufunke Fowler-Amba, said mainstream AI systems were not necessarily designed to accommodate the cultural and educational needs of minority communities and countries such as Nigeria.

She stressed the importance of ensuring that Nigerian children retained their cultural identity while acquiring the competencies required in the global marketplace.

Fowler-Amba said APEN would continue to provide a unified platform for private educators to engage the government on policies affecting the sector.

On the practical application of AI in schools, the association’s Founding Chairman, Mrs. Lai Koiki, said the technology should help reduce teachers’ workloads rather than create fears about job losses.

She said AI could ease administrative burdens, improve lesson planning and streamline student assessment, allowing teachers to concentrate more on classroom mentorship and learners’ development.

Koiki added: “Structured training would help educators acquire the skills needed to remain competitive internationally while maintaining their central role in the learning process.”

She also emphasised APEN’s international engagements, including its relationship with the Council of British International Schools (COBIS) and participation from Kenya and Uganda.

Another member of the Board of Trustees, Dr. Femi Ogunsanya, emphasised the importance of effective governance, continuous professional development and engagement with relevant authorities in sustaining private education institutions.

She said school proprietors needed to understand how to manage institutional change, recruit qualified teachers and provide regular training as AI continued to reshape education.

Ogunsanya added that the Federal Ministry of Education had recognised APEN’s contributions by giving private educators a voice in national education policymaking.

The organisers said the conference would feature specialised breakout sessions for school owners, educational leaders, classroom teachers and parents.

The sessions are expected to provide practical governance frameworks and guidance for implementing human-centred AI practices in schools from November 4.

World.title: Edo to Inaugurate 100mw CCETC Power Plant December
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

The Edo State Government is looking forward to the inauguration of the 100-megawatt CCETC independent power plant in Ologbo, Benin, which it hopes will add 100 megawatts power to electricity generation in the state.

The inauguration date is set for December 2026.

Commissioner for Power, Paul Usenbo, disclosed this during an inspection of the facility, where he assessed construction progress, equipment installation and preparations for testing and inauguration.

Usenbo said the inspection was aimed at establishing clear implementation timelines and verifying the project’s progress against the state government’s target of delivering additional power generation capacity before the end of the year.

He said the inspection also covered the Tahur Industrial Park and its associated 300-metric-tonne energy facility in Ologbo, with the government engaging developers to establish measurable timelines for completing the projects.

According to the commissioner, the projects are part of the government’s broader strategy to increase electricity generation and improve power supply across Edo State’s three senatorial districts.

He said the government was committed to ensuring that the projects delivered tangible benefits to residents and businesses, adding that Governor Monday Okpebholo had continued to prioritise initiatives aimed at expanding electricity access across the state.

Usenbo said the projects had met their second-quarter implementation timelines, expressing optimism about progress towards the government’s inauguration target.

Speaking during the visit, the Marketing Manager, CCETC, Eric Ju, thanked the state government for its continued support and cooperation.

He disclosed that the company had completed the construction and installation of 46 megawatts of generation capacity and planned to commence power supply by the end of 2026.

Ju added that the company would continue working towards the completion of subsequent phases of the project, with the objective of providing more stable electricity and supporting economic activities in Edo State

World.title: Law Reform Conference Seeks More Powers For States, LGs
World.content:
Participants at the maiden Conference of All Law Reform Commissions in Nigeria have called for comprehensive reforms of the country’s legislative framework to address structural imbalances in federalism, strengthen local government autonomy and devolve more powers to states.

The participants also advocated fiscal federalism, a review of the Exclusive Legislative List in favour of states and full judicial federalism as part of measures to strengthen Nigeria’s democratic institutions.

These recommendations were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the two-day conference, hosted by the Edo State Law Reform Commission at the John Odigie Oyegun Public Service Academy, Benin City, from September 28 to 29, 2026.

The conference, which had as its theme, ‘Consolidating Nigeria’s Democracy through Law Reform: Charting the Way Forward,’ featured an opening address by Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, while the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice (AGF), Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), was represented by Otunba Wale Fapohunda (SAN) who delivered the keynote address.

On national security and human rights, the participants stressed the need to strike a balance between safeguarding the country and protecting the fundamental rights of citizens.

They maintained that executive measures taken in the interest of national security must remain subject to judicial scrutiny, while urging civil society organisations to remain vigilant against human rights abuses perpetrated under the guise of security operations.

The conference also called for a coherent national intelligence-sharing system anchored on clearly defined mandates, inter-agency cooperation, accountability and digital readiness to strengthen the country’s response to security challenges.

It further advocated reforms to police investigation procedures in line with international best practices, alongside measures to enhance accountability within law enforcement agencies.

On local government administration, the participants called for reforms to enable councils to discharge their constitutional responsibilities and exercise the autonomy affirmed by the Supreme Court.

They also emphasised the need for effective mechanisms to ensure that increased allocations to local governments translate into improved infrastructure and the provision of essential services, including healthcare, food and shelter.

The communiqué noted that financial autonomy at the grassroots level must deliver tangible benefits to citizens, rather than remain a constitutional provision without corresponding improvements in service delivery.

The participants further called for adequate and sustainable funding, qualified personnel and modern infrastructure for law reform commissions across the country.

They argued that the effectiveness of the commissions would remain limited without the necessary institutional support to conduct research, review existing laws and recommend reforms that reflect contemporary realities.

To address delays in implementing their recommendations, the conference proposed a legal framework compelling the legislative and executive arms of government to consider and act on reports submitted by law reform commissions within specified time frames.

The participants warned that failure by relevant authorities to act on such recommendations undermines the objectives of law reform and limits its potential impact on governance and national development.

On electoral matters, the conference advocated reforms to ensure that pre-election and post-election disputes are resolved before elections or inauguration, where applicable.

According to the communiqué, such measures would help reduce prolonged litigation, promote certainty in the electoral process and ensure that electoral outcomes reflect the will of voters.

The participants also called for a comprehensive review of Nigeria’s tertiary education curriculum to incorporate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and robotics, in response to developments associated with the Fifth Industrial Revolution.

At the end of the conference, the Chairman of the Edo State Law Reform Commission, Hon. Osikhena-Boih Donald, was appointed Pro Tem Chairman of the Forum of State Law Reform Commissions in Nigeria.

The communiqué was jointly signed by Prof. Inegbedion, Chairman of the Communiqué Drafting Committee; Donald; and the Edo State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Prof. Roland Otaru (SAN).

World.title: APC Releases Nationwide Campaign Rally Schedule, As Tinubu Leads Campaign in 12 States
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has released its Nationwide Campaign Rally Schedule for the 2027 presidential election covering 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

Recall that President Bola Tinubu had on Wednesday during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) held at the Presidential Villa hinted that he won’t be available for all the campaign because he would not want to abandon governance.

The campaign is scheduled to run from October 2026 through early January 2027, with Lagos hosting the major closing rally on 9th January 2027.

However, according to the timetable sighted on Thursday, President Tinubu is expected to lead the campaign for his re-election in 12 different states, including Kaduna where the ruling party would officially flag-off the campaign on 24th October, 2026.

The schedule shows President Tinubu would also lead the Port Harcourt campaign scheduled to take place on 7th November.

He would also be on the campaign train to Plateau state on the 14th November, and in Ibadan, Oyo state on the 21st November.

Similarly, he would be available to lead the campaign train in Borno State on 25th November, and in Enugu on the 28th November.

The President is also expected to lead in Sokoto on 5th December, thereafter he would lead in Asaba, Delta state on 12th December.

Tinubu would lead the campaign train to Kano, the votes hub in the north on 17th December, while Bauchi state would play host to the APC campaign machinery on 29th November, with the President leading.

The President would lead the campaign to Yola, Adamawa State, the home state of his main challenger, Atiku Abubakar, on Monday, 4th January 2027, while the grand finale of the campaign would be held in Lagos state on Saturday, 9 January, 2027.

Other campaign schedules include: Owerri, Imo -30th December; Akure, Ondo state – 11th November; Bauchi -29th November; Katsina – 2nd December; Uyo, Akwa Ibom – 18th November; Makurdi, Benue State -30th November.

Others are: Abeokuta, Ogun State, 3rd December; Awka, Anambra state -19th November; Gombe state, 3rd November; Kebbi state -17th November; Edo state – 12th November, Kwara state -10th December.

Also, Osun state will host the campaign on 9th December, Abia state 7th December; Yobe state – 16th November, Zamfara state -14th December; Bayelsa state – 15th December, Niger State 16th December, Ekiti state 5th November.

Also on the schedule are: Ebonyi state, 9th November; Taraba state – 19th December, Jigawa state -10th November, Cross River – 2nd November; Kogi state – 8th December; Nasarawa 4th November; and Adamawa State, 4th January 2027.

Game stores are being shut down in South Africa. What does this mean for you and your job?

A closing-down sale. Retailers usually heavily discount their stock before closing down. Back in 2022, when Game closed eight stores, there were large discounts.

Vouchers and gift cards. It would be advisable to use your gift cards and vouchers while you still can.

Fewer shopping options. With Game closing down, there will be fewer retailer options for you to choose from.

Massmart has not revealed how many jobs will be affected this time. The 2022 closure of eight stores put around 700 jobs at risk. However, Massmart reportedly said that when stores do convert to Walmart them staff will be transferred accordingly.

World.title: Stargazers in South Africa can look forward to this October spectacle
World.content:
The night sky has something special in store for South Africans this October. Image: canva

South African stargazers have another reason to look up this October, as two familiar sights in the night sky are set to appear unusually close together in a celestial event that requires no expensive equipment to enjoy.

The Moon and Saturn will appear side by side this month, and it’s going to be a sight to behold. While the two are separated by an enormous distance in space, their apparent closeness will offer skywatchers an opportunity to spot the ringed planet alongside Earth’s natural satellite.

The pairing will take place just days before October’s full Moon, adding another reason to keep an eye on the night sky.



When to see the Moon and Saturn together

The pairing will be visible during the night of 24–25 October, with the two celestial objects appearing to move across the sky together as the night progresses.

Saturn should look like a steady, golden point of light near the much brighter Moon. Both can be seen without specialist equipment, although a telescope will offer a better view of Saturn.

For the best chance of seeing the pairing, choose a spot with a clear view of the sky and check the local weather forecast before heading outside.

Why do the Moon and Saturn appear close together?

The event is known as a conjunction, which occurs when two celestial objects appear close together from our perspective on Earth.

The Moon and Saturn are not physically close to one another. Saturn is a planet roughly 1.2 billion kilometres away from Earth, while the Moon is our nearest natural celestial neighbour.

Their apparent proximity is the result of their positions in the sky, rather than an actual meeting in space.



Saturn is also putting on a show this month

October is a particularly good month for stargazers to see Saturn because the planet reached opposition on 4 October 2026.

Opposition occurs when Earth lies between the Sun and a planet, placing that planet opposite the Sun in our sky. Saturn consequently appears brighter and remains visible for much of the night around this period.

The Moon–Saturn pairing is therefore an opportunity to spot the ringed planet while it is well placed for observation.

The pairing will also take place shortly before October’s full Moon, traditionally known as the Hunter’s Moon.

The Moon will reach its full phase at approximately 06:11 on Monday, 26 October, South African time.

World.title: IEC to implement Constitutional Court ruling on ANC candidate lists
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) says it will comply with the Constitutional Court’s ruling in favour of the African National Congress (ANC) in a dispute over candidate lists for the 4 November local government elections.

The ruling follows the ANC’s failure to complete the final submission of its candidate lists for six municipalities before the prescribed deadline. The ruling, handed down on Thursday, 15 October, follows the ANC’s appeal against an Electoral Court judgment that upheld the IEC’s decision to exclude the candidates from the ballot.

The South African previously reported that Constitutional Court Justice Rammaka Mathopo said the IEC’s decision to reject the ANC’s candidate lists in the six municipalities had been set aside.



“The first respondent, which is the IEC, is directed to do all things necessary to include the party lists and ward candidate nominations mentioned in paragraph four of this order, and the lists and nominations onto the ballot papers and all other relevant processes for the purposes of the 4 November 2026 local elections,” he said.

The IEC said it respects the authority of the Constitutional Court as the final arbiter and will give effect to its order.

IEC spokesperson Kate Bapela said the Commission’s position throughout the legal proceedings had been guided by its interpretation of the applicable electoral legislation and the need to ensure the consistent application of prescribed electoral processes.

However, she said the IEC recognised its constitutional obligation to implement the Court’s decision.

“The IEC will communicate further details regarding the implementation process once the necessary assessments have been completed. All political parties and stakeholders are urged to cooperate with the Commission during this period.

“The Commission reassures the public that preparations for the 4 November 2026 Local Government Elections remain a priority. It will continue to discharge its constitutional mandate independently, impartially and in accordance with the law,” Bapela said.



Meanwhile, elections analyst, Michael Atkins told the SABC that he was surprised but not shocked by the Constitutional Court’s ruling.

“It was quite clear that the ANC pointed out very calmly that the wording and regulations of the Act was not entirely clear and in my view the IEC didn’t argue the case as crisply as they might have done,” he said.

“Although I believe that the ANC’s interpretation in the end in my own view was not correct, but the case was reasonable. For me the bottom line is that those regulations need to be amended because the system works the way it should work but if the regulations of the law doesn’t spell it out then the law is what counts. It isn’t what a user manual counts,” he added.

ANC VS IEC | Elections analyst Michael Atkins says he is surprised by the Constitutional Court's ruling, arguing that the regulations may need to be amended. He adds that the IEC could have presented its case more persuasively. pic.twitter.com/I27DzYJpoy — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 15, 2026

On 2 September, the IEC revealed that cumulatively, there are 2 274 candidates who were captured but not finally submitted on the Online Candidate Nomination System by the set deadline.

Political parties and independent candidates intending to contest the upcoming elections had until 17:00 on Friday, 28 August, to submit their candidate nominations.

“This phenomenon affects 480 PR and 1 794 ward potential candidates. The unique number of political parties in this situation is 45. The Commission’s position is that, in practical terms, these potential candidates have not been submitted to the Commission and therefore are not in contention for this election,” the IEC said at the time.

World.title: ‘It is a grant, not a pension plan’: South Africans clash over calls for R5 000 monthly payouts
World.content:
A debate over the value of the Older Persons Grant has divided South Africans, with some demanding a dramatic increase and others reminding them what the grant is meant to be.

The discussion played out on The South African’s Facebook page, where users weighed in on whether government can afford to pay pensioners more.

The case for R5 000

Michael Watkins was firm in his view that the government should significantly increase the grant.



“The government needs to increase pension grants to R5 000 per month. There is no excuse as to why they cannot,” he wrote.

His comment drew several reactions, showing that many South Africans share his frustration. Supporters of a higher grant point to rising food, electricity and transport costs, which have made it harder for older persons to stretch their monthly payment.

For many pensioners, this is their only income. Some also use it to support unemployed adult children and grandchildren living under the same roof.

A grant, not a pension

Not everyone agreed with the call for R5 000. Rolleen Melanie Jacobs pushed back with a pointed reminder.

“It is a grant, not a pension plan” she wrote.

Her comment touches on an important distinction. The Older Persons Grant is a social assistance payment funded by taxpayers. Unlike a private pension or retirement annuity, it is not built from a person’s own contributions over their working life.



Those who share her view argue that it was designed as a safety net rather than a full income, and that a sharp increase would put more pressure on an already stretched national budget.

The debate shows how differently South Africans view the role of social grants. While some see them as a right that should match the cost of living, others believe they should remain a basic safety net.

World.title: 111 SAPS officers convicted of serious crimes, including rape
World.content:
A report has revealed that 111 SAPS members were convicted of crimes during the 2025/26 financial year, including serious offences. Image: X

A total of 111 South African Police Service (SAPS) members were convicted of crimes during the 2025/26 financial year, including offences involving deaths resulting from police action and rape.

On Thursday, 15 October, the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID) revealed the figures during its latest reporting to Parliament.

The figures include 28 convictions in cases involving deaths resulting from police action and 10 rape convictions.



The revelations come as IPID battles a growing caseload, with more than 14 000 active cases and fewer than 200 investigators.

SAPS OFFICERS CONVICTED IN DEATH AND RAPE CASES

According to the report, convictions in cases involving deaths resulting from police action increased from 22 in the previous reporting period to 28.

IPID also recorded 464 new cases involving deaths resulting from police action during the 2025/26 financial year.



The directorate investigates criminal allegations against police officers, including deaths in custody, rape, assault and torture.

IPID registered 5 259 new cases during the reporting period.

Of these, 3 468 involved assault and torture allegations, while 669 concerned the discharge of official firearms.



RAPE ALLEGATIONS AGAINST POLICE OFFICERS INCREASE

The report also revealed that 10 police officers were convicted of rape.

In one case, a police officer stationed at Matlelerekeng Police Station in Limpopo received a 10-year prison sentence for rape and an additional two years for child pornography offences.

Meanwhile, IPID recorded 116 new rape allegations against police officers, up from 95 during the previous financial year.



Of the 116 reported incidents, 72 allegedly involved officers on duty, while 44 involved off-duty members.

The increase has raised further concerns about sexual violence involving officers entrusted with protecting the public.

IPID FACES BACKLOG OF MORE THAN 14 000 CASES

IPID continues to struggle with a heavy workload and limited investigative capacity.



The directorate has fewer than 200 investigators handling more than 14 000 active cases.

The figures prompted MPs to question how officers accused of serious crimes entered the police service.

DA MP Dianne Kohler challenged SAPS recruitment and vetting procedures.



“What is your theory on how these rapists, fraudsters, torturers, thieves, and even murderers get into the SAPS in the first place?” Kohler asked.

IPID’s official annual reporting also recorded 84 criminal convictions secured through its investigations, compared with 43 during the previous financial year.

The directorate reported 281 arrests and 994 cases before the courts at the end of March 2026.



The 84 convictions in IPID’s official reporting and the 111 SAPS members cited in the SABC report represent different reported measures.

PARLIAMENT RAISES CONCERNS OVER POLICE ACCOUNTABILITY

Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Police has called for stronger oversight and urgent action to address failures within SAPS.

On Thursday, the committee raised concerns about criminal investigations, forensic services and financial management.



The committee adopted its Budgetary Review and Recommendation Reports on SAPS, IPID and other policing bodies on Wednesday.

MPs warned that continued failures in policing and accountability threatened public safety.

The committee called for corrective measures to address weaknesses in the criminal justice system.



IPID must now confront its mounting caseload while investigating fresh allegations of criminal conduct against police officers.

World.title: All Blacks coach: RWC quarter-final draw against Springboks is ‘crazy’
World.content:
There is very little separating the Springboks and the All Blacks as the top two sides in the current World Rugby rankings, and yet despite this, the arch-rivals appear likely to meet as early as the quarter-final stage of the next World Cup.

The Springboks would be expected to finish top of Pool B comfortably, and the All Blacks – although they have been drawn in Pool A with Australia – would still be backed to finish top of their group too.

Both sides would then face a third-place finisher in the Round of 16, where they’d be overwhelming favourites.



Where it gets interesting is that this pairing of winners from the Round of 16 are then set to meet in the quarter-finals. This puts the Springboks and All Blacks on a collision course for a quarter-final meeting in what would be a repeat of the 2023 World Cup final.

If the Springboks were to overcome the All Blacks, then there could be another huge match up in the semi-finals against France, the team they edged at the quarter-final stage of the last World Cup.

Looking at this draw, All Blacks coach Dave Rennie has again been outspoken in his criticism.

“It just highlights a crazy draw. You look at the football World Cup and the top four ranked sides in the world play each other in the semis, it seems hard to believe that you have got us pitted against South Africa, potentially in a quarter-final, and the winner of that plays France.

“But you know, I mean, it is what it is now. It’s probably been similar before. So look, to win a title you’ve got to beat them all anyway. but that’s the path in front of us.”

Depending on who progresses through this to the final, then it’s most likely that England or Ireland would lie in wait.
