World.title: Sheinbaum signs decree blocking violent and hostile content from minors’ social media feeds: Wednesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

📱 Sheinbaum signs decree to curb harmful online content for minors: Social media sites and online forums will be barred from displaying or recommending content to minors that “generates or promotes” hate speech, violent extremism, self-harm, eating disorders, cyberbullying and illegal conduct. Platforms must also verify users’ ages, classify content by age group and offer parental supervision tools. The decree, drawn up after an Oct. 1 machete attack at a school in Torréon, Coahuila, takes effect one month after its publication in the government’s official gazette today.

🚓 Sheinbaum orders CNDH probe into alleged police torture in Guadalajara: The president said the National Human Rights Commission must conduct a “very thorough investigation” into allegations that Jalisco police tortured people detained at Sunday’s water contamination protest. “How is it possible that in 2026, there is still torture of young people by police?” she asked.

⚖️ Sheinbaum defers to judges on ex-INM chief Garduño’s exoneration: Asked about Francisco Garduño’s exoneration over the 2023 Ciudad Juárez detention center fire that killed 40 migrants, the president said, “It’s what the judges determined.” Lawyers for the victims will challenge the ruling.

Why today’s mañanera matters

At her Wednesday morning press conference, President Sheinbaum signed a decree that will bar social media sites and other online forums from displaying or recommending content to minors that “generates or promotes” hate speech, violent extremism, sexual exploitation or violence, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, cyber-bullying and illegal conduct in general.

The government drew up the decree after a fatal Oct. 1 machete attack at a school in Torréon, Coahuila, that was allegedly perpetrated by twin 18-year-old brothers who authorities say were exposed to violent content and extremist ideology online.

Also of note at today’s mañanera was Sheinbaum’s response to allegations that Jalisco state police tortured people who were detained in Guadalajara on Sunday during a protest against contaminated water. One woman said that police beat her and stepped on her bare feet, causing fractures.

Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus said Tuesday that all 39 people detained during Sunday’s protest had been released. He said that police used excessive force and made “unjust arrests.”

He also said that “serious mistakes that must be investigated and sanctioned” were made.

“… No one should have been exposed to violence,” Lemus said.

Sheinbaum signs ‘safe digital environments’ decree

Presidential legal adviser Luisa María Alcalde told reporters that she and other officials met with representatives of social media and other tech companies to discuss the “decree to guarantee safe digital environments for girls, boys and adolescents,” which was presented by the government last Friday.

“Far from demonstrating resistance, they perfectly understood the need for an instrument of this nature,” she said.

Alcalde said that the decree will be published in the government’s official gazette today and take effect one month later.

The decree will oblige social media sites to detect and “immediately” remove “accounts and content that promote or generate violent conduct,” she said.

📲 SHEINBAUM FIRMA DECRETO PARA QUE PLATAFORMAS DIGITALES EVITEN DIFUNDIR CONTENIDOS VIOLENTOS La presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum da un mes a las plataformas digitales para avanzar en la regulación de contenidos que inciten a la violencia, contra niñas, niños y adolescentes. ⚠️ Advirtió que, si las medidas no funcionan, se promoverá una reforma legal que establecería SANCIONES. Aclaró que no se trata de censura, sino de garantizar espacios digitales seguros. 📱🫡🫡 — Isabel Uribe (@Isa_Uribe) October 14, 2026

Alcalde said that social media sites will also have to “classify content” by its appropriateness for different age groups, verify the age of their users and “establish supervision tools” for mothers, fathers and legal guardians of minors.

Before signing the decree, Sheinbaum noted that social media and “digital platform” companies agreed with the government’s initiative.

“The only thing they asked for was a month to prepare their platforms so that this is a reality,” she said.

Sheinbaum said that the government’s Digital Transformation and Communications Agency will monitor social media sites to ensure that companies are complying with the decree.

“If we see they aren’t complying, we would move onto a law which would involve sanctions for the platforms,” she said.

Sheinbaum orders investigation into allegations of police torture in Guadalajara

Regarding allegations that police tortured people who were detained during a protest against water contamination in Guadalajara on Sunday, Sheinbaum said that the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) has to conduct a “very thorough investigation.”

“Yesterday I was asked about the issue of torture in Jalisco. … What happened in Jalisco can’t be allowed,” she said.

“… In addition to the use of streams of water and tear gas [against protesters], the issue of torturing young people is something that has to disappear in our country,” Sheinbaum said.

“A police force cannot torture anyone,” she said.

Sheinbaum said that the CNDH investigation should examine “who gave the order” to torture detainees and interview “the victims.”

“… How is it possible that in 2026, there is still torture of young people by police?” she asked.

“… We, who came from the fight against [government] repression, cannot allow there to be police forces in Mexico that repress and torture,” Sheinbaum said.

Sheinbaum responds to exoneration of former INM chief

A reporter asked the president her opinion about the exoneration of former National Migration Institute (INM) chief Francisco Garduño, who faced a charge of improper exercise of public service in connection with a 2023 fire in an INM detention center in Ciudad Juárez that killed 40 migrants.

“It’s what the judges determined,” Sheinbaum responded.

Garduño, head of the INM between 2019 and 2025, was exonerated at a court hearing in Ciudad Juárez on Tuesday. Lawyers for the victims said they will challenge the decision.

Sheinbaum said that “a very thorough investigation” that examined “the responsibilities of each person” in connection with the fire was carried out. She then reiterated that the exoneration of Garduño was a decision made by “judges.”

According to authorities, the fire started when two detained migrants set a mattress alight to protest poor conditions in the INM detention center. Those two men survived the blaze and face homicide charges.

The Federal Attorney General’s Office began criminal proceedings against Garduño in April 2023, alleging that he failed to fulfill his duty to “supervise, protect and provide security to the people and facilities” under his control.

In September 2025, the former INM chief issued an apology to victims and relatives of the deceased.

There were “human rights violations that never should have happened” due to “omissions by personnel of the [INM],” he said at the time.

The Associated Press reported that Garduño “called for ‘those responsible’ to be punished and for reparations to be made without recognizing his own responsibility in the tragedy.”

To date, no one has been convicted of criminal wrongdoing in connection with the deadly fire.

World.title: MND Local Puerto Vallarta: Helping out after hurricanes, planning for Día de Muertos
World.content:
By the time you read this, Puerto Vallarta will be recovering from its third consecutive hurricane in the last few weeks. First came Polo, then Rachel, and now Simón — a Category 3 storm currently making its way up the Pacific coast. Luckily, the storms’ eyes stayed offshore, sparing the city the worst impacts. Still, our malecón and beachside resorts have taken a beating from intense tidal surges and waves; many neighborhoods have flooded, and we haven’t been able to safely enjoy the beach since Sept. 23, when the first red flags were raised.

Needless to say, many residents — myself included — are feeling a bit of a hurricane hangover these days and are thinking less about going out on the town and more about helping our communities recover.

So instead of entertainment listings, this week’s events roundup highlights a few volunteer opportunities and organizations that provide disaster relief and organize cleanup efforts after major storms and throughout the year. Whether you live in Puerto Vallarta permanently, seasonally, or just vacation here from time to time, there are ways you can help residents recover through these groups.

We’ve also thrown in what we know so far about Día de Muertos happenings. Even though we’ve been thrashed around by storms lately, this is still Mexico, so the celebrations will go on come hurricanes or high water.

Disaster relief, cleanup and community support organizations

Vallarta Cares

Vallarta Cares is a local charity that mobilizes food, water, hygiene and medical supply distribution to communities affected by natural disasters, including hurricanes, floods and other emergencies. The organization also operates a year-round soup kitchen that serves hundreds of meals daily, provides weekly medical services, including free dental services, and organizes medical brigades throughout the year.

Vallarta Cares was also recently awarded first place in the interior of Jalisco category for the 2026 Premio a la Generosidad Jalisco. You can inquire about volunteer opportunities and make a donation through its website.

Limpia Tu Mar

Limpia Tu Mar organizes trash cleanups along Vallarta’s beaches, rivers and at sea. Since its inception in 2017, the group’s cleanup brigades have removed more than 900 kilograms (1,984 pounds) of plastic, 125 kilograms (275 pounds) of styrofoam, 350 kilograms (771 pounds) of glass and 5,000 kilograms (11,023 pounds) of general garbage from the sea. Each week, volunteers set sail on boats from Puerto Vallarta to remove floating trash from the ocean.

Limpia Tu Mar also hosts one of Mexico’s largest environmental awareness events, the annual International Trash Fishing Tournament. This year’s tournament is coming up Oct. 18, and registration is still open if you want to participate or help sponsor the event. With all the recent storms washing tons of trash and debris into the bay, we could use all the help we can get to clean it up.

Local collection centers and cleanup brigades

If you are in Puerto Vallarta during hurricane season (June through November), local collection centers (centros de acopio) are often set up at community centers, fire stations and churches on short notice to organize relief efforts. Joining local community and business groups on social media is one of the fastest ways to find pop-up volunteering needs immediately following a storm.

One such brigade I join regularly is the Banderas Bay Project, started by local real estate agent Luis Salazar, which organizes monthly trash pickups around Boca de Tomatlán, one of the harder-hit areas from the recent storms.

Planning for Día de Muertos

Día de Muertos — Mexico’s annual celebration honoring departed souls — is around the corner, and that means Puerto Vallarta will again be pulling out all the stops.

This year, the city is participating in the statewide Festival de Las Almas (Festival of the Souls), featuring more than 350 free events across 11 municipalities in Jalisco from Oct. 24 through Nov. 2.

In Vallarta, the city is planning 28 free events and experiences Oct. 31 through Nov. 2 along the historic center, Los Arcos, Muelle de Los Muertos, Isla del Cuale, and, of course, the Malecón, which will again feature a monumental Catrina. The giant beauty has adorned the Malecón for the past several years, each time designed by a different Mexican artist. According to the Puerto Vallarta Tourism Board, this year she will be adorned with waves, whales, manta rays and bougainvillea.

If you do plan on heading downtown for the festivities, I recommend going early before the crowds get too big. Last year, we waited until after dark to go see the Catrina and were stuck in traffic for more than an hour trying to drive from the Marina to the Malecón.

Concierto de Día de Muertos

The Vallarta Symphony Orchestra will perform with the choirs of Puerto Vallarta and the University of Brasília for special Día de Muertos concerts on Oct. 30 at the Iglesia Reina de la Paz in Marina Vallarta at 9 p.m., and on Oct. 31 at the Haramara Auditorium at Universidad Tecnológica de Bahía de Banderas in Nayarit at 7 p.m. Tickets can be purchased from IAMPV.

Debbie Slobe is a writer and communications strategist based in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco. She blogs at Mexpatmama.com and is a senior program director at Resource Media. Find her on Instagram and Facebook.

World.title: US congressional candidate says Mexico is where he gets healthcare as high costs dominate midterm debate
World.content:
Bobby Pulido, a singer and Democratic candidate for the U.S. House of Representatives in Texas’s 15th District, recently said that he does not have health insurance and has had to go to Mexico to receive medical care.

Pulido, who is running against Republican Mónica De La Cruz, made the unexpected remark to Council President and CEO Javier Palomerez during a virtual discussion on Monday with the U.S. Hispanic Business Council.

“I’m going to start off by telling you that I don’t have health insurance, Javier. And I’m embarrassed to tell you that I’ve had to go to Mexico for my health care,” Pulido said, as cited by news outlet Border Report, reportedly the only journalism outlet that accessed the meeting.

Pulido, 52, whose full name is José Roberto Pulido Jr., lives in Edinburg, a border city located in southern Texas. According to Border Report, he also owns a home in Mexico.

During the conversation, Pulido contrasted U.S. President Trump’s reported plans to boost military spending with the difficulties U.S. residents face in obtaining affordable medical care.

“I live in the richest country in the world. Now the president wants to give a million and a half trillion dollars for our military budget when we cannot provide affordable health care to our people,” he said.

Pulido’s statements did not describe what specific illness, procedure or medical emergency has brought him to seek care in Mexico. Nor does the information shared by Border Report specify which Mexican city he visits for treatment, how much he pays or the reasons why he lacks insurance in the United States.

However, this isn’t the first time Pulido has publicly shared that he has traveled to Mexico for healthcare. On Sept. 27, he told Univisión he sought medical services in Mexico due to high costs in the U.S., while questioning the power of insurance companies in that country.

Before turning to politics, Pulido had a renowned career as a Tejano singer, with a fan base spanning Mexico and the U.S. Over the course of a three-decade career, he won two Latin Grammy Awards for Best Tejano Music Album — one of which he won in November 2025.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: The Houthis and the Red Sea Explained in 2026
World.content:
Horn of Africa · Explainer

Key Facts Who they are Ansar Allah, known as the Houthis, an Iran-backed movement led by Abdul-Malik al-Houthi that has held Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, since 2014.

The attacks Strikes on ships began in November 2023, paused after the Gaza ceasefire of October 2025 and resumed against Saudi-linked shipping in 2026.

The 2026 escalation Houthi missiles and drones have struck Saudi refineries and airports since mid-2026, while the group fought for Yemen’s Red Sea coast.

The cost to Egypt Suez Canal revenue fell from about US$10 billion a year to US$3.3 billion and has recovered only to about US$4.4 billion.

Who patrols The EU’s Aspides mission escorts ships, a US-led coalition has guarded the route since December 2023, and a Saudi-led coalition fights the Houthis.

Prediction markets Polymarket gives a 30.5% chance of a Saudi-Houthi ceasefire agreement by 31 December 2026 (15 October, 6:50 a.m. ET).

Still open Who holds Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and whether UN mediation can stop the fighting.

The Houthis have turned the Red Sea into a war zone twice since 2023, first over the war in Gaza and in 2026 against Saudi Arabia. The Suez route they threaten normally carries about 15% of global maritime trade by volume, the IMF said in March 2024.

In September 2026 the Iran-backed movement seized the port of Mocha and Perim Island beside the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea. For US readers the stakes are freight rates, oil prices and American forces in nearby Djibouti.

The US aircraft carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower in the Red Sea, seen from the destroyer USS Mason on 8 January 2024 during the naval operation against Houthi attacks. (Photo: US Navy, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

Who the Houthis Are

The Houthis call themselves Ansar Allah, Arabic for Supporters of God, and take their popular name from the family of their leader, Abdul-Malik al-Houthi. The US State Department designated Ansarallah, as it spells the name, a Foreign Terrorist Organization in March 2025.

The movement has held Sanaa, Yemen’s capital, since 2014 and controls most of the northwest, says Security Council Report, an independent group that tracks the Council. Its forces also hold the Red Sea port of Hodeidah.

Facing them is Yemen’s internationally recognised government, led by Rashad al-Alimi as head of the Presidential Leadership Council and based in Aden. Saudi Arabia leads the military coalition that backs it, formally the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen.

A UN Panel of Experts reported in October 2024 that the Houthis received training, weapons and financial support from Iran, Iraqi armed groups and Lebanon’s Hezbollah. The UN has kept a targeted arms embargo on the group since resolution 2216 of April 2015.

UN sanctions experts appear to have told the Council in August 2026 that Houthi capabilities had grown as more arms were made in Yemen, Security Council Report said. Media reports, it added, placed advisers from Iran’s Revolutionary Guards beside Houthi fighters during the September offensive.

The movement is one of five overlapping conflicts in our pillar guide to Horn of Africa geopolitics. Its grip on the Red Sea coast is why it matters to Africa, Europe and American shippers.

A street in the Old City of Sanaa, the Yemeni capital that the Houthis have held since 2014. (Photo: Rod Waddington, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Why They Attack Shipping

The campaign began in November 2023, and on 19 November Houthi forces seized the Galaxy Leader, a cargo ship linked to an Israeli businessman, and held its crew. Abdul-Malik al-Houthi said in April 2024 that attacks would continue until Israel halted its offensive in Gaza.

The US State Department counted hundreds of Houthi attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden between 2023 and March 2025. The UN Security Council demanded an end to them in resolution 2722 of 10 January 2024.

Attacks ran on into late 2025, including strikes on the Liberia-flagged Scarlet Ray on 31 August and the Dutch-flagged Minervagracht on 29 September. The Houthis then stopped targeting merchant ships and Israel after the US-brokered Gaza ceasefire of October 2025.

The pause broke in 2026, after the US-Israeli war with Iran began on 28 February and the Houthis threatened in June to resume their campaign. In July, the Saudi-led coalition moved to stop an Iranian aircraft, unauthorised by Yemen’s government, from landing in Sanaa, and the Houthis answered with strikes on Saudi Arabia.

The group then declared a naval blockade of Saudi-linked shipping and struck vessels in the strait, as our report on Brent crude at US$100 describes. Strikes on Saudi energy sites followed, as told in our report on the Houthi attack on a Saudi refinery.

On 11 August the Houthis struck the Tanzania-flagged cargo ship Tihamah and killed four seafarers, the UN Secretary-General told the Security Council. On 8 September they fired missiles and drones at southern Saudi Arabia, reportedly injuring 73 people and setting fires at the Jazan refinery.

Houthi strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and on Abha airport on 7 October 2026 reportedly killed three people and wounded 36, Security Council Report noted. Two days earlier, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye agreed to put their Mecca Defense Alliance into practice, including the rapid deployment of agreed forces.

What It Has Done to Trade

Ships sailing between Asia and the Suez Canal must pass the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa. Our Bab el-Mandeb analysis explains why rival powers crowd around it.

The IMF’s PortWatch ship-tracking data showed Suez Canal trade volume down 50% year on year in the first two months of 2024. Traffic around Africa’s Cape of Good Hope surged by an estimated 74% over the same period.

PortWatch data show the slump has lasted, with Suez transits averaging about 74 ships a day in 2023 but only about 41 a day in 2026. Daily passages around the Cape of Good Hope rose from about 49 to about 91, with 2026 counted through 11 October.

Egypt pays the price, because canal tolls are one of its main sources of hard currency. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said in October 2026 that canal revenue fell from about US$10 billion a year to US$3.3 billion, before recovering to about US$4.4 billion.

Sailing round Africa adds days and fuel to every voyage between Asia and Europe. The World Container Index of Drewry, a shipping consultancy, stood at US$4,351 per 40-foot container on 8 October 2026, with Shanghai to Rotterdam at US$3,337.

The route matters more in 2026 because fighting has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf’s main oil exit. Saudi Arabia has grown more reliant on the Red Sea to ship its oil, Security Council Report noted in September 2026.

Who Patrols the Strait

The United States moved first, setting up Operation Prosperity Guardian, a naval coalition of more than 20 countries, in December 2023. US and British forces began striking Houthi targets in Yemen in January 2024, calling it self-defence under the UN Charter.

On 6 May 2025 Washington halted a bombing campaign against the Houthis, and Oman said it had brokered a truce covering attacks on ships. The Houthis said the deal did not cover their attacks on Israel.

The European Union runs Aspides, a naval operation commanded from Larissa in Greece by Rear Admiral Vasileios Gryparis. The EU’s foreign service calls its mandate defensive: it escorts merchant ships and protects them at sea rather than striking Yemen.

Saudi Arabia leads the coalition fighting the Houthis, and its spokesman, Major General Turki Al-Malki, pledged in September 2026 to take all necessary operational measures. Yemen’s government said on 5 October that it had retaken Mocha and positions near the strait with coalition air support.

Our report on how the Saudi-led coalition moved to secure Bab el-Mandeb traces that naval build-up from July 2026. On the African shore, Djibouti hosts the US base at Camp Lemonnier, home to the Combined Joint Task Force-Horn of Africa.

From left, the French frigate Forbin, the carrier USS Dwight D. Eisenhower, the destroyer USS Laboon and the Italian carrier Cavour in the Red Sea on 7 June 2024. (Photo: US Navy, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

The Africa Link

Across the Gulf of Aden, the Houthis have built ties with al-Shabaab, the al-Qaeda affiliate fighting the government of Somalia. More than 100 al-Shabaab fighters have travelled to Yemen for training in drones, weapons and explosives, Garowe Online reported in September 2026, relaying US and regional officials.

The UN Panel of Experts on Yemen reported in October 2024 increased smuggling of small arms between the Houthis and al-Shabaab. Both held weapons from the same production batches, pointing to transfers between them, a common supplier or both.

Houthi trainers have also reportedly gone to Somalia, and a Houthi delegation reportedly visited Jilib, an al-Shabaab stronghold in the south. There is no confirmed evidence that the Houthis have handed over their most advanced missiles or drones, as our report on al-Shabaab fighters trained in Yemen notes.

Perim Island, also called Mayyun, sits in the middle of the Bab el-Mandeb, facing Djibouti. The Houthis captured it on 11 September 2026, a day after taking Mocha, gaining Yemen’s west coast on the Red Sea, Security Council Report said.

That hold soon looked shaky, as government forces pushed back towards the strait in early October. Security Council Report judged that the Houthis seemed to have lost the chokepoint, though control of Perim itself has not been confirmed.

The fighting also pushes people toward Africa, and about 3,000 have crossed the strait to seek refuge in Djibouti, according to the UN refugee agency. UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on 24 September 2026 that 125,000 people had been displaced since early August.

Eritrea, whose ports of Assab and Massawa sit on the Red Sea, watches the same waters. Ethiopia’s bid for its own outlet to the sea, set out in our explainer on Ethiopia’s Red Sea demand, adds a further rivalry on the African shore.

What the Markets Say

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Polymarket bets put a 30.5% chance on a Saudi-Houthi ceasefire agreement by 31 December 2026, against 4.5% by 31 October (15 October, 6:50 a.m. ET). A separate Polymarket market on the Bab el-Mandeb being effectively closed by 31 December traded at 15.5%.

Polymarket’s market on Perim Island no longer being under Houthi control stood at 17.2% for 31 October and 34% for 31 December. On Kalshi, a CFTC-regulated US exchange, traders gave a 60% chance that over 300 ships would cross the Suez Canal in the week to 18 October.

What It Means for US Readers

Freight is the first channel for American importers, and Drewry put the rate from Shanghai to New York at US$10,220 per 40-foot container on 8 October 2026. Higher shipping costs add upward pressure on inflation, the IMF warned in March 2024.

Oil is the second channel: Red Sea routes carried about 12% of seaborne oil in the first half of 2023, the US Energy Information Administration found. With Hormuz disrupted, threats by the Houthis to Saudi Red Sea exports can move the price of gasoline in the United States.

US forces at Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti and US Navy ships in the region operate close to the fighting. Washington lists the Houthis as a Foreign Terrorist Organization, so any business dealing with the group risks US penalties.

What Is Not Known

It is not clear who now holds Perim Island, or whether Yemen’s government can keep the ground it says it retook near the strait in October 2026. Nor is it known whether UN envoy Hans Grundberg, who met Saudi, Omani, Yemeni and Houthi representatives in September, can broker a truce.

Iran’s full role, including the reported Revolutionary Guard advisers in the September offensive, has not been shown in public. How far al-Shabaab has gained Houthi drone skills is known only from officials’ accounts relayed by Garowe Online.

War-risk insurance for the strait is priced voyage by voyage and has no single public index, so the full cost to shippers is hard to measure. A return to the Suez route depends on a lasting halt to attacks, which our Horn of Africa hub tracks alongside Sudan and the rest of the coast.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why are the Houthis attacking ships in the Red Sea?

The Houthis began attacking ships in the Red Sea in November 2023, saying they acted against Israel over the war in Gaza. In 2026 they turned on Saudi-linked shipping after clashes with the Saudi-led coalition and during the US-Israeli war with Iran.

Who supports the Houthis?

Iran backs the Houthis, and UN experts reported in 2024 that the group received training, weapons and money from Iran, Iraqi armed groups and Lebanon’s Hezbollah. The UN has kept an arms embargo on the Houthis since 2015.

Is it safe for ships to sail through the Red Sea now?

Not fully, because the Houthis attacked three commercial vessels between 9 August and 9 September 2026, according to the UN Secretary-General. Security Council Report warned in October 2026 that the Houthis can still hit ships from Yemen’s northern Red Sea coast.

Do the Houthis control the Bab el-Mandeb strait?

The Houthis seized the port of Mocha and Perim Island beside the strait in September 2026. Yemen’s government said in October that it had retaken Mocha and nearby positions, but control of Perim is unconfirmed.

Sources: Security Council Report, Yemen, October 2026 Monthly Forecast, 1 October 2026; Security Council Report, Yemen: Briefing and Consultations, 8 October 2026; Security Council Report, Yemen: Emergency Briefing, 10 September 2026; Security Council Report, The Red Sea: Vote on a Draft Resolution, 12 July 2026; Security Council Report, Yemen monthly forecast, February 2024; Security Council Report, Yemen monthly forecast, 30 April 2024; US State Department, Designation of Ansarallah as a Foreign Terrorist Organization, 4 March 2025; IMF Blog, Red Sea Attacks Disrupt Global Trade (PortWatch data), 7 March 2024; Masrawy, Madbouly on Suez Canal revenue, 4 October 2026; Drewry, World Container Index, 8 October 2026; US Energy Information Administration, Red Sea chokepoints, 4 December 2023; EEAS, EUNAVFOR Aspides, accessed 15 October 2026; US Africa Command, Combined Joint Task Force-Horn of Africa, accessed October 2026; Garowe Online, Houthi and al-Shabaab ties, 8 September 2026; UN Panel of Experts on Yemen, final report (2024), 11 October 2024; IMF PortWatch, daily chokepoint transit data, data to 11 October 2026; Security Council Report, Yemen: Monthly Briefing and Consultations, 13 May 2025.

World.title: Lollapalooza Chile 2027 Santiago Guide
World.content:
CHILE · FESTIVAL GUIDE

Key Facts — Date Friday, 12 March 2027, to Sunday, 14 March 2027, the 15th edition of Lollapalooza Chile; the day-by-day lineup has not been announced yet.

— Venue Parque O’Higgins in Santiago, Chile, just south of the city centre, with Metro stops at Parque O’Higgins and Rondizzoni stations on Line 2.

— Headliners Travis Scott, Charli XCX, The Killers, David Guetta, Queens of the Stone Age and The Neighbourhood lead a bill of more than 80 acts announced on 8 October.

— Start times Set times are not out yet; Santiago runs two hours ahead of US Eastern time on Friday and Saturday, and one hour ahead on Sunday.

— Tickets Ticketmaster Chile is the only official seller; three-day passes are in the Preventa 3 phase, and single-day passes go on sale after the day-by-day lineup.

— Prices A three-day general pass costs CLP 330,400 (about US$337) including fees, or CLP 271,400 (US$276) with the Banco de Chile or Cenco Malls discount.

— Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US citizens need no visa for stays of up to 90 days, and the State Department rates Chile at Level 2, exercise increased caution.

Lollapalooza Chile has named its 2027 lineup, and half of the ten headline names are American acts. Travis Scott, The Killers and Queens of the Stone Age head to a Santiago park in March.

Lollapalooza Chile 2027 takes over Parque O’Higgins in Santiago from Friday, 12 March 2027, to Sunday, 14 March 2027. The festival unveiled its lineup on Thursday, 8 October, led by Travis Scott, Charli XCX, The Killers and David Guetta.

Three-day general passes are sold only through Ticketmaster Chile, at CLP 330,400 (about US$337) in the current phase. For US fans, the trip means a long flight south, a passport and planning around late-summer heat and big crowds.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Why This Festival Matters to US Fans

Lollapalooza began in the United States, and its flagship last ran in Chicago’s Grant Park from 30 July to 2 August 2026. Chile became the brand’s first home outside the United States in 2011, according to The Clinic, a Santiago news outlet.

The 2027 edition is the 15th in Chile, as the anniversary logo on the official poster shows. The Clinic and Marca Chile, the official country brand agency, put 2026 attendance at about 80,000 people a day.

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “US lifts sanctions on Venezuela's Jorge Rodríguez” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Five of the ten headline names are American. Travis Scott is a Houston rapper, The Killers hail from Las Vegas, and Queens of the Stone Age formed in California.

The Neighbourhood, a California band, and US singer Sombr are the other two American names on the top line. Cage the Elephant, Dominic Fike, Leon Bridges, Geese and Violet Grohl, daughter of Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl, add more lower down.

The top line also includes Charli XCX from Britain, David Guetta from France and Fontaines D.C. from Ireland. British dance act The Prodigy and Venezuelan band Rawayana complete the ten headline names.

Emol, the El Mercurio news site, named Francisca Valenzuela, Javiera Mena, Ana Tijoux, Leo Rey and Los Tetas among the Chilean acts. The official poster lists more than 80 acts in all, from British DJ Four Tet to Spanish singer Amaia.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

Dates and Start Times in US Eastern Time

The festival runs on Friday, 12 March 2027, Saturday, 13 March 2027, and Sunday, 14 March 2027. Organisers have not yet said which artists play on which day.

Gate opening and set times have not been published either. Pauta, a Santiago radio and news outlet, reported that single-day passes will go on sale only after the daily lineup appears.

Santiago keeps Chilean summer time, three hours behind UTC, until early April 2027. On Friday and Saturday, US Eastern Standard Time is five hours behind UTC, so Santiago runs two hours ahead of New York.

US daylight saving time starts at 2 a.m. on Sunday, 14 March 2027, the festival’s final day. From then on, Santiago is only one hour ahead of US Eastern time.

As an example, a 10 p.m. set on Friday or Saturday would start at 8 p.m. Eastern. The same set on Sunday would start at 9 p.m. Eastern, but no set times exist yet.

Tickets and Prices

Ticketmaster Chile is the only official seller, according to both the festival’s FAQ and the Ticketmaster event page. Organisers warn that tickets bought elsewhere may be stolen, forged or sold far above face value.

Three-day general passes are now in the Preventa 3 phase, at CLP 295,000 (about US$300) plus CLP 35,400 (US$36) in fees. The total of CLP 330,400 equals about US$337 at 981.82 pesos per dollar, the open.er-api.com rate on 15 October.

A 20% discount for Banco de Chile customers and Cenco Malls app users brings the pass to CLP 271,400 (US$276). The discount does not apply to the service charge, and each discounted tier has a limited stock.

Once Preventa 3 ends, the regular price for the same pass rises to CLP 369,600 (US$376). The official price page listed 16,410 Preventa 3 general passes in stock when checked on 15 October.

Lolla Lounge passes run from CLP 617,200 to CLP 835,600 (US$629 to US$851) across sales phases, before discounts. Platinum passes run from CLP 1,047,200 to CLP 1,306,000 (US$1,067 to US$1,330), with shade, an open bar for adults and premium toilets.

Children under 10 enter free with an adult who holds a ticket, according to the official price page. A three-day parking pass costs CLP 49,000 (US$50) on Ticketmaster, and spaces are limited.

Buying From the United States

The FAQ says buyers abroad must register on Ticketmaster, and the payment card holder must also be the account holder. Purchases from abroad are allowed until about one month before the festival, a deadline organisers say may change.

Buyers abroad can swap their ticket for a wristband only at the Will Call desk. Home delivery of wristbands is offered only inside Chile, so plan time for the pick-up in Santiago.

A peso charge on a US card may also carry a foreign transaction fee from your bank. Keep the order confirmation and your passport at hand, since wristband pick-ups require the purchase QR code and identification.

Getting to Parque O’Higgins

Parque O’Higgins is a large city park south of downtown Santiago, next to the domed arena now called Santander Arena. The festival FAQ points visitors to Metro Lines 2, 3 and 6, using Parque O’Higgins and Rondizzoni stations.

Both named stations sit on Line 2, while Lines 3 and 6 serve as connections. City buses also run nearby, and the FAQ refers riders to the Red Movilidad website for routes and times.

Free bicycle racks are available inside the grounds, according to the organisers. Driving is the hardest option, since parking is limited and sold in advance on Ticketmaster.

Each pass allows only one entry per day, so leaving the park means you cannot return that day. The only exception is for parents who register children at the Kidzapalooza family area.

International flights from the United States land at Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport, northwest of central Santiago. Allow extra time for the drive into the city, especially on a Friday afternoon.

What to Bring and What Is Banned

Bags and backpacks may hold up to 16 litres and must have a single pocket or opening, under the festival’s entry rules. Security checks every bag, and No Bag Express lanes speed up entry for those who carry none.

You may bring a reusable 500 ml bottle and one sealed half-litre plastic bottle of water. Sunscreen must be cream, not aerosol, and power banks are capped at 20,000 mAh.

Alcohol, outside food and drinks, glass, e-cigarettes, selfie sticks and laser pointers are banned. Professional cameras, drones and tripods are also barred, and the whole festival is smoke-free under Chilean law.

Mid-March is late summer in Santiago, so plan for strong sun during long afternoons outdoors. Free water stations are part of the general pass, according to the official price page.

In 2026 the festival ran a cashless wristband system loaded with Lolla Pesos. The payment setup for 2027 has not been published yet.

Safety and Entry Rules for US Visitors

The US State Department rates Chile at Level 2, “exercise increased caution,” in an advisory issued on 19 August 2026. It lists crime, civil unrest and health as the risk indicators.

The department calls petty crime common in Chile, and says street crime happens most often in Santiago and five other cities. Its list of pickpocketing hotspots includes Plaza de Armas, Bellavista and Mercado Central, all popular with visitors.

Keep phones and wallets out of sight in festival crowds and on the Metro after the shows. The State Department advises using regulated taxis with orange or yellow plates, or legal ride-share apps.

It also warns that demonstrations can start with little notice and disrupt Santiago’s buses and Metro. Check local news on festival days, and avoid any protest you come across.

US citizens need no visa for tourist stays of 90 days or less, according to the State Department. Your passport must be valid for the whole stay, with one blank page for each entry stamp.

On arrival, visitors receive a Tourist Card valid for up to 90 days, which they must hand back on departure. The department also says tourists must be able to show at least US$46 a day for expenses.

What It Means for You

For US fans, Lollapalooza Chile 2027 brings Travis Scott, The Killers and Queens of the Stone Age to one Santiago weekend. A three-day general pass costs about US$337 in the current phase, before flights and hotels.

Buy only through Ticketmaster Chile, and wait for the day-by-day lineup before planning around one artist. Book flights and rooms early, because about 80,000 people a day attended the 2026 edition.

Check the State Department advisory again before you fly, because ratings can change. Watch the festival’s official channels for set times, gate times and any change to the entry rules.

What Is Not Known

The day-by-day lineup, set times and gate opening times have not been announced. Prices for single-day passes are also unknown, because those passes go on sale only after the daily lineup.

It is not yet clear how long Preventa 3 will last before regular-price sales begin. The cashless payment system and the final entry rules for 2027 may also change before March.

Connected Coverage

The Rio Times Santiago city guide covers neighbourhoods, transport and costs for visitors and new residents. For events before the festival, see What to Do in Santiago in October 2026.

For more live music in the Chilean capital, see the overview of Santiago concerts in 2026. It covers the big arena and stadium shows on the city’s calendar this year.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Lollapalooza Chile 2027 and who is playing?

The festival runs from Friday, 12 March 2027, to Sunday, 14 March 2027, at Parque O’Higgins in Santiago. Travis Scott, Charli XCX, The Killers and David Guetta lead a bill of more than 80 acts.

How much are Lollapalooza Chile 2027 tickets?

A three-day general pass costs CLP 330,400 (about US$337) in the current Preventa 3 phase, including fees. Ticketmaster Chile is the only official seller, and single-day passes are not on sale yet.

What time is Lollapalooza Chile in US Eastern time?

Santiago is two hours ahead of US Eastern time on Friday and Saturday, and one hour ahead on Sunday. The gap narrows on Sunday because US daylight saving time starts that day, and set times have not been published.

Do US citizens need a visa for Lollapalooza Chile?

No visa is needed for tourist stays of 90 days or less, according to the US State Department. Your passport must be valid for the whole stay and have one blank page for each entry stamp.

World.title: New Order Bogotá Concert 2026 Guide
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

COLOMBIA · MUSIC

Key Facts — Date and venue British band New Order plays one night in Bogotá on Wednesday, 9 December 2026, at Movistar Arena, Diagonal 61C 26-35, beside El Campín stadium. It is the band’s first solo concert in Colombia.

— Start times Doors open at 6:30 p.m. and the show starts at 9 p.m. Bogotá time, which is also 9 p.m. US Eastern because US clocks fall back on 1 November.

— Tickets TuBoleta is the only authorised seller, and its general sale has been open since 5 August. Foreign bank cards are accepted, but those tickets are handed only to the buyer at the box office.

— Prices Listed tickets run from COP 189,000 (about US$59) to COP 699,000 (about US$220) before service fees, or about US$72 to US$264 with fees, as of 15 October 2026.

— Entry for visitors US citizens need no visa for tourist stays of up to 90 days but must file the free online Check-MIG form one to 72 hours before their flight.

— Safety Colombia carries a US Level 3 Reconsider Travel advisory, so book a ride app or a dispatched car for the late trip home instead of hailing a street taxi.

— Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.9 points (October 2026 edition).

New Order brings Blue Monday and four decades of songs to Bogotá for one December night, with tickets on sale through TuBoleta. This guide covers what US visitors need to know, from prices and card rules to transport, entry and safety.

New Order, the British band behind Blue Monday, plays Movistar Arena in Bogotá on Wednesday, 9 December 2026. The New Order Bogotá concert is the band’s first solo show in Colombia and the last date on its 2026 tour list.

TuBoleta, the only authorised ticket seller, lists tickets from COP 189,000 (about US$59) to COP 699,000 (about US$220) before service fees. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. and the show starts at 9 p.m. local time, the same as New York in December.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Who Is Playing and Why It Matters

TuBoleta’s event listing says New Order grew out of Joy Division after singer Ian Curtis died, with Bernard Sumner taking over vocals. It names drummer Stephen Morris and keyboard player Gillian Gilbert among the members who built the band.

The listing says New Order mixed post-punk with New York club sounds on its 1983 album Power, Corruption & Lies. It describes Blue Monday, released the same year, as the best-selling 12-inch single of all time.

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “US lifts sanctions on Venezuela's Jorge Rodríguez” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

For US fans, the listing also highlights the band’s recent American dates. It cites a 2022 US arena tour with the Pet Shop Boys and 2025 festival headline slots in the US and Mexico.

New Order first played Colombia at Festival Estéreo Picnic in 2013 and later returned for Festival Sónar, Publimetro and La República reported. TuBoleta dates that Sónar visit to 2016 and calls the Bogotá date the band’s first solo show in the country.

The band’s official tour page lists two São Paulo nights, on Monday, 23 November, and Wednesday, 25 November. The Fauna Primavera festival in Santiago follows on Saturday, 28 November, then Buenos Aires on Tuesday, 1 December.

Lima’s Veltrac Music Festival comes on Saturday, 5 December, four days before Bogotá closes the run. Fans planning a longer trip can also read about the extra São Paulo show the band added in Brazil.

Date, Doors and Start Times

The show is on Wednesday, 9 December 2026, with doors at 6:30 p.m. and the start at 9 p.m. local time. Movistar Arena and TuBoleta list the same times, and no second Bogotá date has been announced.

Colombia stays on UTC minus five hours all year because it does not use daylight saving time. US clocks fall back on Sunday, 1 November, so 9 p.m. in Bogotá is 9 p.m. Eastern and 6 p.m. Pacific.

The arena and TuBoleta both set the minimum age at 14. Neither page gives an end time or set length, so plan the ride home before the night begins.

No opening act has been announced for the Bogotá show. TuBoleta warns that times may change for operational or weather reasons, or on the instructions of the authorities.

Tickets and Prices for the New Order Bogotá Concert

TuBoleta states that it is the only authorised ticket operator, and the band’s official tour page links to it for Bogotá. Publimetro and Noticias Caracol name Páramo Presenta as the promoter, while TuBoleta lists Promotora Colombia SAS as responsible.

Sales opened with a Movistar Total presale on Friday, 31 July, and an Aval banks presale on Monday, 3 August. The general sale began on Wednesday, 5 August, and runs until tickets sell out.

Prices are set in two stages, and each section moves to the higher price once its stage-one allocation sells. In stage one, upper-tier Piso 3 tickets start at COP 189,000 (about US$59) plus a COP 39,000 (about US$12) fee.

The Platea, the general-admission floor, costs COP 299,000 (about US$94) plus COP 61,000 (about US$19) in stage one. In stage two it rises to COP 339,000 (about US$107) plus a COP 69,000 (about US$22) fee.

Numbered second-tier seats run from COP 339,000 (about US$107) to COP 399,000 (about US$125), depending on section and stage. The Tribuna Fan Sur, the south fan stand, costs COP 699,000 (about US$220) plus COP 142,000 (about US$45).

TuBoleta warns that prices can change with supply and demand, so these figures are as listed on 15 October 2026. Each order is limited to six tickets, and delivery charges apply to web, phone and outlet sales.

Sectors 201, 219, 301 and 319 may have restricted views, depending on how the stage is built. Sectors 206, 214, 306 and 314 are alcohol-free zones, with no sale or drinking of alcohol.

How US Visitors Can Pay

Cards issued by foreign banks are accepted from the general sale stage, which is already open. However, tickets bought with an international card are handed over only at the box office, to the buyer in person.

Carry the ID used for the order, and leave time for collection before doors open at 6:30 p.m. local time. The listing does not say which box office or opening hours apply, so ask TuBoleta customer service first.

Getting There

Visitors from the United States fly into El Dorado International Airport, the international airport serving Bogotá. US citizens need no visa for tourist stays of up to 90 days, the State Department says.

Travellers must also complete Colombia’s free online Check-MIG form between one and 72 hours before their flight. The State Department recommends a passport valid for six months and warns that Colombia may deny entry without a return ticket.

Movistar Arena stands at Diagonal 61C 26-35, beside El Campín stadium in central Bogotá. The arena tells riders of TransMilenio, the city’s bus rapid transit network, to use the station named Movistar Arena.

City buses on Calle 63 and Carrera 30 also stop nearby, and the arena offers more than 100 free bicycle parking spaces. Drivers can use partner car parks at El Campín stadium and the Palacio de los Deportes, at prices each operator sets.

The arena advises using trusted ride-hailing apps or registered taxis to get there. On a Wednesday night, demand after the show may be high, so agree on a pickup point before you go in.

Safety and Costs for Visitors

The US State Department rates Colombia at Level 3, Reconsider Travel, in an advisory issued on Tuesday, 31 March 2026. It warns that ride-by robberies of phones, bags and valuables are common.

The advisory says many US citizens have been drugged, robbed and even killed by criminals posing as dates. It also tells visitors never to leave food or drinks unattended at a bar or restaurant.

US government employees may not hail street taxis, and the State Department urges visitors to use a dispatch service or app. Bogotá is a high-altitude city, so learn the symptoms of altitude sickness before a long night out.

Inside the arena, keep the phone holding your ticket in a front pocket and carry one card with a little cash. TuBoleta notes that visibly pregnant women will not be admitted, following the recommendations of the authorities.

With fees, the cheapest listed ticket costs about US$72 and a stage-one floor ticket about US$113. Dollar figures in this guide use open.er-api.com rates of 15 October 2026, or COP 3,183 per US$1.

What It Means for You

For US fans, the New Order Bogotá concert is the band’s first solo arena show in Colombia. The cheapest listed ticket costs about US$72 with fees, and the 9 p.m. start matches New York time.

Buy only from TuBoleta, and remember that international-card tickets must be collected in person at the box office. File the Check-MIG form before flying, and use an app or a dispatched car for the ride back.

What Is Not Known

No opening act, set length or end time has been announced. The listing also does not say which box office handles international-card collections or when it opens.

TuBoleta does not show which sections have already moved from stage-one to stage-two prices. It says technical and sponsor reserves may still go on sale, so availability by section can change.

Connected Coverage

For neighbourhoods, costs and daily life in the capital, see the Bogotá city guide for expats and visitors. For other concerts and festivals this season, read what to do in Bogotá in October 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the New Order Bogotá concert?

New Order plays Movistar Arena in Bogotá on Wednesday, 9 December 2026. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. and the show starts at 9 p.m. local time, the same as New York.

Where can I buy tickets?

TuBoleta is the only authorised seller, online at tuboleta.com. Foreign cards work in the general sale, but those tickets are collected only by the buyer at the box office.

How much do tickets cost?

Listed prices run from COP 189,000 (about US$59) to COP 699,000 (about US$220) before service fees. Prices are set in two stages and rise as sections sell, so check the listing before buying.

Do US citizens need a visa for Colombia?

No, US citizens can visit Colombia as tourists for up to 90 days without a visa. They must complete the free online Check-MIG form between one and 72 hours before their flight.

World.title: Ultra-Trail Cape Town 2026 Guide
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · SPORT GUIDE

Key Facts — Date The race runs from Friday, 20 November to Sunday, 22 November 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa. Registration and the race expo open on Thursday, 19 November at the V&A Waterfront.

— Venue All six races finish at Gardens Rugby Football Club in Oranjezicht, below Table Mountain. The courses cross Table Mountain National Park and the Cape Peninsula.

— Start times The 100-mile race starts on Friday at 5 p.m. local time (10 a.m. ET). The 100 km race starts on Saturday at 4 a.m. local time (9 p.m. ET Friday).

— Entries Entries are sold through Quicket, the official seller linked from the race website. On 15 October places remained in the 100 km and 100-mile races, while the four shorter races were sold out.

— Prices The 100 km entry costs about US$331 (R5,495) and the 100-mile entry about US$392 (R6,495). The sold-out shorter races cost from about US$66 (R1,095) to US$245 (R4,055).

— How to watch in the US No US television broadcast or 2026 live stream had been announced by 15 October. Each runner’s progress will appear on live tracking on the official race website on race day.

— What it means for you A 100 km finish inside 21 hours or a 100-mile finish inside 45 hours qualifies for the 2028 Western States lottery. US citizens need no visa for stays under 90 days.

Cape Town’s big trail ultra closes the 2026 World Trail Majors season on the slopes of Table Mountain. Places remain only in the two longest races, and the refund and substitution window shuts at midday on 28 October.

Ultra-Trail Cape Town, a six-race trail running festival on Table Mountain, runs from Friday, 20 November to Sunday, 22 November 2026. The organiser lists races from 16 km to 100 miles, all finishing at Gardens Rugby Football Club in Cape Town.

For US readers, the draw is a World Trail Majors finale that an American won over 100 km last year. Finishes inside set times in the two longest races also qualify runners for the 2028 Western States Endurance Run.

Why It Matters to US Runners

The World Trail Majors is an international circuit of independent trail races, including Black Canyon Ultras in Arizona and Transgrancanaria in Spain. Its 2026 calendar, published on the circuit’s website, ends with Cape Town on 20 to 22 November.

The organiser’s UT100 page calls the 100 km event the final race of the World Trail Majors. Elite runners chasing the circuit’s season rankings therefore close their circuit season on Table Mountain.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Eritrea accuses Ethiopia of eyeing a Red Sea port” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Americans have done well here recently. Jeff Mogavero of the United States won the 2025 UT100 in 11 hours, 4 minutes and 53 seconds, iRunFar reported.

He beat Dmitry Mityaev, a neutral athlete, by 31 seconds in a sprint finish, according to Runner’s World South Africa. Tara Fraga, another American, finished third in the women’s race behind Sunmaya Budha of Nepal.

The field is broad as well as fast. IOL, a South African news site, reported that the 2025 edition drew 2,800 runners from 66 countries.

The Western States Endurance Run, a 100-mile race in California, publishes a list of approved qualifying races. It names both the Cape Town 100 km and 100-mile races of November 2026 as qualifiers for its 2028 race.

The qualifying time limits are 21 hours for the 100 km and 45 hours for the 100 miles. The 2028 qualifying window runs from Monday, 9 November 2026 to Sunday, 7 November 2027.

Prize money is modest by US road-racing standards but real. The 100-mile winner receives R80,000 (about US$4,825) and the UT100 winner R75,000 (about US$4,524), according to the race pages.

The Six Races and the Course

The organiser, Summit Events, stages six races, from a 100-miler and a 100 km down to 16 km. RMB, a bank brand of South Africa’s FirstRand group, is the title partner.

The other five races cross sections of Table Mountain, Lion’s Head, Signal Hill, Llandudno, Hout Bay and upper Kirstenbosch. Table Mountain National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage area, and the trails are steep and technical.

The 100-mile race covers 163 km, about 101 miles, with 14 aid stations and a 45-hour cut-off. It heads south to Silvermine, Kalk Bay, Simon’s Town, Kommetjie and Noordhoek before returning to Gardens.

The UT100 covers 99.1 km, about 61.6 miles or roughly 2.3 marathons. It has nine aid stations, a 26-hour cut-off and two big early climbs, on Table Mountain and Karbonkelberg.

Crews may help runners only within 100 metres of aid stations, under the race rules. The 100-mile race allows pacers on a 105.7 km section between the Llandudno and Alphen aid stations.

Race Schedule in Local and US Eastern Time

Cape Town keeps South African Standard Time, two hours ahead of UTC, with no daylight saving. US daylight saving ends on Sunday, 1 November, so race weekend sits seven hours ahead of New York.

The official race-week schedule lists the starts below, with US Eastern times added. Expected winning times are the organiser’s estimates, not guarantees.

Tuesday, 17 November: Tuesday Trails community run on Table Mountain, meeting at Kloof Corner at 5:45 p.m. local time (10:45 a.m. ET).

Tuesday Trails community run on Table Mountain, meeting at Kloof Corner at 5:45 p.m. local time (10:45 a.m. ET). Thursday, 19 November: registration and expo from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time (3 a.m. to noon ET). The venue is The Avenue, Two Oceans Aquarium, V&A Waterfront.

registration and expo from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time (3 a.m. to noon ET). The venue is The Avenue, Two Oceans Aquarium, V&A Waterfront. Friday, 20 November: Peninsula Traverse 55 km from Llandudno at 6 a.m. local time (11 p.m. ET Thursday).

Peninsula Traverse 55 km from Llandudno at 6 a.m. local time (11 p.m. ET Thursday). Friday, 20 November: Kickstarter 16 km from Beau Constantia at 8:30 a.m. local time (1:30 a.m. ET).

Kickstarter 16 km from Beau Constantia at 8:30 a.m. local time (1:30 a.m. ET). Friday, 20 November: UTCT 100-mile race from Gardens Rugby Football Club at 5 p.m. local time (10 a.m. ET).

UTCT 100-mile race from Gardens Rugby Football Club at 5 p.m. local time (10 a.m. ET). Saturday, 21 November: UT100 at 4 a.m. local time (9 p.m. ET Friday); winners expected about 1:30 p.m. (6:30 a.m. ET).

UT100 at 4 a.m. local time (9 p.m. ET Friday); winners expected about 1:30 p.m. (6:30 a.m. ET). Saturday, 21 November: Explorer 23 km from the Alphen Trail at 9 a.m. local time (2 a.m. ET).

Explorer 23 km from the Alphen Trail at 9 a.m. local time (2 a.m. ET). Sunday, 22 November: Table Mountain 35 km at 6 a.m. local time (11 p.m. ET Saturday).

Table Mountain 35 km at 6 a.m. local time (11 p.m. ET Saturday). Sunday, 22 November: prize giving at 1 p.m. local time (6 a.m. ET); last 100-mile finishers by 2 p.m. (7 a.m. ET).

Entries, Prices and Deadlines

The organiser’s entry button leads to Quicket, a South African ticketing platform, which lists Summit Events as the organiser. On 15 October, Quicket showed six entry tiers, four of them marked sold out.

The organiser’s entry page prices the 100 km at R5,495 (about US$331) and the 100 miles at R6,495 (about US$392). Those are the two tiers still in stock, while the sold-out tiers ranged from R1,095 (about US$66) to R4,055 (about US$245).

IOL reported on 8 October that the shorter distances sold out earlier in the year. It added that places remained in the UT100 and the 100-mile race, which matches the Quicket listing.

Rand amounts in this guide are converted at R16.58 per US$1, the open.er-api.com rate on 15 October 2026. A US card may add a foreign transaction fee to any payment in rand.

The deadlines are tight for anyone entering now. Under the Quicket terms, refunds fall to 30% from 2 October and end at midday on Wednesday, 28 October (6 a.m. ET).

Substitutions, upgrades and downgrades are also allowed only until that midday deadline. A substitute runner pays the entry fee plus an admin fee of R250 (about US$15).

The 100-mile race requires a finish in a trail race of at least 50 km within the previous 24 months. Runners who enter without one must email it to the organisers by midday on 28 October.

Age limits apply across the programme. Runners must be 20 or older for the four longest races, 18 for the 23 km and 16 for the 16 km.

How to Watch From the United States

No US television broadcaster or streaming service had announced coverage of the 2026 race by 15 October. The official website links to the race’s Instagram, Facebook, X and Strava accounts, but not to any video stream.

Before the 2025 race, Nova News, a South African news site, said race broadcasts would stream live on YouTube. Whether a stream will run in 2026 has not been confirmed.

The race rules say each runner’s progress will appear on a live tracking system on the official website on race day. Runners are recorded electronically at timing points along the route, so fans can follow them from home.

The timing suits early risers in the eastern United States. The UT100 leaders are expected around 6:30 a.m. ET on Saturday, with the first 100-mile finishers due minutes later.

Getting There and Getting Around

Visitors fly into Cape Town International Airport, and the race village lies in the City Bowl, the central district below Table Mountain. Its suburb, Oranjezicht, is a residential area on the mountain’s lower slopes.

The organiser says there is no parking at the race village or at any start venue. An official Park and Ride runs from Cape Town High School on Hatfield Street, Gardens, on MyCiTi buses from Thursday to Sunday.

The organiser advises allowing 30 to 45 minutes for boarding, the ride and traffic. Ride-hailing drop-off points for each start are listed on the race FAQ page.

Spectators are asked to avoid Llandudno, where parking and space are very limited. The organiser suggests cheering instead in and around Hout Bay and at the Hout Bay aid station.

Southern Sun, the official accommodation partner, offers discounted rates to spectators and families at participating hotels. The organiser names SunSquare Cape Town Gardens, close to the race village, among them.

Safety and Costs for Visitors

The US State Department rates South Africa at Level 2, exercise increased caution, in an advisory issued on 27 May 2025. It cites crime, terrorism, civil unrest and kidnapping, and warns of smash-and-grab attacks on cars.

The advisory also warns that hiking can be dangerous and that some US citizens have died doing it. It advises carrying enough water, never hiking alone and preparing for sudden weather changes.

The race is run in a spirit of semi self-sufficiency, and every runner must carry the compulsory gear list. Each missing item can bring a time penalty of 15 to 30 minutes, under the race rules.

Weather on the mountain can swing sharply even in late November, early summer in the Southern Hemisphere. The organiser warns of single-digit Celsius mornings on Table Mountain and afternoons above 30°C (86°F).

US citizens need no visa for stays under 90 days, according to the State Department. Passports need two consecutive blank visa pages and must stay valid for 30 days after departure.

Beyond the entry fee, budget for long-haul flights, several nights in Cape Town and race-week transport. Compare flight and hotel prices early, since the race falls at the start of the southern summer travel season.

What It Means for You

For US trail runners, Cape Town offers a Western States qualifier and a World Trail Majors finale in the southern summer. Only the 100 km and 100-mile places were still on sale on 15 October.

Anyone entering should act before midday on 28 October, when refunds, substitutions and the 100-mile qualifier deadline all close. Spectators should plan around the Park and Ride, since there is no parking at the race village.

Fans at home can follow the official live tracking, with the leaders due in the early morning, Eastern time. Check the State Department advisory again before you fly, because ratings can change.

What Is Not Known

Neither Quicket nor the organiser publishes how many places remain in the 100 km and 100-mile races. A final entry deadline, if places do not sell out first, is not published on the pages checked.

No 2026 elite start list had been announced by 15 October. A 2026 video stream and any US broadcast are also unconfirmed.

Connected Coverage

The Rio Times Cape Town city guide covers neighbourhoods, transport and costs for visitors and new residents. For this month’s events, see What to Do in Cape Town in October 2026.

Cricket fans can read the South Africa vs Australia Cape Town Test 2026 guide. For background, see South Africa Regions and Provinces Explained and South Africa Politics Explained.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Ultra-Trail Cape Town 2026?

Ultra-Trail Cape Town runs from Friday, 20 November to Sunday, 22 November 2026, with registration from Thursday, 19 November. All six races finish at Gardens Rugby Football Club below Table Mountain.

Can US runners still enter Ultra-Trail Cape Town?

On 15 October, Quicket still listed places in the 100 km and 100-mile races, while the shorter races were sold out. Refunds and substitutions end at midday on 28 October, Cape Town time.

What time does the 100 km race start in US Eastern time?

The UT100 starts at 4 a.m. local time on Saturday, 21 November, which is 9 p.m. ET on Friday, 20 November. The 100-mile race starts earlier, at 10 a.m. ET on Friday.

Does Ultra-Trail Cape Town qualify for Western States?

Yes, the Western States list names both the 100 km and 100-mile races of November 2026 as qualifiers for 2028. Runners must finish inside 21 hours for the 100 km or 45 hours for the 100 miles.

World.title: Nairobi’s International Theatre Festival Opens 4 November
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

KENYA · NAIROBI THEATRE FESTIVAL

Key Facts — Dates The 11th Kenya International Theatre Festival, known as KITFest, runs ticketed shows from Wednesday, 4 November, to Sunday, 15 November 2026.

— Venue and city Every listed performance is at the Kenya National Theatre on Harry Thuku Road in central Nairobi. Shows use four spaces: the Main Auditorium, Ukumbi Mdogo, Cheche and an outdoor stage.

— Start times Shows start between 11:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. Nairobi time. That is 3:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. US Eastern once US clocks change on Sunday, 1 November.

— Tickets TheatreKE is the official box office for single shows and festival passes, online at theatreke.com. A few outdoor events, such as Poetry After Lunch, are free.

— Prices Single shows mostly cost KES 500 to KES 1,800 (about US$4 to US$14). Passes run KES 2,000 to KES 13,000 (about US$15 to US$100), and Story Za Thuita charges non-residents KES 2,500 (about US$19).

— Programme The programme lists 54 performances of 41 productions from Kenya and 16 other countries. A US poetry and music show plays Friday, 13 November, at 7:00 p.m. (11:00 a.m. US Eastern).

— Not confirmed Whether any public event takes place on Tuesday, 3 November, is not confirmed. The programme of the Night Experience events included in the passes has not been published.

Kenya’s international theatre festival returns to Nairobi for a 12-day run in November. Tickets for 54 listed performances are on sale now.

The Kenya International Theatre Festival, known as KITFest, opens its 11th edition in Nairobi on Wednesday, 4 November 2026. Ticketed shows run at the Kenya National Theatre until Sunday, 15 November.

For US visitors, single tickets start at about US$4 for students, and 7:00 p.m. shows begin at 11:00 a.m. US Eastern time. Americans need an Electronic Travel Authorisation, and Kenya’s government ties a travel health insurance policy to it.

What KITFest Is and Why It Matters

KITFest is run by the Kenya International Theatre Festival Trust, a non-profit that promotes theatre in Kenya and across Africa. Its co-host is the Kenya Cultural Centre, the state agency that runs the Kenya National Theatre.

The festival’s website calls the centre the country’s oldest state cultural institution. This year’s theme, Reimagining Theatre, opens what the organisers call a new decade for the festival.

The organisers count more than 200 Kenyan artists and 184 international artists in the 2026 edition. The box office lists 54 performances of 41 productions, from Kenya and 16 other countries.

The Nairobi paper Business Daily reported that the tenth edition, in November 2025, featured more than 50 performances from 22 countries. It said an open call drew far more applications than the festival could host.

The 2026 edition is dedicated to the late Sungu Dudi, known as Terano, named as its official festival face. The organisers credit him with redefining the festival’s brand, creative identity and stage presence.

For Nairobi, the festival is also a trade fair for theatre. The KITFest African Theatre Market runs from Friday, 6 November, to Sunday, 8 November, for festival directors scouting touring work.
