This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The 2026 Programme Day by Day

The programme mixes Kenyan productions with touring work from Latin America, Europe, Asia and across Africa. All times below are Nairobi time, as published by the official box office.

Wednesday, 4 November: The Masks from South Africa at 5:00 p.m., Octopus Garden from Venezuela at 6:00 p.m. and Polish Heritage in Motion at 7:00 p.m.

Thursday, 5 November: Palunko’s Wife, a non-verbal physical comedy from Croatia, at 4:00 p.m., and After Silence from Brazil at 7:00 p.m.

Friday, 6 November: an Argentine take on Romeo and Juliet at 7:00 p.m. in the Main Auditorium.

Saturday, 7 November: Lion King Jr. Musical, a Kenyan production, at 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m., plus Guerrier from Canada at 5:00 p.m.

Monday, 9 November: Sakuntala, A Love Lore, from India at 7:00 p.m.

Wednesday, 11 November: Pyjamas for Five from Ghana at 5:00 p.m. and Batsumi, A Dirge for the Left Behind, from South Africa at 7:00 p.m.

Thursday, 12 November: Cafe Jallal Project from Israel at 7:00 p.m.

Friday, 13 November: La Mona Simona from Spain at 5:00 p.m. and the US production at 7:00 p.m.

Sunday, 15 November: two Kenyan works, Echos from the Lake at 2:00 p.m. and No Laughing Matter at 7:00 p.m., close the run.

Several events are free, including Poetry After Lunch on the outdoor stage on 5 and 12 November. A free show from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mushikishiki Vibes, plays the same stage on 11 November.

The US Production on 13 November

The only production listed from the United States is Changing the World One Poem at a Time. It plays the Main Auditorium on Friday, 13 November, at 7:00 p.m., which is 11:00 a.m. in New York.

The box office describes a multidisciplinary show that fuses dramatic storytelling, live music and original poetry. In it, Josephus moves through scenes built on live instruments, movement and call-and-response moments with the audience.

A facilitator listed as Josephus III, from the US, also appears among the festival’s workshop leaders. Another masterclass, The Director at Work, is led by Jerry Mofokeng Makhetha, who studied theatre directing at Columbia University in New York.

That directing session is listed for Friday, 6 November, and other workshops cover playback theatre and Indian Kutiyattam training. Check each workshop listing on the festival website for times and who may attend.

Tickets, Passes and Prices

The organisers name TheatreKE as the official box office for both single tickets and festival passes. Prices are converted at KES 129.73 per US$1, the open.er-api.com rate of 15 October 2026.

Single show, student ticket: KES 500 (about US$4)

Single show, early bird: KES 1,000 (about US$8)

Single show, advance: KES 1,200 (about US$9)

Single show, couple: KES 1,800 (about US$14)

Day Pass, all paid shows on one day: KES 2,000 (about US$15)

Curated 5-Show Pass: KES 4,800 (about US$37)

Week Pass, all paid shows in week one or week two: KES 7,000 (about US$54)

Season Pass, every paid show from 4 to 15 November: KES 13,000 (about US$100)

These tiers apply to the US show and most listings, but Story Za Thuita charges non-residents KES 2,500 (about US$19). Penalty sells advance seats at KES 1,500 (about US$12), so check each listing before you pay.

The Season Pass adds VIP opening and closing receptions and a complimentary festival programme. Every pass also includes entry to the festival’s Night Experience events, whose line-up has not been published.

Buy only through TheatreKE or the ticket links on the festival’s own website. Tickets offered by resellers on social media may not be valid at the door.

The Venue and How to Get There

The Kenya National Theatre sits on Harry Thuku Road in central Nairobi, the address of the Kenya Cultural Centre. Festival shows use four spaces there: the Main Auditorium, Ukumbi Mdogo, Cheche and an outdoor stage.

The State Department says ride-share apps such as Uber and Bolt are common in Kenyan cities. It advises against hailing taxis on the street and points visitors to hotel-booked services or airport kiosks.

It calls matatus, the private minibuses, and boda bodas, the motorcycle taxis, risky and bars US government staff from them. For a 7:00 p.m. show, plan your ride home before the curtain rises.

Evening traffic in Nairobi can be heavy, especially when it rains. Leave extra time if you are coming from the suburbs or straight from the airport.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

US citizens need an Electronic Travel Authorisation, applied for online at etakenya.go.ke before departure. The official portal says fees start at US$30, with standard processing taking up to 72 hours.

An expedited option costs an extra US$100 and is processed immediately, the portal adds. The government’s eCitizen insurance site says Kenyan travel health insurance is tied to the ETA for non-African travellers.

The State Department says passports must be valid for six months beyond arrival, with two blank pages. Travellers arriving from a yellow fever country must also show proof of vaccination.

The department rates Kenya at Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, in an advisory issued on 28 July 2026. It cites crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest, health and other risks, and says not to travel to Eastleigh and Kibera.

Kenyan hospitals generally do not accept US health insurance, Medicare does not pay abroad, and payment is usually due upfront. The department strongly recommends supplemental insurance that covers medical evacuation.

Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case in Nairobi in early October, and The Standard reported no curbs on public gatherings. The CDC listed no Ebola travel notice for Kenya on 15 October; recheck it and the latest Rio Times report before flying.

Kenya keeps East Africa Time all year, three hours ahead of GMT. Once US clocks fall back on Sunday, 1 November, Nairobi is eight hours ahead of New York.

Early November usually falls in Nairobi’s short rainy season, so pack a light rain jacket for the outdoor stage. Evenings in the highland capital can also feel cool.

What It Means for You

For a US visitor already in Kenya for a safari, KITFest offers an evening of world theatre for about US$9. A Season Pass at about US$100 covers every paid show over 12 days.

Expats in Nairobi can use a Day Pass at about US$15 to see several shows on one weekend day. Daytime options include Lion King Jr. Musical at 11:00 a.m. on Saturday, 7 November.

What Is Not Known

The tickets page gives the dates as 4 to 15 November, but the festival’s theatre market page says 3 to 15 November. No public performance on Tuesday, 3 November, appears on the box office.

The Night Experience line-up and the full workshop schedule have not been published in detail. Seat availability per show is not public, and the organisers have not said whether any show will be streamed.

What Comes Next

The first ticketed show, The Masks from South Africa, starts at 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, 4 November. The festival closes on Sunday, 15 November, with No Laughing Matter at 7:00 p.m.

Programme changes would appear first on TheatreKE and the festival’s own channels. Ticket holders should check their booking email in the days before each show.

Connected Coverage

The Rio Times Nairobi city guide covers neighbourhoods, transport and costs for visitors and new residents. For more events in the city, see What to Do in Nairobi in October 2026.

Before you fly, read about Kenya’s travel insurance rule for US visitors and the Kenya Security and Crime Explained 2026 pillar. For the wider arts scene, see Kenya Culture, the Key Figures to Know in 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where is the Kenya International Theatre Festival in 2026?

Ticketed shows run from Wednesday, 4 November, to Sunday, 15 November 2026, at the Kenya National Theatre in Nairobi. It is the 11th edition of the festival, under the theme Reimagining Theatre.

How much do KITFest tickets cost?

Most single shows on TheatreKE cost KES 500 to KES 1,800 (about US$4 to US$14), and a few cost more. Festival passes cost KES 2,000 to KES 13,000 (about US$15 to US$100).

Is there a US production at KITFest 2026?

Yes, the box office lists Changing the World One Poem at a Time from the United States, on Friday, 13 November. It plays the Main Auditorium at 7:00 p.m. and blends storytelling, live music and original poetry.

World.title: Alcaraz vs Fonseca São Paulo 2026 Guide
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

BRAZIL · TENNIS GUIDE

Key Facts — Date Saturday, 12 December 2026, when Carlos Alcaraz plays João Fonseca in the São Paulo Super Match, an exhibition rematch of their December 2025 meeting in Miami.

— Venue Nubank Parque, the former Allianz Parque and home of the Palmeiras football club, at Avenida Francisco Matarazzo 1705 in the Água Branca district of São Paulo.

— Start time Gates open at 2 p.m. and play starts at 5 p.m. São Paulo time, which is noon and 3 p.m. US Eastern, because Brazil no longer uses daylight saving time.

— Tickets Eventim is the official seller, online and at the stadium’s Box Office A, and it listed tickets as available on 15 October 2026, with up to six per order.

— Prices Full-price seats run from BRL 300 (about US$60) in the upper south stand to BRL 6,450 (about US$1,280) courtside, and half-price tickets start at BRL 150 (about US$30).

— How to watch in the US No US television or streaming partner had been announced by 15 October 2026, and no broadcaster had been named for any country, including Brazil.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US citizens need a Brazilian visa approved before travel, and the State Department rates Brazil at Level 2, exercise increased caution, so book early and plan your transport.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Carlos Alcaraz and João Fonseca meet again in December, this time in a São Paulo football stadium. Here is what US fans need to know about tickets, times, travel and the open questions.

Carlos Alcaraz, the Spanish world No. 3, plays Brazil’s João Fonseca at Nubank Parque in São Paulo on Saturday, 12 December 2026. The São Paulo Super Match is an exhibition, and play starts at 5 p.m. local time, or 3 p.m. US Eastern.

Eventim, the official ticket seller, still listed seats as available on 15 October, with full prices from about US$60 to US$1,280. For US fans, the trip also means a Brazilian visa approved in advance and a long flight south.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Why This Rematch Matters to US Fans

Alcaraz won the Australian Open on 1 February 2026, beating Novak Djokovic in the final to complete a career Grand Slam. The ATP Tour, which runs the men’s professional circuit, called him the youngest man in the Open Era to do so.

A wrist injury kept him out from the Barcelona Open in April until the US Open in late August. He won his first title since then in Tokyo on Tuesday, 6 October, beating Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic 7-6, 6-4.

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “US lifts sanctions on Venezuela's Jorge Rodríguez” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Fonseca stood 29th in the ATP rankings published on Monday, 5 October, while Alcaraz stood third. At Roland Garros in Paris this year, Fonseca beat Djokovic from two sets down and reached his first Grand Slam quarterfinal.

The pair played an exhibition at loanDepot park, the Miami Marlins’ baseball stadium, on Monday, 8 December 2025. Alcaraz won 7-5, 2-6, 10-8, with a match tiebreak in place of a third set, Jovem Pan reported.

The São Paulo rematch was announced on Monday, 22 December 2025, two weeks after the Miami match. Alcaraz said he was very excited to play in such an iconic stadium, InfoMoney, a Brazilian business site, reported.

For US fans, it is a chance to see the reigning Australian Open champion against a Brazilian star in a football arena. It falls in the off-season, after the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, for which Alcaraz has already qualified.

Schedule in São Paulo and US Eastern Time

The official event page sets a 5 p.m. start on Saturday, 12 December, with gates opening at 2 p.m. local time. Organisers have listed no other matches or guests on the bill so far.

São Paulo stays three hours behind UTC all year, because Brazil ended daylight saving time by decree in April 2019. US clocks fall back on Sunday, 1 November 2026, so Eastern Standard Time will apply on match day.

That puts the 5 p.m. start at 3 p.m. in New York and noon in Los Angeles. The 2 p.m. gate opening is noon on the US East Coast.

The match format has not been published, so its likely length is unclear. In Miami, a 10-point match tiebreak replaced a full third set, but no such rule has been announced for São Paulo.

How to Buy São Paulo Super Match Tickets

Eventim, the official seller, sells tickets on its Brazilian website and at Box Office A of Nubank Parque. The box office is at Rua Palestra Itália 200, Gate A, in the Perdizes district.

It opens Tuesday to Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. local time, except on holidays and event days. Processing fees apply at the box office unless you pay in cash.

A presale for Itaú bank customers began on Tuesday, 1 September, and general sale opened on Thursday, 3 September. That was a new sales round, after a first batch went on sale on 23 and 24 December 2025.

Full-price tickets start at BRL 300 (about US$60) in the upper south stand, the Arquibancada Superior Sul. Seats in the upper tier cost BRL 950 (about US$188), the official listing shows.

Lower-tier seats cost BRL 1,950 (about US$387) or BRL 2,450 (about US$486), depending on the zone. Hot Seat packages cost BRL 4,450 (about US$883), including a BRL 2,000 (about US$397) service fee.

Courtside and Itaú Baseline Seats cost BRL 6,450 (about US$1,280), including BRL 2,950 (about US$585) in fees. The Hot Seat, courtside and baseline packages include an open bar and food.

The event page also sells a Nagairô package with a Japanese dining experience from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m. local time. It has a single price of BRL 4,500 (about US$893), with no half-price option.

Half-price tickets, called meia-entrada, start at BRL 150 (about US$30), but only groups set by Brazilian law qualify. These include students, people aged 60 or over, people with disabilities and some low-income young people.

General-sale orders are limited to six tickets, including no more than two at half price. Children aged 15 or under must attend with a parent or guardian, while 16- and 17-year-olds may attend alone.

Buy only from Eventim or the box office, and avoid resellers on social media or outside the stadium. Tickets from strangers may be fake, cloned or already used.

Brazilian tickets are charged in reais, so a US card may add a foreign transaction fee. Keep the order confirmation and the card used for the purchase until after the match.

How to Watch in the US

No US broadcaster or streaming service had been announced for the São Paulo Super Match by 15 October 2026. The official event page names no broadcaster for any country, including Brazil.

In Brazil, the Miami exhibition in December 2025 aired on the pay channel SporTV and streamed on Globoplay, MKT Esportivo reported. No deal for the São Paulo rematch has been made public yet.

US viewers should follow the official accounts of both players, the event’s producer 30e and Eventim for any announcement. A stream would start around 3 p.m. Eastern on Saturday, 12 December, if one is offered.

Getting to Nubank Parque

Nubank Parque is the new name of Allianz Parque, the Palmeiras stadium in the Água Branca district west of downtown. Nubank, the Brazilian digital bank, announced the name on Monday, 4 May 2026, after a public vote.

The main rail link is Palmeiras-Barra Funda station, on Metro Line 3-Red, which also serves suburban trains and an intercity bus terminal. Viaje na Viagem, a Brazilian travel site, puts it about 800 metres from the stadium, or up to 15 minutes on foot.

The site advises leaving the station by the Avenida Auro Soares de Moura Andrade exit and walking toward Avenida Francisco Matarazzo. A bus corridor on Francisco Matarazzo also has a stop in front of the arena.

The stadium has about 1,500 parking spaces, bookable in advance through the operator Estapar, the travel site says. Two neighbouring shopping malls, Bourbon and West Plaza, also sell parking, the site adds.

Most flights from the United States land at São Paulo/Guarulhos International Airport, in a neighbouring city north-east of São Paulo. Allow plenty of time for the trip into the city, and avoid a flight that lands on match day.

Safety, Visas and Costs for Visitors

The US State Department rates Brazil at Level 2, “exercise increased caution,” in an advisory dated 31 August 2026. It warns of urban violent crime, including armed robbery, and of express kidnappings that force victims to withdraw or transfer cash.

The advisory tells visitors not to resist a robbery, to watch their drinks and to use ATMs in secure places. Keep phones out of sight in the crowds around the stadium and on the metro after the match.

US citizens need a visa approved before they travel to Brazil, the State Department says. The Rio Times Brazil visa guide for US citizens explains the electronic visa, its cost and the steps.

The State Department also asks for one blank passport page for each entry and exit stamp. Check your passport’s expiry date before you apply for the visa.

December is summer in São Paulo, and the roof of Nubank Parque covers the stands but not the playing area. Bring a light rain jacket, because organisers have not said what happens if rain interrupts play.

Conversions in this guide use 5.04 reais per US dollar, the open.er-api.com rate on 15 October 2026. Budget for a ticket priced in reais plus card fees, metro fares and the visa.

What It Means for You

For US fans, the São Paulo Super Match offers Alcaraz against a home favourite, with full-price tickets from about US$60. It falls on a Saturday afternoon, so a long weekend in São Paulo can cover the trip.

Apply for the Brazilian visa first, then buy tickets only from Eventim or the stadium box office. Book flights and a hotel early, because the match falls in the busy run-up to the holidays.

Keep checking the official event page for the format, any broadcast deal and changes to the line-up. Exhibitions depend on both players being fit, and Fonseca has struggled with injuries in 2026.

What Is Not Known

No US or Brazilian broadcaster has been announced, and the match format and length have not been published. Organisers have also not said whether rain would delay the match or move it to another date.

Fonseca stepped away from the tour in September after back, wrist, shoulder and abdominal problems in 2026, the Folhapress news service reported. He set no return date, Gazeta Esportiva also reported, so his fitness for December is not yet clear.

It is not known how many seats remain in each zone, or whether the cheapest half-price tickets have sold out. Organisers have not said whether any other matches or guests will be added to the programme.

Connected Coverage

The Rio Times São Paulo city guide covers neighbourhoods, transport and costs for visitors. For this month’s events, see What to Do in São Paulo in October 2026.

Fans planning ahead can read What to Do in São Paulo in November 2026. The profile João Fonseca, the Teen Star Reshaping Brazil’s Tennis Business looks at his commercial impact at home.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where is Alcaraz vs Fonseca in São Paulo?

Carlos Alcaraz plays João Fonseca at Nubank Parque in São Paulo on Saturday, 12 December 2026. Play starts at 5 p.m. local time, which is 3 p.m. US Eastern.

How much are tickets for the São Paulo Super Match?

Full-price tickets on Eventim run from BRL 300 (about US$60) to BRL 6,450 (about US$1,280) courtside. Half-price tickets from BRL 150 (about US$30) are reserved for groups set by Brazilian law, such as students.

How can I watch Alcaraz vs Fonseca in the US?

No US broadcaster or stream had been announced by 15 October 2026. If coverage is added, the match would start at 3 p.m. Eastern on Saturday, 12 December.

Do US citizens need a visa to attend the match in Brazil?

Yes, US citizens need a Brazilian visa approved before travel, according to the US State Department. Brazil offers an electronic visitor visa, so apply several weeks before the trip.

World.title: Kenya Petrol Jumps 6% to US$1.75 a Litre
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Energy: Kenya

Key Facts —Who. Kenya’s Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA), which sets a legal maximum pump price every month. —What. Nairobi’s maximum price for super petrol rises Sh12.93 to Sh226.96 a litre (about US$1.75, or US$6.62 a US gallon); diesel rises Sh9.90 to Sh227.76 and kerosene Sh28.49 to about Sh220. —Why. EPRA’s director-general blamed the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has pushed up the cost of imported fuel; Kenya imports all of its refined products. —When. The new caps apply from 15 October to 14 November 2026, after a September–October cycle in which prices were left unchanged. —Why it matters. Kenya is a travel and trade gateway for East Africa, and fuel feeds into transport and food costs. Rate used: US$1 = Sh129.71 (RT, 15 October 2026).

Kenya’s fuel regulator has raised pump prices sharply for 15 October to 14 November, with super petrol up 6% and kerosene up 15%. It links the rise to the conflict in the Middle East.

What EPRA Changed on 14 October

EPRA announced its monthly review on Wednesday 14 October 2026, and the new maximum prices apply from midnight. In Nairobi, super petrol rises from Sh214.03 to Sh226.96 a litre, a gain of 6%.

Diesel moves from Sh217.86 to Sh227.76, up 4.5%. Kerosene, the cooking and lighting fuel of many low-income households, jumps Sh28.49 to about Sh220, a rise of roughly 15%.

Prices differ by town because of transport costs. In the port city of Mombasa, super petrol is capped at about Sh223.8 a litre.

These are ceilings, not fixed prices. A station may charge less than the cap but never more.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on EPRA (Kenya) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Numbers in US Dollars

At Sh129.71 to the US dollar (RT, 15 October 2026), a litre of super petrol in Nairobi costs about US$1.75. That equals roughly US$6.62 per US gallon.

Diesel costs about US$1.76 a litre and kerosene about US$1.70. The month’s increase works out at about 10 US cents a litre for petrol, 8 cents for diesel and 22 cents for kerosene.

We converted every shilling figure at the same rate, so the comparisons stay consistent. Kenya’s own pump prices are set in shillings.

Why Prices Rose

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. He said it has disrupted petroleum supply chains and pushed up international import costs.

Kenya does not refine its own fuel and buys finished petrol, diesel and kerosene abroad. That leaves pump prices closely tied to global shipping and refining costs.

The rise follows a pause. For 15 September to 14 October, EPRA left all three prices unchanged, as we reported in our

earlier look at how the monthly cap works.

Who Feels It First

Higher diesel and kerosene prices tend to reach households through transport and food. Local media reported that minibus (matatu) operators are among those hit, and diesel also drives the cost of moving freight.

A matatu minibus and a traffic police officer in Kenya. File photo.

Kerosene matters most for the poorest homes, which is why a 15% rise in one cycle stands out. The next price review is due on Saturday 14 November.

For context on how much of the pump price is tax, see our report on

Kenya’s fuel price cap and the tax share. Our wider Kenya coverage tracks the cost-of-living picture.

What to Watch Next

EPRA’s next monthly review is due around Saturday 14 November, and it will show whether import costs have eased. Until then, Tuesday 20 October is Mashujaa Day, a public holiday.

Pump prices are one input into Kenya’s inflation, so the next consumer price reading will show how far the rise has spread. We will report it when the statistics office publishes.

What It Means for You

Visitors planning a safari or a coastal trip should expect higher taxi, shuttle and rental-car costs from this week. Expats living in Nairobi or Mombasa will see it first in transport and in groceries that travel by road.

Investors in East African consumer and transport companies should watch margins, since fuel is a large operating cost. In dollar terms the monthly rise is modest, at about 10 US cents a litre for petrol.

What Is Not Known

We could not open EPRA’s own notice, so prices come from Kenyan outlets that cite it and agree with each other to within a few cents. Small differences between reports, such as Sh219.85 and Sh219.87 for Nairobi kerosene, are rounding.

It is also unclear how much of the rise reflects import costs and how much reflects any change in state support for pump prices. Prices for the cycle from 15 November will depend on the oil market and on EPRA’s review.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did Kenya’s fuel prices rise on 15 October 2026?

In Nairobi, super petrol rose Sh12.93 to Sh226.96 a litre and diesel rose Sh9.90 to Sh227.76. Kerosene rose Sh28.49 to about Sh220. At Sh129.71 per US dollar, petrol costs about US$1.75 a litre.

Why did EPRA raise fuel prices?

EPRA’s director-general, Edward Mwirigi Kinyua, attributed the rise to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and raised import costs. Kenya imports all of its refined fuel.

How long do the new fuel prices last?

The new maximum prices apply from 15 October to 14 November 2026. EPRA reviews them monthly, with the next announcement due around 14 November.

Are these fixed prices at every station?

No. They are maximum retail prices, so a station can charge less but not more. Prices also vary by town, and Mombasa’s petrol cap is about Sh223.8 a litre.

What does the rise mean for travellers to Kenya?

Visitors should expect somewhat higher costs for taxis, shuttles and rental cars. The increase is about 10 US cents a litre for petrol, so the effect on a short trip is small.

World.title: Wizkid Plays Abuja’s Eagle Square on 13 December 2026
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

NIGERIA · ABUJA CONCERT

Key Facts — Date Sunday, 13 December 2026, when Wizkid headlines the Live Out Loud Music Festival in Abuja, five days before he is billed to open Detty December Fest in Lagos.

— Venue and city Eagle Square, the open-air ceremonial ground in the Central Business District of Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, where President Bola Tinubu took office in May 2023.

— Start times Gates open at 4 p.m. and Wizkid is due on stage at 10 p.m. Abuja time, which is 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. US Eastern.

— Tickets Tix Africa is the official seller, at wizkid.tix.africa and on its Wizkid Live Abuja event page. The Standard Early Bird tier had sold out by 15 October 2026.

— Prices Standard tickets cost NGN 50,000 (about US$38), and a Gold Table for eight with drinks and food costs NGN 2,562,500 (about US$1,924).

— Entry rules The night is for over-18s, and under-18s enter only with a ticketed adult guardian. There is no re-entry, bags are searched and professional cameras and drones are banned.

— For US visitors A Nigerian visa is required before travel, and the US rates Nigeria Level 3, Reconsider Travel. Abuja is not among the Do Not Travel areas.

— Not confirmed Supporting acts, Wizkid’s set length, any booking fee, refund terms and the number of standard tickets left have not been published.

Wizkid has added an Abuja homecoming show to his December in Nigeria. Tickets for the Eagle Square night are on sale now, and the early bird tier is already gone.

Wizkid headlines the Live Out Loud Music Festival at Eagle Square in Abuja on Sunday, 13 December 2026. Tix Africa, the official seller, lists standard tickets at NGN 50,000 (about US$38).

The organiser gives gates at 4 p.m. and Wizkid on stage at 10 p.m., which is 4 p.m. US Eastern. US visitors need a Nigerian visa and should read the State Department’s Level 3 advisory before booking.

Who Wizkid Is and Why This Show Matters

Wizkid is one of Nigeria’s best-known Afrobeats singers and a Grammy winner. The Recording Academy lists his 2021 Best Music Video award for “Brown Skin Girl” with Beyoncé and Blue Ivy Carter.

The academy also lists five further nominations, including “Essence” with Tems. At the 68th Grammy Awards, he was nominated for Best African Music Performance for “Gimme Dat” with Ayra Starr.

Wizkid announced the Abuja date this week with flyers on his verified Instagram account. Voice of Nigeria, the state-owned international broadcaster, reported the announcement on Wednesday, 14 October.

The Nigerian music site NotJustOk published the date, the Eagle Square venue and the Tix Africa listing on Tuesday, 13 October. The Abuja show is billed as “Wizkid Live in Abuja” within the Live Out Loud Music Festival brand.

Nova Flair Media and Entertainment hosts the event on Tix Africa and appears among the sponsors on the festival website. Heineken, Hennessy, Desperados, Trace and Transcorp Hotels are also listed as sponsors.

The Abuja night opens a busy December for the singer at home. Organisers of Detty December Fest in Lagos have billed him for their opening night on Friday, 18 December.

Eagle Square has hosted big December concerts before. Davido headlined a Heineken-backed show there on 14 December 2025, the Nigerian culture site Culture Custodian reported.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Nigeria expat life Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Tickets and Prices

Tix Africa is the only seller named by the organiser, through wizkid.tix.africa and the Tix Africa event page. Every ticket button on the festival website leads to that store.

On Thursday, 15 October, Tix Africa listed three ticket types for the night. Amounts are converted at NGN 1,331.83 per US$1, the open.er-api.com rate of 15 October 2026.

Standard Early Bird: sold out

Standard: NGN 50,000 (about US$38)

Gold Table for eight: NGN 2,562,500 (about US$1,924, or about US$241 per guest)

The Gold Table package seats eight and includes bottles of Hennessy VS, Moët champagne, Lord’s Dry Gin and Best Cream Liqueur. It also adds Heineken and Desperados mixers, ciders, water and a food platter.

The event page does not say whether a booking fee is added at checkout. Buy only from Tix Africa, since tickets resold on social media may be fake or already used.

Eagle Square and How to Get There

Eagle Square is a large open-air ceremonial ground in the Central Business District of Abuja, the federal capital. President Bola Tinubu was sworn in there on 29 May 2023, the Nigerian newsroom ICIR reported.

The organiser gives the address simply as Eagle Square, CBD, Abuja, with a map link on its website. Gates open at 4 p.m., and Tix Africa lists the programme running until 11:55 p.m.

The house rules are strict for a festival night. Entry is for over-18s, and under-18s get in only with a ticketed adult guardian.

There is no re-entry once a guest leaves the grounds, so keep the wristband on. Bags are searched at the gate, and professional cameras and drones are banned.

Abuja’s Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport lies outside the city centre, so plan the transfer before landing. The State Department says ride-share apps are safer than traditional taxis in Nigeria.

It advises checking the driver and vehicle before getting in and sharing trip details through the app. It also warns against hailing taxis on the street, especially at night.

Expect slow traffic around the Central Business District as the crowd arrives and leaves. Agree on a pickup point away from the main gate before the show ends.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

US citizens need a visa for Nigeria and must apply before they travel, the State Department says. The Nigeria Immigration Service runs an online e-Visa portal at evisa.immigration.gov.ng.

Passports must be valid for at least six months beyond arrival, with one blank page for each entry stamp. Travellers older than nine months must show yellow fever and polio vaccination certificates on arrival.

Cash above US$10,000 must be declared on entry and exit, the department says. Dual nationals need a valid Nigerian passport to leave the country.

The State Department rates Nigeria at Level 3, Reconsider Travel, in an advisory issued on 12 June 2026. The Federal Capital Territory, which includes Abuja, is not among its Do Not Travel areas.

The department warns that terrorists target crowds at large public events, including celebrations and sporting contests. It also says violent crime is common throughout Nigeria and kidnappings for ransom happen often.

US government help is limited outside Abuja, Lagos and their surroundings, the department notes. It urges travellers to enrol in its Smart Traveler Enrollment Program before departure.

Nigeria runs on West Africa Time, one hour ahead of GMT, with no daylight saving time. In December, Abuja is six hours ahead of New York.

What It Means for You

For a US fan planning a Nigerian December, the Abuja show adds a second Wizkid date at about US$38 a ticket. Pairing it with the Lagos festival opening on 18 December lets one trip cover both cities.

The bigger costs are the visa, the flights and safe transport, not the ticket itself. Book a ride-share or a hotel car for the return trip, since the programme ends close to midnight.

What Is Not Known

No supporting acts have been announced, and Wizkid’s set length is not published. The event page also does not show how many standard tickets remain or what the early bird tier cost.

The festival website pairs the date with Saturday, but 13 December 2026 falls on a Sunday, as Tix Africa shows. Tix Africa also labels its 5 p.m. to 11:55 p.m. programme UTC, while NotJustOk gives those times as Abuja time.

Refund terms are not stated on the event page, and it is not known whether the concert will be filmed or streamed. The Nigerian news site PM Parrot says details of other performers and further dates are expected in the coming weeks.

What Comes Next

The next step is the announcement of supporting acts on the festival website and Tix Africa. Five days after Abuja, Wizkid is due to open Detty December Fest in Lagos on Friday, 18 December.

Any change to gates, set times or the date would come from the organiser and Tix Africa. Buyers should keep the confirmation email and check their Tix Africa account in the week before the show.

Connected Coverage

For the Lagos leg of a December trip, the Rio Times Lagos city guide covers neighbourhoods, transport and costs. The Lagos festival Wizkid opens is covered in Detty December Fest Lagos Runs 18 to 30 December.

For events in the capital this month, see What to Do in Abuja in October 2026. Safety background is in Nigeria Security and Crime Explained 2026.

For the wider picture, Nigeria Explained covers the country, its politics and its economy. Nigeria Culture, the Key Figures to Know in 2026 profiles the artists shaping its music scene.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where does Wizkid play in Abuja?

Wizkid headlines the Live Out Loud Music Festival at Eagle Square in Abuja on Sunday, 13 December 2026. Gates open at 4 p.m., and he is due on stage at 10 p.m. local time.

How much are tickets, and who sells them?

Tix Africa is the official seller, with standard tickets at NGN 50,000 (about US$38). A Gold Table for eight costs NGN 2,562,500 (about US$1,924).

Do US citizens need a visa to attend?

Yes, the State Department says US citizens need a visa for Nigeria and must apply before they travel. The Nigeria Immigration Service runs an online e-Visa portal for applications.

World.title: Costa Rica Moves 2,700 Corals Deeper to Escape El Niño Heat
World.content:
Scientists in Costa Rica have moved 2,700 corals into deeper water in the Gulf of Nicoya to shield them from ocean heat driven by El Niño. Warming Pacific waters are raising the risk of bleaching on the reefs. The corals belong to the restoration project run by the State Distance University (UNED) at Isla Tortuga, off the southern tip of the Nicoya Peninsula. Researchers relocated them from about 5 meters (16 feet) down to 13 meters (43 feet), where the water stays cooler than near the surface.

UNED researcher Yeison Lizano Rojas, who leads the Isla Tortuga project, said El Niño is already putting Costa Rica’s corals under heat stress. The university warned that if high temperatures persist, that stress can lead to bleaching and, eventually, to the death of the corals. Bleaching happens when heat breaks down the partnership between corals and the microscopic algae that live in their tissue. Those algae, known as zooxanthellae, supply most of the coral’s food and energy.

Under prolonged stress, the coral expels them, loses its color and weakens. A bleached coral is not necessarily a dead one. According to UNED, some corals recover once water temperatures return to normal, which is why the team is trying to buy them time in deeper, cooler water. The team has also paused the routine work of the nursery.

Coral gardening, fragmentation and the installation of new structures are on hold, while monitoring of bleaching, water temperature, salinity and other conditions has been stepped up. Lizano said extreme heat is one of the main challenges facing marine conservation. He stressed that restoration and scientific monitoring are what allow reefs to become more resilient.

The threat reaches well beyond Costa Rica. In June, the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration warned that El Niño could trigger a fifth global coral bleaching event, with the eastern Pacific at greatest risk. NOAA said El Niño could raise Pacific sea surface temperatures by more than 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit), and put the chance of mass bleaching in the region between June and September at 60% to 90%.

The two most recent global bleaching events, in 2023 and 2025, affected 84% of the world’s reef area, according to NOAA. The Isla Tortuga project began in mid-2024 as a partnership between UNED’s Puntarenas campus, the National Learning Institute (INA) and tour operator Bay Island Cruises, which provides boats and logistics.

By June 2025, the team had planted its 2,000th coral and installed 43 nursery structures, and UNED reported that the cultivated corals were growing up to four times faster than corals in the wild.The relocation comes in a week of contrasting news for Costa Rica’s reefs. Days earlier, researchers raised coral larvae in Costa Rica for the first time. On land, El Niño has also been linked to the rainfall deficit that has left Guanacaste drying out this year.

Healthy reefs feed and shelter fish, protect coastlines and support the diving, snorkeling and fishing that coastal communities around the Gulf of Nicoya rely on. UNED warned that losing them would ripple through the marine species that depend on reefs for food, shelter and reproduction, and through the fishing and tourism built around them.

World.title: Some Liberia Hospital Patients Have Waited Nearly a Week in a Chair for a Bed
World.content:
Patients at Hospital Enrique Baltodano Briceño in Liberia, the main public hospital for Guanacaste, say they have spent days sleeping in emergency-room chairs while waiting for a bed. Images and video shared by a patient show more than 10 people asleep in chairs in the hospital’s emergency area in the early hours of Tuesday.

They are dressed in hospital gowns and covered with sheets, some connected to IV stands, with their names written on paper taped to the wall or the backs of the chairs. One patient said he had been waiting five days and did not know what would happen next with his care. Another, in a separate video, said he had been waiting six days.

A young man with an 8-millimeter (0.3-inch) kidney stone said Monday that he had been sitting in a chair since the morning of Friday, October 9, waiting to be admitted so a urologist could see him. He estimated that about 30 people were in the same situation and said some were sleeping on the floor on improvised sheets because no stretchers were available.

The same patient said the public health system had scheduled his ultrasound for 2028, so his employer paid for one with a private doctor before he went to the hospital. The Costa Rican Social Security System (CCSS), which runs the hospital, had not responded to questions from local media sent Monday morning, and the hospital has not commented publicly.

The strain is not new. In December 2025, then-CCSS executive president Mónica Taylor told a legislative commission that the Liberia emergency department was collapsed and saturated and acknowledged that the institution had not even prioritized a project to expand it. At the time, the emergency department was running at 143% of capacity, the fifth most overcrowded in Costa Rica, according to figures presented to lawmakers. Hospitalization and surgery beds were 91% to 100% full, and some patients remained in the emergency department for up to 15 days.

A plan to expand and remodel the hospital’s emergency service dates to 2013 but had not reached the pre-investment stage as of late 2025. The hospital serves the entire Chorotega health region. Waiting is a national problem for the CCSS. The institution had 1,476,536 cases on its waiting lists as of July 31.

The CCSS has not said how many patients are currently waiting for beds in Liberia or when the expansion project will move forward.

World.title: Belize Water Services showcases automated water and ice vending pilot project at Regional Conference
World.content:
Belize Water Services showcases automated water and ice vending pilot project at Regional Conference

By Zoila Palma: Belize Water Services Ltd. (BWS) showcased its innovation in water accessibility at the 35th Annual Caribbean Water and Wastewater Association (CWWA) Conference and Exhibition, where Senior Project Manager Amber Gongora presented the company’s automated water and ice vending machine pilot project in San Pedro.

The initiative provides residents with convenient access to safe and affordable drinking water and ice through an advanced reverse osmosis filtration system. The pilot project aims to improve affordability for island families while offering an accessible option for obtaining drinking water and ice.

Beyond improving access to these essential supplies, the project introduces a sustainable revenue model designed to support future water network expansions and infrastructure development. The approach seeks to connect improved customer access with long-term investment in water services.

BWS continues to explore innovative solutions to strengthen water accessibility, affordability and sustainability across Belize.

World.title: FCD and PACT explore Cebada Cave in the Chiquibul
World.content:
FCD and PACT explore Cebada Cave in the Chiquibul

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Friends for Conservation and Development (FCD) and personnel from the Protected Areas Conservation Trust and Belize Nature Conservation Fund (PACT/BNCF) have visited Cebada Cave in the Chiquibul National Park.

Cebada Cave is the third section of the Chiquibul Cave System, recognized as the largest known cave system in Central America.

The visit was part of a project implemented by FCD with funding from the Belize Nature Conservation Fund.

It highlighted the work of FCD’s Karst rangers, who document, monitor and protect the park’s fragile underground environments with guidance from the Institute of Archaeology at NICH.

FCD says the Chiquibul is more than a protected forest. Its caves and archaeological sites preserve traces of the ancient Maya, including their ceremonial practices, traditions and beliefs.

World.title: Prime Minister says China’s sanctions “uncalled for” and “unjustified”; reiterates Belize’s support for Taiwan
World.content:
Prime Minister says China’s sanctions “uncalled for” and “unjustified”; reiterates Belize’s support for Taiwan

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceno is leading a high level delegation at the 2026 World Bank and IMF meetings in Thailand.

And, during an interview with Focus Taiwan, PM Briceno said that China’s sanctions against Foreign Affairs Minister Francis Fonseca were “uncalled for,” “unjustified,” “wrong” and “illegal.”

“We are very concerned and disappointed that China would take such a position,” Briceño added.

“We believe that we are an independent country and, as an independent country, we should be allowed to make our own decisions,” he said. “We believe that we are doing the right thing by standing with Taiwan.”

The Prime Minister further reiterated Belize’s support for Taiwan.

World.title: International News: CARICOM observes Caribbean Statistics Day under theme of strengthening resilience
World.content:
International News: CARICOM observes Caribbean Statistics Day under theme of strengthening resilience

By Zoila Palma: The Caribbean Community (CARICOM) is observing Caribbean Statistics Day on October 15, 2026, under the theme “Harmonizing Data, Strengthening Resilience,” highlighting the importance of reliable and comparable statistics in regional development and decision-making.

CARICOM Secretary-General Dr. Carla Barnett highlighted the importance of high-quality, harmonized statistics in helping Caribbean countries respond to challenges and strengthen resilience. “Our collective resilience and overall sustainable development depend on our shared ability to know, measure and act,” Barnett said.

Caribbean Statistics Day is observed annually to highlight the critical role of statistics in regional integration and sustainable development.

World.title: Friends for Conservation and Development, conservation partners visit Cebada Cave to protect Maya Heritage
World.content:
Friends for Conservation and Development, conservation partners visit Cebada Cave to protect Maya Heritage

By Zoila Palma: Personnel from Friends for Conservation and Development (FCD) and the Belize Nature Conservation Fund (BNCF) recently visited Cebada Cave, the third section of the Chiquibul Cave System, as part of efforts to protect Belize’s natural and cultural heritage. The visit formed part of a project implemented by FCD with funding from BNCF.

The Chiquibul National Park is home to caves and archaeological sites that preserve evidence of ancient Maya ceremonial practices, traditions, beliefs and way of life. The Chiquibul Cave System is recognized as the largest known cave system in Central America, making the protection and monitoring of its fragile underground environments important to safeguarding the country’s heritage.

The visit highlighted the vital role of FCD’s Karst rangers in documenting, monitoring and protecting these underground environments, with guidance from the Institute of Archaeology under the National Institute of Culture and History (NICH).

World.title: Belize Culture Fund supports 24 cultural and creative initiatives nationwide
World.content:
Belize Culture Fund supports 24 cultural and creative initiatives nationwide

By Zoila Palma: The National Institute of Culture and History (NICH) hosted the 2026 Belize Culture Fund Grant Awards, celebrating 24 individuals and institutions receiving funding to preserve, protect and promote Belize’s rich cultural heritage.

This year, the Belize Culture Fund doubled its allocation to BZD $60,000, providing 20 grants of $2,000 each and four Institute Grants of $5,000 each. The funding is intended to support cultural initiatives and strengthen Belize’s creative and cultural sectors.

Francis Fonseca, Minister of Culture, delivered the keynote address, expressing appreciation to the grant recipients for their steadfast commitment to culture in all its forms. He reminded recipients that “Culture is WHO and WHAT we are,” highlighting the importance of protecting Belize’s cultural identity for future generations.

Councilor Eliude Miller also congratulated the 24 recipients, recognizing their creativity, dedication and passion for keeping Belizean culture vibrant.

World.title: PM Briceno: “Energy security is urgent priority
World.content:
PM Briceno: “Energy security is urgent priority

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceño says energy security remains an urgent priority for Belize, with his Government determined to expand the country’s energy capacity through support from the Millennium Challenge Compact (MCC) and its partnership with the United States.

In a video message shared on Facebook while attending the 2026 World Bank-IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, Briceño emphasized the importance of reliable electricity for Belizeans and the need to strengthen the country’s energy capacity.

“Energy security is another urgent priority. Belizeans deserve reliable electricity we are determined to expand our energy capacity supported by the millennium challenge compact and our partnership with the US,” Briceño said.

Energy security was also discussed during Briceño’s October 13 bilateral meeting with Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) President Ilan Goldfajn. Their discussions covered efforts to address high electricity costs, expand renewable energy generation, strengthen transmission infrastructure and advance regional energy integration through SIEPAC.

The meeting also addressed support for Belize Electricity Limited (BEL), the submarine cable upgrade to San Pedro and opportunities for increased IDB technical and financial engagement in Belize’s energy sector.

World.title: Strengthening Agriculture means protecting livelihoods and food security, Prime Minister says
World.content:
Strengthening Agriculture means protecting livelihoods and food security, Prime Minister says

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceño says Belize is seeking international support for small and medium-sized farmers as his Government works to strengthen agriculture, protect livelihoods and safeguard food security.

In a video message shared on Facebook while attending the 2026 World Bank-IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, Briceño highlighted the importance of securing support that delivers tangible benefits for Belizeans.

“We are also seeking support for small and medium sized farmers they have endured repeated hardships, strengthening agriculture means protecting their livelihoods and our food security,” Briceño said.

Strengthening the sector is also essential to protecting the livelihoods of farming families and maintaining Belize’s ability to produce food.

Briceño said Belize’s delegation is working to ensure the country’s needs are heard and addressed during the international meetings, as the Government pursues partnerships and support for national development priorities.

World.title: Guilty by report?
World.content:
CHUCK... questioned whether the Integrity Commission’s practice of publicly identifying categories of people whose matters have been referred to it could fuel perceptions of corruption

JUSTICE Minister Delroy Chuck has questioned whether the Integrity Commission’s (IC’s) practice of publicly identifying categories of people whose matters have been referred to it could fuel perceptions of corruption, even when those matters do not result in findings of wrongdoing.

Speaking at Wednesday’s meeting of Parliament’s Integrity Commission Oversight Committee, Chuck argued that reporting such figures could create an impression of widespread corruption even when investigations might not lead to charges.

“You must say how many investigations you have started and so on, but when you start, if you see in your report that you’re investigating permanent secretaries, you have… 18 or so permanent secretaries, even if you have three where you’re investigating, all of them come under scrutiny, and so when you say you’re investigating six, nine parliamentarians, every single one of us come under scrutiny,” he expressed.

The minister questioned whether the commission’s reporting approach was helping or hurting Jamaica’s efforts to fight corruption, arguing that the public needed to see clear results from investigations, rather than repeated references to matters still being examined.

He also questioned whether the country was getting value for money from the anti-corruption body, given the resources spent on its work and the need to demonstrate progress in tackling corruption.

“Because all I’m really saying is, yes, if there is corruption, expose it, find it, but… far too many of your reports are actually saying you are investigating, and at the end of the day nothing comes of it, or you don’t hear about it, and I am concerned, because when people speak about corruption, they should at least be able to say we have investigated these, we have charged so many for failing to report,” Chuck said.

However, Opposition spokesman on finance Julian Robinson rejected the suggestion that the commission should be blamed for the effects of its reporting, arguing that public accountability required it to explain the work it was doing and the progress of its investigations.

Robinson said the commission had to report on the nature of matters referred to it, while the public should also question why so many matters were being brought to its attention.

“As far as I know, you get to an investigation, having gone through a process, and you have met a particular threshold to determine that somebody

should be investigated. Part of your accountability mandate must be to report where you are in a process, which means whether it is public officials, parliamentarians, you must indicate of the number, how many have reached so-and-so, so I don’t share the view that the issue is with the Integrity Commission. If there are a lot of people under investigation, then the issue must be why are there so many people under investigation?” Robinson questioned.

The debate prompted director of investigation at the Integrity Commission Kevon Stephenson to explain the distinction between matters referred to the commission and cases that proceed to a formal investigation.

Stephenson said not every complaint or referral led to an investigation, as each matter had to be assessed before a decision was made. He told the committee that only a small fraction of matters referred to the commission proceeded to investigation.

“I think the public could appreciate that when matters are reported to the commission as under [Section] One of the Second Schedule, there is no guarantee that those complaints will be investigated, because an assessment has to be done on each of those complaints for a decision to be made under Section 47 of the legislation as to whether an investigation will be conducted,” Stephenson said.

He added that investigations could also be discontinued if the evidence did not provide a sufficient basis to continue. In those circumstances, the director of investigation was required to issue findings to the commission, but those findings were not made public.

Stephenson said reports reached Parliament when a completed investigation found a breach of a code, policy or law. He also explained that the annual report’s description of matters referred to the commission should not be interpreted as a list of cases actively under investigation.

Stephenson suggested that if Parliament is dissatisfied with what the law required the commission to include in its annual report, any change in policy would need to be reflected in legislation.

In the meantime, committee Chairman Pearnel Charles Jr said the concerns about reputational damage had to be considered without restricting the commission’s work.

“The commission must fearlessly carry out its work. But fear perhaps can be spelled in two ways, F-E-A-R and F-A-I-R. So as you fearlessly carry it out, it must be fair to the persons who you may have thoughts of, but not established evidence about,” Charles Jr said.

Furthermore, director of information and complaints at the commission Joeth Jones also criticised the media for what she described as a failure to give sufficient attention to positive compliance findings in the commission’s reports.

Jones said parliamentarians had performed relatively well in meeting their statutory obligations, but argued that this aspect of the commission’s work was not receiving adequate coverage.

“The media does not pick up that,” Jones told the committee, referring to the group’s compliance performance.

World.title: Secret location
World.content:
CHANG... we handed them over to The International Organisation for Migration and they made arrangements for them as to where they are to stay (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

THE location of the first batch of 22 third-country nationals (TCNs) that arrived in the island on Monday will remain concealed says National Security Minister Dr Horace Chang.

Responding to questions posed by journalists at a post-Cabinet media briefing at Jamaica House Wednesday, Chang maintained that though he is aware of where the TCNs are being housed, it’s not his “privilege” to announce where they are.

“I cannot give you their housing. We handed them over to International Organisation for Migration (IOM) and they made arrangements for them as to where they are to stay. The officers were in Jamaica and they looked at a number of hotels; they now have the responsibility of where they are to stay. In fact, they can move them at anytime,” said Chang.

The group, which arrived under an agreement signed between the Jamaican and United States (US) governments in June this year, comprises of 15 males and seven females, representing seven nationalities.

According to the Government, under the agreement, up to 25 asylum seekers who have unresolved migration cases in the US will temporarily transit through Jamaica en route to their home countries every two weeks.

But Chang on Tuesday shared that he is unaware of when the next batch of TCNs will arrive.

“I cannot tell you when others will arrive. We have a 14-day gap. As I’ve indicated, we can get another trip after 14 days, but there’s no guarantee. It’s not like these are designated numbers as we have with the involuntary returned migrants that we receive — our own citizens. Every two weeks, we know we get a batch, a flight, anywhere from 50 to 75 individuals. The TCNs depend on the number which might penetrate the barrier getting into the United States, as well as where they are from and what the State Department will decide or Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) will decide where they’re sending them and to which country,” he said.

According to Chang, no limitations will be placed on the TCNs during their stay in the country.

“They are individuals from different cultures, and what they do is up to them. They are here as visitors and they are working closely with the IOM in terms of conveying relevant information. The IOM will extract the information they require to prepare them for transit to their home country. They are free to do as they wish, like any visitor to Jamaica.

“They are individuals, who just like you in this room are regular working people who have sought to migrate, but done so illegally to the United States. The ones we accept, there are no criminals in there. They’re just families looking for a better life and we are accommodating their transition back home,” Chang reiterated.

Responding to concerns about the number of people who may want to seek asylum, Chang told journalists that the issue is not one of the Government but that of the institution which deals with the applications.

“The commissioner that deals with asylum or refugee status is a public body. It’s like a court. The documents are available. And I’m not saying we’ll not say how many…It’s their right to do so. And if they do so, it will be established. The asylum committee will sit, and the public will have access to it,” he said adding that the process can be lengthy, but the Government will notify the public as the numbers are available.

“They may ask to stay without going to asylum. It’s their freedom to do so. They are here as visitors, and if they have a skill set that is in high demand, they may. Doesn’t mean we have to accept it, but they can apply for that as well as apply for refugee status. They have a number of options,” he said.

According to Chang, their options will be discussed with them by the IOM.

“The IOM will interrogate and not only make arrangements for their movement, if they seek other alternative arrangements, then the IOM will inform us and we take it from there. But that is an important part of the nature of the IOM. As indicated, the United Nations body, they do this kind of activity globally as a trusted organisation in humanitarian relief activity. And, therefore, we allow them to proceed without any interference,” he said.

World.title: Sizzla, Chronic Law among acts for Smooth Thoughts rhythm
World.content:
Chronic Law.

After two years of planning and production, eastern entertainment Promotions is gearing up for the release of its latest musical project, Smooth Thoughts rhythm, on Friday, October 16.

The project features an impressive line-up of established and emerging dancehall acts, including Sizzla, Chronic Law, Skippa, Nation Boss, Silk Boss, Shawn Storm, Karnage, Hot Turbine, Lisa Hyper, and Krish Fullforce.

According to Judah Nugent, of Eastern Entertainment Promotions, the rhythm represents another milestone for the entertainment company, which has spent the past 14 years contributing to Jamaica’s music and entertainment landscape.

“It took us approximately two years to complete the project. One of the main factors was the availability of some of the artistes, as everyone has their own schedules and professional commitments,” Nugent explained.

“Coordinating the different artistes and ensuring that everything came together took time, but we remained committed to seeing the project through. We believe good things take time, and we are excited to finally share Smooth Thoughts rhythm with the world,” he added.

Eastern Entertainment Promotions serves as executive producer of the project, overseeing its development, artiste coordination, and overall production. Nugent said the decision to assemble such a diverse line-up was deliberate, as the team wanted to capture different musical styles and perspectives while maintaining a cohesive sound.

“We wanted to bring together a diverse group of artistes, each with their own style, personality and musical identity. Every artiste brings something different to the rhythm, and that variety allows listeners to experience different perspectives and expressions within one cohesive project,” he said.

While dancehall rhythms are often associated with Chronic Law high-energy entertainment, Nugent explained that Smooth Thoughts rhythm was conceptualised to offer listeners a more reflective musical experience.

“The name Smooth Thoughts really speaks for itself. This is the type of project you can sit back with, relax, spend time with your thoughts, and genuinely resonate with each track,” he shared. “Music is not always just about dancing and having a good time; it can also be about personal experiences, reflection, and connecting with something that speaks to you.”

Adding to the excitement surrounding Friday’s release will be the world première of Chronic Law’s official music video for Streets, which will debut on the same day.

Nugent explained that the coordinated releases form part of a wider promotional strategy aimed at generating greater visibility for the project and encouraging listeners to explore the contributions of the other artistes.

“Chronic Law has a strong connection with dancehall audiences, and we believe the video première will generate excitement and help draw attention to the wider rhythm project,” he said. “Pairing the two releases gives fans more than one reason to engage with the music on the day. Our intention is to create a coordinated release moment that encourages people to watch the video, discover the rhythm, explore the other tracks, and support all the artistes involved.”

Founded in 2012, Eastern Entertainment Promotions has established a presence in Jamaica’s entertainment industry through event staging and music production. Its previous musical projects include Heaven Gates rhythm.

For Nugent, the latest release underscores the company’s commitment to creating opportunities for Jamaican entertainers while expanding its reach beyond the island.

He is particularly hopeful that Smooth Thoughts rhythm will attract international attention and enjoy longevity in an increasingly competitive music industry. “We want the project to receive strong support from fans, DJs, radio personalities, streaming audiences and the wider music industry.

We also hope it creates greater exposure for the artistes involved and opens doors to new opportunities for everyone who contributed to making it happen,” he said. “Ultimately, we want the rhythm to have longevity. We do not want it to be something people listen to only on release day. We want listeners to keep returning to it, discovering their favourite tracks and sharing the music with others.”

The project is expected to be available across major digital streaming platforms, subject to final distribution arrangements.

Meanwhile, Eastern Entertainment Promotions is also preparing for the 12th staging of its signature event, Eastern Extravaganza, scheduled for New Year’s Day, January 1, 2027.

Nugent said the event remains an important part of the company’s journey, with further announcements expected in the coming months.

World.title: Chilling confession
World.content:
Ruddock was heard on video telling detectives that he was instructed by his now deceased pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, pictured here, to carry out the gruesome, human-sacrifice killing of Taneka Gardner.

A seven-member jury in the Andre Ruddock murder trial in the Home Circuit Court in downtown Kingston on Wednesday watched video recording of the accused appearing composed as he admitted to detectives that he cut the throat of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner on October 17, 2021 at Pathways International Restoration Kingdom Ministries in Albion, St James.

Ruddock was heard in the video telling the detectives at a police station in St James, in the presence of two justices of the peace, that he was instructed by his now deceased pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, to carry out the gruesome, human-sacrifice killing of Gardner at the church.

In the video, Ruddock was seen calmly answering the 42 questions posed to him by detectives as he gave them a picture of what led up to him cutting Gardner’s throat.

Ruddock was even seen sipping what appeared to be water from a 1.5 litre bottle as he sat with his back against a wall.

The detectives did not appear to be aggressive towards him, and neither did it appear that he was forced or threatened in any way to say what he told them and the justices of the peace.

Ruddock was asked questions and he provided the responses. After the questions and answers were read out to him, Ruddock was invited to sign the document, which he stood up and completed on the table that was before him and the detectives.

One of the detectives thanked Ruddock for cooperating with them and expressed that he wished everything worked out well for him.

After the playing of the video in court, prosecutor LaToya Bernard continued her examination-in-chief of a detective corporal who was one of the two detectives present inside the room with Ruddock and the two justices of the peace. She invited him to tell the court what he did after Ruddock signed the question-and-answer document.

The detective said he packed up the video recording equipment and created two DVDs which contained all that Ruddock told them.

The prosecutor then went on to ask the witness where he was on October 21, 2021 and what activities he carried out in relation to the case.

The detective, who is now at the rank of corporal, asked to see his written statement which he gave in the matter in order to refresh his memory.

He was shown the statement and then he began to explain that he and another detective were given certain instructions by a superior.

He explained that electronic items taken from the murder scene were transported to the police’s cybercrime division where they were handed over to an analyst.

“Items included cell phones, cameras, a digital video recorder and memory cards. The analyst gave me a receipt in return and I subsequently handed over the receipt to Detective Inspector McLeod on my return to the Falmouth Police Station,” he said.

He explained that he saw the body of Taneka Gardner more than once after it was removed from the church.

“After making arrangements with the father of Taneka Gardner, I met with him at the Archer’s Funeral Home located in Spanish Town, St Catherine. We were there for the post-mortem of Taneka Gardner,” he said, explaining that a pathologist confirmed to him that Gardner’s death was as a result of a slash to the throat.

World.title: THERE’S HOPE!
World.content:
West Indies’ Captain Shai Hope plays a shot during their fourth T20 international cricket match against India at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad, India, on Wednesday. (Photo: AFP)

HYDERABAD, India (CMC) — West Indies Captain Shai Hope produced another scintillating knock while Keemo Paul came up trumps with the ball as the regional side carved out a 24-run win over host India here in the fourth T20I on Wednesday.

Shai Hope’s latest century, his fourth of the trip, helped to propel the men in maroon to 247 for three while Paul’s five-wicket haul, supported by Gudakesh Motie’s restrictive spell, sent the series into a decider in Bengaluru as India could only manage to get 223 on the newly laid Hyderabad pitch.

Put in to bat, Hope combined with Jewel Andrew to get things going quickly against an unchanged India side. The teenager immediately set the tone, crunching a clean six off Arshdeep Singh’s second ball.

A 17-run over gave West Indies momentum, and Hope quickly tapped into his red-hot form.

Mayank Yadav attempted to rattle the visitors with early pace but occasionally overdid it, including a bouncer that flew over Samson’s head. On a patchy outfield, West Indies relied on clearing the ropes, racing to 79 for one, their highest T20I Powerplay score against India.

Axar Patel’s introduction in the Powerplay gave India a breakthrough when he removed Andrew for 21, but Shimron Hetmyer wasted little time, targeting Arshdeep’s slot offerings.

Naman Dhir, who had been among the wickets, ran into a negative matchup against Hope and conceded 19 in his only over.

West Indies’ incoming batters maintained the tempo. Prince Yadav surprised Hetmyer with a crafty bouncer to get him out for 33, but Rovman Powell capitalised in a 22-run Axar over.

By the time Sherfane Rutherford arrived, Hope had raced to 75. The left-hander tore into Mayank’s final spell, taking 22 runs as West Indies moved past 200.

India’s fielding also faltered: Mayank botched a Rutherford catch, and Tilak could not sight a straight hit off the final ball as Hope completed his century.

Hope’s unbeaten 102, which included four fours and nine sixes, saw the right-hander become the first West Indies player to three T20I hundreds.

India’s reply began brightly. Samson launched a straight hit over Roston Chase’s head and almost single-handedly controlled the Powerplay as Abhishek Sharma struggled for strike.

Chase conceded 25 in his second over, and by the third over India had raced to 50 without loss.

But on a dry surface with no dew, West Indies’ seamers adapted better, mixing their pace to restrain India. Paul struck with his first ball, using a short delivery and smart field placement to hand India their first setback as Sanju Samson held out in the deep for 56.

Three balls later, Ishan Kishan fell attempting to repeat a six.

Abhishek, starved of strike, scratched his way to 29 off 24. Shreyas Iyer made 16 off 11, ball bowled by Motie, stagnating India in the middle.

Unlike West Indies, India could not capitalise on the short balls from the pacers, managing just 32 off 31 at that length.

Tilak Varma (43) and Nitish Reddy (41) adjusted well to forge a 70-run recovery in 5.2 overs, but the late surge collapsed when both departed, leaving the tail with a mountain to climb.

Paul, who claimed the last three wickets, ended with five for 41 while Motie claimed two for 13.

The result marked the first time West Indies defeated India in India while defending a total in T20Is, after six failed attempts. The series is now tied at 2-2 with the final game set for Saturday at 8:30 am Jamaica time.

World.title: Shan’s Heroes’ Weekend Spread
World.content:
Rich, flavourful, and slow-cooked to tender perfection, Shanice Gore’s curry goat brings bold Jamaican spices and authentic island flavour to the table. With Heroes’ Weekend coming up, it’s the perfect dish to gather family and friends around for a hearty, satisfying meal worth celebrating!

Serves: 6 Ingredients

3 lb goat meat, cut into pieces 1 whole onion, chopped 2 stalks scallion, chopped 4 cloves garlic, crushed 1 Scotch bonnet pepper 2 tsp all-purpose seasoning 3 tbsp curry powder, using your favourite brand 2 tbsp cooking oil Hot water, added gradually as needed 2 medium carrots, sliced 2 medium Irish potatoes, peeled and cubed 1 tsp pimento berries Additional onion, garlic and scallion, to taste, for finishing Method

1. Clean and trim the goat meat, then pat dry. Season with the onion, scallion, garlic, Scotch bonnet, allpurpose seasoning and curry powder.

2. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the seasoned goat and sauté for 5–8 minutes, stirring occasionally.

3. Cover, reduce the heat and allow the meat to simmer in its own juices. Add hot water gradually as the liquid reduces, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. Continue simmering until the goat is tender, approximately 2–3 hours, depending on the meat.

4. Once the goat is tender, add the carrots, Irish potatoes, pimento and additional onion, garlic and scallion. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding a little more hot water if needed.

5. Simmer for another 20–30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the gravy reaches your preferred consistency.

6. Serve hot with rice and peas and a fresh salad.

Shan’s tip: Keep the Scotch bonnet whole for flavour with less heat, or chop it for a spicier curry. A little fresh cilantro stirred in towards the end also adds lovely flavour.

World.title: Diddy rushed to hospital after prison fight with Dudus — report
World.content:
American rapper P Diddy and Jamaican drug lord Christopher 'Dudus' Coke a

American music mogul Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs was reportedly rushed to hospital on Wednesday after allegedly getting into a physical altercation with convicted Jamaican drug lord Christopher ‘Dudus’ Coke.

According to a TMZ report, the confrontation reportedly erupted after Combs allegedly caused trouble that resulted in disciplinary action against fellow inmates.

During the alleged scuffle, Combs reportedly sustained a head injury and was subsequently transported to an outside medical facility for treatment.
