World.title: IMD announces onset of winter monsoon in south Peninsular India, summer monsoon withdrawal completes on normal date
World.content:
Thursday saw a timely withdrawal of the Summer Monsoon (Photo: PTI).

A diagrammatic representation of the Southwest Monsoon withdrawal.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The southwest (summer) monsoon withdrew from the entire country on Thursday, exactly on the date of its normal withdrawal, while the northeast (winter) monsoon rainfall activity simultaneously commenced over part of south Peninsular India, IMD said.Summer monsoon normally starts withdrawing from west Rajasthan on Sept 17 and its withdrawal process ends on Oct 15. This year, the withdrawal started on Sept 19. Last year, the complete monsoon withdrawal happened by Oct 16.âWith the onset of the northeast Monsoon, a wet spell with isolated heavy falls is likely over many parts of south Peninsular India till Oct 21,â said the Met department. The parts of south India that witnessed winter rainfall showers on Thursday include Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, south interior Karnataka and Kerala.IMD has already predicted a ânormalâ winter monsoon in south Peninsular India during the Oct-Dec period. Overall, south Peninsular India receives about 30% of its annual rainfall during the northeast monsoon season (Oct to Dec). Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal receive approximately 48% of their annual rainfall during the season.Normal winter monsoon rainfall this year may bring some relief to the region, which received the fourth-lowest summer monsoon rainfall since 1901 and the second-lowest since 2001.Though the country as a whole recorded a deficit of nearly 13% during the June-Sept summer monsoon period â the fourth-lowest season since 2001 and 13th lowest since 1901 â the deficit in Karnataka was as high as 30% followed by 28% in Kerala, 25% in Andhra Pradesh and 20% in Tamil Nadu.

World.title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Thursday launched the Jan Neeti Bharat party and announced that it would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career to pursue politics independently.

In a video message on X, Mittal said the party will focus on making people central to policymaking and ensuring that the government remains accountable to them throughout its five-year term, rather than only on election day.

"Politics rules over you. In Jan Neeti, you will be the ones who rule," she said, announcing the party's name and its decision to contest the state polls due early next year.

Her decision to launch a party of her own places her among a group of civil servants who left government service before their scheduled retirement to enter politics.

Here are 10 former civil servants who made the transition from bureaucracy to politics before completing their service.

1. Yashwant Sinha

Yashwant Sinha resigned from the Indian Administrative Service in 1984 to enter active politics. He joined the Janata Party and subsequently became associated with the Janata Dal before joining the BJP.

Sinha first served as Union finance minister in the Chandra Shekhar government in 1990-91.





Under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he returned to the finance ministry in 1998 and held the portfolio until 2002, when he became external affairs minister.

His political career also included membership of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Sinha later distanced himself from the BJP and joined the Trinamool Congress in 2021, before contesting the 2022 presidential election as the opposition's joint candidate.

2. Ajit Jogi

Ajit Jogi left the IAS in 1986 to enter politics and joined the Congress. He had served as a district collector before moving into political life and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha.

Jogi's biggest political breakthrough came in 2000, when Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh. He became the newly created state's first chief minister, holding office until 2003.

After years in the Congress, Jogi broke away from the party in 2016 and founded the Janata Congress Chhattisgarh, seeking to establish an independent regional political platform.

His career stands out as an example of a former administrator moving from district-level governance to the leadership of a newly formed state and later attempting to build a party of his own.

3. Mani Shankar Aiyar

Mani Shankar Aiyar resigned from the Indian Foreign Service in 1989 to enter politics. He had served as a diplomat for more than two decades and spent part of his career on deputation to the Prime Minister's Office under Rajiv Gandhi.

Aiyar joined the Congress and won the Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha seat in Tamil Nadu in 1991. He went on to become a prominent party leader and served as Union minister for petroleum and natural gas during the UPA government.

He also held the panchayati raj portfolio and was involved in efforts to strengthen local self-government institutions.

4. Arvind Kejriwal

Arvind Kejriwal resigned from the Indian Revenue Service in 2006 after working in the income tax department.

He had become involved in the Right to Information movement and founded the non-governmental organisation Parivartan to address citizens' grievances.

His political journey gathered momentum during the Ana Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which campaigned for a stronger anti-corruption law. In 2012, Kejriwal founded the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), choosing to build a political organisation rather than join an established party.

AAP made its electoral debut in the 2013 Delhi assembly elections, when Kejriwal defeated then chief minister Sheila Dikshit. He became Delhi chief minister in December 2013 and returned to the post after the party's victories in 2015 and 2020.

5. KJ Alphons

KJ Alphons took voluntary retirement from the IAS in 2006 and entered electoral politics in Kerala. He contested the Kanjirappally assembly seat in Kerala as an independent candidate supported by the Left Democratic Front and won.

Alphons later founded the Jana Shakti platform before joining the BJP in 2011. His political journey subsequently took him to Parliament, when he became a Rajya Sabha member.

In 2017, he was inducted into the Narendra Modi government as Union minister of state for tourism, with independent charge, and also handled electronics and information technology.

His transition from a civil servant known for urban development initiatives to a state-level politician and Union minister is an example of an officer moving across political formations during his career.

6. Satyapal Singh

Satyapal Singh, a 1980-batch IPS officer of the Maharashtra cadre, opted for voluntary retirement in January 2014 while serving as Mumbai police commissioner, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.

He joined the BJP and contested the Baghpat Lok Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh in 2014, defeating Rashtriya Lok Dal chief Ajit Singh. He retained the constituency in the 2019 general election.

Singh served as Union minister of state for human resource development and water resources during the Modi government's first term.

Before entering politics, he had served in several police leadership roles and was known for his work in law enforcement.

7. OP Choudhary

OP Choudhary, a 2005-batch IAS officer, resigned from the service in 2018 while serving as Raipur collector to enter politics. He joined the BJP and contested the Kharsia assembly constituency in Chhattisgarh in the same year.

Choudhary lost that election but returned to the electoral contest in 2023, this time winning the Raipur City South seat.

He was subsequently inducted into the Chhattisgarh government as a minister.

His career highlights the uncertain transition from administration to politics. Unlike officers who win their first election, Choudhary's initial defeat did not end his political ambitions. He returned five years later and secured a place in the state Cabinet.

8. Aparajita Sarangi

Aparajita Sarangi, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre, took voluntary retirement in 2018 while serving as joint secretary in the Union rural development ministry.

She joined the BJP in November that year and contested the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Bhubaneswar. Sarangi won the seat, defeating Biju Janata Dal candidate Arup Patnaik.

She retained the constituency in the 2024 general election, establishing herself as a BJP leader in Odisha.

Sarangi's transition was particularly swift: she moved from a senior central government position to an electoral contest within months of leaving the service and subsequently secured two consecutive Lok Sabha victories.

9. AK Sharma

AK Sharma, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre, took voluntary retirement in January 2021, around 18 months before his scheduled superannuation.

Sharma had spent a substantial part of his career working in the Prime Minister's Office and was associated with Narendra Modi's administration during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister and later as prime minister.

After leaving the service, Sharma joined the BJP and was elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council.

He subsequently became a minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, handling portfolios including urban development and energy.

His move demonstrated how a senior bureaucrat with experience in the central administration could enter state politics and secure a position in the Cabinet without first contesting a direct assembly election.

10. Asim Arun

Asim Arun, a 1994-batch IPS officer, took voluntary retirement in January 2022 while serving as Kanpur police commissioner.

He joined the BJP soon afterwards, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.

Arun contested the Kannauj assembly seat and won, entering a constituency associated with the Samajwadi Party. He was subsequently inducted into the Yogi Adityanath government.

His political entry came within weeks of his voluntary retirement, making him one of the clearest recent examples of a serving police officer moving directly into electoral politics before the end of his career.

Bonus: K Annamalai

K Annamalai, a 2011-batch IPS officer of the Karnataka cadre, resigned from the police service in September 2019, before completing his tenure. He had served as superintendent of police in Udupi and Chikkamagaluru districts before leaving the force.

He joined the BJP in August 2020 and rose rapidly through the party's ranks. In July 2021, he was appointed the BJP's Tamil Nadu president, becoming one of the party's most prominent faces in the state.

Annamalai contested the 2021 Tamil Nadu assembly election from Aravakurichi but lost to the DMK's R Elango. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, he contested from Coimbatore but lost to DMK candidate Ganapathi P Rajkumar.

In June 2026, Annamalai quit the BJP following differences with the party leadership over its political strategy in Tamil Nadu and launched a new political movement, 'We The Leaders'. World.title: ‘Track maintenance works during festival season disrupt holiday travel plans’
World.content:
The track maintenance works undertaken by the Indian Railways during the festive season are leading to cancellation/rescheduling of trains and, in turn, affecting holiday travel plans, alleged passengers.

While South Western Railway (SWR) has cancelled day train services between Bengaluru and Mangaluru/Karwar during the Navaratri/Dasara holidays to undertake track maintenance works on the Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat section, Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd., (KRCL) has cancelled services of Mangaluru Central-Madgaon-Mangaluru Central Passenger (56616/56615) between Karwar and Madgaon for a few days and rescheduled services for some other days between October 1 and October 20 for maintenance works between Madgaon and Karwar.

Though the KRCL had announced the Madgaon-Mangaluru Central Passenger would depart with a 2.40 hours delay against the scheduled departure on Tuesday at 2.15 p.m., the train operated late up to 4.53 hours till Surathkal to reach Mangaluru Central with a four-hour delay at 2 a.m., instead of 9.55 p.m. on October 14, said Uday Bhandarkar, a passenger from Kundapura.

While the corporation had not announced any rescheduling of the service for October 14, the train operated with 4.30 hours delay till Surathkal to reach Central with 3.22 hours delay at 1.17 a.m. on October 15.

Coincides with Navaratri

Mr. Bhandarkar regretted that the track maintenance works scheduled by the KRCL coincide with the Navaratri celebrations wherein thousands of people from coastal Karnataka travel to Goa to offer prayers to their family deities. Returning to places along the coast beyond midnight with families is difficult. With public transport virtually not available in those hours, it would be highly difficult and unsafe for families to reach home, he said.

Change schedule

Mr. Bhandarkar said, “While we understand that track infrastructure and power maintenance are essential for safety, scheduling these works during major festivals causes distress among passengers.

“We request the Railways to postpone the ongoing track and power maintenance works for at least one week until the Navaratri festival concludes,” he said.

As per the KRCL notification, Madgaon-Mangaluru Central Passenger would have a 90-minute delayed start on October 16 and 18 and 160 minutes on October 20.

Cascading effect

The KRCL spokesperson told The Hindu that the delays on October 13 and 14 were due to major track renewal works on the Madgaon-Karwar section. As the KRCL predominantly operates on a single line section, delays in one section would have a cascading effect on train movements in subsequent sections affecting the onward journey.

World.title: 11 teams to take part in fifth edition of ‘Pili Parba’ in Mangaluru on October 18
World.content:
As many as 11 teams will take part in the fifth edition of ‘Pili Parba’, to be organised by Kudla Samskrutika Prathistana at the Nehru Maidan here on October 18.

Talking to reporters on behalf of the prathistana on Thursday, Mangaluru City South MLA D. Vedavyasa Kamath said the teams are from Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Kasaragod districts. Though there was demand for more teams, the prathistana restricted the number to 11. A total of 10 teams took part in the fourth edition of the event last year.

Mr. Kamath said every team would be given 22 minutes to perform, which includes time for team members to come in a procession to the four stages where they would display different skills of traditional ‘Tiger dance’. Apart from giving cash prizes to the first three teams, prizes for “Disciplined team”, “Best Tiger procession”, “Parbada Pili”, “Kappu Pili”, “Mari Pili”, “Mudi”, “Taase”, “Bannagaarike”, and “Dharanimandala” will be given. The top three teams will receive cash prizes of ₹5 lakh, ₹3 lakh and ₹2 lakh, and individual prizes will also be given. Each participating team will receive participation prize amount of ₹50,000.

He said a gallery has been set up to accommodate 6,000 people to watch performances on all the four stages. A total of six umpires will adjudicate the performance, and a third umpire will also be there. There will be replay facility. The performances will be shown on LCD screens at the venue, and will go on till 10 p.m., Mr. Kamath said.

Honorary-president of prathistana Giridhar Shetty also spoke on the occasion.

World.title: Bombe Mane returns with tales of tradition
World.content:
A vibrant collection of dolls that tell the stories of the heritage city and mythological tales have returned to households in Mysuru as Dasara unfolds.

Setting up a Bombe Mane(Dasara Doll Show) during Dasara is an annual tradition affair for many households in Mysuru. A house located at 2nd Cross in Ramachandra Agrahara, known for its Bombe Mane for the past three decades, has once again opened its doors to a magnificent collection of dolls with distinctive artistic designs.

The house has a dedicated floor for the arrangement of dolls. The display curated by Hemalatha Kumaraswamy and her family, brings to life a numerous characters and episodes of Indian mythology with particular focus on the Ramayana and the Mahabharata. Incarnations of Rama and Krishna form the central theme of the display, alongside traditional Pattada Raja Rani dolls.

The dolls are displayed on nine tiered platforms. Activities largely associated with the Mysuru palace and its Dasara celebrations have found a unique place in this Bombe Mane. Dolls depicting Jamboo Savari, private durbar, Nandi Dhwaja, Jatti Kalaga and erstwhile Mysuru royals, specially designed by artists, are the highlights of display. Some of iconic structures existing in around the city built during the era of Wadiyars are featured in doll show.

Mythological characters like Shakunthala and King Dushyantha have also inspired the curator, adding another dimension to the collection. There are family dolls too highlighting wedding, naming ceremony and other events.

The dolls featured in Bombe Mane have been sourced from various parts of the country and the massive collection of these colourful dolls attracts the visitors not only from Mysuru, but from other cities too.

However, Ms. Hemalatha said there is a perceptible decline in Bombe Mane tradition lately. “As younger generation show less interest, Bombe Mane tradition has gradually declined in Mysuru. Several households have discontinued their display of dolls house following the demise of older generation,” said Ms. Hemalatha.

Waste materials transformed

Meanwhile, a variety of waste materials undergo artistic transformation in the hands of Sundareshan in Saraswathipuram, where Bombe Mane located at 5th Main attracts the visitors with the theme of patriotism.

Dolls commemorating the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram, Kittur Chennamma are among the major attraction. Curated by Bhanumathi Sundareshan, the Bombe Mane features large-sized dolls dressed in traditional attire. “We invite children every evening and explain to them the tradition of Bombe Mane,” says Ms. Sundareshan. Their family offers Bombe Bagina to kids visiting their home.

Meanwhile, Dr. Pooja, a medical professional, has preserved dolls that are a more than a century old. The tradition started by older generation continues to flourish in their household located on 3rd Stage of Vijayanagara.

During each day of Navaratri festival, Chamundeshwari doll is adorned in a saree, whose colour correspondence to that of presiding deity of Chamundi Hill, said Dr. Pooja.

As part of ‘Mane Mane Gombe’, Madhuri P. at 33rd Cross Bhagadi, Rashmi at 2nd Cross J.P. Nagara, Geetha Srihari near Mahashakthi Ganapathi Devalaya, Giridarshini Layout, Pushparaju near RTO Circle, Usharao at Srirampura, Lakshminagaraju at Sharada Devi Nagara, Suma Mahadev, near Gopika Agarbathi Factory, Agrahara, Rajeshwari Ganesh at 15th Cross, Aravinda Nagara, Ramamani Gurudut at 4th Cross, Chayaraja Gopal at 4th Cross, Uttaradhimutt Road, displayed dolls in their Bombe Mane.

World.title: Maharashtra declares 40 more talukas drought-hit, announces ₹5,000 aid for farmers
World.content:
The Maharashtra government on Wednesday declared 40 more talukas in the State drought-hit and decided to deposit an advance relief amount of ₹5,000 in the bank accounts of farmers ahead of Diwali.

Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said, “More 40 regions are added, the drought measures will be implemented in all announced drought regions.”

He also warned cooperative societies, district banks, nationalised banks and microfinance companies against pressuring farmers to recover loans.

Relief measures

The government had earlier declared 265 talukas drought-hit. With 40 more talukas added to the list, the total has risen to 305. Trigger 1 and Trigger 2 have been applied in these talukas, making them eligible for assistance under the Centre’s National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) guidelines. The measures include a complete waiver of examination fees for students in drought-hit talukas, without any eligibility criteria.

“The government will purchase the fodder cultivated by farmers at a guaranteed price to make fodder available for animals,” Mr. Fadnavis said, outlining the fodder policy.

Minister of State for Relief and Rehabilitation Makrand Jadhav Patil said the government had decided to implement 12 measures to provide relief to farmers. These include exemption from land revenue, restructuring of crop loans, a stay on the recovery of agriculture-related loans, exemption from current electricity bills for agricultural pumps, and a waiver of examination fees for school and college students.

Water management

Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule reiterated that tankers should be used only as a last resort to address water scarcity. He directed officials to restart water supply schemes that had been shut down due to pending electricity bills or a lack of transformers.

Mr. Bawankule, who chairs the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Drought, also sought proposals from District Collectors for district-wise measures within 15 days.

“Before the drinking water situation becomes critical, wells where water is available should be acquired to overcome water scarcity. Water supply schemes which are 75 to 80 percent complete should be completed on priority. Tanker App and GPS system should be started to ensure proper and smooth water supply,” he said.

He urged the districts concerned to use funds available under the Fifteenth Finance Commission to clear pending electricity bills. Other districts were directed to take steps to clear their dues under the one-time settlement scheme.

Meanwhile, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has decided to suspend water supply across the city every Thursday from October 15. It will also prohibit the use of drinking water for construction and initiate the closure of vehicle-washing centres until the next monsoon.

“The State has received less rainfall due to the El Niño effect and as the El Niño effect is expected to continue till next year, it is necessary to manage the available water storage economically and in a very well-planned manner,” the PMC said in a statement.

The civic body’s decision follows a Government Resolution issued by the State Water Resources Department on October 6, directing micro-planning of available water storage in dams across the State, based on availability and usage. The resolution also called for measures to secure drinking water supplies and mitigate the impact of a possible drought-like situation.

World.title: Health Minister rules out withdrawal of hospital billing transparency order
World.content:
Health Minister U.T. Khader has ruled out withdrawing the Food Safety and Drugs Administration (FSDA) Department’s circular mandating hospital pharmacies to disclose the purchase price and maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills, even as the Karnataka Pharma Retailers and Distributors Organisation (KPRDO) has sought its withdrawal on legal and operational grounds.

“The landing-cost disclosure issue is before the Supreme Court, and the requirement will depend on the court’s order. There are no plans to withdraw the order on displaying the MRP and purchase costs,” Mr. Khader told The Hindu on Thursday.

Retailers’ contention

The KPRDO, in a representation to the Minister and Food Safety and Drugs Administration Commissioner K. Srinivas, argued that the circular, issued under the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments (KPME) Act, 2007, could not impose additional requirements on hospital pharmacies operating under licences issued under the Central Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

“Singling out the healthcare sector to disclose wholesale procurement prices on retail invoices, while other retail businesses operate under the standard MRP system, is inherently biased,” KPRDO president C. Jayaram said.

The organisation also cited fluctuating procurement costs and the burden of updating hospital information systems to print batch-wise landing prices on individual bills. Disclosing purchase prices without context could trigger disputes between patients and hospital staff, Mr. Jayaram said.

If margins on particular medicines were considered excessive, they should be regulated through the Union government’s existing price-control mechanisms, including the Drugs (Prices Control) Order and the National List of Essential Medicines, he argued.

Itemised bills mandatory

Mr. Khader said the State would continue enforcing requirements on the display of treatment and service charges and the issue of itemised bills by private medical establishments.

In 2023, the Health Department directed private medical establishments to display their treatment and service rates prominently at reception desks and provide patients with complete rate booklets under Section 10 (1) of the KPME Act.

The department has also directed hospitals to issue itemised bills, following complaints that some establishments were charging consolidated rates for treatments and services without providing a breakdown of individual charges. The requirement is covered under the KPME Amendment Act, 2017, the Minister said.

World.title: Wildlife photography exhibition opens at Hawa Mahal in Visakhapatnam
World.content:
Nearly 150 photographs showcasing India’s rich wildlife and biodiversity, from tigers in their forest strongholds to the diverse landscapes across the country, are drawing visitors to Hawa Mahal on Beach Road in Visakhapatnam.

The exhibition, WildVizag 2.0, was inaugurated on Saturday as part of World Wildlife Week 2026. Ravindra Dhama, Divisional Forest Officer, Visakhapatnam, formally opened the exhibition as the chief guest. Bobbili MLA Swethakumar Rangarao Bobbili attended as the special guest. Members of the Nagarjunasagar Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) team were also present.

The exhibition features the work of 25 wildlife photographers, with photographs from four States highlighting India’s biodiversity, landscapes and wildlife. It also seeks to create awareness about the forests and wildlife of Andhra Pradesh.

The NSTR team has set up a stall displaying wildlife rescue kits and equipment, offering visitors an opportunity to interact with its staff and learn about the use of the equipment, field protection and conservation efforts.

The exhibition received an encouraging response from students and the public on the opening day. About 85 students from Silver Oaks International School and 30 students from St. Joseph’s Women’s College visited the gallery.

The exhibition will be open on October 4 from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. at Hawa Mahal, Beach Road.

World.title: NHAI to conduct technical study for two RoBs at Kallumthazham
World.content:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) will directly conduct a technical study to evaluate the feasibility of constructing two railway overbridges (ROBs) and an approach road to resolve the severe traffic congestion at Kallumthazham, N.K. Premachandran, MP has said after discussions with NHAI chairperson Santosh Kumar Yadav.

Earlier, an expert committee from TKM College of Engineering was tasked with examining technical solutions for the gridlock at Kallumthazham junction. Based on their findings, a meeting chaired by the MP at Kollam Collectorate had decided that a consultancy should be appointed to conduct a comprehensive feasibility study on constructing two railway overbridges and an approach road.

As per the decision of the Collectorate meeting, the MP submitted a representation to NHAI officials urging the speedy appointment of a consultancy. However, pointing out their official policy that NHAI itself directly executes the construction of all railway overbridges along national highways, the authorities assured the MP that the agency will directly undertake the technical study without engaging an external consultancy. “Considering the urgency of the long-pending traffic bottleneck, NHAI officials have been requested to expedite the technical evaluation and arrive at an immediate decision to begin the work,” said the MP.

World.title: Joint sitting of Parliament endorses emergency, governor's rule in KP amid opposition outcry
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A joint sitting of Parliament on Thursday gave its approval to the Centre’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid a strong protest from the opposition.

The joint session had been summoned to discuss separate resolutions on the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, where the opposition’s PTI was in power.

During the session, which was addressed by both members of the treasury and opposition benches, the government justified its decision while the PTI lambasted the Centre and the allegations levelled against the party.

The Centre took the measures on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

During Thursday’s joint sitting, opposition members turned up carrying placards inscribed with slogans, such as “emergency na manzoor (emergency is unacceptable)”.

PM Shehbaz, who attended part of the session, shook hands with opposition leaders of both the Senate and the NA, pictures and footage showed.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled the two proclamations and separate resolutions regarding the emergency and governor’s rule.

After hours-long debate, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq put the two resolutions to a vote, while opposition members chanted “emergency unacceptable”.

The resolutions approving emergency and governor’s rule were then passed.

At the outset of the proceedings, Chaudhry also presented a motion under Rule 232 of the Parliament (Joint Sitting) Rules 1973 to suspend certain sub-rules so he could move the resolutions.

As loud noes echoed and opposition members chanted “emergency na manzoor”, the speaker again put the motion to a vote by asking the members to stand up, which was then adopted with 214-56 votes.

Subsequently, Chaudhry moved two resolutions before the joint sitting — one for approving the Proclamation of Emergency under Article 232 and the second for the proclamation of governor’s rule under Article 234.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar then opened the discussion on the two resolutions and said members of the treasury benches were ready to reply to any query raised by the opposition.

Explaining the constitutional process to approve the resolution for emergency, he said the joint sitting could reject it by a total majority, ie 51 per cent. Similarly, the resolution for governor’s rule also required a total majority of votes for approval.

The joint sitting also offered prayers for the lives lost, mostly of children, in a roof collapse in Peshawar.

The joint session took place a day after both Houses of Parliament, in separate sittings, passed resolutions endorsing the imposition of emergency in KP.

According to Article 232 , if the “president acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed” before both Houses of the Parliament for approval by each House within 10 days.

Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months”, unless a joint sitting approves its extension. However, such a measure shall not remain in force for more than six months.

Naqvi notes ‘clear stance’ of PTI lawmakers

Speaking during Thursday’s joint sitting, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi urged the opposition to stick to facts when recounting the dialogue held with the government, asserting that the Centre had “no option left” but to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP.

“By God, our hearts did not want to do this,” Naqvi remarked, adding that the treasury members were trying their best so that the measures were not taken in KP.

“I will request only that you let facts remain facts. […] We had no option left, after which we did this and you will definitely oppose it, but we should consider the facts,” the minister said as he sought to provide a “clarification” on the allegations levelled by the opposition.

“Please do not say that we misused terrorism.”

He also refuted what he said was the opposition’s stance that the government delegation left the talks. “We did not get up and leave […] we did not even urge you to hurry up.”

Naqvi, who was part of the government’s delegation during the Oct 3 talks, emphasised: “We tried until the last minute […] It was our effort until the last hour that this (emergency/governor’s rule) is not imposed.”

The minister said the federal government offered its KP counterpart to declare emergency in “12 districts, on which you said fine, let’s do it”. He claimed that PTI’s Asad Qaiser, who was present during the talks, was willing to sign an agreement, but he advised the latter to consult the KP government first.

Pointing towards the opposition benches, Naqvi affirmed that the government was not levelling allegations against them. “I vouch for those sitting here that you were not even a single step behind on [countering] terrorism,” he added.

The minister referred to a video clip — later sharing it on his X account — in which KP Information Minister Shafi Jan was asked to declare that the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) was a terrorist group.

“Those individuals in the TTP who are against the state are terrorists,” Jan responded.

Addressing the opposition members, Naqvi further said: “I believe that you, and those we spoke to, particularly Asad Qaiser sahib, as he responded on [the issue] of terrorism that day, I guarantee that even we were not thinking of the things they were speaking on.”

He went on to acknowledge that all those present in the meeting “had an absolutely clear stance [on terrorism] that we will do this for Pakistan”.

The interior minister, holding a paper, said he suggested to even exclude a term about the PTI calling off its long march, but PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman insisted on keeping it.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi holds a paper during a joint sitting of Parliament on Thursday. — screengrab via DawnNewsTV

Naqvi noted that Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional, had not gone to the site of “even a single operation with the army and only used to say ‘I cannot afford this politically’”.

The minister recalled his efforts to sort out differences between the Centre and KP, such as meetings between Afridi and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the issue of provincial funds.

While saying he did not deem it appropriate to speak about Afridi in his absence, Naqvi claimed he and the PTI leader had discussed a plan to strengthen police forces in five KP districts.

He said the federal government wanted a meeting of the provincial apex committee to be held.

“A press release had to be issued, which would state that we will fight against terrorism together. You can ask for that press release, what was written in it and what happened; everything is before you.”

He recalled that some personnel were martyred in an attack “the same day”, adding that it took place in February.

“We requested the CM sahib and took him to the funerals with us. That was the last day when CM KP attended the funeral of any army officer or jawaan (soldier),” he added.

The minister concluded his speech by reaffirming the Centre’s determination to fight the wave of terrorism. He said the fight could not be waged on “under two [different] policies” of the federation and the province.

He urged the PTI to hold discussions with the KP government on what matters were wrong, adding: “No political party should be accused of terrorism. This is a major thing. But if something has happened, it should be fixed.”

Gohar objects to allegations of ‘backing terrorists’

Speaking on the Parliament’s floor, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said the country was going through a “very fragile situation”.

He lamented that the KP government was accused of “backing terrorists”.

“The prime minister has alleged that we are supporting terrorists. We are disappointed to hear that. You have to apologise to the entire population of KP and us,” he said.

“Prime minister, you have given a message to the entire world that one of the federating units of the country was backing terrorists,“ Gohar added.

He highlighted that the opposition stood with the government during a war with India. “But today we are called supporters of terrorists,” he regretted.

Barrister Gohar rejected the proclamation of emergency and declared that the PTI will make the country stronger and eradicate terrorism when it comes into power again.

He also rejected the government’s claims that PTI leaders did not attend funerals of martyrs, recalling that he himself had attended multiple funerals in KP.

Gohar said the PTI was willing to engage in dialogue with the government provided that its demands were met.

He lamented that speeches of opposition members were not shown in the media.

Dar defends ‘difficult decision’

Speaking towards the end of the debate, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar defended the federal government’s “difficult decision” to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP.

Dar said that the decision was “categorically” in accordance with the Constitution and appealed to the opposition “not to misinterpret or misquote facts” to save personal politics.

“Let me remind you of the history,” he said, saying that the menace of terrorism emerged after the 2014 Army Public School attack in Peshawar.

The PML-N leader recalled that a multi-party moot was held following the attack, with PTI in attendance and on board with the counterterrorism decisions, including the National Action Plan (NAP).

The deputy premier recalled that Operation Zarb-i-Azb and Operation Raddul Fasaad were launched against terrorists, adding that data showed their activities had “ended after the operations”.

“We all are Pakistanis […], but we all have the clarity in our minds regarding the facts,” Dar emphasised. Referring to the opposition, Dar said he could see the PTI was against terrorism, but asked who those “few” were who he alleged opened the borders and let the terrorists enter Pakistan.

“There are a few individuals in the party (PTI) who are responsible for the terrorism reaching its peak,” he claimed. “For how long will we keep repeating the same mistakes due to our petty politics and some individuals?” he asked.

On political reconciliation, Dar said that the menace of terrorism should be dealt with before any other matter. “If not now, then when?”

He also criticised Afridi for holding mobilisation campaigns across Pakistan while his province reeled from the threat of terrorism. Dar contended that the province had “collapsed in terms of governance”.

Referring to the federal cabinet’s Oct 11 meeting in which the decision was made to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, Dar said that PM Shehbaz left the meeting by saying “it’s now or never” to deal with the deteriorating security situation.

Achakzai blames ‘faulty decisions’

Speaking in the Parliament, NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai blamed “faulty decisions” of the country’s rulers for the current situation.

He enquired about the whereabouts of Afridi, who was reported to be in preventative custody.

Achakzai, who leads the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), accused PML-N’s Sadiq of not running the house judiciously as the speaker.

He said the opposition was ready for dialogue on issues such as empowerment of Parliament and eradicating terrorism of all kinds.

“If you hold dialogue on these issues, we will give unconditional support,” he added.

The opposition leader compared the KP imbroglio to the 1971 separation of East Pakistan, noting that Afridi was called a “terrorist”.

“Were multiple attacks on the heads of different political parties in the past in KP committed by Sohail Afridi?” he asked.

Achakzai said terrorism was introduced by those who had brought fighters for the Soviet-Afghan war. “When the Afghan war was over, these terrorists were left free in the tribal areas of the country and they started killing Pakistanis,” he added.

The opposition leader then mentioned the reported deaths during the July unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK).

The TTAP chief sought meetings of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan with his family, friends and party workers. He questioned who had “sent” ex-premier Nawaz Sharif to exile in Saudi Arabia and who “murdered” ex-PM Benazir Bhutto.

The NA speaker took exception to Achakzai’s remarks on his chairing of the session.

“You are saying to me that I am not running the House correctly. You have not read Rule 30. Someone takes their mobile phone; someone disrupts [the proceedings].”

Sadiq further said recordings of members’ speeches that were “anti-state” would not be uploaded on the NA’s social media accounts.

Meanwhile, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas accused the government’s delegation of derailing the dialogue with the opposition, including the Oct 3 talks.

The Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief said some more time should have been allowed to make the talks successful and called for resolving the public’s issues instead of blaming each other.

The senator contended that people voted for the PTI in large numbers during the February 2024 general elections in reaction to Imran’s imprisonment.

Noting that this was his first tenure as a parliament member, Abbas said he realised that the Constitution was a safeguard of the rights of people. He further claimed he did not receive a salary or any perks and privileges from the Senate.

‘We kept waiting’: PPP’s Rehman recounts Oct 3 talks

In her remarks, PPP’s Rehman asked the PTI to define its agenda and reasons for its long march, which the party had announced to stage towards Islamabad but remained within KP.

The senator added that President Asif Ali Zardari and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had insisted on resolving issues through dialogue because terrorism was a red line for them.

She called on the opposition not to dictate to the government and to avoid giving lectures on patriotism.

Rehman emphasised that everyone was trying to find common ground and “a path of action”.

The PPP leader objected to the opposition’s claims that the government delegation left the Oct 3 talks.

“We kept waiting for you. The speaker and I ordered food for you as leaving was not being considered. We could have sat till 5am or 6am,” she said.

Rehman asserted, “We had said we would wait further […] This is not fair to say that we said ‘we are leaving’. Definitely not. Opposite.”

Speaking on the topic, the NA speaker — who chaired the talks — also remarked, “What was the hurry in launching the long march?”

Sadiq referred to a post on X made by Afridi about going ahead with the long march even as the negotiations were underway.

“You said to ignore it, so we kept ignoring it till 3am, so I think, if you want to sit again [at the table] then do not go into further details. Those things took place in confidence; bury them here.”

The PPP vice president remarked that the country faced several emergencies, including those regarding education and poverty, that needed to be seen holistically.

“If you think PPP is going to support any sort of emergency which is against the Constitution, you are wrong,” she declared.

“This Constitution has bound the country together through difficult times. We remember the lessons from the fall of Dhaka,” she said.

“PPP has seen many phases of the path towards democracy. It (martial law) was a dark chapter in history; we do not want the country to go through such an experience again,” Rehman said, recalling “sacrifices” made by her party.

JUI-F says no ‘evidence’ presented

Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), who had earlier submitted a resolution opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, contended that no documentary evidence was presented before the Parliament for the decision.

He argued that the proclamation under Article 234 required a report from the KP governor, but in this case, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had not presented a report explaining why governor’s rule was necessary.

The JUI-F senator said the security situation in Balochistan was also grave and pointed out that a provincial government now had its writ in the Katcha areas without an emergency being imposed there.

Murtaza stressed that free and transparent elections under a fair election commission were the only solution to the existing problems.

World.title: Saudi Arabia accuses Iran of encouraging Houthis in latest escalation
World.content:
A Saudi foreign ministry official on Thursday accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis in the latest escalation of their fight with the kingdom, adding that it continues to arm and train the group.

“Iran continues to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN security council resolutions,” Dr Rayed Krimly, deputy minister for public diplomacy at the foreign ministry, said during a virtual briefing with reporters.

“We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran,” he later said.

The official said the kingdom however remained in communication with Iran, even if Tehran appeared unwilling to offer concessions.

“We continue to have direct communications with Iran,” Krimly told reporters.

“Overall, it doesn’t seem yet that the Iranians are able to provide the necessary concessions for a solution.”

The official went on to accuse the Houthis of refusing to meet in Oman in recent weeks as fighting ramped up between the two sides.

“At the beginning of this escalation, we asked them to meet in Muscat, Oman and they refused,” he added.

“This was the last communication which happened a few weeks ago.”

The world’s top crude oil exporter has in recent days come under sustained attack, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the deadliest in years, as the war with the Houthis dramatically escalates.

Yemen’s civil war reignited in July after a UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle East war that has rocked the region and roiled energy supplies and markets.

The conflict in the country has caused what the United Nations calls one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, leaving most of the nation’s population dependent on aid.

The Saudi-led coalition has fought the Houthis since 2015 after they seized Yemen’s capital Sanaa and forced out the internationally recognised government from the city, until a UN-brokered ceasefire in 2022.

Saudi-led coalition says Houthis attempted to attack dozens of Saudi facilities

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen said on Thursday that the Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said at a press conference that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others.

The coalition also said Houthi attacks on Abha airport, in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border, had killed three people and wounded 28.

Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of “regional actors,” including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats.

The spokesperson also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen’s mountainous areas.

He called on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and said the group should read the coalition’s statement carefully and “between the lines”.

Shortly after the coalition’s statement, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Makkah and Madina.

World.title: Teacher, 30 students killed in Peshawar school roof collapse
World.content:
PESHAWAR: At least 31 people, including 30 students and a female teacher, were killed when a school roof collapsed in the provincial capital’s Afridi Abad area on Thursday.

Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) spokesperson Muhammad Asim initially told Dawn that the death toll had risen to 33, including a female teachers and students aged between seven and 14 and a female teacher.

Later, he said that 30 students students and a female teacher had been killed. According to the official list of casualties shared by LRH, a total of 61 people were brought to the facility, of which 30 were discharged after being treated.

Residents gather during a search operation after a roof collapsed at a school in Peshawar on October 15. —AFP

A spokesman for Rewscue 1122 said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way.

“When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside,” spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said.

Speaking to Geo News, Peshawar Deputy Commissioner Afaq Wazir confirmed that the rescue operation launched after the collapse had concluded.

“Rescue teams have cleared all the debris, and no more injured children are at the scene,” he said.

Following the incident, an emergency was declared at the hospital, said the LRH spokesperson in an earlier statement.

Peshawar DC earlier told Dawn that the roof of Al-Khair School had collapsed, trapping students beneath the debris. According to a statement issued by his office, students were present in their classrooms when the incident occurred.

A rescue official told AFP that the ceiling came down on the students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two storeys. Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed said the building’s structure was weak.

“Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse,” AFP quoted him as saying.

A girl who was injured after a school roof collapse receives first aid at a hospital in Peshawar October 15, 2026. —AFP

Speaking to Dawn, Samiullah, a parent who rushed to the site after hearing about the incident, said he had rescued three girls, all under the age of eight.

“I received a call from home at around 8:50am and reached the site about 10 minutes later, at around 9am. We have six children studying at the school,” he said.

“When I saw the building, I thought my son, who was in a ground-floor classroom beneath the collapsed first floor, had also died. However, he had left the classroom to drink water,” he added.

Resident Sohail told AFP “everyone began screaming in panic” after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse.

“When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said.

Volunteers and relatives shift the body of a victim, killed after a roof collapsed at a school, into an ambulance outside a hospital in Peshawar on October 15, 2026. —AFP

KP governor orders audit

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed grief over the deaths in the school roof collapse and sought a detailed report on the incident. He also directed the authorities to determine the cause of the collapse.

“The loss of precious lives of innocent children is an extremely painful tragedy,” he said, according to a statement, extending his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families.

He prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured children and directed the authorities concerned to provide them with the best possible medical facilities.

In another statement on his X account, the KP governor added that he had also directed a structural safety audit of educational institutions across the province to “identify potential risks and ensure that immediate corrective measures are taken wherever necessary”.

“We cannot allow the safety of our children to be compromised,” Kundi wrote.

Later, Kundi also attended the funeral prayers of the dead. Speaking to the media, he said that a team had been constituted to probe the incident and the inquiry was underway.

“The first step will be to determine who issued the no-objection certificate to the school,” he said. Kundi also announced that the bereaved families would be given Rs1m as compensation while the injured would be given Rs200,000.

“A transparent investigation into the incident will be conducted and those responsible will be identified,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Elementary and Secondary Education Department constituted a fact-finding committee to probe the incident and tasked it with submitting a report on Thursday.

The committee included: Javid Iqbal, the chairman of the Private Schools Regularity Authority; Muhammad Farooq, the deputy secretary of the Elementary and Secondary Education Department; and a member to be co-opted by a committee.

The committee was tasked with probing the incident and ascertaining the facts that led to the roof collapse, unearthing the factors that led to it, suggesting measures to prevent such incidents in the future and making appropriate recommendations.

Separately, KP Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed ordered Peshawar CCPO to oversee the rescue operation and directed the traffic police to establish a “green corridor” to ensure uninterrupted movement of ambulances.

Rescue and police teams were directed to utilise all available resources, a statement said.

“In this hour of grief, KP police stands with the affected families,” the IGP was quoted as saying.

Residents and rescue workers gather near an ambulance after a school roof collapse in Peshawar Pakistan on October 15.—Reuters

PM Shehbaz takes ‘serious notice’

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken “serious notice” of the incident, as he offered his condolences to the bereaved families in a post on X.

“Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country,” DPM Dar said.

He added that “ensuring the safety and protection of our children must remain paramount”.

“All necessary measures must be taken to provide immediate assistance to those affected, ensure the best possible medical care for the injured, and strengthen safety standards in our schools to prevent such tragedies from recurring.”

PM Shehbaz also phone the KP governor according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister offered condolences to the families of the deceased and directed authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to the injured and all possible assistance to the affected families, the statement said.

The prime minister also sought a comprehensive report on the incident.

The governor briefed the prime minister on the incident and informed him that the school owner had been arrested and an investigation into the incident had been launched.

The prime minister directed that all aspects of the incident be examined and action be taken against those responsible in accordance with the law, the statement added.

Condolences

President Asif Ali Zardari also expressed “profound shock and grief” over the tragic school incident in a statement on X.

“This heart-wrenching tragedy has plunged the entire nation into shock,” he said, extending his condolences to the families of the children killed.

He directed relevant authorities to provide top-notch medical facilities to the injured and extend assistance to the affected families. “In this hour of sorrow, the entire nation shares equally in the grief of the affected families,” he said.

President Zardari emphasised the need for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the incident and to ensure that all educational institutions’ buildings were following safety standards.

PM Shehbaz expressed “deep grief and sorrow” over the incident, in a statement shared by his office. He extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured, directing that “all possible medical assistance” be provided.

PM Shehbaz has also issued instructions to expedite relief operations, the statement said.

In a post on X, he said: “My heart is with the families grieving the loss of their children and a teacher in the tragic roof collapse at a school in Peshawar. No parent should have to endure such pain. I extend my deepest condolences and pray for strength for every family affected.”

He said that he had directed that the injured receive the best possible care.

“We will ensure a thorough investigation into this tragedy and take every necessary step to protect the safety of children in schools across the country,” he said.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also expressed grief over the incident.

In a post on X, he said he was “deeply saddened” by the tragedy, adding that the thought of parents sending their children to school in the morning only to receive news of their deaths was heartbreaking.

He expressed solidarity with the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.

Bilawal’s sister, MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari, also extended condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the swift recovery of the injured.

She said schools must be places of learning and protection, adding that those responsible for ensuring children’s safety must be held accountable.

Unicef also expressed its deep sadness over the incident. Unicef representative in Pakistan, Pernille Ironside, said in a statement: “Unicef extends its deepest condolences to the bereaved families and communities affected by this devastating incident.”

“Our thoughts are also with the injured children; we wish them a swift and full recovery. Unicef stands ready to support the government’s response by providing psycho-social support to affected children, families and communities,” she said.

Unicef called for urgent action to ensure that all schools, public and private, meet building safety standards and undergo regular safety inspections.

“These standards must be strictly enforced to prevent such tragedies in future,” Ironside said.

“Every child has the right to learn in a safe environment, where children can learn, grow and thrive, protected from harm. Going to school should never put a child’s life at risk,” she said.

People stand near rubble after a school roof collapse in Peshawar, October 15, 2026. —Reuters

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) said it was “appalled” by the deaths.

“It is important to stress that this was not an accident but a preventable failure, given that police have reportedly attributed the collapse to a weak structure carrying excessive construction,” it said, noting that a similar incident this year had killed 14 children at a tuition centre in Lahore.

The commission called for an “independent, time-bound” inquiry with the findings to be made public. It also stressed the need for accountability of the school owner and the regulators “who allowed unsafe buildings to operate”, compensation for the families affected, and mandatory structural audits of all public and private schools.

Roof collapse incidents

Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, often attributed to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials.

In July, three girls, aged 3 to 13, were killed after a portion of the outer wall of a government primary school near Umerkot collapsed and the rubble fell on them.

The same month, a child died, and at least five other people were injured after the roof of an under-construction private school building collapsed in Lahore’s Baghbanpura neighbourhood.

On June 30, 14 children lost their lives when the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. The incident had come less than two months after four children were killed and 20 people injured after the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan collapsed.

A probe into the DG Khan incident revealed that construction for an extension of the tuition centre’s building was under way when the roof of the classroom collapsed.

Last week, two men died in Pakpattan after the roof of their house collapsed during heavy rain and a windstorm.

In June, a labourer was killed, and three others were injured when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed in Khawaspur locality of Lalamusa, Gujrat. The same month, two people were injured after the roof of a house collapsed in Lahore’s Nishtar area. In August, a couple was killed, and their daughters were injured after the roof of their house in Shahzad Town, Islamabad, collapsed following three days of heavy rainfall.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Trump says military execution of Fort Hood gunman will not be livestreamed
World.content:
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the execution of the Fort Hood gunman would not be livestreamed, but that immediate families of the victims would be able to view it in person.

Nidal Hasan’s execution — scheduled for Dec 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.

“I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well-meaning people would rather not watch him die through streaming or through any other visual device,” Trump wrote.

“He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed. That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!”

Some of Trump’s fellow Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, as well as religious leaders and international observers, had expressed doubts about the Pentagon’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan.

Recent polls have also shown a majority of Americans opposed livestreaming it.

The United Nations said streaming the execution would amount to “torture,” while the president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops said it was a “barbaric promotion of a culture of death,” and both Australia and Britain’s prime ministers described it as “abhorrent”.

Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was sentenced to death in August 2013, after a military jury found him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder.

Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was left partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair from being shot by police during his arrest.

The shooting came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be deployed to Afghanistan.

Under US military law, a US president must approve an execution by firing squad. President Donald Trump did so on Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s recommendation, the Pentagon said last week.

The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.

World.title: Imaan, Hadi to face jail trial in security breach case
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Thursday directed the counsels and witnesses in a case against incarcerated rights activist and lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to appear at the Adiala jail for the next hearing after police suggested a jail trial citing limitations in transporting the accused to the court.

The court also directed the Adiala jail superintendent to arrange a meeting between Imaan and her counsel in accordance with the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978, after the defence submitted an affidavit detailing alleged difficulties faced at a previous meeting.

The instructions came from ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra, who was presiding over the proceedings of a case that pertains to the alleged disruption of a security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest. Imaan and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, have been accused of removing barriers from the route. The couple was indicted in the case on Oct 7.

The lawyers representing them have been seeking a meeting with them, and they boycotted the proceedings at the previous hearing on Wednesday after the judge decided to record the prosecution witnesses’ statements despite the defence’s request to defer the exercise until they could meet the accused.

At the outset of Thursday’s hearing, defence counsels Aimal Khan Mandokhail and Riasat Ali Azad appeared before the court, with the former submitting an affidavit detailing the alleged difficulties he faced while meeting his client, Imaan, at the Adiala jail.

The affidavit stated that the lawyer had received a certified copy of the court order regarding a meeting with his client at 2:52pm and reached the jail at 3:50pm on Wednesday.

Mandokhail stated in the affidavit that he presented the order to the Adiala jail’s deputy superintendent and sought a private meeting with his client in line with the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978 and the court’s directives.

He was allowed to meet the accused at 4:45pm after a wait of nearly an hour, the affidavit said, adding that the meeting took place in a conference room instead of a separate private room.

“The confidentiality of the conversation could not be maintained as everything was being recorded,” he stated.

The affidavit further said that Mandokhail had brought copies of case documents for his clients but was not allowed to take them inside or hand them over to the accused.

Two female constables remained with Imaan, the door was left open and male staff stood outside, allowing jail personnel to “overhear” the conversation, it added.

The meeting continued until 5:10pm, according to the affidavit.

It said that during the discussion, the accused clarified that they were not boycotting the trial. They expressed their desire to appear before the court in person, citing difficulties in following proceedings and consulting their lawyers over video link because of audio and internet issues. They also asked the counsel to challenge the court orders instructing that they join the proceedings via a video link.

Lawyer Riasat Ali Azad told the court that Mandokhail had not been allowed to take the case record into the meeting. Mandokhail said that although the meeting had taken place, an “effective discussion” on the case had not been possible.

Judge Sipra asked jail authorities why the accused had not been produced before the court and whether they had submitted a report in this regard.

He directed that the SSP (Headquarters) be summoned if no report was forthcoming, following which the hearing was briefly adjourned until 11am.

Police suggest jail trial

When proceedings resumed, the judge directed Superintendent of Police (Headquarters) Pari Gul to appear before the court within 15 minutes, saying the officer should be informed that only a 15-minute window was available.

Before the official’s arrival, the court was informed that jail authorities had formally requested a vehicle to transport Imaan and Hadi to the court, but Islamabad police had responded that they lacked the required vehicle and three constables to accompany them.

Later, SP (Headquarters) explained that a large police contingent was deployed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. She suggested that Imaan and Hadi’s trial be held on jail premises.

The court was informed that the SP’s office had moved a request for a jail trial, but no final decision had been taken. Gul sought two to three hours to update the court while state counsel Ali Azad urged the judge to fix a date for the next hearing.

Judge Sipra observed that he had been repeatedly directing that the accused be produced before the court, adding that police could have made the request earlier. Expressing dismay over the police’s conduct, he said he wanted to know exactly what the police were doing as their “actions have completely altered the course of the matter”.

Lawyer Azad argued that police should produce accused persons in court daily.

“Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha are not terrorists that bringing them to court would pose significant challenges, and they could even arrive in a tonga,” he remarked. He questioned how a trial could proceed in the absence of the accused and requested that the proceedings not be recorded.

At this point, Imaan’s mother, former human rights minister Shireen Mazari, asked the authorities to explain how her daughter and Hadi were once brought to court at 10pm and 12 vehicles had arrived when they were presented before the court.

Subsequently, Imaan and Hadi appeared before the court via a video link, and Judge Sipra briefed them on the proceedings.

SP Gul said a formal notification regarding the jail trial would be issued the same day.

Hadi informed the court that he had no objection to appearing in person or undergoing a jail trial. However, he emphasised that lawyers and journalists should also be allowed to attend proceedings at the jail.

The court adjourned the hearing until Friday and directed the lawyers and witnesses to appear at the Adiala Jail for the next session.

Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case pertaining to controversial social media posts.

The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and Hadi were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

World.title: ECP rejects Punjab govt's proposal for holding LG polls in April 2027
World.content:
ISLAMABAD/LAHORE: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday rejected the Punjab government’s proposal for pushing local government polls to April next year.

Earlier this month, the electoral body proposed holding local government elections in Punjab on December 14 and sent a draft of the suggested schedule to the Punjab chief secretary for consultation.

However, the Punjab government on Wednesday proposed holding the elections in phases on April 4, 11 and 18, citing smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January.

On Thursday, the ECP rejected the government’s request. The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja.

The commission was briefed that in response to ECP’s letter on Oct 2 and draft election programme, the Punjab government replied on Oct 14 that due to dense fog and severe cold weather in December and the commencement of Ramazan in February, it wanted to hold local government elections in three phases in April 2027, a handout by the commission said.

According to the statement, the ECP termed the Punjab government’s reply “unsatisfactory” and said a consultative process with the provincial government had been completed on Aug 20, in which the provincial government had agreed to hold local government elections in Punjab between Dec 15 and Jan 15, 2027.

“Now, the provincial government wants to change the proposed time frame,” the commission said.

The statement said that keeping in view its constitutional and legal responsibilities, the ECP had decided to hold local government elections in Punjab and issue the election schedule immediately. It directed its office to immediately present the draft election programme for Punjab for the commission’s approval.

The ECP said it had asked the provincial government to provide list of officers to appoint as district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers. Expressing disappointment over non-provision of lists so far, it directed the provincial government to provide the lists within a week.

Punjab seeks delay

The Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department had written to the ECP on Wednesday seeking to delay the local government polls.

The letter, which conveyed the ministerial committee’s decision, cited smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January, followed by the commencement of Ramazan in February, as reasons for not holding the elections as scheduled.

The letter said the cabinet’s ministerial committee had held its second meeting on October 5, during which it deliberated at length on the ECP’s draft election schedule.

The committee discussed scenarios arising from the likely tough weather conditions and Ramazan, the letter stated.

It proposed holding the local government elections in phases to facilitate the effective deployment of election staff and security personnel, the efficient transportation of polling materials, better administrative oversight and improved accessibility for voters.

The phased approach would also help avoid adverse weather conditions typically experienced during December and January and the period immediately following Ramazan, the letter said.

The letter added that the Punjab cabinet considered the committee’s recommendations early on Wednesday and approved a proposal to hold the elections in three phases on April 4, 11 and 18, 2027, all of which fall on Sundays.

The cabinet also decided that the allocation of districts among the three phases may be deliberated and thereafter mutually agreed with the ECP in a dedicated meeting, keeping in view administrative, logistical, security and geographical considerations as well as weather conditions, the letter said.

LG polls

The last local government elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013. Polling took place in phases between October and December 2015, and elected councils assumed office in 2017 after indirect elections for mayors and chairpersons. Since then, local body polls in Punjab have experienced repeated delays.

The PTI government had dissolved the elected local bodies in April 2019 before they completed their tenure. The move was later struck down by the Supreme Court, which restored them. They eventually completed their term on Dec 31, 2021.

Successive provincial governments repeatedly amended or replaced the Punjab Local Government Act. Each legislative change required the ECP to restart preparations, including delimitation and election planning. Changing laws and administrative delays by successive governments contributed significantly to the postponement of the local body elections.

Under Article 140A of the Constitution and the Elections Act, local government elections should be held within 120 days of the expiry of local bodies’ terms. Since the councils’ term ended in Dec 2021, elections were due by April 2022, but they have been repeatedly postponed.

On October 5, the ECP, in a meeting, upheld that it was prepared to hold local government polls across the province.

World.title: India expected to overtake Japan as world's 4th largest economy in 2027: IMF
World.content:
India is expected to become the world’s fourth-largest economy by 2027, overtaking Japan, according to International Monetary Fund (IMF) projections that on Thursday laid out the Asian nations’ contrasting trajectories.

The IMF said Japan would remain the fourth-largest country by nominal gross domestic product this year, but in 2027 India is set to take its place, with a GDP reaching $4.52 trillion.

Japan is slated to slip to sixth place that year, falling behind both India and the United Kingdom, the projection showed.

India has shown strong growth in recent years despite global economic headwinds, with the IMF this week raising its forecasts for 2026 growth to hit 7.0 per cent.

Japan, by contrast, is plagued by an ageing population and other structural problems that have seen the Asian giant’s growth stagnate.

The United States is the world’s largest economy, followed by China and Germany.

Releasing the IMF’s regional economic outlook for Asia-Pacific on Thursday, Asia Director Krishna Srinivasan said India entered the current energy price shock caused by the US-Israel war on Iran from a strong position.

“India entered this with very strong fundamentals,” he said. “Growth was strong, fiscal prudence was pretty much enshrined, they had lots of reserves and so on. And so in that context, they have responded well to the shock.”

Growth in Japan, by contrast, is projected to slow to 0.7pc in 2026, with the country hard hit by an increase in energy prices —and wider inflation— that has seen the Bank of Japan raise interest rates to their highest level in three decades.

The country, long haunted by deflation, has seen a sustained increase in consumer prices since the spring of 2022, and spiking energy prices from the Iran war have further fuelled those rises.

The fall of the yen, which hit its lowest level in 40 years against the dollar over the summer, is further driving up the cost of imports.

Japan’s ageing population is also weighing on economic activity.

The IMF’s Srinivasan said Japan’s economy was benefiting from the boom in artificial intelligence investments, but not as much as its regional neighbours.

The benchmark Nikkei index in Tokyo fell by nearly five per cent on Thursday, dragged down by a plunge in tech stocks amid doubts over the profitability of the AI sector.

World.title: Student's suicide case: Islamabad court grants interim bail to co-suspect
